His father's name, יונה, and his native city come from the anonymous prologue to ספר המסעות; the year is approximate. See the Jewish Encyclopedia, the National Library of Israel and the translated primary prologue.

ר׳ בנימין בן יונה מטודלה.place: Tudela and the Ebro route toward Zaragoza
ר׳ בנימין בן יונה מטודלה.event: Around 1165–1166, according to a widely accepted reconstruction, ר׳ בנימין בן יונה מטודלה leaves Tudela and follows the Ebro corridor through Zaragoza, Tortosa, Tarragona and Barcelona. Alternative scholarship begins the journey as early as 1159–1160, so 1165 is a map anchor rather than an exact departure date. His purpose is not stated and proposed identities as merchant, pilgrim or communal investigator remain hypotheses. See the University of Manchester study and the Auñamendi Basque Encyclopedia.

On the west-to-east European route, ר׳ בנימין בן יונה מטודלה passes through Girona and Narbonne and records the Jewish communities and scholars of Béziers, Montpellier, Lunel, Posquières, Saint-Gilles, Arles and Marseille. The year is approximate; the ordered itinerary, not an individual calendar date, is secure. See the route and translated text in the Fordham Medieval Sourcebook and the Jewish Encyclopedia.

After sailing from Marseille toward Genoa, ר׳ בנימין בן יונה מטודלה travels through Pisa and Lucca to Rome, whose monuments and Jewish community he describes in unusual detail. He then follows the Italian peninsula through Campania and Apulia to the Adriatic crossing at Otranto. The year is an approximate itinerary marker. See the primary itinerary and contents and the scholarly Literature of Travel and Exploration.

Traveling by Corfu and the Greek coast through Corinth, Thebes and Thessaloniki, ר׳ בנימין בן יונה מטודלה reaches Constantinople. His account describes the imperial capital, Hagia Sophia, ceremonial life, commerce and the constrained position of its Jewish population. The sequence is secure, but the year is approximate. See the Fordham edition of the itinerary and Literature of Travel and Exploration.

After crossing the Aegean and moving along the coasts of Anatolia, Syria and Lebanon, ר׳ בנימין בן יונה מטודלה reaches the Land of Israel and describes Acre, Jerusalem, Bethlehem, Hebron and other biblical sites. Jerusalem is a probable personal visit, although modern scholars warn that errors and difficult Crusader-period travel conditions make some individual Holy Land stops uncertain. The year is approximate. See Literature of Travel and Exploration and the National Library of Israel.

Proceeding through Damascus, Aleppo, Harran and Mosul, ר׳ בנימין בן יונה מטודלה reaches Baghdad, where he gives an extensive account of the caliphate, the exilarch and the city's academies and Jewish population. Baghdad is generally accepted as a firsthand destination. Reports extending toward Central Asia, India and China increasingly depend on informants and are therefore not mapped as his personal movements. See the Jewish Encyclopedia and the critical University of Manchester study.

On the return journey, ר׳ בנימין בן יונה מטודלה is probably in Egypt around 1171, describing Fustat, Cairo and Alexandria in substantial detail. The exact route between Mesopotamia and Egypt is debated, and descriptions of India, China and other distant lands are not proof that he visited them. See Literature of Travel and Exploration and the Jewish Encyclopedia.

From Alexandria, ר׳ בנימין בן יונה מטודלה sails toward Sicily and records Messina and Palermo, the final places in his itinerary treated with the density characteristic of firsthand observation. Later brief notices about Germany, Bohemia and northern France are generally treated as reported information rather than proof of visits. The year is approximate. See Literature of Travel and Exploration and the Fordham Medieval Sourcebook.

In the Jewish year 4933 (1173 CE), ר׳ בנימין בן יונה מטודלה returns with his travel notes to Castile. An anonymous editor's prologue says that the resulting Hebrew book preserves what he saw and what he learned from trustworthy people. The source does not say that he died in 1173, despite that date's frequent later use as a death year; his subsequent life is unknown. See the translated primary prologue, the Jewish Encyclopedia and the University of Manchester chronology review.

ר׳ שלמה בן אברהם אבן פרחון.event: ר׳ שלמה בן אברהם אבן פרחון is conventionally placed at birth around 1130 in Qal'a, identified by Encyclopaedia Judaica and the Jewish Encyclopedia as Calatayud in Aragon. The date is an authority-file approximation, and some modern Hebrew accounts instead connect the name Qal'a with Qal'at Bani Hammad in North Africa; the marker therefore records the prevailing identification rather than certainty. See Encyclopaedia Judaica, the Jewish Encyclopedia and the Wikimedia authority data.

By the later 1150s, ר׳ שלמה בן אברהם אבן פרחון has left Iberia and reached Salerno. In the preface to his lexicon he explains that local readers knew the Hebrew dictionary of ר׳ מנחם בן סרוק but lacked access to the Judaeo-Arabic grammatical and lexical achievements of Andalusian scholars; this intellectual need motivates his Hebrew synthesis. The year 1155 is only an approximate pre-1160 map anchor, not a documented arrival date. See the Jewish Encyclopedia and Encyclopaedia Judaica.

On 1 Kislev 4921, in late 1160, ר׳ שלמה בן אברהם אבן פרחון completes מחברת הערוך in Salerno. Written in Hebrew, its grammatical introduction and root lexicon make the philology of ר׳ יהודה חיוג׳ and ר׳ יונה אבן ג׳נאח accessible beyond the Arabic-reading Jewish world. The work also preserves original exegetical, ritual and historical notes. See Encyclopaedia Judaica, the Jewish Encyclopedia and the National Library of Israel catalogue.

ר׳ משה בן מימון.event: ר׳ משה בן מימון is born in Córdoba, conventionally on 14 Nisan 4898 (1138), into the family of the dayan ר׳ מימון בן יוסף. Older scholarship and catalogues sometimes use 1135. He receives his foundational Torah education from his father, within an Andalusian legal tradition linked to ר׳ יוסף אבן מיגאש and ר׳ יצחק אלפסי; claims that he personally studied with ר׳ יוסף אבן מיגאש are chronologically impossible. See the National Library of Israel and the Biblioteca Nacional de España.

ר׳ משה בן מימון.place: Córdoba and the family's Andalusian exile
ר׳ משה בן מימון.event: The Almohad capture of Córdoba forces the family of ר׳ משה בן מימון to leave the city as the new regime removes the protected legal status traditionally accorded to Jews and Christians and imposes conversionist pressure. The family's movements during the following decade are poorly documented; Almería and other Iberian locations are proposed, but the map does not invent a continuous route. See the Biblioteca Nacional de España and the National Library of Israel.

By approximately 1159–1160, ר׳ משה בן מימון and his family are living in Fez. Here he continues פירוש המשנה and writes or completes works associated with persecution, especially אגרת השמד. Medieval Muslim biographical testimony alleges an outward conversion to Islam, while Jewish sources and modern scholars debate the episode; the record therefore does not present it as settled fact. See the Biblioteca Nacional de España, the Hebrew Maimonides Heritage Center and the scholarly biography by Moshe Halbertal.

On 4 Iyar 4925, ר׳ משה בן מימון and his family leave Fez by sea; after a dangerous voyage they reach Acre on 3 Sivan 1165. His own commemorative account records the storm and arrival. Later that year he visits Jerusalem and Hebron before continuing to Egypt. See the Hebrew chronology and primary quotations at the Maimonides Heritage Center and the National Library of Israel.

In the autumn of 1165, ר׳ משה בן מימון visits Jerusalem and prays at the holy site he calls the Great and Holy House; on 9 Marḥeshvan he goes to Hebron and the Cave of Machpelah. The exact identification of the Jerusalem prayer location should not be expanded beyond his wording into an unsupported architectural claim. See the documented dates at the Maimonides Heritage Center and the National Library's Hebrew biography.

After a short stay in Alexandria, ר׳ משה בן מימון settles permanently in Fustat, the commercial and Jewish centre adjoining Cairo. He completes פירוש המשנה around 1168, serves as a dayan, develops a transregional responsa practice and begins the sustained legal work culminating in משנה תורה. See the National Library of Israel and Cambridge's account of his Egyptian autograph manuscripts.

Around 1169–1170, David, the younger brother and commercial supporter of ר׳ משה בן מימון, dies in an Indian Ocean shipwreck while carrying family capital. ר׳ משה later describes prolonged grief; economic responsibility and his existing medical learning help push medicine from scholarship into an intensive profession. The shipwreck is not mapped abroad because its exact location is uncertain and ר׳ משה was not present. See the National Library of Israel and the scholarly biographical overview in PubMed Central.

In 1172, ר׳ משה בן מימון writes אגרת תימן to Jews facing persecution and a destabilizing messianic claimant. The event remains mapped at Fustat, where he wrote; Yemen is the destination of the letter, not evidence of his physical presence. See the manuscript and work survey at the National Library of Israel and the broader account at My Jewish Learning.

By approximately 1177–1178, ר׳ משה בן מימון completes the main recension of משנה תורה, a fourteen-book Hebrew codification of the whole halakhic system. He continues revising the text, and its lack of explicit source citations provokes criticism from figures including ר׳ אברהם בן דוד מפושקיירא and the Baghdad circle. See Oxford Bibliographies, the Stanford Encyclopedia of Philosophy and Cambridge's autograph evidence.

By the mid-1180s, ר׳ משה בן מימון is an established physician connected to the Ayyubid ruling elite, particularly the powerful administrator al-Qāḍī al-Fāḍil. The familiar statement that he was Saladin's personal physician is often overstated; the secure evidence places him within the courtly medical circle. His surviving letter to ר׳ שמואל אבן תיבון describes exhausting daily travel between Fustat and Cairo and a heavy patient load. See Cambridge University's biographical account, the Hebrew CET biography and the critical medical editions at Brill.

Around 1190, ר׳ משה בן מימון completes מורה הנבוכים for his advanced student ר׳ יוסף בן יהודה אבן שמעון. Soon afterward, controversy over resurrection and criticism from the Baghdad academy of ר׳ שמואל בן עלי lead him to issue מאמר תחיית המתים in 1191. During portions of his Egyptian career he also exercises the functions associated with Head of the Jews, though the exact dates and formal title are debated. See the Stanford Encyclopedia of Philosophy, the Library of Congress manuscript and the National Library of Israel.

On 20 Tevet 4965 (13 December 1204), ר׳ משה בן מימון dies in Fustat. His son ר׳ אברהם בן הרמב״ם succeeds to communal leadership and develops an influential pietist synthesis. A powerful tradition holds that ר׳ משה's remains were carried to Tiberias, where his tomb is venerated, but some scholarship argues that he remained buried in Egypt; Fustat is therefore the secure death marker and Tiberias a separately acknowledged burial tradition. See the National Library of Israel and the summary of the burial dispute at the Tomb of Maimonides reference page.

ר׳ אליעזר בן יואל הלוי.event: ר׳ אליעזר בן יואל הלוי is conventionally born around 1140 at Bonn into a distinguished scholarly family. See Encyclopaedia Judaica.

During his studies ר׳ אליעזר בן יואל הלוי learns from ר׳ יהודה בן קלונימוס and other Rhineland masters; he also studies under his father and ר׳ יהודה החסיד. The year is approximate. See Encyclopaedia Judaica.
At Bingen, ר׳ אליעזר בן יואל הלוי and his family narrowly escape an attack and lose their property, books and manuscripts. The conventional placement is approximate. See the Jewish Encyclopedia.
At his father’s request, ר׳ אליעזר בן יואל הלוי accepts the rabbinate of Cologne around 1200 and becomes a leading Ashkenazic halakhic authority. See the Jewish Encyclopedia.
ר׳ אליעזר בן יואל הלוי develops the halakhic compilation אבי העזרי, known as ספר ראבי״ה, together with related material called אבי אסף. The date is approximate. See Encyclopaedia Judaica.
After his brother ר׳ אורי is martyred, ר׳ אליעזר בן יואל הלוי suffers impaired sight and dictates teachings to students, including ר׳ יצחק בן משה מווינה. See Encyclopaedia Judaica.
ר׳ אליעזר בן יואל הלוי participates in the Mainz synod of about 1220–23, addressing the religious and social governance of Ashkenazic communities. See the Jewish Encyclopedia.
ר׳ אליעזר בן יואל הלוי dies around 1225, probably at Cologne. The date and place remain approximate. See Encyclopaedia Judaica.

ר׳ הלל בן אליקים.event: ר׳ הלל בן אליקים belongs to the Byzantine Greek rabbinic world of the twelfth century. No source preserves his birthplace or a secure city, so Thessaloniki is used only as a regional cartographic anchor and 1150 as a conventional activity boundary. See the scholarly summary of ר׳ הלל בן אליקים as a twelfth-century Byzantine scholar and the Jewish Encyclopedia.

Around the later twelfth century, ר׳ הלל בן אליקים composes commentaries on ספרא and ספרי, repeatedly engaging the explanations of ר׳ שלמה יצחקי and ר׳ יצחק בן מלכי־צדק. The year is approximate because the manuscripts are not dated by the author. See the Jewish Encyclopedia and the National Library manuscript record.

The surviving evidence for ר׳ הלל בן אליקים does not establish a death date or place. The year 1200 closes a cautious twelfth-century map interval rather than asserting a documented death, and no invented journey is added. See the scholarly discussion of Byzantine rabbinic literature.

ר׳ שמואל בן יהודה אבן תיבון.event: ר׳ שמואל בן יהודה אבן תיבון is born around 1150 at Lunel and is educated by his father ר׳ יהודה בן שאול אבן תיבון and other local teachers in rabbinic literature, Arabic, medicine and philosophy. See the Stanford Encyclopedia of Philosophy.
ר׳ שמואל בן יהודה אבן תיבון is documented at Béziers in 1199 during the mobile scholarly and commercial career that accompanied his translation work. See the Jewish Encyclopedia.

At Arles, ר׳ שמואל בן יהודה אבן תיבון completes his Hebrew translation of מורה הנבוכים in 1204 after corresponding with ר׳ משה בן מימון about difficult terminology. See the Stanford Encyclopedia chronology.

Between 1204 and 1210, ר׳ שמואל בן יהודה אבן תיבון travels in Iberia and consults manuscripts of Aristotle’s Meteorology at Barcelona and Toledo. The year is an approximate midpoint. See the Stanford Encyclopedia chronology.
ר׳ שמואל בן יהודה אבן תיבון visits Alexandria in pursuit of books and intellectual contacts, returning from the first of two Egyptian journeys in 1210. See the Stanford Encyclopedia chronology.

Returning from a second Alexandrian journey, ר׳ שמואל בן יהודה אבן תיבון composes ביאור המלות הזרות, his glossary to the philosophical vocabulary of מורה הנבוכים. Alexandria is retained as the nearest defensible coordinate rather than inventing a position at sea. See the Jewish Encyclopedia.

ר׳ שמואל בן יהודה אבן תיבון dies around 1230 after settling in Marseille. A later tradition of burial in Tiberias is judged improbable by the Jewish Encyclopedia and is not mapped as fact. See the Jewish Encyclopedia and Larousse.

ר׳ עזריאל בן מנחם מגירונה.event: ר׳ עזריאל בן מנחם מגירונה is placed in Girona from the conventional map year 1160. This is not a securely documented birth date: authoritative modern references say that no personal details survive and identify him only as active in the early thirteenth century. The conventional date is retained for filename and map compatibility. See Encyclopaedia Judaica, the Bibliothèque nationale de France catalogue, and the Jewish Encyclopedia's Girona entry.

Around the opening of the thirteenth century, ר׳ עזריאל מגירונה belongs to the emerging Girona kabbalistic centre. A preserved letter from his teacher ר׳ יצחק סגי נהור to Girona appears to criticize the disclosure of esoteric teachings to wider audiences. The evidence establishes the relationship but does not prove a separate journey by ר׳ עזריאל to Provence, so the point remains at Girona. See Encyclopaedia Judaica and the Jewish Theological Seminary overview.

ר׳ עזריאל מגירונה develops שער השואל, a question-and-answer exposition of the ten sefirot. It distinguishes the unknowable אין סוף from the revealed sefirotic life of divinity and adapts Neoplatonic reasoning to explain emanation, unity and creation. The year is an approximate activity marker rather than a dated publication. See a fifteenth-century witness in the National Library of Israel Ktiv catalogue and the analysis in Encyclopaedia Judaica.

During his Girona activity, ר׳ עזריאל מגירונה writes or develops commentaries on ספר יצירה, talmudic aggadah and the liturgy. His prayer interpretations understand acts such as answering אמן as channels for divine emanation. Because overlapping texts circulated under the names of ר׳ עזרא בן שלמה and ר׳ משה בן נחמן, modern attribution depends on terminology and manuscript comparison rather than printed title pages alone. See the Jewish Theological Seminary, BnF description of the critical corpus, and Encyclopaedia Judaica.

ר׳ עזריאל מגירונה sends a substantial epistle from Girona to Burgos answering kabbalistic questions. This documents correspondence, not physical travel to Burgos. Some manuscripts assign the letter to ר׳ יעקב בן יעקב הכהן of Soria, but textual scholarship restores it to ר׳ עזריאל. See Encyclopaedia Judaica and the recent reassessment in Tarbiz.

By the mature phase of Girona Kabbalah, the poet ר׳ משולם בן שלמה דפיירה praises ר׳ עזריאל מגירונה as a leader of the city's kabbalists and as his teacher. ר׳ עזריאל's thought also closely parallels early kabbalistic formulations by ר׳ משה בן נחמן, although recent scholarship treats a direct teacher–student relationship as plausible rather than proven. See Encyclopaedia Judaica and the Hebrew University study הקבלה בגרונה במאה השלוש עשרה: עזריאל ורמב״ן, הערכה מחודשת.

The year 1238 is retained only as a conventional endpoint used by some modern catalogues for ר׳ עזריאל מגירונה; it is not a securely documented death year and may reflect the longstanding confusion with ר׳ עזרא בן שלמה. No reliable death place or burial site is known. Compare the cautious Encyclopaedia Judaica biography with the conventional dates in the Bibliothèque nationale de France catalogue.

ר׳ דוד קמחי.event: ר׳ דוד קמחי is born around 1160 at Narbonne to ר׳ יוסף קמחי, in a family of Iberian émigré grammarians. Bibliothèque nationale de France authority record
After his father’s early death, ר׳ דוד קמחי is educated by his elder brother ר׳ משה קמחי and later supports himself by teaching Talmud to younger students. Encyclopaedia Judaica biography
ר׳ דוד קמחי develops מכלול and ספר השרשים, works that consolidate Andalusi Hebrew grammar and lexicography for a European Hebrew readership. Jewish Encyclopedia

ר׳ דוד קמחי undertakes his extensive biblical commentary programme, beginning with Chronicles and emphasizing grammar and peshat while engaging rabbinic and philosophical interpretation. Encyclopaedia Judaica biography

As an emissary supporting the writings of ר׳ משה בן מימון, ר׳ דוד קמחי travels toward Toledo to enlist ר׳ יהודה אבן אלפכאר; illness at Ávila forces him to abandon the mission and continue the debate by correspondence. Encyclopaedia Judaica biography

ר׳ דוד קמחי dies around 1235 in Narbonne after a career that made his grammar, lexicon, and biblical commentaries foundational across Jewish and Christian scholarship. Bibliothèque nationale de France authority record

ר׳ מאיר בן טודרוס הלוי אבולעפיה.place: Burgos, Kingdom of Castile; probable birthplace
ר׳ מאיר בן טודרוס הלוי אבולעפיה.event: ר׳ מאיר בן טודרוס הלוי אבולעפיה is born around this time, probably at Burgos, into the prominent Abulafia family. The National Library of Israel uses 1170, while reference works offer approximate dates from about 1165 to 1180; the marker therefore represents a documented regional tradition, not a precise birthplace and date. See the National Library of Israel authority record and Jewish Encyclopedia.

ר׳ מאיר בן טודרוס הלוי אבולעפיה.place: Toledo, Kingdom of Castile; move approximate
ר׳ מאיר בן טודרוס הלוי אבולעפיה.event: By the end of the twelfth century, ר׳ מאיר בן טודרוס הלוי אבולעפיה is associated with Toledo after moving there with his father, ר׳ טודרוס בן יהודה הלוי אבולעפיה. Toledo—not a recoverable modern street address—became the center of his academy, court service, writing, and communal authority. The year is an approximate map anchor because the sources do not preserve a dated itinerary. See the biographical synthesis and cited scholarship in Meir ha-Levi Abulafia.

From Toledo, ר׳ מאיר בן טודרוס הלוי אבולעפיה writes to the sages of Lunel challenging formulations attributed to ר׳ משה בן מימון on bodily resurrection and the interpretation of rabbinic aggadah. This is correspondence, not evidence that he travelled to Lunel. The exchange opens the first Maimonidean controversy and is preserved through ספר האגרות. See the National Library of Israel and this source study of the controversy.

By approximately his mid-thirties, ר׳ מאיר בן טודרוס הלוי אבולעפיה serves among Toledo’s three dayyanim and heads a yeshiva. His judicial work and teaching establish Toledo as the secure geographical center of his mature career; the year is representative rather than an attested appointment date. See the biographical accounts in Meir Abulafia and Meir ha-Levi Abulafia.

During the early thirteenth century, ר׳ מאיר בן טודרוס הלוי אבולעפיה develops the Talmudic project later known as יד רמה. The exact dates of individual tractates cannot be securely fixed, so 1210 marks an active Toledo teaching and writing phase rather than a claimed publication year. Surviving witnesses include Bava Batra, Sanhedrin, Kiddushin, and fragments on Gittin. Consult the National Library manuscript record, the Ktiv Gittin-fragment record, and Sefaria’s work record.

After the death of his father, ר׳ טודרוס בן יהודה הלוי אבולעפיה, ר׳ מאיר בן טודרוס הלוי אבולעפיה succeeds to the communal honorific nasi in Toledo. The title reflects the family’s elite communal standing alongside his established judicial and scholarly authority. See the contemporary-biographical summary in the Jewish Encyclopedia.

ר׳ מאיר בן טודרוס הלוי אבולעפיה.place: Toledo, Kingdom of Castile; year approximate
ר׳ מאיר בן טודרוס הלוי אבולעפיה.event: When opponents seek to renew the campaign against ר׳ משה בן מימון in the 1230s, ר׳ מאיר בן טודרוס הלוי אבולעפיה declines to participate despite his earlier criticism. The episode shows that his 1202 objections should not be collapsed into every later anti-Maimonidean movement. The map remains at Toledo because the evidence concerns correspondence and policy, not travel. See Meir Abulafia and the fuller bibliographical account in Meir ha-Levi Abulafia.

ר׳ מאיר בן טודרוס הלוי אבולעפיה.place: Toledo, Kingdom of Castile; death-place disputed
ר׳ מאיר בן טודרוס הלוי אבולעפיה.event: ר׳ מאיר בן טודרוס הלוי אבולעפיה dies in 1244, conventionally on 18 Nisan 5004 (29 March). Toledo is used because it was his securely documented career center and some references place his death there; another modern account gives Burgos. The disagreement is retained rather than assigning false certainty. Compare the date in the Jewish Encyclopedia, Toledo in the German biographical record, and Burgos in the English biographical record.

ר׳ יהודה בן יוסף אבן אלפכאר.event: ר׳ יהודה בן יוסף אבן אלפכאר is born in Toledo during the last third of the twelfth century. The displayed year 1170 is a conventional approximate marker rather than an exact date. He belongs to a prominent family originally from Granada and established in Toledo, including his court-physician father ר׳ יוסף אלפכאר. See the Real Academia de la Historia biography and the Jewish Encyclopedia family entry.

By the reign of Ferdinand III, ר׳ יהודה אלפכאר is an eminent physician, learned communal figure and politically connected member of Toledo Jewry. Reference works describe him as physician-in-ordinary to Ferdinand III, although surviving evidence is clearer about his Toledo influence than about the precise terms of his royal appointment. See the Real Academia de la Historia and Jewish Encyclopedia.

During the renewed controversy over the writings of ר׳ משה בן מימון, ר׳ דוד קמחי attempts to reach Toledo and enlist ר׳ יהודה אלפכאר for the Maimonidean party. Illness prevents the meeting, so the debate proceeds by letter. This point remains at Toledo because it maps ר׳ יהודה's documented location, not ר׳ דוד's route. See the dated historical introduction and primary text at Daat, the Encyclopaedia Judaica overview, and the Jewish Encyclopedia account.

ר׳ יהודה אלפכאר answers ר׳ דוד קמחי in highly crafted rhymed Hebrew prose. He attacks philosophical allegorization and the elevation of speculative premises over Scripture, while explicitly recognizing ר׳ משה בן מימון as a great but fallible human scholar. The surviving manuscript tradition opens one reply with ‘יגער ה׳ בך השטן, דוד הוא הקטן’. Read the textual study at Daat and consult the National Library of Israel catalogue for Frankfurt Ms. Oct. 99.

The correspondence establishes ר׳ יהודה אלפכאר as one of the major intellectual voices opposing the Maimonidean party. His medical and philosophical education complicates any simple picture of the opponents as enemies of all rational learning; the dispute concerns the authority and permissible reach of philosophy in interpreting Torah. His harsh treatment of ר׳ דוד קמחי, however, draws disapproval even from associates. See the Jewish Encyclopedia and the scholarly controversy overview.

ר׳ יהודה בן יוסף אבן אלפכאר dies in 1235, probably in Toledo. His letters survive in fifteenth- and sixteenth-century manuscript witnesses and in later printed collections, making his polemic far better documented than the details of his private life or medical practice. See the Real Academia de la Historia, National Library catalogue for Vatican Ms. ebr. 507, and Frankfurt Ms. Oct. 99.

ר׳ אלעזר בן יהודה מוורמייזא.place: Mainz, Holy Roman Empire; probable birthplace
ר׳ אלעזר בן יהודה מוורמייזא.event: ר׳ אלעזר בן יהודה מוורמייזא is born probably at Mainz around 1176 into the Kalonymus scholarly family. See the Jewish Encyclopedia biography.
In his formative years, ר׳ אלעזר בן יהודה מוורמייזא studies pietistic and esoteric traditions with ר׳ יהודה החסיד at Regensburg. The year is approximate. See the Jewish Encyclopedia.

According to Leopold Zunz’s reconstruction, ר׳ אלעזר בן יהודה מוורמייזא serves as cantor in Erfurt before his Worms rabbinate. The date is approximate and the attribution is presented cautiously. See the source discussion.

ר׳ אלעזר בן יהודה מוורמייזא establishes himself in Worms and becomes one of the community’s leading rabbinic authorities. The exact year is approximate but precedes the securely dated 1196 attack. See the Jewish Encyclopedia.

On 22 Kislev 1196, two attackers enter the home of ר׳ אלעזר בן יהודה מוורמייזא, wound him and his son, and murder his wife Dulcea, daughters Belet and Hannah, and son Jacob. He records the tragedy in prose and liturgical lament. See the biographical account.
ר׳ אלעזר בן יהודה מוורמייזא participates in the Mainz synod connected with the communal enactments known as תקנות שו״ם. See the Jewish Encyclopedia chronology.
ר׳ אלעזר בן יהודה מוורמייזא dies at Worms in 1238, leaving a major halakhic, exegetical and esoteric corpus. See the Jewish Encyclopedia.

ר׳ שלמה בן אברהם מן ההר.event: ר׳ שלמה בן אברהם מן ההר belongs to Montpellier’s rabbinic world and flourishes in the first half of the thirteenth century. No documentary birth year survives; 1180 is an explicit approximate map bound. See Encyclopaedia Judaica.
As rabbi and Talmudic teacher at Montpellier, ר׳ שלמה בן אברהם מן ההר teaches a circle including ר׳ יונה בן אברהם גירונדי and ר׳ דוד בן שאול. The year is approximate. See the Jewish Encyclopedia.

ר׳ שלמה בן אברהם מן ההר and his two principal supporters appeal to northern French authorities, whose ban targets study of מורה הנבוכים, ספר המדע and secular philosophy. Maimonidean Provençal communities answer with counter-sanctions. See the modern encyclopedia account.

Maimonidean books are burned by Christian authorities amid the controversy. Polemical sources blame ר׳ שלמה בן אברהם מן ההר and his followers, but modern scholarship judges direct informing extremely unlikely; the map records the dispute without converting accusation into fact. See Encyclopaedia Judaica’s qualification.

The later fate of ר׳ שלמה בן אברהם מן ההר is unknown. The year 1235 is used only as an approximate closing map bound after his documented activity, not as a proven death date. See the Jewish Encyclopedia statement that his fate is unknown.

ר׳ ישעיה בן מאלי דטראני.event: ר׳ ישעיה בן מאלי דטראני is traditionally dated as born around 1180 in Trani. See the Jewish Encyclopedia.

By the early thirteenth century ר׳ ישעיה בן מאלי דטראני is active in northern Italy, with Venice identified by early biographical sources as a principal residence. The displayed year is approximate. See the Jewish Encyclopedia.

ר׳ ישעיה בן מאלי דטראני develops the successive recensions of תוספות רי״ד and participates in a wide correspondence network connecting Italian and Ashkenazic scholars. The year is representative rather than a dated publication. See the Jewish Encyclopedia.

In his mature period ר׳ ישעיה בן מאלי דטראני is associated with פסקי רי״ד, ספר המכריע and biblical commentary. This map returns him to his securely attested place-name, Trani, without claiming a precisely dated move. See the Jewish Encyclopedia.
ר׳ ישעיה בן מאלי דטראני is traditionally placed as dying around 1250. The exact year and death place remain uncertain. See the Jewish Encyclopedia.

ר׳ יצחק בן משה מווינה.event: ר׳ יצחק בן משה מווינה is probably born in Bohemia around 1180 into a learned family; exact town and year are unknown. Sefaria author profile
During his early travels, ר׳ יצחק בן משה מווינה studies at Regensburg under ר׳ יהודה החסיד; the year is approximate. Jewish Encyclopedia
ר׳ יצחק בן משה מווינה reaches Paris around 1217 and makes ר׳ יהודה בן יצחק שירליאון his principal teacher. Jewish Encyclopedia
Returning east, ר׳ יצחק בן משה מווינה studies at Worms with ר׳ אלעזר מוורמייזא and then with scholars at Speyer. Jewish Encyclopedia
At Würzburg, ר׳ יצחק בן משה מווינה heads a yeshiva and teaches the young ר׳ מאיר בן ברוך מרוטנבורג. Jewish Encyclopedia
ר׳ יצחק בן משה מווינה settles for a substantial period in Vienna, serving as אב בית דין and ראש ישיבה; the initial year is approximate. Jewish Encyclopedia

Around 1260, ר׳ יצחק בן משה מווינה completes אור זרוע near the end of his life; the map uses this approximate year as both composition and lifespan endpoint amid conflicting chronologies. Jewish Encyclopedia

ר׳ אברהם בן הרמב״ם.event: ר׳ אברהם בן הרמב״ם is born in Fustat on 13 June 1186, the son of ר׳ משה בן מימון. See the Routledge Encyclopedia of Philosophy and the National Library of Israel authority record.

After the death of ר׳ משה בן מימון, eighteen-year-old ר׳ אברהם בן הרמב״ם succeeds him as nagid and as a principal communal and judicial authority of Egyptian Jewry. See Encyclopedia.com and the Routledge Encyclopedia of Philosophy.

By the early thirteenth century, ר׳ אברהם בן הרמב״ם is forming a pietist circle that emphasizes inward intention, disciplined prayer, prostration and solitude. Proposed liturgical practices provoke communal opposition and petitions, though his programme presents them as restorations of Jewish tradition. The displayed year is approximate. See the Routledge account and Da'at's Hebrew study.

ר׳ אברהם בן הרמב״ם serves as physician in the Ayyubid court, associated with Sultan al-Malik al-Kamil, while continuing as nagid and head of the Jewish court. See Encyclopedia.com. The year marks the securely attested reign context rather than a precisely dated appointment.

In Fustat, ר׳ אברהם בן הרמב״ם brings the vast המספיק לעובדי השם toward completion, integrating halakhic observance, ethics and a demanding path of spiritual cultivation. Only parts of the original work survive. See the Routledge Encyclopedia of Philosophy and a modern scholarly Hebrew edition.
ר׳ אברהם בן הרמב״ם writes מלחמות השם, defending ר׳ משה בן מימון amid renewed controversy over his writings. See the Encyclopaedia Judaica-derived entry.

ר׳ אברהם בן הרמב״ם dies in Fustat on 7 December 1237 after more than three decades as nagid. His son ר׳ דוד הנגיד succeeds to the leadership. See the Routledge Encyclopedia of Philosophy and the National Library of Israel.

ר׳ יחיאל בן יוסף מפריז.event: ר׳ יחיאל בן יוסף מפריז is born near the end of the twelfth century, probably in Meaux; 1190 is an approximate map convention. Biographical chronology
In Paris, ר׳ יחיאל בן יוסף מפריז succeeds ר׳ יהודה שירליאון and leads a large Tosafist academy. Jewish Encyclopedia
ר׳ יחיאל בן יוסף מפריז is the principal Jewish defender of the Talmud in the Paris disputation convened after Nicholas Donin’s accusations. Jewish Encyclopedia
In Paris, ר׳ יחיאל בן יוסף מפריז witnesses the aftermath of the trial as large quantities of Talmudic manuscripts are publicly burned. Jewish Encyclopedia: Paris
ר׳ יחיאל בן יוסף מפריז emigrates with family and disciples to Acre and establishes a yeshiva carrying the French Tosafist tradition to the Land of Israel. Jewish Encyclopedia: Paris
ר׳ יחיאל בן יוסף מפריז is commonly reported to die in Acre in 1268; alternate dates and burial traditions remain disputed. Daat Encyclopedia

ר׳ משה בן נחמן.place: Girona, County of Barcelona, Crown of Aragon
ר׳ משה בן נחמן.event: ר׳ משה בן נחמן is born in Girona in 1194 and grows up within its Jewish community. His Girona origin is reflected in the appellation Gerondi and in his Catalan name, Bonastruc ça Porta. See the National Library of Israel biography and the scholarly overview in Encyclopaedia of Religion.

ר׳ משה בן נחמן.place: Barcelona and Girona, Crown of Aragon; study period approximate
ר׳ משה בן נחמן.event: As a young scholar, ר׳ משה בן נחמן studies the Talmudic traditions transmitted by ר׳ יהודה בן יקר in Barcelona and by ר׳ נתן בן מאיר מטרינקטייל, gaining access to the methods of the northern French Tosafists while retaining Spanish and Provençal learning. The year is a representative anchor because no dated student itinerary survives. See the biographical study in Encyclopaedia of Religion and the Encyclopaedia Judaica article.

ר׳ משה בן נחמן.place: Girona, Crown of Aragon; literary activity approximate
ר׳ משה בן נחמן.event: By the early thirteenth century, ר׳ משה בן נחמן has begun the halakhic and Talmudic writing that establishes his school, including מלחמות ה׳ in defense of ר׳ יצחק אלפסי and novellae that combine Sephardi learning with Tosafist analysis. The date marks a broad Girona period rather than a first-publication claim. See the Jewish Encyclopedia and Encyclopaedia of Religion.

ר׳ משה בן נחמן.place: Girona, Crown of Aragon; correspondence network
ר׳ משה בן נחמן.event: During the renewed controversy over the writings of ר׳ משה בן מימון, ר׳ משה בן נחמן attempts to mediate between defenders and opponents. He criticizes philosophical excesses but refuses a simple rejection of ר׳ משה בן מימון’s halakhic authority. His letters reach communities outside Girona, but correspondence is not treated as physical travel. See the National Library of Israel and the detailed account in the Jewish Encyclopedia.

ר׳ משה בן נחמן.place: Royal Palace, Barcelona, Crown of Aragon
ר׳ משה בן נחמן.event: King James I orders ר׳ משה בן נחמן to defend Judaism in the Barcelona Disputation against the Dominican convert Pablo Christiani. Held in July 1263 before the royal court, the sessions concern messianic claims, the status of Jesus, and Christian readings of rabbinic aggadah. Two partisan records survive: רמב״ן’s Hebrew account and a shorter Latin account. See the University of Texas source introduction and the University of Konstanz primary-source edition.

After circulating his account of the disputation, ר׳ משה בן נחמן faces Dominican accusations of blasphemy. A royal tribunal imposes punishment while church pressure seeks a harsher sentence; the legal aftermath, rather than an immediate expulsion on the debate’s final day, explains his eventual departure. See Robert Chazan’s study, Barcelona and Beyond, and the documentary discussion in the Jewish Encyclopedia.

Having left the Crown of Aragon, ר׳ משה בן נחמן reaches the port of Acre in 1267 and enters the Land of Israel. Acre becomes his principal eastern base and later teaching center; the surviving record does not securely reconstruct every stage of the Mediterranean voyage. See the National Library of Israel biography.

In Jerusalem, ר׳ משה בן נחמן encounters a severely diminished Jewish community, organizes communal prayer, and describes the city’s condition in a letter to his son. Tradition connects this renewal with the institution later called the Ramban Synagogue, though the present structure should not be treated as an unchanged thirteenth-century building. See the National Library of Israel and the preserved Jerusalem-letter discussion at Kotar.

ר׳ משה בן נחמן.place: Bethlehem and Hebron, Kingdom of Jerusalem
ר׳ משה בן נחמן.event: During his first period in the Land of Israel, ר׳ משה בן נחמן visits Bethlehem and Hebron. These visits belong to his documented encounter with biblical geography and should not be mistaken for permanent residence in either town. See the Hebrew biography and itinerary summary at the National Library of Israel.

ר׳ משה בן נחמן settles in Acre, gathers students, teaches, and continues revising פירוש התורה in light of texts, traditions, and geographical observations encountered in the Land of Israel. A surviving manuscript notice explicitly associates a late exposition with Acre. See the National Library manuscript record and the NLI biography.

ר׳ משה בן נחמן.place: Acre, Kingdom of Jerusalem; final base, death place uncertain
ר׳ משה בן נחמן.event: ר׳ משה בן נחמן dies around 1270 after spending his final years in the Land of Israel, with Acre his last securely documented scholarly base. His burial place is unknown; later traditions variously identify Acre, Haifa, Hebron, and Jerusalem, so no supposed tomb is presented as certain. See the National Library of Israel and the older source survey in the Jewish Encyclopedia.

ר׳ משה מקוצי.event: ר׳ משה מקוצי is conventionally placed as born around 1200 in or near Coucy, the locality preserved in his name. The exact date and birthplace are not documented. See Encyclopaedia Judaica and the Jewish Encyclopedia.
As a young scholar, ר׳ משה מקוצי studies in Paris under ר׳ יהודה בן יצחק שירליאון and absorbs the northern French Tosafist tradition. The displayed year is approximate. See the Jewish Encyclopedia.

ר׳ משה מקוצי.place: Jewish communities of France and Provence
ר׳ משה מקוצי.event: ר׳ משה מקוצי begins an itinerant preaching mission through France in 1235, urging observance of commandments together with justice and ethical responsibility. See the Jewish Encyclopedia.

In 1236 ר׳ משה מקוצי continues through Spain, delivering public instruction in synagogues and addressing breaches of Jewish family and ritual law. See the Jewish Encyclopedia and the Braginsky Collection.
ר׳ משה מקוצי is one of four rabbis compelled to participate in the Paris disputation defending the Talmud against Nicholas Donin’s accusations. See Encyclopaedia Judaica.

By about 1250 ר׳ משה מקוצי completes ספר מצוות גדול, a comprehensive code designed to preserve practical law after the Parisian attacks on the Talmud. The completion date is variously given as 1247 or 1250. See Sefaria’s work record and the Jewish Encyclopedia.

ר׳ משה מקוצי dies around 1260; neither the precise year nor place is securely known, so the marker uses his documented northern French region without false local precision. See Chabad’s traditional biography and Encyclopaedia Judaica.

ר׳ יעקב בן ששת גירונדי.event: ר׳ יעקב בן ששת גירונדי is placed at Girona from the conventional map year 1200. This is not a documented birth date: neither his birth year nor his death year is known. The surname Gerondi identifies his association with Girona, and historical reference works describe him as a thirteenth-century kabbalist of the city. See the National Library of Israel authority record, Encyclopaedia Judaica, and the Jewish Encyclopedia.

By the middle decades of the thirteenth century, ר׳ יעקב בן ששת participates intellectually in Girona's kabbalistic circle alongside contemporaries such as ר׳ משה בן נחמן and ר׳ עזריאל מגירונה. He repeatedly uses teachings associated with ר׳ יצחק סגי נהור but does not identify him as his own teacher, so direct discipleship remains unproved. See the scholarly discussion by Joseph Dan, Tel Aviv University and Encyclopaedia Judaica.

Around 1240, ר׳ יעקב בן ששת composes משיב דברים נכוחים, a systematic response to מאמר יקוו המים by ר׳ שמואל אבן תיבון. Across thirty chapters he defends creation, providence, prayer and recompense through kabbalistic interpretation while demonstrating an ambivalent, informed engagement with science rather than blanket hostility to it. The date is approximate. Consult the National Library catalogue for the critical edition, Revue des Études Juives review, and the Jewish Encyclopedia.

Approximately in this period, ר׳ יעקב בן ששת writes שער השמים, also known from its opening as משה קיבל. Its elaborate rhymed prose presents traditions concerning the sefirot and divine names and combines mystical exposition with polemic against philosophical approaches. The precise composition year is not secure. See the National Library of Israel manuscript record and Jewish Encyclopedia.

During his mid-thirteenth-century activity, ר׳ יעקב בן ששת is also associated by modern scholarship with ספר האמונה והבטחון. The work circulated for centuries under the name of ר׳ משה בן נחמן; comparison with משיב דברים נכוחים supports attribution to ר׳ יעקב, though its complicated manuscript history should not be hidden. The displayed year is representative, not an exact publication date. See the public-domain National Library edition and Encyclopaedia Judaica.

ר׳ יונה בן אברהם גירונדי.event: ר׳ יונה בן אברהם גירונדי is born around 1200 and comes from Girona’s Jewish scholarly community. The exact birth year is conventional. See the Jewish Encyclopedia and Hebrew biography.

As a young scholar, ר׳ יונה בן אברהם גירונדי studies with ר׳ שלמה בן אברהם מן ההר in Montpellier and becomes a leading member of his traditionalist circle. The year is approximate. See the Jewish Encyclopedia biography.
ר׳ יונה בן אברהם גירונדי, his teacher ר׳ שלמה בן אברהם מן ההר and ר׳ דוד בן שאול support a ban against study of the philosophical works of ר׳ משה בן מימון. See the Encyclopaedia Judaica account.

Later testimony says that news of the 1242 burning of Talmud manuscripts in Paris moves ר׳ יונה בן אברהם גירונדי to acknowledge publicly in Montpellier that his earlier anti-Maimonidean campaign was wrong. The map does not infer that he travelled to Paris. See the sourced biographical discussion.

After leaving Provence, ר׳ יונה בן אברהם גירונדי teaches in Barcelona; ר׳ שלמה בן אברהם אבן אדרת becomes his outstanding pupil. The year is approximate. See the Hebrew biography of his disciple and biographical overview.

ר׳ יונה בן אברהם גירונדי settles in Toledo, teaches a major academy and develops the ethical and Talmudic teachings transmitted in his works and by his students. The year is approximate. See the biographical account.

ר׳ יונה בן אברהם גירונדי dies in Toledo in November 1263, before carrying out a reported plan to travel to the Land of Israel and pray at the grave of ר׳ משה בן מימון. See the Jewish Encyclopedia chronology.

ר׳ צדקיה בן אברהם הרופא.event: ר׳ צדקיה בן אברהם הרופא is conventionally placed as born around 1210 into Rome’s Anaw scholarly family. Exact dates are unknown. See the Jewish Encyclopedia.
During his formation, ר׳ צדקיה בן אברהם הרופא studies in the Ashkenazic sphere under ר׳ יעקב מווירצבורג; the year is approximate. See the Jewish Encyclopedia.

Back in Rome, ר׳ צדקיה בן אברהם הרופא works within the Italian halakhic tradition associated with his teacher ר׳ ישעיה בן מאלי דטראני and maintains contact with Ashkenazic authorities. See the Jewish Encyclopedia.

Around this period ר׳ צדקיה בן אברהם הרופא compiles שבולי הלקט, organizing 372 sections of ritual law and preserving Italian and Ashkenazic traditions. The year is approximate. See the Sefaria text and work description.
ר׳ צדקיה בן אברהם הרופא is conventionally placed as dying around 1280 in the Roman scholarly environment; the exact date is not preserved. See the biographical overview.

ר׳ יצחק מקורביל.event: ר׳ יצחק מקורביל is conventionally placed as born around 1210 in northern France; the precise place and year are not documented, and Corbeil is used as his defining locality. See the Jewish Encyclopedia.
ר׳ יצחק מקורביל studies at the academy of his father-in-law ר׳ יחיאל מפריז. The year is approximate within his early scholarly formation. See the Jewish Encyclopedia.
During his formation, ר׳ יצחק מקורביל studies with the scholars of Évreux, especially ר׳ שמואל מאיוורא. The year is approximate. See the Jewish Encyclopedia.

Established at Corbeil, ר׳ יצחק מקורביל teaches a circle of Tosafist scholars including ר׳ פרץ בן אליהו מקורביל. The displayed year marks continuing activity rather than a documented appointment. See the Jewish Encyclopedia.

At his students’ urging, ר׳ יצחק מקורביל completes עמודי הגולה—ספר מצוות קטן—in 1277 and promotes it as a practical programme of regular study. See the Jewish Encyclopedia and French Wikipedia’s sourced summary.
ר׳ יצחק מקורביל dies in 1280, conventionally located at Corbeil, after his ספר מצוות קטן has begun spreading through France and Germany. See the Jewish Encyclopedia.

ר׳ מאיר בן ברוך מרוטנבורג.place: Worms, Holy Roman Empire; year approximate
ר׳ מאיר בן ברוך מרוטנבורג.event: ר׳ מאיר בן ברוך מרוטנבורג is born around 1215–1220 in Worms into a distinguished scholarly family; his father ר׳ ברוך serves on the local court. See Encyclopaedia Judaica and the Neue Deutsche Biographie.

ר׳ מאיר בן ברוך מרוטנבורג.place: Würzburg, Holy Roman Empire; year approximate
ר׳ מאיר בן ברוך מרוטנבורג.event: As a young student ר׳ מאיר בן ברוך מרוטנבורג studies in Würzburg before continuing through the German and French Tosafist academies. The year is approximate. See the German scholarly biography.

In Paris ר׳ מאיר בן ברוך מרוטנבורג studies under ר׳ יחיאל מפריז and other French Tosafists, witnesses the 1240 disputation and sees the Talmud publicly burned in 1242; he responds with the elegy שאלי שרופה באש. See the Jewish Encyclopedia.

ר׳ מאיר בן ברוך מרוטנבורג.place: Rothenburg ob der Tauber; year approximate
ר׳ מאיר בן ברוך מרוטנבורג.event: After returning from France, ר׳ מאיר בן ברוך מרוטנבורג establishes his principal academy at Rothenburg ob der Tauber, attracting students and answering communities across Europe. The year is approximate. See Encyclopaedia Judaica and the German biography.
After his father’s death, ר׳ מאיר בן ברוך מרוטנבורג returns to Worms while remaining the foremost Ashkenazic legal authority of his generation. See the Jewish Encyclopedia chronology.

In spring 1286 ר׳ מאיר בן ברוך מרוטנבורג attempts to leave the empire with his family and followers, but is recognized and arrested in Lombardy before being delivered to Emperor Rudolf I. See Encyclopaedia Judaica.

ר׳ מאיר בן ברוך מרוטנבורג.place: Ensisheim fortress, Alsace; transfer year approximate
ר׳ מאיר בן ברוך מרוטנבורג.event: Held first at Wasserburg and then at Ensisheim, ר׳ מאיר בן ברוך מרוטנבורג continues studying, teaching visitors and issuing responsa despite limited access to books. The transfer year is approximate. See Encyclopaedia Judaica and the Neue Deutsche Biographie.
On 2 May 1293 ר׳ מאיר בן ברוך מרוטנבורג dies in captivity at Ensisheim. See the Jewish Encyclopedia and German national biography.

ר׳ מאיר בן ברוך מרוטנבורג.place: Heiliger Sand Jewish Cemetery, Worms; posthumous burial
ר׳ מאיר בן ברוך מרוטנבורג.event: In 1307 the body of ר׳ מאיר בן ברוך מרוטנבורג is finally released after Alexander ben Salomon Wimpfen pays a large ransom, and is buried at Heiliger Sand in Worms. This posthumous event does not extend his lifespan beyond 1293. See Encyclopaedia Judaica and the authenticated grave image.

ר׳ אליעזר מטוך.event: ר׳ אליעזר מטוך is conventionally placed as born around 1220 in northern France; his exact birth year, town, and patronymic are unknown. Encyclopaedia Judaica biography

ר׳ אליעזר מטוך.place: Northern French and German scholarly circles
ר׳ אליעזר מטוך.event: During his formation, ר׳ אליעזר מטוך studies with ר׳ יצחק בן משה מווינה; the location and year are not precisely documented, so the marker remains regional. Encyclopaedia Judaica biography

By the second half of the thirteenth century, ר׳ אליעזר מטוך is established at Touques, where he leads a Tosafist academy and teaches ר׳ חיים פלטיאל; the year is approximate. Encyclopaedia Judaica biography
At Touques, ר׳ אליעזר מטוך produces the redaction known as תוספות טוך, adapting earlier French Tosafot and adding גליון תוספות; the date represents his mature editorial period. Jewish Encyclopedia
The map closes the life of ר׳ אליעזר מטוך at Touques in 1290, reflecting only that he died before 1291 rather than a documented exact death date. Encyclopaedia Judaica biography

ר׳ חזקיה בן מנוח.place: France; precise locality unknown; year approximate
ר׳ חזקיה בן מנוח.event: ר׳ חזקיה בן מנוח is born around 1220 in France. Neither the exact year nor town is known; the broad coordinate deliberately avoids false precision. See the Encyclopaedia Judaica entry.

Around 1240 ר׳ חזקיה בן מנוח compiles חזקוני, a Pentateuch commentary drawing on midrash, halakhah and approximately twenty earlier commentaries while preserving numerous French glosses. See the scholarly encyclopedia and work chronology.

ר׳ חזקיה בן מנוח.place: France; death place and year unknown
ר׳ חזקיה בן מנוח.event: The documentary trail for ר׳ חזקיה בן מנוח ends in the mid-thirteenth century. The project uses about 1260 as a finite approximate map endpoint, not a claimed exact death date. See the Encyclopaedia Judaica entry.

ר׳ יצחק בן מאיר הלוי מדורא.event: ר׳ יצחק בן מאיר הלוי מדורא is conventionally dated as born around 1220. The precise birthplace is unknown. See the Jewish Encyclopedia.

ר׳ יצחק בן מאיר הלוי מדורא studies within the Tosafist tradition and is associated with ר׳ טוביה בן אליה מווינה and ר׳ מאיר בן ברוך מרוטנבורג. Because sources do not securely date a particular residence, this regional point is approximate. See the biographical overview.
By the later thirteenth century, ר׳ יצחק בן מאיר הלוי מדורא is established at Düren and recognized as an important German halakhic authority. See the Jewish Encyclopedia.
Around this period ר׳ יצחק בן מאיר הלוי מדורא composes שערי דורא, a practical code of dietary and related ritual law. The composition year is approximate. See the Jewish Encyclopedia.
ר׳ יצחק בן מאיר הלוי מדורא is conventionally placed as dying around 1300; the exact date is not known. See the biographical overview.

ר׳ יצחק בן ישראל.event: ר׳ יצחק בן ישראל was born around 1230. The birthplace is not securely documented; the marker is shown at the earliest documented location only as a visual approximation.

ר׳ יצחק בן ישראל.place: Toledo, Kingdom of Castile; probable workshop location
ר׳ יצחק בן ישראל.event: Around 1245–1255, ר׳ יצחק בן ישראל copies the monumental three-volume Hebrew Bible now preserved in Marseille as Bibliothèque municipale MS 1626. Institutional cataloguing assigns the manuscript to central Castile and identifies Toledo as the probable place of manufacture. Toledo is therefore a strong codicological localization, though the surviving record does not supply a modern building or street. See the Biblissima manuscript catalogue and its IIIF digitization record.

ר׳ יצחק בן ישראל.place: Toledo and Burgos scribal network, Kingdom of Castile
ר׳ יצחק בן ישראל.event: By the middle of the thirteenth century, ר׳ יצחק בן ישראל is situated within the Ben Israel family network of specialist biblical scribes working principally in Toledo and Burgos. The evidence defines a workshop and kinship network rather than a securely dated personal move between the two cities, so the marker remains at Toledo and does not invent a journey to Burgos. See Katrin Kogman-Appel’s reconstruction of the family workshops in Jewish Book Art Between Islam and Christianity.

ר׳ יצחק בן ישראל.place: Toledo, Kingdom of Castile; documentary association
ר׳ יצחק בן ישראל.event: A documentary reconstruction of the Ben Israel family records ר׳ יצחק בן ישראל in 1282, extending his attested presence beyond the production date of the Marseille Bible. The source does not justify attaching a new office, residence, or journey to this notice; it confirms continuing activity within the Castilian scribal milieu. See the family diagram and documentary discussion in Kogman-Appel’s study.

ר׳ יצחק בן ישראל.place: Toledo, Kingdom of Castile; place uncertain
ר׳ יצחק בן ישראל.event: A tombstone dated 1297 has been associated by scholarship with ר׳ יצחק בן ישראל, providing the likely endpoint of his documented life. The publication’s family reconstruction supplies the date but does not warrant a precise modern burial-site coordinate; Toledo is retained as the center of his known professional network and the location is explicitly uncertain. See the genealogical and documentary reconstruction in Jewish Book Art Between Islam and Christianity.

ר׳ אהרן בן יוסף הלוי מברצלונה (הרא״ה).event: Around 1235, ר׳ אהרן בן יוסף הלוי is probably born in Girona into a distinguished scholarly family descended from ר׳ זרחיה הלוי, בעל המאור. The exact birth year is conventional and the birthplace probable rather than certain. See Jewish Encyclopedia and Encyclopaedia Judaica.

By the middle of the thirteenth century, ר׳ אהרן בן יוסף הלוי studies with his elder brother ר׳ פנחס הלוי and with ר׳ משה בן נחמן. In this Catalan school he encounters ר׳ שלמה בן אדרת, later his colleague and principal halakhic opponent. The year is approximate. See Jewish Encyclopedia.

By his mature career, ר׳ אהרן בן יוסף הלוי is identified with Barcelona, hence הרא״ה מברצלונה. He teaches, decides law and develops the independent method later transmitted especially by ר׳ יום טוב בן אברהם אשבילי. The starting year is approximate. See the National Library of Israel and Encyclopaedia Judaica.

In 1284/1285, the king appoints ר׳ אהרן בן יוסף הלוי rabbi in Zaragoza to help end continuing communal dissension. The authority of his rulings there remained strong for generations. See Jewish Encyclopedia and Encyclopaedia Judaica.

Around 1286—placed by some older reconstructions closer to 1291—ר׳ אהרן בן יוסף הלוי spends a short period in Toledo before returning to Barcelona. The evidence supports only a brief residence, not a long rabbinic tenure. See Jewish Encyclopedia and its history of Jewish Toledo.

After returning to Barcelona, ר׳ אהרן בן יוסף הלוי remains a leading independent authority. In the late thirteenth century he writes בדק הבית, a close critique of תורת הבית by ר׳ שלמה בן אדרת; the latter responds in משמרת הבית. The composition year is unknown, so 1290 is approximate. See Sefaria and the National Library of Israel.

ר׳ אהרן בן יוסף הלוי מברצלונה (הרא״ה).place: Place of death unknown; Barcelona is the final documented base
ר׳ אהרן בן יוסף הלוי מברצלונה (הרא״ה).event: ר׳ אהרן בן יוסף הלוי dies sometime before 1303; neither the exact year nor place is securely documented. The coordinate retains Barcelona only as his final well-supported base and is not proof that he died there. A reported late move to Montpellier derives from a likely textual misreading and is omitted. See Jewish Encyclopedia and Encyclopaedia Judaica.

ר׳ שלמה בן אברהם אבן אדרת.event: ר׳ שלמה בן אברהם אבן אדרת is born in Barcelona in 1235 into a prosperous Jewish family. See the National Library of Israel authority record and biographical chronology.

In Barcelona, ר׳ שלמה בן אברהם אבן אדרת studies principally with ר׳ יונה גירונדי and is also shaped by ר׳ משה בן נחמן and ר׳ יצחק בן אברהם. The year is an approximate study-period marker, not a precisely dated appointment. See the Hebrew scholarly biography.

By the later thirteenth century, ר׳ שלמה בן אברהם אבן אדרת is Barcelona’s leading rabbi and an international decisor. His responsa answer communities across Europe and the Mediterranean; 1270 is a representative career marker rather than a securely documented accession year. See the biographical and works overview.

During his mature Barcelona rabbinate, ר׳ שלמה בן אברהם אבן אדרת develops his Talmudic novellae and the legal architecture of תורת הבית. The exact composition dates are not recoverable, so this is a cautious representative date. See the Hebrew account of his writings.

On 26 July 1305, ר׳ שלמה בן אברהם אבן אדרת and the Barcelona leadership issue a time-limited restriction on teaching Greek natural science and metaphysics to students under twenty-five; medicine is exempted. See the documented summary of the decree.

ר׳ שלמה בן אברהם אבן אדרת dies in Barcelona in 1310, leaving a vast responsa corpus, Talmud commentaries and legal manuals that remain central to halakhic literature. See the National Library chronology.

ר׳ משה בן שם טוב די ליאון.event: ר׳ משה בן שם טוב די ליאון is born about 1240; León is traditional, while Guadalajara is also proposed and the year itself is estimated. Sourced biographical overview
A manuscript of מורה הנבוכים is copied for the young ר׳ משה בן שם טוב די ליאון, providing an early documentary trace of his intellectual life. Hebrew biographical summary
By 1286, ר׳ משה בן שם טוב די ליאון is living and writing in Guadalajara, where he remains documented through 1293 and circulates early Zoharic material. Hebrew biographical summary
At Guadalajara, ר׳ משה בן שם טוב די ליאון circulates manuscripts of the זוהר while also composing Hebrew kabbalistic works under his own name. Encyclopedia of World Biography
ר׳ משה בן שם טוב די ליאון establishes his later home in Ávila after periods in Guadalajara and Valladolid, continuing his kabbalistic writing and circulation. Sourced biographical overview
ר׳ משה בן שם טוב די ליאון dies at Arévalo in 1305 while returning toward his home in Ávila. Sourced biographical overview

ר׳ פרץ בן אליהו מקורביל.event: ר׳ פרץ בן אליהו מקורביל is conventionally placed as born around 1240 in northern France; only his later thirteenth-century activity is secure. Encyclopaedia Judaica biography
During his formation, ר׳ פרץ בן אליהו מקורביל studies with ר׳ יחיאל מפריז; the displayed year is approximate. Jewish Encyclopedia
ר׳ פרץ בן אליהו מקורביל studies the Tosafist tradition of Évreux under ר׳ שמואל מאיוורא; the year is approximate. Jewish Encyclopedia
ר׳ פרץ בן אליהו מקורביל travels through Brabant during the wider scholarly journeys reported by his biographers; no single town is securely identified. Jewish Encyclopedia
During a stay in Germany, ר׳ פרץ בן אליהו מקורביל becomes acquainted with ר׳ מאיר בן ברוך מרוטנבורג and later transmits notes on his customs. The date is approximate. Encyclopaedia Judaica biography
Back at Corbeil, ר׳ פרץ בן אליהו מקורביל teaches in the academy of ר׳ יצחק בן יוסף מקורביל and begins glossing the newly completed ספר מצוות קטן. Jewish Encyclopedia
As a leading teacher at Corbeil, ר׳ פרץ בן אליהו מקורביל delivers and edits Tosafist lectures studied across France, Germany, and Spain; the year marks his mature period. Jewish Encyclopedia: Tosafot
ר׳ פרץ בן אליהו מקורביל dies before 1298, probably in 1295; the exact final town is not securely known. Jewish Encyclopedia

ר׳ מנחם בן שלמה המאירי.event: ר׳ מנחם בן שלמה המאירי is born in Perpignan in 1249, then within the Catalan-Provençal cultural world. Sourced biographical overview
During his formation, ר׳ מנחם בן שלמה המאירי studies the Provençal Talmudic tradition associated with ר׳ ראובן בן חיים of Narbonne; the year is approximate. Encyclopaedia Judaica biography
At Perpignan, ר׳ מנחם בן שלמה המאירי begins the principal composition period of בית הבחירה, his systematic Talmudic commentary. Encyclopaedia Judaica
ר׳ מנחם בן שלמה המאירי completes the main phase of בית הבחירה after approximately thirteen years of work. Encyclopaedia Judaica
Following the French expulsion of 1306 and resulting disputes over custom, ר׳ מנחם בן שלמה המאירי writes מגן אבות in defence and explanation of Provençal practice. Sourced biographical overview
ר׳ מנחם בן שלמה המאירי dies in Perpignan in 1315; his works remain largely manuscript-bound until their modern rediscovery and publication. Sourced biographical overview

ר׳ אבא מארי בן משה הירחי.event: ר׳ אבא מארי בן משה הירחי נולד בקירוב בלוניל, שממנה נגזר הכינוי הירחי; התאריך משוער. Jewish Encyclopedia
ר׳ אבא מארי בן משה הירחי הנהיג במונפלייה את ההתנגדות לפרשנות אלגורית קיצונית והחל לפנות אל ר׳ שלמה בן אדרת בבקשת התערבות. Jewish Encyclopedia
ר׳ אבא מארי בן משה הירחי עמד במרכז המחלוקת שהובילה את ר׳ שלמה בן אדרת לפרסם בברצלונה הגבלה על לימודי פילוסופיה לצעירים; המיקום מציין את מקום פעילותו, לא את מקום פרסום החרם. Jewish Encyclopedia
לאחר גירוש יהודי צרפת עזב ר׳ אבא מארי בן משה הירחי את מונפלייה ועבר תחילה בארל. French biography and cited scholarship
ר׳ אבא מארי בן משה הירחי השתקע בפרפיניאן וערך שם את תכתובת המחלוקת בספר מנחת קנאות; קורותיו לאחר מכן אינן ידועות. Jewish Encyclopedia
זהו קצה־זמן משוער בלבד לחיי ר׳ אבא מארי בן משה הירחי: המקורות אינם מתעדים את מקום מותו או את שנתו המדויקת לאחר פעילותו בפרפיניאן. Jewish Encyclopedia

ר׳ אשר בן יחיאל.event: ר׳ אשר בן יחיאל is born about 1250 in western Germany, probably in or near Cologne, into a distinguished scholarly family. Encyclopaedia Judaica biography
At Worms, ר׳ אשר בן יחיאל studies under ר׳ מאיר בן ברוך מרוטנבורג and is appointed to his teacher’s rabbinical court. Encyclopaedia Judaica biography
After ר׳ מאיר בן ברוך מרוטנבורג is imprisoned, ר׳ אשר בן יחיאל helps lead the unsuccessful ransom effort and emerges as a principal authority of German Jewry. Chabad biography
Fearing a fate like his teacher’s, ר׳ אשר בן יחיאל leaves Germany in 1303 and travels through Provence on the route toward Spain. Encyclopaedia Judaica biography
In Barcelona, ר׳ אשר בן יחיאל is welcomed by ר׳ שלמה בן אברהם אדרת, whose recommendation helps secure his later Toledo appointment. Sourced biographical overview
ר׳ אשר בן יחיאל accepts leadership of Toledo’s Jewish community and establishes an academy that carries Ashkenazi Tosafist learning into Spain. Jewish Encyclopedia: Toledo
ר׳ אשר בן יחיאל dies in Toledo on 9 Cheshvan 5088 (1327), leaving the academy to his scholarly family and disciples. Chabad biography

ר׳ אברהם בן יצחק מן ההר.event: ר׳ אברהם בן יצחק מן ההר is conventionally placed as born around 1250 in Provence; neither the year nor town is documented. Encyclopaedia Judaica biography
By the later thirteenth century, ר׳ אברהם בן יצחק מן ההר is an established Montpellier scholar and contemporary of ר׳ מנחם בן שלמה המאירי; the year is approximate. Sourced biographical overview
At Montpellier, ר׳ אברהם בן יצחק מן ההר composes Talmudic commentaries that regularly interpret the sugya through the legal conclusions of ר׳ משה בן מימון. Survey of later Provençal Rishonim
Near the end of his life, ר׳ אברהם בן יצחק מן ההר moves to Carpentras and joins the בית דין of ר׳ מרדכי בן יוסף; the displayed year is approximate. Sourced biographical overview
ר׳ אברהם בן יצחק מן ההר dies around 1315, conventionally mapped at his final documented community of Carpentras. Hebrew biographical summary

ר׳ מאיר הכהן מרוטנבורג.event: ר׳ מאיר הכהן מרוטנבורג is conventionally placed as born around 1250. No secure town or exact year survives, so this point represents Germany without false local precision. See the Encyclopaedia Judaica entry.

ר׳ מאיר הכהן מרוטנבורג belongs to the scholarly circle of his teacher ר׳ מאיר בן ברוך מרוטנבורג. The year marks an approximate mature-study phase, not a precisely dated arrival. See Encyclopaedia Judaica.

Around the late thirteenth century, ר׳ מאיר הכהן מרוטנבורג compiles the material known as הגהות מיימוניות, preserving Ashkenazic rulings alongside משנה תורה. The year is an editorial approximation. See the work overview.
ר׳ מאיר הכהן מרוטנבורג is conventionally understood to have died around 1300; neither the date nor location is securely recorded. See the biographical summary.

ר׳ מרדכי בן הלל הכהן.event: ר׳ מרדכי בן הלל הכהן is born around 1250 into a prominent German rabbinic family; the exact town is not documented, so no false city precision is used. Jewish Encyclopedia
During his scholarly formation, ר׳ מרדכי בן הלל הכהן becomes an older pupil of ר׳ מאיר בן ברוך מרוטנבורג and begins issuing independent rulings. The year is approximate. Jewish Encyclopedia
At Goslar, ר׳ מרדכי בן הלל הכהן successfully defends his legal right of residence, but the bitterness of the dispute prompts him to leave. Jewish Encyclopedia
ר׳ מרדכי בן הלל הכהן settles in Nuremberg and continues compiling the halakhic material known as ספר המרדכי. Jewish Encyclopedia
On 1 August 1298, ר׳ מרדכי בן הלל הכהן, his wife, and their five children are murdered with Nuremberg’s Jews during the Rintfleisch massacres. Jewish Encyclopedia: Rindfleisch persecutions

ר׳ יום טוב בן אברהם אשבילי.event: ר׳ יום טוב בן אברהם אשבילי is born around 1250 into a family associated with Seville; the date is approximate. See Encyclopaedia Judaica’s biography.
As a young scholar, ר׳ יום טוב בן אברהם אשבילי studies in Barcelona under ר׳ שלמה בן אברהם אבן אדרת and ר׳ אהרן הלוי. The year is approximate. See Encyclopaedia Judaica.

An official Aragonese document identifies ר׳ יום טוב בן אברהם אשבילי as a hakham and dayan of Zaragoza, securely locating his mature communal career. See Tamar Marvin’s scholarly reference entry and Encyclopaedia Judaica.

By around 1300 he is producing influential Talmudic novellae and responsa while serving as a leading Spanish authority. This year represents a composition period, not a separately documented relocation. See the Ritva reference entry.
ר׳ יום טוב בן אברהם אשבילי dies by approximately 1330, probably in the Aragonese setting of his documented career. The exact death year and town remain uncertain. See Tamar Marvin’s reference entry.

ר׳ יעקב בן הרא״ש.event: ר׳ יעקב בן הרא״ש is born around 1269–1270 in Cologne, son of ר׳ אשר בן יחיאל. See the Real Academia de la Historia and Jewish Encyclopedia.
Fleeing danger in Germany, ר׳ יעקב בן הרא״ש travels with his family to Iberia and pauses in Barcelona while his father proceeds toward Toledo. See the Real Academia de la Historia.
By 1314, ר׳ יעקב בן הרא״ש is permanently established in Toledo, working in the scholarly and judicial circle led by ר׳ אשר בן יחיאל. See the Real Academia de la Historia.

After the death of ר׳ אשר בן יחיאל, ר׳ יעקב בן הרא״ש continues editing his father’s legal legacy and developing ארבעה טורים. The year marks this mature period, not a precisely dated beginning of composition. See the Jewish Encyclopedia.
By about 1340, ר׳ יעקב בן הרא״ש has completed the four-part legal architecture that will shape later halakhic codes. See the New York Public Library.
Under the project’s conventional chronology, ר׳ יעקב בן הרא״ש dies in Toledo around 1343; authorities also place his death before 1340. See the Real Academia de la Historia and Jewish Encyclopedia.

ר׳ יעקב בן מאיר מנורדהאוזן.event: ר׳ יעקב בן מאיר מנורדהאוזן is conventionally placed as born around 1270. No exact birth date or town is known. The estimate fits the tradition that he was a younger student of ר׳ מאיר בן ברוך מרוטנבורג. See the Hebrew biographical entry.

According to later scholarly reconstruction, ר׳ יעקב בן מאיר מנורדהאוזן belongs to the final generation of students associated with ר׳ מאיר בן ברוך מרוטנבורג. The year and physical stay are approximate. See the Hebrew biographical entry.

ר׳ יעקב בן מאיר מנורדהאוזן leads a yeshiva at Nordhausen. He is probably the compiler of פסקי תוספות, though modern scholarship treats the identification as a reasoned attribution rather than certainty. See the Hebrew biographical entry.

During the Black Death persecutions, ר׳ יעקב בן מאיר מנורדהאוזן, his son ר׳ מאיר, his students and the Jewish community are burned and killed. Contemporary civic evidence records the community’s destruction; Jewish martyrology preserves the account of their final prayers and self-sacrifice. See the Jewish Encyclopedia and the Nordhausen historical account.

ר׳ אהרן בן יעקב הכהן.event: ר׳ אהרן בן יעקב הכהן is conventionally placed as born around 1280 in a Provençal scholarly family; Narbonne is more strongly supported than the older Lunel attribution. Encyclopaedia Judaica summary
At Narbonne, ר׳ אהרן בן יעקב הכהן absorbs and records the local customs and teachings later preserved throughout ארחות חיים; the year is approximate. Encyclopaedia Judaica summary
In the expulsion ordered by Philip IV, ר׳ אהרן בן יעקב הכהן is driven from France with the wider Jewish population. Sourced biographical overview
After exile from Provence, ר׳ אהרן בן יעקב הכהן apparently passes through northeastern Spain before proceeding to Majorca; the precise itinerary and year are uncertain. Encyclopaedia Judaica summary
On Majorca, ר׳ אהרן בן יעקב הכהן completes ארחות חיים by or before 1327, preserving Provençal law and custom in exile. Jewish Virtual Library: Majorca
The map closes the life of ר׳ אהרן בן יעקב הכהן on Majorca around 1330 as an explicitly approximate endpoint; his exact death year and place are unknown. French biobibliographical notice

ר׳ אשתורי הפרחי.event: ר׳ אשתורי הפרחי is born around 1280 into a Provençal rabbinic family; the exact town is uncertain, so Carpentras is used as a regional anchor. See Ishtori HaParchi.
ר׳ אשתורי הפרחי studies Torah, medicine and science in Montpellier under ר׳ יעקב בן מכיר אבן תיבון. The year is approximate. See the biographical account.
Expelled from France, ר׳ אשתורי הפרחי reaches Barcelona and translates a Latin pharmacological work into Hebrew. See the documented biography.
During his eastward migration, ר׳ אשתורי הפרחי travels through Egypt before entering the Land of Israel. The year is approximate. See Ishtori HaParchi.
ר׳ אשתורי הפרחי initially settles in Jerusalem but leaves after roughly a year. See the biographical account.
ר׳ אשתורי הפרחי settles in Beit She’an, practises medicine and begins years of systematic travel through the Land of Israel. See Yad Ben-Zvi’s historical study.
After extensive field research, ר׳ אשתורי הפרחי completes כפתור ופרח in 1322 and submits it to scholars for review. See ויקישיבה.
ר׳ אשתורי הפרחי dies around 1355 at Beit She’an, his home for most of his life in the Land of Israel. See the standard biography.

ר׳ לוי בן גרשון.event: ר׳ לוי בן גרשון is born in 1288, probably at Bagnols-sur-Cèze in Languedoc. Encyclopaedia Judaica biography
At Orange, his principal lifelong residence, ר׳ לוי בן גרשון begins the twelve-year composition of מלחמות ה׳. Stanford Encyclopedia of Philosophy
ר׳ לוי בן גרשון completes מעשה חושב, an original Hebrew treatise on arithmetic, combinatorics, and mathematical proof. Encyclopaedia Judaica biography
ר׳ לוי בן גרשון completes מלחמות ה׳ and begins the extended sequence of biblical commentaries that occupies the following decade. Stanford Encyclopedia of Philosophy

During one of his visits to Avignon, ר׳ לוי בן גרשון participates in the papal city’s learned environment while continuing astronomical observation; his principal home remains Orange. Stanford Encyclopedia of Philosophy
ר׳ לוי בן גרשון completes his Torah commentary and a broad group of commentaries on the Prophets and Writings. Stanford Encyclopedia of Philosophy bibliography
ר׳ לוי בן גרשון dies in 1344. His final place is uncertain; later tradition places it at Perpignan, while modern biographies chiefly associate his life with Orange. Encyclopaedia Judaica biography

ר׳ ירוחם בן משולם.event: ר׳ ירוחם בן משולם is born around 1290 in Provence; the town is unknown, so Avignon is used only as a regional map anchor. See Encyclopaedia Judaica.

ר׳ ירוחם בן משולם.place: Provence and the French expulsion routes
ר׳ ירוחם בן משולם.event: The expulsion of Jews from France displaces ר׳ ירוחם בן משולם, who wanders through several countries before reaching Castile. See Encyclopaedia Judaica.
ר׳ ירוחם בן משולם settles in Toledo and studies in poverty under the רא״ש and ר׳ אברהם בן משה איסמעיל. The year is approximate. See Encyclopaedia Judaica.
ר׳ ירוחם בן משולם begins composing ספר מישרים, arranging civil law by subject and source. See the biographical account.
After completing ספר מישרים, ר׳ ירוחם בן משולם turns to the life-cycle code תולדות אדם וחוה at the urging of fellow scholars. See Rabbeinu Yerucham.
ר׳ ירוחם בן משולם dies around 1350. Toledo, his documented scholarly centre, is used because the precise death place is not independently preserved. See Encyclopaedia Judaica.

ר׳ דוד בן יוסף אבודרהם.event: ר׳ דוד בן יוסף אבודרהם is conventionally placed in Seville around 1300; his exact birth date is unknown, while his later Seville activity is documented. Jewish Encyclopedia
In Seville, ר׳ דוד בן יוסף אבודרהם completes his comprehensive commentary on blessings, prayers, and the synagogue calendar. Jewish Encyclopedia
The map closes the life of ר׳ דוד בן יוסף אבודרהם in Seville at an explicitly approximate endpoint; no reliable death date or later residence is known. Biographical chronology

ר׳ משה בן יהושע נרבוני.event: ר׳ משה בן יהושע נרבוני is born around 1300 at Perpignan. See the specialist manuscript study.
At thirteen, ר׳ משה בן יהושע נרבוני begins formal philosophical study with his father and later trains in medicine. See Moses of Narbonne.
By the mid-1340s, ר׳ משה בן יהושע נרבוני is active in Soria during his extensive philosophical and medical travels. See the French historical account.
During Black Death violence, a mob attacks the Jewish community of Cervera. ר׳ משה בן יהושע נרבוני escapes but loses his books and property. See the documented biography.
After fleeing Cervera, ר׳ משה בן יהושע נרבוני works in Barcelona and writes on Ibn Tufayl’s philosophical narrative. See Moses of Narbonne.
ר׳ משה בן יהושע נרבוני continues his itinerant medical and philosophical career in Toledo. The year is approximate. See the French historical account.
ר׳ משה בן יהושע נרבוני completes his major commentary on מורה נבוכים and dies around 1362, apparently during an attempted return north; Soria is the last secure base. See the specialist study.

ר׳ וידאל די טולושא.event: ר׳ וידאל די טולושא is born around 1300, probably in the Toulouse region; both year and identification of his birthplace remain debated. See the Jewish Encyclopedia and summary of the geographic debate.
By approximately this period, ר׳ וידאל די טולושא resides in Villefranche-de-Conflent before his later Barcelona career. The year is approximate. See the biographical summary.

In Barcelona, ר׳ וידאל די טולושא works in the scholarly circle of his colleague ר׳ ניסים בן ראובן and composes Maggid Mishneh. The displayed year marks an approximate composition period. See the Jewish Encyclopedia and Daat’s Hebrew reference entry.
ר׳ וידאל די טולושא dies around 1378, probably in Catalonia; neither the exact year nor death town is secure. See the Jewish Encyclopedia and traditional chronology.

ר׳ מנחם בן אהרן אבן זרח.event: ר׳ מנחם בן אהרן אבן זרח is born around 1310, probably at Estella, to a family displaced from France in 1306. See the National Library of Israel.

In the massacre of 5–6 March 1328, the parents and four brothers of ר׳ מנחם בן אהרן אבן זרח are murdered. Seriously wounded, he survives through the intervention of a knight. See the biographical account.

Following the massacre, ר׳ מנחם בן אהרן אבן זרח studies for two years under ר׳ יהושע אבן שועיב. The precise town is not preserved, so Estella remains the regional anchor. See the documented biography.

ר׳ מנחם בן אהרן אבן זרח.place: Alcalá de Henares, Crown of Castile
ר׳ מנחם בן אהרן אבן זרח.event: ר׳ מנחם בן אהרן אבן זרח moves to Alcalá and studies Talmud and Tosafot under ר׳ יוסף אבן אל־עיש, later learning extensively from ר׳ יהודה בן הרא״ש. See the biographical chronology.

ר׳ מנחם בן אהרן אבן זרח.place: Alcalá de Henares, Crown of Castile
ר׳ מנחם בן אהרן אבן זרח.event: ר׳ מנחם בן אהרן אבן זרח succeeds ר׳ יוסף אבן אל־עיש as rabbi of Alcalá and teaches there for eight years. See the standard biography.
After civil war destroys his property, ר׳ מנחם בן אהרן אבן זרח settles in Toledo under the patronage of ר׳ שמואל אברבנאל. See the biographical account.
In Toledo, ר׳ מנחם בן אהרן אבן זרח composes צדה לדרך for ר׳ שמואל אברבנאל. The displayed year is an approximate composition anchor. See the National Library of Israel.
ר׳ מנחם בן אהרן אבן זרח dies in Toledo in July 1385. See the National Library of Israel.

ר׳ ניסים בן ראובן גירונדי.event: ר׳ ניסים בן ראובן גירונדי is conventionally born around 1310, probably in Barcelona, although Girona and an earlier date are also reported. Real Academia de la Historia
In Barcelona, ר׳ ניסים בן ראובן גירונדי copies and donates a Torah scroll, a firmly dated witness to his residence and learning. Real Academia de la Historia
By about 1340, ר׳ ניסים בן ראובן גירונדי is active in Barcelona as a jurist and scholar, later heading a major academy. Chabad biography
During his Barcelona leadership, ר׳ ניסים בן ראובן גירונדי and other communal notables are imprisoned after a false accusation and subsequently released. Chabad biography
ר׳ ניסים בן ראובן גירונדי dies in Barcelona in the winter of 1375–1376, possibly during an epidemic. Real Academia de la Historia

ר׳ יצחק בר ששת ברפת.event: ר׳ יצחק בר ששת ברפת is born in Valencia in 1326. Encyclopaedia Judaica biography
In Barcelona, ר׳ יצחק בר ששת ברפת studies under ר׳ פרץ הכהן and ר׳ ניסים בן ראובן גירונדי while initially earning his living in commerce. Chabad biography
ר׳ יצחק בר ששת ברפת is imprisoned in Barcelona with other Jewish leaders after a false accusation and is later released. Chabad biography
ר׳ יצחק בר ששת ברפת accepts rabbinic leadership in Zaragoza, departing from his earlier reluctance to hold salaried office. Biographical chronology
After leaving Zaragoza, ר׳ יצחק בר ששת ברפת serves the Jewish community of Calatayud before returning to Valencia. Biographical chronology
Following the 1391 persecutions in Valencia, ר׳ יצחק בר ששת ברפת escapes Iberia and settles in Algiers, where he becomes a principal rabbinic authority. Encyclopaedia Judaica biography
ר׳ יצחק בר ששת ברפת dies in Algiers in 1408 and is buried there. Chabad biography

ר׳ חסדאי בן אברהם קרשקש.event: ר׳ חסדאי בן אברהם קרשקש is born in Barcelona around 1340 and later studies in the academy of ר׳ ניסים בן ראובן גירונדי. Stanford Encyclopedia of Philosophy
By 1370, ר׳ חסדאי בן אברהם קרשקש is established in Barcelona as a Talmudic scholar and judge. Stanford Encyclopedia of Philosophy
ר׳ חסדאי בן אברהם קרשקש leaves Barcelona to serve the Jewish community of Zaragoza as rabbi and leading communal representative. Stanford Encyclopedia of Philosophy
From Zaragoza, ר׳ חסדאי בן אברהם קרשקש responds to the 1391 persecutions, in which his son is killed, by aiding survivors and rebuilding devastated communities. Stanford Encyclopedia of Philosophy
