In Zaragoza, ר׳ חסדאי בן אברהם קרשקש completes אור ה׳, his sustained critique of Aristotelian philosophy and reconstruction of Jewish doctrine. Stanford Encyclopedia of Philosophy
ר׳ חסדאי בן אברהם קרשקש dies in Zaragoza in late 1410 or January 1411. Stanford Encyclopedia of Philosophy

ר׳ יוסף בן דוד חביבא.event: ר׳ יוסף בן דוד חביבא is born in Christian Spain around the mid-fourteenth century, probably in or near Zaragoza. The year and exact birthplace are approximate. See the Israeli Ministry of Education survey and the Jewish Encyclopedia.

By the later fourteenth century, ר׳ יוסף בן דוד חביבא studies in Barcelona in the circles of ר׳ ניסים בן ראובן and ר׳ חסדאי קרשקש. The displayed year is approximate. See the Eretz Hemdah review and biographical summary.

Around this period ר׳ יוסף בן דוד חביבא is associated with Zaragoza and composes the commentary later known as Nimukei Yosef. Both year and precise place of composition remain approximate. See the Eretz Hemdah review.

ר׳ יוסף בן דוד חביבא dies in Spain sometime before 1440; 1420 is retained only as a conventional approximate map endpoint. See the Eretz Hemdah biographical note. The coordinate is deliberately regional rather than a claim about his death town.

ר׳ יצחק בן משה הלוי דוראן.event: ר׳ יצחק בן משה הלוי דוראן is born around 1350, probably at Perpignan or elsewhere in Catalonia. See the scholarly encyclopedia account.

ר׳ יצחק בן משה הלוי דוראן studies Talmud, philosophy, medicine and science and becomes a tutor in the Crescas family. The year is approximate; Barcelona is used as a regional anchor. See Profiat Duran.
During the anti-Jewish violence of 1391, ר׳ יצחק בן משה הלוי דוראן is forcibly baptised and recorded under the name Honoratus de Bonafide. See the scholarly biography.

Having escaped and returned openly to Judaism, ר׳ יצחק בן משה הלוי דוראן writes the satirical anti-conversion letter אל תהי כאבותיך. The location reflects his established Perpignan association. See the works chronology.
ר׳ יצחק בן משה הלוי דוראן compiles חשב האפוד, an astronomical and calendrical almanac. See Profiat Duran.
ר׳ יצחק בן משה הלוי דוראן composes כלימת הגוים, a historical and textual critique of Christianity. See the biographical bibliography.
ר׳ יצחק בן משה הלוי דוראן completes מעשה אפוד, his major Hebrew grammar and educational programme. See Wellsprings.

ר׳ יצחק בן משה הלוי דוראן dies around 1414/15. His death place is unknown; Perpignan is retained as his best-established base rather than asserting an unproved eastern journey. See the scholarly encyclopedia account.

ר׳ יעקב בן משה הלוי מולין.event: ר׳ יעקב בן משה הלוי מולין is born in Mainz around 1360 to ר׳ משה הלוי מולין; the year is approximate. See the BnF authority record and National Library profile.

ר׳ יעקב בן משה הלוי מולין.place: Wiener Neustadt and Austria; year approximate
ר׳ יעקב בן משה הלוי מולין.event: As a young scholar ר׳ יעקב בן משה הלוי מולין studies in Austria, including under ר׳ שלום מנוישטאדט; the year is approximate. See the Encyclopaedia Judaica biography.

After his father's death ר׳ יעקב בן משה הלוי מולין returns to Mainz, assumes communal leadership and establishes an influential yeshiva; the conventional year is approximate. See the Hebrew encyclopedia account.
During the Hussite-war crisis ר׳ יעקב בן משה הלוי מולין provides halakhic and communal leadership, organising prayer, fasting and assistance for threatened communities. See the historical summary.
Late in life ר׳ יעקב בן משה הלוי מולין serves in Worms, where he dies in 1427 and is buried in the Holy Sands cemetery. See the SchUM gravestone record.

ר׳ שמעון בן צמח דוראן.event: ר׳ שמעון בן צמח דוראן is born in Palma on Majorca in 1361 and receives a broad Jewish and scientific education. See Encyclopaedia Judaica via Encyclopedia.com and the Jewish Encyclopedia.
After the 1391 violence destroys Jewish life in Majorca and costs him his fortune, ר׳ שמעון בן צמח דוראן escapes with his family to Algiers. See Encyclopaedia Judaica.
In Algiers, ר׳ שמעון בן צמח דוראן and ר׳ יצחק בר ששת formulate communal statutes in 1394, while the former increasingly serves as judge and halakhic authority. See Jewish Encyclopedia.

By the early fifteenth century ר׳ שמעון בן צמח דוראן stands at the head of Algerian rabbinic life and answers questions from communities around the western Mediterranean. The displayed year is approximate. See Encyclopaedia Judaica.
ר׳ שמעון בן צמח דוראן dies in Algiers in 1444, leaving a major responsa corpus and an Algerian rabbinic dynasty. See the Jewish Encyclopedia.

ר׳ יוסף אלבו.place: Monreal del Campo, Aragon; probable birthplace
ר׳ יוסף אלבו.event: ר׳ יוסף אלבו is born around 1380, probably at Monreal in Aragon. The place and year are conventional rather than documentary certainties. See the Stanford Encyclopedia of Philosophy and Jewish Encyclopedia’s caution.
In his formative years, ר׳ יוסף אלבו studies with ר׳ חסדאי קרשקש, whose critique of Aristotelianism strongly shapes him. The date is approximate. See the Stanford Encyclopedia of Philosophy.
Representing the Jewish community of Daroca, ר׳ יוסף אלבו participates prominently in the coercive Disputation of Tortosa of 1413–1414. See the Stanford biographical sketch.
After the Jewish community of Daroca is devastated in 1415, ר׳ יוסף אלבו relocates to Soria, where he serves as rabbi and preacher. See the Stanford Encyclopedia of Philosophy.

At Soria, ר׳ יוסף אלבו completes ספר העיקרים around 1425, formulating existence of God, revelation and reward and punishment as the three roots of divine religion. See the Stanford study and the Hebrew text.
ר׳ יוסף אלבו is documented preaching at Soria in 1433, confirming his continued activity there after completion of his major work. See the Jewish Encyclopedia.
ר׳ יוסף אלבו dies around 1444, probably in Soria; the exact circumstances are unknown. See the Stanford chronology and Metzler biographical entry.

ר׳ יעקב בן יהודה וייל.event: ר׳ יעקב בן יהודה וייל is born between about 1380 and 1390 at Weil; 1385 is used as the map midpoint. See the Hebrew biography.
As a young scholar, ר׳ יעקב בן יהודה וייל studies in the Mainz yeshiva of ר׳ יעקב בן משה הלוי מולין. The year is approximate. See the Jewish Encyclopedia.

By 1422 ר׳ יעקב בן יהודה וייל serves at Nuremberg after receiving ordination and authorization from ר׳ יעקב בן משה הלוי מולין. He avoids displacing the senior local scholar ר׳ זלמן כ״ץ. See the biographical overview.
ר׳ יעקב בן יהודה וייל is called to the rabbinate of Erfurt and becomes an authority consulted by distant German communities. The arrival year is approximate. See the Jewish Encyclopedia.

From Erfurt, ר׳ יעקב בן יהודה וייל issues the rulings later collected as שו״ת מהרי״ו and the authoritative laws of slaughter and inspection. The year represents the mature corpus, not its later printing. See the Jewish Encyclopedia.

ר׳ יעקב בן יהודה וייל dies before or by 1456, prior to the expulsion of Erfurt’s Jews. The exact death date and place are unknown; Erfurt is used as his last documented centre. See the Hebrew biography.

ר׳ ישראל איסרלין.event: ר׳ ישראל איסרלין is born in Regensburg around 1390. See the Jewish Virtual Library and German authority record.
After losing his father young, ר׳ ישראל איסרלין is educated in Wiener Neustadt in the home of his uncle and teacher ר׳ אהרן בלומל. The year is approximate. See the Jewish Virtual Library.
The anti-Jewish persecution known as the Vienna Gesera kills the mother and uncle of ר׳ ישראל איסרלין, a defining rupture in his family and scholarly world. See Jewish Virtual Library.
By about 1425 ר׳ ישראל איסרלין is established at Marburg, today Maribor, where he serves as a rabbinic authority. See the Croatian Encyclopaedia and IxTheo authority record.
Around 1445 ר׳ ישראל איסרלין returns to Wiener Neustadt as rabbi and head of its court and yeshiva, becoming a central authority for Ashkenazic communities. See the Jewish Virtual Library.
ר׳ ישראל איסרלין dies in Wiener Neustadt around 1460. His rulings remain foundational for later Ashkenazic practice. See Deutsche Digitale Bibliothek.

ר׳ יהודה הלוי מינץ.event: ר׳ יהודה הלוי מינץ is born around 1405 at Mainz, the city reflected in his family name. Jewish Encyclopedia
ר׳ יהודה הלוי מינץ relocates from the German lands to Padua and begins the long rabbinic and educational career that makes his yeshiva an international centre. Referenced biographical synthesis

As rabbi and rosh yeshiva, ר׳ יהודה הלוי מינץ establishes Ashkenazi patterns of advanced Talmud study in Padua and draws pupils from many communities; the year represents an extended activity. Encyclopedia Daat
ר׳ יהודה הלוי מינץ issues communal rulings and ordinances and participates in a major dispute with Elijah Delmedigo; the displayed year is approximate. Jewish Encyclopedia
ר׳ יהודה הלוי מינץ dies at Padua on 27 September 1508 after approximately forty-seven years of rabbinic leadership. Referenced date synthesis

ר׳ משה בן אליהו קפשאלי.event: ר׳ משה בן אליהו קפשאלי is born around 1420 at Candia into a prominent Cretan Jewish family. Encyclopaedia Judaica

As a young man, ר׳ משה בן אליהו קפשאלי travels through the German lands to study in Ashkenazi yeshivot. The sources do not securely identify one city, so the point uses Mainz only as a regional cartographic anchor. Jewish Encyclopedia
By about 1450, ר׳ משה בן אליהו קפשאלי is serving as rabbi of Constantinople, shortly before the Ottoman conquest. Jewish Encyclopedia

After Mehmed II conquers Constantinople, ר׳ משה בן אליהו קפשאלי is recognized as the city’s senior Jewish authority, with judicial and fiscal responsibilities. Scholarly study of Ottoman religious administration

A dispute over the family-law rulings of ר׳ משה בן אליהו קפשאלי reaches ר׳ יוסף קולון in Italy; fuller communal testimony ultimately clears his reputation. The year is approximate. Encyclopaedia Judaica
Under Bayezid II, ר׳ משה בן אליהו קפשאלי helps receive and organize assistance for Jews expelled from Spain, including fairer distribution of communal taxation. Hebrew biographical synthesis
ר׳ משה בן אליהו קפשאלי dies in Constantinople around 1495 after more than four decades of communal leadership. Jewish Encyclopedia

ר׳ יצחק עראמה.event: ר׳ יצחק עראמה is born around 1420, probably in or near Zamora; the city is certain as his earliest scholarly centre, while the precise birthplace remains uncertain. Encyclopedia Daat
ר׳ יצחק עראמה heads a Torah academy in Zamora; the displayed year is approximate because the office is documented without a precise appointment date. Encyclopaedia Judaica
Appointed rabbi and preacher in Tarragona, ר׳ יצחק עראמה develops public sermons defending Jewish belief against compulsory Christian preaching; the year is approximate. Encyclopedia Daat
ר׳ יצחק עראמה moves to Fraga and continues his rabbinic and homiletical work; these sermons form part of the intellectual foundation of עקדת יצחק. Referenced biographical synthesis
At Calatayud, ר׳ יצחק עראמה serves as rabbi, head of the academy and head of the rabbinical court, bringing his Spanish career to its mature stage; the year is approximate. Encyclopedia Daat
The expulsion from Spain forces ר׳ יצחק עראמה into exile. He settles in Naples and continues preparing his writings. Encyclopaedia Judaica
ר׳ יצחק עראמה dies in Naples about two years after the expulsion, leaving עקדת יצחק as his defining legacy. Encyclopedia Daat

ר׳ יוסף בן שלמה קולון טרבוט.event: ר׳ יוסף בן שלמה קולון טרבוט is born around 1420 at Chambéry into a learned family. See the Daat Encyclopedia and biographical overview.
By about 1469 ר׳ יוסף בן שלמה קולון טרבוט serves as rabbi at Piove di Sacco, an early securely named station in his northern Italian career. See the biographical overview.
ר׳ יוסף בן שלמה קולון טרבוט serves the community of Mestre during his movement among northern Italian rabbinates. See the biographical overview.
ר׳ יוסף בן שלמה קולון טרבוט holds a rabbinic position at Bologna before his Mantuan period. The transition date is approximate. See the biographical overview.
ר׳ יוסף בן שלמה קולון טרבוט teaches and adjudicates at Mantua. A conflict with ר׳ יהודה מסר ליאון later divides the community. See the Jewish Encyclopedia — Mantua.
Following the communal controversy, Mantua’s ruler orders both ר׳ יוסף בן שלמה קולון טרבוט and ר׳ יהודה מסר ליאון to leave. See the Jewish Encyclopedia — Mantua.
ר׳ יוסף בן שלמה קולון טרבוט settles at Pavia, where he heads a yeshiva and continues producing influential responsa. See the biographical overview.
ר׳ יוסף בן שלמה קולון טרבוט dies at Pavia in 1480. His responsa are collected and printed posthumously. See the French biographical entry and Daat Encyclopedia.

ר׳ יצחק אבוהב.event: ר׳ יצחק אבוהב is born in Toledo in 1433 into the distinguished Aboab family. Real Academia de la Historia
Following the death of his teacher ר׳ יצחק קנפנטון, ר׳ יצחק אבוהב succeeds to leadership within the Castilian academy; the precise appointment date is approximate. Real Academia de la Historia

ר׳ יצחק אבוהב.place: Buitrago del Lozoya, Crown of Castile
ר׳ יצחק אבוהב.event: ר׳ יצחק אבוהב lives and teaches for a period at Buitrago, one of the documented centres of his Castilian academy career; the year is approximate. Referenced biographical synthesis
At Guadalajara, ר׳ יצחק אבוהב leads advanced study and teaches a circle that includes ר׳ אברהם זכות; the displayed year represents an extended period. Real Academia de la Historia
After the expulsion decree, ר׳ יצחק אבוהב joins a delegation of Jewish leaders in Lisbon to negotiate with John II for the admission of Spanish refugees. Jewish Encyclopedia
ר׳ יצחק אבוהב, his family and close associates receive permission to settle at Porto under comparatively favourable conditions. Real Academia de la Historia
ר׳ יצחק אבוהב dies at Porto in January 1493, only months after the expulsion; his pupil ר׳ אברהם זכות delivers the eulogy. Real Academia de la Historia

ר׳ יצחק בן יהודה אברבנאל.event: ר׳ יצחק בן יהודה אברבנאל is born in Lisbon in 1437 to Don Judah Abarbanel, within a wealthy Sephardi family with roots in Seville. National Library of Israel biography

Serving the court of Afonso V, ר׳ יצחק אברבנאל uses his position and wealth to raise funds for the redemption of Jewish captives seized after Portugal’s conquest of Arzila. National Library of Israel biography

After João II moves against the Braganza faction, ר׳ יצחק אברבנאל flees Portugal across the border into Castile, losing much of his property and later entering the financial service of Ferdinand and Isabella. Biographical chronology

ר׳ יצחק בן יהודה אברבנאל.place: Castile and Valencia, Crown of Aragon
ר׳ יצחק בן יהודה אברבנאל.event: ר׳ יצחק אברבנאל attempts unsuccessfully to persuade the Catholic Monarchs to revoke the expulsion decree and leaves Iberia with the exiles, sailing toward Naples. National Library of Israel biography
In Naples, ר׳ יצחק אברבנאל enters the service of Ferrante I and Alfonso II and resumes the biblical commentary interrupted by his political career. Encyclopaedia Judaica biography
When French forces seize Naples, ר׳ יצחק אברבנאל follows the displaced royal household to Messina before continuing as a refugee to Corfu. National Library of Israel biography
During a short refuge on Corfu, ר׳ יצחק אברבנאל continues his scholarship before settling on the Apulian coast. Encyclopaedia Judaica biography
At Monopoli, ר׳ יצחק אברבנאל enters his most sustained period of post-expulsion writing, completing biblical, philosophical, and messianic works between 1496 and 1503. Oxford intellectual biography
ר׳ יצחק אברבנאל settles in Venice, where the republic employs his experience in negotiations concerning Portuguese commerce and where he completes further commentaries. Treccani biography

ר׳ יצחק בן יהודה אברבנאל dies in Venice on 23 September 1508 and is taken for burial at Padua. The cemetery was later destroyed and the exact grave is no longer identifiable. National Library of Israel biography

ר׳ יוסף יעבץ.event: ר׳ יוסף יעבץ is born around 1440 in Lisbon according to the biographical introduction to a modern critical edition. Machon Shlomo Aumann

After the Spanish expulsion, ר׳ יוסף יעבץ joins the displaced Iberian Jewish population in Portugal and preaches consolation and religious steadfastness. Lisbon is retained as a national anchor because no secure town is stated for this stage. Nechama Leibowitz commentator profile

Continuing his exile, ר׳ יוסף יעבץ passes through Sicily. Palermo is used as an island-level cartographic anchor because the biographical source does not identify a precise settlement. Nechama Leibowitz commentator profile
ר׳ יוסף יעבץ reaches Naples among the Iberian exiles and continues developing sermons centred on providence and the meaning of expulsion. Nechama Leibowitz commentator profile
ר׳ יוסף יעבץ settles at Mantua, where he writes much of his theological and exegetical corpus and encourages ר׳ יהודה חייט to comment on מערכת האלהות; the year is approximate. Jewish Encyclopedia

ר׳ יוסף יעבץ dies around 1508, conventionally associated with his final centre at Mantua. The date follows the National Library of Israel; older references disagree. National Library of Israel authority record

ר׳ עובדיה מברטנורא.event: ר׳ עובדיה מברטנורא is born in or closely associated from youth with Bertinoro around 1445. The exact year remains uncertain. See the National Library of Israel authority record and Encyclopaedia Judaica.
Before emigrating, ר׳ עובדיה מברטנורא serves as rabbi in Bertinoro and Città di Castello. The displayed year is approximate. See Encyclopaedia Judaica.
On 29 October 1486 ר׳ עובדיה מברטנורא leaves Italy for the Land of Israel, traveling first through Rome and then southward. See the Jewish Encyclopedia.
During his Mediterranean journey, ר׳ עובדיה מברטנורא spends about three months in Palermo preaching and teaching after stops at Naples and Salerno. See Encyclopaedia Judaica.

Early in 1488 ר׳ עובדיה מברטנורא passes through Alexandria and Cairo; the Egyptian Nagid reportedly attempts to retain him before he continues via Gaza, Hebron and Bethlehem. See Encyclopaedia Judaica.

On 25 March 1488, shortly before Passover, ר׳ עובדיה מברטנורא arrives in Jerusalem. His contemporary letter records the city and its struggling Jewish community. See the 1488 Letter from Jerusalem and Jewish Encyclopedia.
In 1491 ר׳ עובדיה מברטנורא temporarily leaves Jerusalem and serves the Hebron community, later returning to Jerusalem. See Encyclopaedia Judaica.
Back in Jerusalem, ר׳ עובדיה מברטנורא leads the community, strengthens poor relief and establishes a yeshiva. The return year is approximate. See the Jewish Encyclopedia.
ר׳ עובדיה מברטנורא dies in Jerusalem around 1515; sources place his death before about 1516 but do not preserve a secure date. See the National Library of Israel.

ר׳ אברהם זכות.event: ר׳ אברהם זכות is born at Salamanca on 12 August 1452 and receives both rabbinic and scientific education. Max Planck Institute — Islamic Scientific Manuscripts Initiative
ר׳ אברהם זכות completes the Hebrew astronomical tables and canons known as החיבור הגדול, calculated for Salamanca. Jewish Encyclopedia

Expelled from Spain, ר׳ אברהם זכות enters Portugal and serves the royal court as an authority on astronomy and navigation. Lisbon is used as the court-centred map anchor. Max Planck Institute biography
The Almanach Perpetuum, adapted from the tables of ר׳ אברהם זכות, is printed at Leiria in Latin and Castilian and becomes an important navigational resource. Referenced publication synthesis
Driven from Portugal by the forced-conversion crisis, ר׳ אברהם זכות reaches North Africa after a difficult exile and settles in Tunis. Jewish Encyclopedia
In Tunis, ר׳ אברהם זכות completes ספר יוחסין, his influential chronology of Jewish history and chains of rabbinic tradition. Hebrew edition description
ר׳ אברהם זכות dies around 1515, probably in Damascus. Other traditions place his final years or death in Jerusalem, and the evidence does not permit certainty. Max Planck Institute biography

ר׳ אליהו מזרחי.event: ר׳ אליהו מזרחי is born around 1455 into Constantinople’s Romaniote Jewish community. Posen Library
As a young scholar, ר׳ אליהו מזרחי teaches Talmud, mathematics and other sciences in a school he develops in Constantinople; the displayed year is approximate. Posen Library
ר׳ אליהו מזרחי succeeds ר׳ משה קפשאלי as the leading rabbinic and communal authority of Constantinople. Sources differ slightly on whether the transition began in 1495 or 1498. Posen Library

Amid the resettlement of Iberian exiles, ר׳ אליהו מזרחי raises relief funds and helps mediate the changing relations among Constantinople’s Jewish congregations; the year represents an extended activity. Posen Library
ר׳ אליהו מזרחי dies in Constantinople. His Torah supercommentary and mathematical writings are printed posthumously and circulate widely. National Library of Israel authority record

ר׳ יעקב בן שלמה אבן חביב.event: ר׳ יעקב בן שלמה אבן חביב is born at Zamora around 1460; modern studies allow an earlier date near 1445–1450. See the Jewish Encyclopedia and Nechama Leibowitz commentator profile.

Before the expulsion, ר׳ יעקב בן שלמה אבן חביב becomes a leading Talmud scholar and heads a yeshiva at Salamanca. The displayed year is approximate because sources establish the pre-1492 office but not its start date. See the Hebrew biographical profile.

Expelled from Spain with his family, ר׳ יעקב בן שלמה אבן חביב first takes refuge in Portugal. Because the surviving biography does not identify a secure town, Lisbon serves only as a national cartographic anchor. See the Hebrew biographical profile.

After Portugal’s forced-conversion crisis, ר׳ יעקב בן שלמה אבן חביב settles in Salonica and becomes a leader of its large community of Iberian exiles. See the Encyclopaedia Judaica and the Hebrew profile.

ר׳ יעקב בן שלמה אבן חביב supervises the first printing of עין יעקב at the press of Judah Gedaliah. He dies after Zeraim and Moed appear; his son ר׳ לוי בן חביב completes the publication. See the Jewish Encyclopedia and the first-edition catalogue description.

ר׳ יעקב בן יוסף פולק.event: ר׳ יעקב בן יוסף פולק is born around 1460 or 1470, probably in Poland or the German lands; surviving evidence does not identify the place securely. YIVO Encyclopedia
ר׳ יעקב בן יוסף פולק serves as rabbi and rosh yeshiva in Prague with ר׳ יצחק מרגליות, after studying under the latter’s father ר׳ יעקב מרגליות. Jewish Encyclopedia

A controversial ruling by ר׳ יעקב בן יוסף פולק validating a minor woman’s refusal of marriage provokes an extended dispute with ר׳ יהודה מינץ and other authorities and contributes to his departure from Prague. Encyclopaedia Judaica biography
In Kraków, ר׳ יעקב בן יוסף פולק organizes a major Talmudic academy and receives a royal appointment as rabbi of Poland or, according to a narrower reading, Lesser Poland. YIVO Encyclopedia

After communal disputes, ר׳ יעקב בן יוסף פולק leaves Kraków. His academy and hillukim method continue through his leading student ר׳ שלום שכנא. The precise departure year is approximate. Hebrew biographical synthesis
An approbation may place ר׳ יעקב בן יוסף פולק in Constantinople in 1532, possibly while travelling toward Jerusalem; the identification and itinerary remain uncertain. Encyclopaedia Judaica biography

ר׳ יעקב בן יוסף פולק.place: Lublin, Kingdom of Poland; traditional attribution
ר׳ יעקב בן יוסף פולק.event: Traditional chronology says ר׳ יעקב בן יוסף פולק dies at Lublin in 1541. Modern scholarship doubts whether the tombstone once attributed to him was actually his, so the final location is not certain. YIVO Encyclopedia

ר׳ יוסף בן שלמה טאיטאצק.event: ר׳ יוסף בן שלמה טאיטאצק is born around 1465 in Castile. No secure town is documented, so Toledo serves only as a regional cartographic anchor. Encyclopedia Daat

The expulsion from Spain drives ר׳ יוסף בן שלמה טאיטאצק and his family into Portugal. Lisbon is used as a national anchor because the sources do not establish a precise town. Hebrew biographical profile
Following Portugal’s forced-conversion crisis, ר׳ יוסף בן שלמה טאיטאצק settles at Salonica and begins building the yeshiva and communal leadership associated with his name. Encyclopedia Daat

ר׳ יוסף בן שלמה טאיטאצק is established as head of a major yeshiva and leader of the Portuguese congregation, offices he holds for roughly four decades; the start year is approximate. Encyclopedia Daat

During Solomon Molcho’s preaching in Salonica, ר׳ יוסף בן שלמה טאיטאצק supports the charismatic messianic figure, reflecting the spiritual ferment of the exile generation. Referenced biographical synthesis
ר׳ יוסף בן שלמה טאיטאצק dies in Salonica in 1546 after decades of yeshiva and communal leadership. Daf Yomi rabbinic chronology

ר׳ משה אלשקר.event: ר׳ משה אלשקר is born in Zamora in 1466 and later studies with ר׳ שמואל ולנסי. Encyclopedia Daat
Expelled from Spain, ר׳ משה אלשקר survives a dangerous Mediterranean voyage involving shipwreck and pirates and settles in Tunis, where he helps lead the community. Encyclopaedia Judaica
Spanish incursions into North Africa force ר׳ משה אלשקר to flee. After additional travel, he establishes a yeshiva at Patras in Greece. Encyclopaedia Judaica
ר׳ משה אלשקר is appointed a dayan in Cairo and participates in the court associated with ר׳ דוד בן זמרא, while answering legal questions from distant communities. Daat introduction to his writings
About three years before his death, ר׳ משה אלשקר leaves Egypt for the Land of Israel and spends a period in Safed amid the controversy over renewed ordination. Hebrew biographical synthesis
After moving from Safed to Jerusalem, ר׳ משה אלשקר dies there in 1542. His responsa are printed eleven years later. Encyclopedia Daat

ר׳ יעקב בירב.event: ר׳ יעקב בירב is born around 1474 at Maqueda near Toledo and later studies with ר׳ יצחק אבוהב. Referenced biographical synthesis
Driven from Spain by the expulsion, ר׳ יעקב בירב reaches Fez, where the Sephardi refugee community recognizes the young Talmudist as a rabbinic leader. Jewish Encyclopedia
ר׳ יעקב בירב serves and teaches in Tlemcen after leaving Fez, building his reputation among North African Sephardi communities; the year is approximate. Referenced biographical synthesis
Before 1522 ר׳ יעקב בירב lives briefly in Jerusalem, but oppressive economic conditions lead him and his pupils back toward Egypt. Referenced biographical synthesis
A dated responsum places ר׳ יעקב בירב in Damascus in 1527, one stage in his leadership across Ottoman Syria and Egypt. Jewish Encyclopedia
ר׳ יעקב בירב becomes rabbi in Cairo in 1533 before establishing his principal late-career centre in Safed. Jewish Encyclopedia

Twenty-five Safed rabbis confer renewed semikhah on ר׳ יעקב בירב. He then ordains ר׳ יוסף קארו, ר׳ משה מטראני, and other scholars, seeking to establish a central authoritative court. Encyclopaedia Judaica on semikhah

During the controversy with ר׳ לוי בן חביב of Jerusalem over the legality of renewed semikhah, ר׳ יעקב בירב withdraws temporarily to Damascus and defends the Safed enactment. Posen Library — Kuntres ha-Semikhah
ר׳ יעקב בירב dies in Safed on 3 April 1546 and is buried in the old Jewish cemetery, leaving the renewed ordination to the scholars he had ordained. Referenced date and burial biography

ר׳ עובדיה ספורנו.event: ר׳ עובדיה ספורנו is born at Cesena around the middle of the 1470s to Jacob di Rubino, in a Jewish banking family of Catalan origin with strong connections to Bologna. The exact year is unknown; circa 1475 is the conventional map date. See the archival Dizionario Biografico degli Italiani and Encyclopaedia Judaica.

By 1498, ר׳ עובדיה ספורנו is living in Rome and pursuing medicine, philosophy, mathematics and philology. From 1498 to 1500 he gives Johannes Reuchlin private instruction in Hebrew and probably Maimonidean philosophy, a relationship remembered in Reuchlin's De rudimentis Hebraicis. See Treccani's archival biography and the Treccani Reuchlin entry.

ר׳ עובדיה ספורנו.place: Ferrara, Duchy of Ferrara; now Italy
ר׳ עובדיה ספורנו.event: In 1501 ר׳ עובדיה ספורנו is documented at Ferrara, where he receives his medical degree. He is already married to Allegra, from the prominent Norsa banking family. This was a documented study and qualification visit, not his permanent settlement. See the source-based account in the Dizionario Biografico degli Italiani.

After his medical qualification, ר׳ עובדיה ספורנו returns to Rome and remains closely connected with the city until 1527. He practises medicine, participates in banking interests and becomes a communal notable with relationships reaching papal court circles. The chronicle of דוד הראובני records him among leading Roman Jews during the latter's 1524 visit. See Treccani and Encyclopaedia Judaica.

Following the Sack of Rome in 1527, ר׳ עובדיה ספורנו relocates to Bologna. There he practises medicine, shares in the credit enterprise of his brother ר׳ חננאל ספורנו, serves as a rabbi in the court of Avraham HaKohen and teaches a select circle. See the documented chronology in the Dizionario Biografico degli Italiani.

ר׳ עובדיה ספורנו publishes his philosophical אור עמים in Bologna in 1537 through the Hebrew press of the Associates of the Silk Art, whose revival he probably helped lead. His commentary on Pirkei Avot follows in a Bologna machzor in 1540, and the revised Latin Lumen gentium in 1548. See Treccani and the autograph manuscript record at the National Library of Israel.

ר׳ עובדיה ספורנו dies in Bologna in 1550, after making surviving wills in 1547 and 1549. Notarial records confirm the year. His brother ר׳ חננאל ספורנו later edits the Torah commentary for its first printing in Venice in 1567. Bologna's later expulsions and destruction of its Jewish cemetery mean that his burial place is no longer identifiable. See the archival Italian biography and Encyclopaedia Judaica.

ר׳ דוד בן שלמה אבן זמרא.event: ר׳ דוד בן שלמה אבן זמרא is born in Spain around 1479. Sources do not securely identify the town, so the coordinate represents central Spain rather than the often-repeated but unverified Seville claim. See Louis Jacobs, Theology in the Responsa and the Jewish Encyclopedia.

After the expulsion from Spain, the young ר׳ דוד בן שלמה אבן זמרא reaches Safed with his family and studies in its Sephardi community. His own responsum places him there at about age thirteen. See the Jewish Encyclopedia and Kestenbaum biographical description.

In his early thirties, ר׳ דוד בן שלמה אבן זמרא leaves the Land of Israel for Fez and joins the rabbinic circle associated with ר׳ יצחק שולאל. The exact year is approximate. See the Kestenbaum scholarly biography.

ר׳ דוד בן שלמה אבן זמרא settles in Cairo, where he becomes a judge, teacher and major halakhic authority. The year is approximate and precedes his securely dated communal succession. See Louis Jacobs and the Jewish Encyclopedia.

After the Ottoman conquest, ר׳ דוד בן שלמה אבן זמרא succeeds ר׳ יצחק שולאל as head of Egyptian Jewry and leads Cairo’s rabbinical court and yeshiva. See the scholarly discussion in research on the Egyptian chief rabbinate and Louis Jacobs.
After roughly four decades of leadership in Egypt, ר׳ דוד בן שלמה אבן זמרא relinquishes office and returns to the Land of Israel, initially residing in Jerusalem. See the Jewish Encyclopedia.

ר׳ דוד בן שלמה אבן זמרא settles for his final years in Safed, then a major centre of halakhah and kabbalah. The displayed year is approximate; sources securely establish the Jerusalem-to-Safed sequence but not a precise moving date. See Louis Jacobs and the Jewish Encyclopedia.
ר׳ דוד בן שלמה אבן זמרא dies in Safed in 1573 after a career spanning post-expulsion Spain, North Africa, Egypt and the Land of Israel. See Louis Jacobs.

ר׳ מאיר קצנלנבוגן.event: ר׳ מאיר קצנלנבוגן is born at Katzenelnbogen around 1482. See the Jewish Encyclopedia and Treccani.
As a young scholar, ר׳ מאיר קצנלנבוגן studies in Prague under ר׳ יעקב פולק. The year is approximate. See the Jewish Encyclopedia.
ר׳ מאיר קצנלנבוגן reaches Padua, joins the academy of ר׳ יהודה מינץ and marries into the Minz family. The exact arrival year is not documented and is mapped approximately. See Treccani and Wikishiva.
By the 1520s, ר׳ מאיר קצנלנבוגן has succeeded his father-in-law ר׳ אברהם מינץ as rabbi and rosh yeshiva of Padua. The displayed year is approximate. See the Jewish Encyclopedia.

The Padua edition of משנה תורה prepared by ר׳ מאיר קצנלנבוגן becomes the subject of the Bragadin–Giustiniani printing dispute; ר׳ משה איסרליש supports his publishing rights. This records his documented Venetian communal and printing activity, not a permanent move. See the Jewish Virtual Library.
ר׳ מאיר קצנלנבוגן presides over the Ferrara rabbinic synod convened after the Italian Hebrew-book crisis. See the Jewish Virtual Library.
ר׳ מאיר קצנלנבוגן dies in Padua on 12 January 1565 after decades of communal and academic leadership. See Wikimedia’s authority record.

ר׳ לוי בן חביב.event: ר׳ לוי בן חביב is born around 1483 in Zamora, son of ר׳ יעקב בן חביב. Some reference works round his birth to 1480. Encyclopaedia Judaica

The Spanish expulsion drives the family of ר׳ לוי בן חביב into Portugal. During the later forced-conversion campaign he is baptized against his will while still a youth; Lisbon is used only as a national map anchor. Jewish Encyclopedia
Having escaped Portugal, ר׳ לוי בן חביב openly returns to Judaism in Salonica, studies in its Sephardi academies and becomes a teacher; the displayed year is approximate. Encyclopedia Daat
After the death of his father ר׳ יעקב בן חביב, ר׳ לוי בן חביב completes and publishes the unfinished portions of עין יעקב. Jewish Encyclopedia
ר׳ לוי בן חביב makes an initial move to Jerusalem but soon returns temporarily to Salonica. Jewish Encyclopedia
ר׳ לוי בן חביב settles permanently in Jerusalem and becomes the city’s leading rabbinic authority, working to preserve its economically fragile community. Encyclopedia Daat
When Safed’s scholars under ר׳ יעקב בירב attempt to renew semikhah, ר׳ לוי בן חביב rejects the procedure and authors the arguments preserved in קונטרס הסמיכה. Posen Library
ר׳ לוי בן חביב dies in Jerusalem around 1545. Sources range from 1541 to 1548; this record follows Encyclopaedia Judaica’s c.1545. Encyclopaedia Judaica

ר׳ יוסף קארו.event: According to the traditional chronology, ר׳ יוסף קארו is born in Toledo in 1488; modern scholarship acknowledges uncertainty over the exact Iberian birthplace. See Encyclopaedia Judaica via Encyclopedia.com.

After the Spanish expulsion, the family of ר׳ יוסף קארו takes refuge in Portugal; the available sources do not securely identify a town, so the coordinate is deliberately non-building-specific. See Encyclopaedia Judaica.
Following Portugal’s forced-conversion crisis, ר׳ יוסף קארו reaches the Ottoman Empire and initially lives with his family in Constantinople. See Encyclopaedia Judaica.
By 1522, ר׳ יוסף קארו is living in Adrianople and developing בית יוסף, the comprehensive commentary on ארבעה טורים. See Encyclopaedia Judaica.

During his later Ottoman period, ר׳ יוסף קארו heads a rabbinical academy at Nikopol and is in contact with ר׳ שלמה הלוי אלקבץ. The year represents an approximate stage rather than a precisely dated move. See Encyclopaedia Judaica.
ר׳ יוסף קארו settles in Safed around 1535–1536, joins its rabbinical court and becomes one of the city’s principal teachers and decisors. See Encyclopaedia Judaica.
ר׳ יוסף קארו receives the renewed semikhah from ר׳ יעקב בירב and becomes a central participant in Safed’s attempted restoration of ordination. See Encyclopaedia Judaica.
ר׳ יוסף קארו dies in Safed on 24 March 1575, after completing the works that made him the defining codifier of later halakhah. See Encyclopedia of Religion.

ר׳ משה בן יוסף מטראני.event: ר׳ משה בן יוסף מטראני is born in Salonika to a family of Italian-Sephardi origin. See Encyclopaedia Judaica.
As a boy, ר׳ משה בן יוסף מטראני studies Talmud in Adrianople under his uncle ר׳ אהרן מטראני. The year is approximate. See the Posen Library author profile.
At about sixteen, ר׳ משה בן יוסף מטראני settles in Safed and studies under ר׳ יעקב בירב. See Encyclopaedia Judaica.
ר׳ משה בן יוסף מטראני begins his long service as rabbi and dayan of Safed, eventually heading an academy and becoming one of the city’s two leading halakhists with ר׳ יוסף קארו. See Sefaria.
After the death of ר׳ יוסף קארו, ר׳ משה בן יוסף מטראני becomes Safed’s senior communal authority. See Encyclopaedia Judaica.
Under the chronology used by this record, ר׳ משה בן יוסף מטראני dies in 1580 and is buried in Safed. Some catalogues instead give 1585. See Encyclopaedia Judaica.

ר׳ שלמה הלוי אלקבץ.event: ר׳ שלמה הלוי אלקבץ is born around 1505, probably in Salonica, into a family of Iberian exiles. See ANU Museum and the National Library of Israel.
Around his marriage, ר׳ שלמה הלוי אלקבץ completes מנות הלוי and presents it in place of conventional wedding gifts; he had studied under ר׳ יוסף טאיטאצאק. See the National Library of Israel.
Before emigrating, ר׳ שלמה הלוי אלקבץ stays in Adrianople, teaches a mystical circle and composes several works. The year is approximate. See ANU Museum.
On the Balkan route, ר׳ שלמה הלוי אלקבץ encounters ר׳ יוסף קארו at Nikopol. The date is approximate. See ANU Museum.
ר׳ שלמה הלוי אלקבץ settles in Safed, teaches Torah and kabbalah, and helps shape the practice of receiving Shabbat outdoors in song. See National Library of Israel.
During the flourishing Safed period, ר׳ שלמה הלוי אלקבץ composes לכה דודי. Its exact composition year is unknown, so 1540 is an approximate map point. See the National Library of Israel.
ר׳ שלמה הלוי אלקבץ dies in Safed around 1584; competing traditions place his death somewhat earlier. See ANU Museum.

ר׳ שמואל בן משה די מדינה.event: ר׳ שמואל בן משה די מדינה is born in Salonika in 1506. See the National Library of Israel authority record.

By early adulthood, ר׳ שמואל בן משה די מדינה has emerged from the academies of ר׳ יוסף טאיטאצאק and ר׳ לוי בן חביב and becomes a leading teacher in Salonika. The year is approximate. See the Daat responsa introduction.

ר׳ שמואל בן משה די מדינה heads a major Salonikan yeshiva and answers questions from across the Ottoman and Mediterranean Jewish worlds. The displayed year represents his mature leadership rather than a precisely dated appointment. See the Daat scholarly introduction.

During his long Salonikan career, ר׳ שמואל בן משה די מדינה undertakes a communal mission to Constantinople. The surviving summaries do not securely date the journey, so 1565 is an explicitly approximate midpoint. See the Daat biography.
ר׳ שמואל בן משה די מדינה dies in Salonika on 2 Cheshvan 5350 (1589). See the National Library of Israel.

ר׳ משה אלשיך.event: ר׳ משה אלשיך is born in Adrianople in 1508. See the Encyclopaedia Judaica biography.
As a young scholar, ר׳ משה אלשיך studies in Salonika under ר׳ יוסף טאיטאצאק and ר׳ יוסף קארו. The year is approximate. See Sefaria’s author profile.
ר׳ משה אלשיך settles in Safed, where he becomes a dayan, academy head and renowned preacher. See the scholarly encyclopedia account.

Around 1590, ר׳ משה אלשיך travels as an emissary for the struggling Safed community through Syria and Ottoman lands; Aleppo represents one documented regional centre, not a claim to a precisely dated stay. See the Encyclopaedia Judaica biography.

A court record places ר׳ משה אלשיך in Damascus in 1593. The standard chronology assigns his death to this year, although other traditions place it later in Safed. See the Electronic Jewish Encyclopedia.

ר׳ שלום שכנא מלובלין.event: ר׳ שלום שכנא מלובלין is born approximately in Lublin around 1510; alternative traditions suggest an earlier birth around 1490–1495. See the National Library of Israel and Jewish Encyclopedia.

As a young scholar, ר׳ שלום שכנא מלובלין studies under ר׳ יעקב פולק and absorbs the pilpul method. The date is approximate, and no unsupported Kraków residence is asserted. See the Jewish Encyclopedia.
By 1528, ר׳ שלום שכנא מלובלין is already renowned as a teacher, and hundreds come to study at his Lublin yeshiva. See the Jewish Encyclopedia.
ר׳ שלום שכנא מלובלין receives royal recognition as one of the senior rabbis overseeing Polish Jewish communal affairs while continuing to lead the Lublin yeshiva. See Hamichlol.

In his mature Lublin academy, ר׳ שלום שכנא מלובלין teaches a generation of authorities including his son-in-law ר׳ משה איסרליש. The displayed year is representative rather than a precisely dated lesson. See the Jewish Encyclopedia.
ר׳ שלום שכנא מלובלין dies in Lublin on 29 October 1558. His instruction not to print his manuscripts helps explain why his influence survived mainly through students. See the Jewish Encyclopedia.

ר׳ שלמה בן יחיאל לוריא.place: Brest-Litovsk, Grand Duchy of Lithuania; now Brest, Belarus
ר׳ שלמה בן יחיאל לוריא.event: ר׳ שלמה בן יחיאל לוריא is born in 1510, according to the prevailing Brest tradition. Some authorities instead give Poznań, and the record preserves that disagreement rather than pretending certainty. See the Polish Museum of the History of Polish Jews biography and Encyclopaedia Judaica.

ר׳ שלמה בן יחיאל לוריא.place: Poznań, Kingdom of Poland; approximate youth period
ר׳ שלמה בן יחיאל לוריא.event: During childhood, ר׳ שלמה בן יחיאל לוריא spends formative years with his grandfather ר׳ יצחק קלויבר in Poznań. The displayed year is approximate. See the Hebrew Daat biography.

ר׳ שלמה בן יחיאל לוריא.place: Lublin, Kingdom of Poland; approximate study period
ר׳ שלמה בן יחיאל לוריא.event: As a young scholar, ר׳ שלמה בן יחיאל לוריא studies in Lublin under ר׳ שלום שכנא, in the same scholarly world as ר׳ משה איסרליש. The precise starting year is not documented and is shown approximately. See the biographical account.

ר׳ שלמה בן יחיאל לוריא.place: Brest-Litovsk, Grand Duchy of Lithuania; approximate rabbinate
ר׳ שלמה בן יחיאל לוריא.event: In early adulthood, ר׳ שלמה בן יחיאל לוריא serves the Brest scholarly community, probably including rabbinic leadership, before his move to Volhynia. The date and exact office remain imperfectly documented. See Encyclopaedia Judaica.

ר׳ שלמה בן יחיאל לוריא.place: Ostroh, Volhynia, Grand Duchy of Lithuania; now Ukraine
ר׳ שלמה בן יחיאל לוריא.event: Around 1550, ר׳ שלמה בן יחיאל לוריא becomes rabbi and head of the yeshiva in Ostroh, building a major centre of Talmud study. See the Polish biographical record and Daat.

ר׳ שלמה בן יחיאל לוריא moves to Lublin and leads its great yeshiva, eventually establishing an independent academy. His scholarship and responsa make Lublin his principal mature centre. See the Hebrew chronology and the biographical account.

ר׳ שלמה בן יחיאל לוריא dies in Lublin on 7 November 1573 and is buried in the Old Jewish Cemetery. Some Hebrew chronologies express the year as 5334, producing occasional 1574 cataloguing; the civil date supports 1573. See the POLIN-linked biography.

ר׳ אליעזר בן אליהו אשכנזי.event: ר׳ אליעזר בן אליהו אשכנזי is born in 1512 at an unknown location, probably in the eastern Mediterranean; Salonika is used as the earliest documented educational location, not a claimed birthplace. See the Jewish Encyclopedia and Posen Library.
ר׳ אליעזר בן אליהו אשכנזי studies under ר׳ יוסף טאיטאצאק in Salonika. The year is approximate. See Posen Library.
ר׳ אליעזר בן אליהו אשכנזי begins serving as a rabbi in Egypt, probably at Fustat, where he becomes known as a scholar, physician and communal authority. See the Jewish Encyclopedia.
Forced to leave Egypt, ר׳ אליעזר בן אליהו אשכנזי becomes rabbi of Famagusta for about two years. See Encyclopaedia Judaica.
ר׳ אליעזר בן אליהו אשכנזי reaches Venice but leaves after a disagreement with ר׳ מאיר קצנלנבוגן and his son ר׳ שמואל יהודה. See the Jewish Encyclopedia.
In Prague, ר׳ אליעזר בן אליהו אשכנזי signs first among the founders of the communal burial society and acts as a leading authority. See the Jewish Encyclopedia.
After further travel, including toward Crimea, ר׳ אליעזר בן אליהו אשכנזי returns to Italy and serves in Cremona. See Posen Library.
While serving in Gniezno, ר׳ אליעזר בן אליהו אשכנזי completes מעשי ה׳. See Encyclopaedia Judaica.
ר׳ אליעזר בן אליהו אשכנזי settles in Kraków, probably serving at the head of its rabbinical court. See the Jewish Community of Kraków.
ר׳ אליעזר בן אליהו אשכנזי dies in Kraków on 13 December 1585 and is buried in the Remuh Cemetery. See the Jewish Community of Kraków.

ר׳ בצלאל בן אברהם אשכנזי.event: ר׳ בצלאל בן אברהם אשכנזי is born around 1520 in the Land of Israel, probably in Jerusalem or Safed; the sources do not securely choose between them. Encyclopaedia Judaica biography
ר׳ בצלאל אשכנזי moves to Cairo and studies under ר׳ דוד אבן זמרא, while retaining the influence of his earlier teacher ר׳ ישראל די קוריאל. Encyclopaedia Judaica biography

After ר׳ דוד אבן זמרא leaves Egypt, ר׳ בצלאל אשכנזי succeeds him as head of the Egyptian rabbis and leads an academy attended by ר׳ יצחק לוריא אשכנזי and other major scholars. Encyclopaedia Judaica biography

In Cairo, ר׳ בצלאל אשכנזי develops אספת זקנים, later called שיטה מקובצת, by copying and arranging manuscript commentaries of Geonim and Rishonim according to the Talmudic text. The year is an approximate scholarly marker. Da’at Hebrew encyclopedia

ר׳ בצלאל אשכנזי settles in Jerusalem and is recognized as leader by both Sephardi and Ashkenazi communities, mediating the city's severe taxation dispute and strengthening its institutions. Jewish Encyclopedia
ר׳ בצלאל אשכנזי revisits Egypt in 1591 on communal business before apparently returning to Jerusalem. Encyclopaedia Judaica biography
ר׳ בצלאל בן אברהם אשכנזי dies in the early 1590s, apparently in Jerusalem; 1592 is used as an approximate map endpoint within the scholarly range 1591–94. Encyclopaedia Judaica biography

ר׳ יהודה ליווא בן בצלאל.event: ר׳ יהודה ליווא בן בצלאל is born approximately in the second decade of the sixteenth century, probably in Poznań; sources range from about 1512 to 1525. See the Jewish Encyclopedia and Encyclopaedia Judaica.
ר׳ יהודה ליווא בן בצלאל becomes Landesrabbiner of Moravia at Nikolsburg, directing communal governance and patterns of Talmud study. See the Jewish Encyclopedia.

After leaving the Moravian chief rabbinate, ר׳ יהודה ליווא בן בצלאל settles in Prague, founds the Klaus yeshiva and organizes communal institutions and Mishnah-study societies. See Encyclopaedia Judaica.
Passed over for Prague’s chief rabbinate, ר׳ יהודה ליווא בן בצלאל accepts a call to his native Poznań. See the Jewish Encyclopedia.
ר׳ יהודה ליווא בן בצלאל returns to Prague as rabbi and renews his communal and educational leadership. See the Jewish Encyclopedia.
On 23 February 1592, ר׳ יהודה ליווא בן בצלאל receives an audience with Emperor Rudolf II at Prague Castle; the subject is not securely recorded. See the Jewish Encyclopedia.
Later in 1592, ר׳ יהודה ליווא בן בצלאל returns to Poznań as chief rabbi and writes major ethical works there. See the Jewish Encyclopedia.
By about 1597, ר׳ יהודה ליווא בן בצלאל returns to Prague as chief rabbi and begins the final, exceptionally productive publishing period of his life. See the Jewish Encyclopedia.
ר׳ יהודה ליווא בן בצלאל dies in Prague in 1609 and is buried in the Old Jewish Cemetery. Later Golem stories are literary legend rather than documented biography. See the Jewish Encyclopedia.

ר׳ שמואל יהודה קצנלנבוגן.event: ר׳ שמואל יהודה קצנלנבוגן is born in Padua in 1521 to ר׳ מאיר קצנלנבוגן and Hannah, a descendant of ר׳ יהודה מינץ. See the Jewish Museum of Padua and Posen Library.
As a young scholar, ר׳ שמואל יהודה קצנלנבוגן studies and works alongside his father, the מהר״ם מפדובה. The year is approximate. See Posen Library.

ר׳ שמואל יהודה קצנלנבוגן contributes annotations to the Venice edition of Maimonides’ משנה תורה; this is a documented scholarly association with the edition, not necessarily a permanent move. See the bibliographical biography.
After his father’s death, ר׳ שמואל יהודה קצנלנבוגן is elected rabbi of Venice and becomes an influential teacher and communal authority. See Posen Library.
A pupil publishes the twelve sermons of ר׳ שמואל יהודה קצנלנבוגן in Venice. See the National Library of Israel.
ר׳ שמואל יהודה קצנלנבוגן dies on 25 March 1597 and is buried in Padua; ר׳ יהודה אריה ממודנה delivers his funeral oration. See the Jewish Museum of Padua.

ר׳ משה קורדובירו.event: ר׳ משה קורדובירו is born in 1522. His birthplace is not securely known; Safed is shown as the earliest documented setting of a life spent almost entirely there, not as a precise birthplace claim. See Encyclopaedia Judaica and the Jewish Encyclopedia.

At age twenty, ר׳ משה קורדובירו begins intensive Kabbalah study under his brother-in-law ר׳ שלמה הלוי אלקבץ, while remaining a halakhic student of ר׳ יוסף קארו. See Encyclopaedia Judaica and the Jewish Virtual Library.
ר׳ משה קורדובירו completes פרדס רימונים, his systematic synthesis of the major earlier schools of Kabbalah. See Encyclopaedia Judaica and the National Library of Israel.
By mid-century, ר׳ משה קורדובירו serves Safed as a dayan and rosh yeshiva and leads a circle of kabbalistic students. The displayed year is approximate. See the Jewish Virtual Library.
About a decade after פרדס רימונים, ר׳ משה קורדובירו completes אילימה רבתי and continues his extensive אור יקר commentary on the Zohar. See Encyclopaedia Judaica.
ר׳ משה קורדובירו dies in Safed on 25 June 1570. ר׳ יצחק לוריא had arrived shortly before his death and is remembered as one of his final students. See the Jewish Encyclopedia.

ר׳ גדליה בן יוסף אבן יחיא.event: ר׳ גדליה בן יוסף אבן יחיא is born at Imola in 1526 according to modern authority data; older sources give 1515. See Posen Library and Encyclopaedia Judaica.
As a young scholar, ר׳ גדליה בן יוסף אבן יחיא studies in Ferrara. The year is approximate. See the biographical chronology.
At Ravenna, ר׳ גדליה בן יוסף אבן יחיא begins composing the chronicle that becomes שלשלת הקבלה. See the Revue des Études Juives study.
ר׳ גדליה בן יוסף אבן יחיא resides in Rovigo until the anti-Talmud campaign of 1562 disrupts his life. The displayed year marks this established period. See the biographical account.
After the burning and suppression of the Talmud in Italy, ר׳ גדליה בן יוסף אבן יחיא briefly relocates to Salonika. See the documented itinerary.
ר׳ גדליה בן יוסף אבן יחיא returns to Imola in 1567, but papal expulsion policies soon force renewed migration. See the biographical chronology.
Expelled with other Jews under Pope Pius V and suffering major financial loss, ר׳ גדליה בן יוסף אבן יחיא moves to Pesaro. The year is approximate. See the biographical account.
ר׳ גדליה בן יוסף אבן יחיא returns to Ferrara, remaining there until about 1575 before further wandering. See the biographical chronology.
ר׳ גדליה בן יוסף אבן יחיא completes שלשלת הקבלה and dies in 1587, probably at Alessandria in northern Italy rather than Alexandria in Egypt. See the German biographical assessment and Posen Library.

ר׳ מרדכי בן אברהם יפה.event: ר׳ מרדכי בן אברהם יפה is born in Prague around 1530 to a distinguished rabbinic family. YIVO notes 1525 or 1530; the conventional 1530 is used here. See the YIVO Encyclopedia.

ר׳ מרדכי בן אברהם יפה.place: Poland, principally Kraków and Lublin; approximate study period
ר׳ מרדכי בן אברהם יפה.event: As a young scholar, ר׳ מרדכי בן אברהם יפה studies under ר׳ משה איסרליש and ר׳ שלמה לוריא and learns Kabbalah from ר׳ מתתיהו דלקרוט. The marker uses Kraków as the strongest institutional anchor while acknowledging study across the Polish scholarly network. See YIVO.
ר׳ מרדכי בן אברהם יפה becomes head of a Prague yeshiva in 1553, beginning his public teaching career. See the YIVO chronology.

When Emperor Ferdinand expels the Jews of Bohemia in 1561, ר׳ מרדכי בן אברהם יפה leaves Prague for Venice. During approximately ten years there he studies astronomy, philosophy, calendar science and Kabbalah, disciplines later incorporated into his writings. See YIVO and the referenced chronology.

ר׳ מרדכי בן אברהם יפה.place: Grodno, Grand Duchy of Lithuania; now Belarus
ר׳ מרדכי בן אברהם יפה.event: After returning from Italy, ר׳ מרדכי בן אברהם יפה becomes rabbi of Grodno. Standard chronologies differ slightly over the dates of his Polish-Lithuanian pulpits, so this record preserves their sequence without assigning simultaneous offices. See YIVO and the Hebrew biography.
ר׳ מרדכי בן אברהם יפה moves to the Kremenets rabbinate around 1587 after leaving Grodno. See the cross-referenced chronology and YIVO.

ר׳ מרדכי בן אברהם יפה serves as rabbi and rosh yeshiva in Lublin and participates in intercommunal leadership. The first two parts of his לבושים are printed there in 1590. See the Library of Congress Hebrew-book finding aid and YIVO.
ר׳ מרדכי בן אברהם יפה returns to Prague in 1592 and succeeds ר׳ יהודה ליווא בן בצלאל as the city’s rabbi. See the YIVO biography and Hebrew Yeshiva encyclopedia.
ר׳ מרדכי בן אברהם יפה moves to Poznań in 1599, again following ר׳ יהודה ליווא בן בצלאל, and serves as chief rabbi for the rest of his life. See YIVO.

ר׳ מרדכי בן אברהם יפה dies in Poznań on 7 March 1612, 3 Adar II 5372, after thirteen years as the community’s chief rabbi. A surviving fragment of his tombstone has been identified despite destruction of the cemetery. See the YIVO chronology and the Hebrew tombstone account.

ר׳ משה איסרליש.event: ר׳ משה איסרליש is born around 1530 in Kraków to ר׳ ישראל איסרל, a wealthy scholar and communal notable. YIVO Encyclopedia
As a young scholar, ר׳ משה איסרליש studies in the celebrated yeshiva of ר׳ שלום שכנא, absorbing the Ashkenazi legal tradition that later shapes his codification. Menachem Elon biography
By about age twenty, ר׳ משה איסרליש returns to Kraków, serves as rabbi and dayan, and heads a yeshiva whose students carry his rulings throughout central and eastern Europe. Menachem Elon biography

The synagogue founded by his father and associated with ר׳ משה איסרליש is established in Kazimierz; it becomes the institutional centre of his teaching and enduring local memorial. Wikimedia Commons synagogue record
The glosses of ר׳ משה איסרליש, known as המפה, are printed with שולחן ערוך, embedding Ashkenazi rulings and customs within the code of ר׳ יוסף קארו. YIVO Encyclopedia

ר׳ משה איסרליש dies in Kraków on 18 Iyar 5332, corresponding to 10–11 May 1572, and is buried in the Remuh Cemetery beside the synagogue bearing his name. Wikimedia Commons authority and grave collection

ר׳ יצחק לוריא אשכנזי.event: ר׳ יצחק לוריא אשכנזי is born in Jerusalem in 1534 to an Ashkenazi father and a Sephardi mother. Referenced biographical synthesis
After his father’s death, ר׳ יצחק לוריא אשכנזי moves with his mother to Cairo and is raised in the household of his wealthy maternal uncle Mordecai Frances. Referenced biographical synthesis

ר׳ יצחק לוריא אשכנזי studies Talmud and halakhah in the Egyptian scholarly world, notably under ר׳ בצלאל אשכנזי, while his surviving signature appears in a legal document of this period. Wikimedia Commons manuscript record

According to the early biographical tradition, ר׳ יצחק לוריא אשכנזי spends extended periods in seclusion near the Nile studying the Zohar and developing his mystical discipline; the year is representative rather than exact. Referenced biographical synthesis
ר׳ יצחק לוריא אשכנזי returns to the Land of Israel and spends a short period in Jerusalem before moving north to Safed. Referenced biographical synthesis

Settling in Safed, ר׳ יצחק לוריא אשכנזי joins the city’s kabbalistic culture, encounters ר׳ משה קורדובירו, and begins teaching the disciples who preserve Lurianic Kabbalah. Referenced biographical synthesis
ר׳ יצחק לוריא אשכנזי teaches a close circle headed by ר׳ חיים ויטאל, transmitting the doctrines and prayer practices later organized as the כתבי האר״י. Wikimedia Commons record of the Ari synagogue
ר׳ יצחק לוריא אשכנזי dies during an epidemic on 5 Av 5332, corresponding to 5 August 1572, and is buried in Safed’s ancient Jewish cemetery. Referenced date and burial biography

ר׳ דוד בן שלמה גנז.event: ר׳ דוד בן שלמה גנז is born in Lippstadt in 1541, a year he records himself. See the Biographical Dictionary of the Czech Lands.

ר׳ דוד בן שלמה גנז.place: Frankfurt am Main, Holy Roman Empire
ר׳ דוד בן שלמה גנז.event: During his youth, ר׳ דוד בן שלמה גנז studies Talmud in Bonn and Frankfurt. The year is approximate. See Deutsche Biographie.
ר׳ דוד בן שלמה גנז studies in the academy of ר׳ משה איסרליש in Kraków. The year is approximate. See Deutsche Biographie.
ר׳ דוד בן שלמה גנז settles in Prague and studies with ר׳ סיני בן בצלאל and the מהר״ל. See the Czech scholarly biography.

During a brief stay in Nordheim with his father-in-law, ר׳ דוד בן שלמה גנז studies Euclid and deepens his mathematical work. The date is approximate. See the Biographical Dictionary of the Czech Lands.
ר׳ דוד בן שלמה גנז publishes צמח דוד in Prague, creating a major Hebrew synthesis of Jewish and general chronology. See Deutsche Biographie.

In Rudolfine Prague, ר׳ דוד בן שלמה גנז engages contemporary astronomy in the milieu of Tycho Brahe and Johannes Kepler. The year represents his mature scientific activity. See the Cambridge scholarly study.
ר׳ דוד בן שלמה גנז dies in Prague on 25 August 1613 and is buried in the Old Jewish Cemetery. See the Czech scholarly biography.

ר׳ חיים ויטאל.event: ר׳ חיים ויטאל is born in Safed around 1 Cheshvan 5303 (1542; some older references print 1543) to Joseph Vital Calabrese, a scribe whose family came from Calabria in southern Italy. See the Encyclopaedia Judaica-derived biography and המכלול.

As a youth, ר׳ חיים ויטאל studies halakhah and Talmud in the academy of ר׳ משה אלשיך. He later enters the kabbalistic world associated with ר׳ משה קורדובירו and briefly pursues alchemy and other esoteric disciplines, which he subsequently regrets. See החכם היומי and the scholarly encyclopedia account.

When ר׳ יצחק לוריא settles in Safed, ר׳ חיים ויטאל becomes his principal disciple. For nearly two years he listens to, questions and records the האר״י's teachings on creation, divine emanation, exile, prayer, souls and reincarnation. See the Encyclopaedia Judaica account and Chabad's biography of the האר״י.

After the death of ר׳ יצחק לוריא in 1572, ר׳ חיים ויטאל organizes a circle that receives the master's teachings through him and begins the long work of arranging his notes. Other disciples, including ר׳ יוסף אבן טבול and ר׳ ישראל סרוג, do not accept his exclusive authority, producing competing channels of transmission. See המכלול and the scholarly biography.

ר׳ חיים ויטאל.place: Egypt and Ein al-Zeitun, Ottoman Empire
ר׳ חיים ויטאל.event: After a period in Egypt, ר׳ חיים ויטאל returns to Ottoman Palestine in 1577, visiting Ein al-Zeitun north of Safed before continuing to Jerusalem. The evidence supports travel through these places but not a long Egyptian rabbinate. See the referenced multilingual chronology and החכם היומי.

ר׳ חיים ויטאל establishes himself in Jerusalem, where he teaches and leads a yeshivah for roughly eight years while continuing to organize the Lurianic corpus. Later stories connect his departure with pressure from the Ottoman governor over a legendary opening of the Gihon; that supernatural framing is tradition rather than independently verifiable political documentation. See החכם היומי and the German biographical chronology.

Around 1585, ר׳ חיים ויטאל leaves Jerusalem for Damascus amid conflict with local Ottoman authority. This first Damascene stay is brief, because he returns to Safed the following year. See החכם היומי and המכלול.

ר׳ חיים ויטאל returns to Safed in 1586. During this later Safed period he receives rabbinic ordination from his former teacher ר׳ משה אלשיך and suffers a prolonged illness; copies of portions of his guarded manuscripts circulate without his full control. Sources differ on whether the ordination occurred immediately or closer to 1590–1594. See המכלול and the Encyclopedia of Religion account.

Around 1594, ר׳ חיים ויטאל settles permanently in Damascus. He teaches Kabbalah, gathers a restricted circle of students and is associated with the Sicilian Jewish congregation, while continuing to revise his writings and dream diary. See the history of Damascus Jewry and the referenced biography.

ר׳ חיים ויטאל dies in Damascus in 1620, traditionally on 30 Nisan 5380, while reportedly preparing to return to Safed. He is traditionally buried in Damascus's old Jewish cemetery. A later claim that his remains were secretly transferred to Israel has not been demonstrated, so the map retains Damascus as the historical burial place. See the Jewish Encyclopedia and the burial-tradition assessment.

ר׳ אברהם די בוטון.event: ר׳ אברהם די בוטון is born about the middle of the 1540s in Salonica to the rabbinic scholar ר׳ משה די בוטון. The year is approximate. Encyclopaedia Judaica biography
ר׳ אברהם די בוטון studies at the yeshiva of ר׳ שמואל די מדינה together with ר׳ מרדכי קלעי, entering Salonica’s leading circle of halakhic scholarship. Encyclopaedia Judaica biography

Following publication of כסף משנה by ר׳ יוסף קארו, ר׳ אברהם די בוטון reshapes לחם משנה so that it records his independent innovations and carefully notes agreements and differences. Encyclopaedia Judaica biography

By the early 1590s ר׳ אברהם די בוטון serves as rabbi of Salonica’s wealthy Apulian congregation, leads a Talmudic academy, and answers legal questions from across the Sephardi diaspora. Encyclopaedia Judaica biography

A later biographical chronology places ר׳ אברהם די בוטון in the Land of Israel in 1601; this brief late-life stage is less secure than his Salonikan career and is marked as approximate. Biographical chronology and references
ר׳ אברהם די בוטון is reported at Constantinople in 1603, the last dated notice associated with his life. Biographical chronology and references

ר׳ אברהם די בוטון dies during a plague sometime between 1603 and 1609; 1605 is used only as a map midpoint. His לחם משנה, first printed at Venice in 1604, becomes a standard commentary on משנה תורה. Encyclopaedia Judaica biography

ר׳ מנחם עזריה מפאנו.event: ר׳ מנחם עזריה מפאנו is born in 1548, conventionally at Fano; one Hebrew authority tradition gives Bologna. See Treccani and the National Library of Israel.
As a young scholar, ר׳ מנחם עזריה מפאנו studies in Ferrara under ר׳ ישמעאל חנינא of Valmontone. The year is approximate. See the Encyclopaedia Judaica account.
Following the destructive 1570 earthquake, ר׳ מנחם עזריה מפאנו and his brothers assist victims; his wealth also supports Jewish scholarship and printing. See the Encyclopaedia Judaica biography.
ר׳ מנחם עזריה מפאנו takes responsibility for helping publish ר׳ יוסף קארו’s כסף משנה, sent to Mantua shortly before Karo’s death. See the biographical account.

ר׳ מנחם עזריה מפאנו.place: Reggio Emilia, Duchy of Modena and Reggio
ר׳ מנחם עזריה מפאנו.event: During his mature career, ר׳ מנחם עזריה מפאנו is active in Reggio as a teacher, decisor and transmitter of Kabbalah. The displayed year is approximate. See the Encyclopaedia Judaica account.

The responsa of ר׳ מנחם עזריה מפאנו are printed in Venice, reflecting his standing throughout Italian Jewry; this is a publication event, not proof of permanent residence. See the bibliographic biography.
ר׳ מנחם עזריה מפאנו dies in Mantua on 4 Av 5380 (1620). See the National Library of Israel and Treccani.

ר׳ שלמה אפרים מלונטשיץ.event: ר׳ שלמה אפרים מלונטשיץ is born around 1550 in Łęczyca, the Polish town from which the name Luntschitz derives. The National Library authority record identifies him as ר׳ שלמה אפרים בן ר׳ אהרן לונטשיץ. See the National Library of Israel, the Jewish Encyclopedia and the modern biographical synthesis in Shlomo Ephraim Luntschitz.

As a young scholar, ר׳ שלמה אפרים מלונטשיץ studies in Lublin under ר׳ שלמה לוריא (מהרש״ל), whose disciplined Talmudic and textual approach forms an important part of his intellectual background. The displayed year is approximate because the sources preserve the relationship but not an enrollment date. See the biographical summary and the scholarly study cited there, Leonard Levin’s Seeing with Both Eyes.

By this period, ר׳ שלמה אפרים מלונטשיץ is established as a preacher and scholar and serves as rosh yeshiva in Lviv. His first major work, עיר גיבורים, is printed at Basel in 1580; the printing location is not treated as proof that he personally resided in Basel. See the Jewish Encyclopedia and the modern biographical summary.

ר׳ שלמה אפרים מלונטשיץ publishes עוללות אפרים, four parts of biblical and Talmudic ethical sermons, at Lublin in 1590. אורח לחיים follows there in 1595, confirming his growing reputation as a moralist and public preacher. See the detailed bibliography in the Jewish Encyclopedia.

During a life-threatening illness, the name שלמה is added to אפרים. In his introduction to כלי יקר, ר׳ שלמה אפרים מלונטשיץ relates this naming episode. The year follows the traditional chronology and is retained as approximate. See the Hebrew biographical account and the modern summary.

ר׳ שלמה אפרים מלונטשיץ publishes כלי יקר on the Pentateuch at Lublin. Its fusion of textual exegesis, midrash, ethical teaching and critique of communal failings makes it his defining work and a lasting component of מקראות גדולות. See the digitized bibliographical record at the National Library of Israel and the Jewish Encyclopedia.

ר׳ שלמה אפרים מלונטשיץ is appointed rabbi and leading preacher in Prague after having served as rosh yeshiva in Lviv. He remains a central rabbinic figure there for the rest of his life, in the intellectual world shaped by ר׳ יהודה ליווא בן בצלאל (מהר״ל). See the Jewish Encyclopedia and the modern biographical synthesis.

In Prague, ר׳ שלמה אפרים מלונטשיץ publishes שפתי דעת, extending the homiletical project of כלי יקר. The following year he composes penitential liturgical poems commemorating the community’s deliverance after hostile forces entered Prague on 2 Adar 1611. See the bibliography and historical note in the Jewish Encyclopedia.

ר׳ שלמה אפרים מלונטשיץ publishes עמודי שש, a collection of sermons that includes forceful criticism of sterile pilpul and educational priorities detached from ethical transformation. See the Jewish Encyclopedia and the work summary.

ר׳ שלמה אפרים מלונטשיץ dies in Prague on Thursday, 7 Adar 5379 and is buried in the Old Jewish Cemetery. The gravestone date corresponds to 21 February 1619 Gregorian; the Jewish Encyclopedia’s 3 March reflects the contemporary calendar difference. See the gravestone-based date discussion, the Jewish Encyclopedia and the National Library authority record.

ר׳ שמואל אליעזר הלוי איידלס.event: ר׳ שמואל אליעזר הלוי איידלס is born in 1555. The Jewish Encyclopedia gives Poznań, while other traditions give Kraków or nearby Kazimierz; Poznań is used as the canonical anchor and the disagreement is retained. See the Jewish Encyclopedia and Daat’s Hebrew biography.

With the financial support of his mother-in-law Edel, ר׳ שמואל אליעזר הלוי איידלס directs a large yeshiva in Poznań from about 1585. He adopts the name Eidels in acknowledgement of her sustained support for the scholars. See the Jewish Encyclopedia biography.

At a rabbinic gathering during the Lublin fair, ר׳ שמואל אליעזר הלוי איידלס signs a decree opposing the use of money to obtain rabbinic appointments, demonstrating his recognized standing before holding his later communal pulpits. See Daat and the Jewish Encyclopedia.
After the closure of the Poznań academy, ר׳ שמואל אליעזר הלוי איידלס becomes rabbi of Chełm in 1610 and serves there until his call to Lublin. See the contemporary-reference biography.

ר׳ שמואל אליעזר הלוי איידלס is elected rabbi and rosh yeshiva of Lublin in 1614, directing one of Polish Jewry’s major academies while continuing publication of his Talmudic novellae. See the Jewish Encyclopedia and Hebrew biography.

After Lublin, ר׳ שמואל אליעזר הלוי איידלס serves as rabbi in Tykocin before his final move to Ostroh. The surviving standard biographies establish the sequence but not an exact installation year; 1618 is an approximate transition marker. See the Jewish Encyclopedia chronology.
By the mid-1620s, ר׳ שמואל אליעזר הלוי איידלס is rabbi and rosh yeshiva of Ostroh, his final and enduring communal centre. See the Jewish Encyclopedia and the Hebrew authority page.

ר׳ שמואל אליעזר הלוי איידלס dies in Ostroh on 30 November 1631 and is buried there. His integrated halakhic and aggadic commentaries later become standard companions to the printed Talmud. See the Jewish Encyclopedia.

ר׳ יהושע פלק כ״ץ.event: ר׳ יהושע פלק כ״ץ is born in Lublin around 1555. See Encyclopaedia Judaica and the Lublin community biography.
As a young scholar, ר׳ יהושע פלק כ״ץ studies in the circles of ר׳ משה איסרליש and ר׳ שלמה לוריא. The year is approximate. See Encyclopaedia Judaica.
ר׳ יהושע פלק כ״ץ settles in Lemberg and heads a yeshiva supported by Joseph Edels. The exact starting year is uncertain. See Encyclopaedia Judaica.
At the 1607 fair meeting of the Council of Four Lands, proposals advanced by ר׳ יהושע פלק כ״ץ receive communal approval. See the biographical summary.
ר׳ יהושע פלק כ״ץ participates in issuing a get in Vienna, provoking a celebrated halakhic controversy with major Polish authorities. See the documented biography.
ר׳ יהושע פלק כ״ץ dies in Lemberg on 29 March 1614. See Encyclopaedia Judaica.

ר׳ מאיר בן גדליה מלובלין.event: ר׳ מאיר בן גדליה מלובלין is born in Lublin in 1558 into a learned rabbinic family. Jewish Encyclopedia.
At about twenty-four, ר׳ מאיר בן גדליה מלובלין becomes head of the Lublin yeshiva, a post he holds until 1587. Encyclopaedia Judaica summary.
Before turning thirty, ר׳ מאיר בן גדליה מלובלין is appointed dayan and head of the Kraków yeshiva. His principal teacher is his father-in-law ר׳ יצחק הכהן שפירא. Jewish Encyclopedia.
ר׳ מאיר בן גדליה מלובלין becomes rabbi of Lemberg around 1595 and leads its community and academy until 1613. Encyclopaedia Judaica summary.
ר׳ מאיר בן גדליה מלובלין returns to Lublin as rabbi and rosh yeshiva. Jewish Encyclopedia.
ר׳ מאיר בן גדליה מלובלין dies in Lublin on 3 May 1616. Jewish Encyclopedia.

ר׳ ישעיהו הלוי הורוביץ.event: ר׳ ישעיהו הלוי הורוביץ was born in Prague in 1558 to ר׳ אברהם הלוי הורוביץ. See the CET biographical lexicon.
ר׳ ישעיהו הלוי הורוביץ began serving as rabbi of Dubno, one of several major communal offices he held in Poland and central Europe. See the German chronology and Daat.
ר׳ ישעיהו הלוי הורוביץ served the important community of Ostroh before moving westward. The precise opening year varies in biographical summaries. See Daat’s Hebrew biography.

ר׳ ישעיהו הלוי הורוביץ.place: Frankfurt am Main, Holy Roman Empire
ר׳ ישעיהו הלוי הורוביץ.event: ר׳ ישעיהו הלוי הורוביץ became rabbi of Frankfurt am Main and headed its yeshiva. See the German biographical chronology.
The Fettmilch uprising drove Frankfurt’s Jews into exile; ר׳ ישעיהו הלוי הורוביץ left with the community and returned to Prague, where he became a leading rabbi. See biographical account.

After his first wife’s death, ר׳ ישעיהו הלוי הורוביץ travelled through the Ottoman Empire and reached Jerusalem on 6 Kislev 5382, joining and leading its Ashkenazic community. See Daat’s dated account.
The Jerusalem pasha imprisoned ר׳ ישעיהו הלוי הורוביץ and other communal leaders for ransom. After release, he left the city. See German chronology.
After leaving Jerusalem, ר׳ ישעיהו הלוי הורוביץ passed through Safed and settled in Tiberias. The year is approximate because the final chronology is disputed. See Hebrew source-critical biography.

Traditional chronology places the death of ר׳ ישעיהו הלוי הורוביץ in Tiberias on 11 Nisan 5390 (24 March 1630), with burial near ר׳ משה בן מימון. Recent scholarship argues that he probably died in Tevet 5386, so this date is conventional rather than certain. See Hebrew source discussion and the official sacred-sites record.

ר׳ יום טוב בן משה צהלון.event: ר׳ יום טוב בן משה צהלון is born around 1559. His exact birthplace is unknown, so Safed—his earliest securely documented scholarly home—is used only as a regional approximation. See the biographical summary and Encyclopaedia Judaica.
As a young scholar, ר׳ יום טוב בן משה צהלון studies under ר׳ משה מטראני and ר׳ משה אלשיך and receives semikhah from the Alshich. The year is approximate. See Yom Tov Tzahalon.
At about twenty-five, ר׳ יום טוב בן משה צהלון is asked by ר׳ שמואל יפה of Constantinople to rule on a difficult case, demonstrating his early halakhic authority. See the documented biography.

In a dispute between Jerusalem’s Sephardi and Ashkenazi congregations, ר׳ יום טוב בן משה צהלון rules for the Ashkenazi community. The year is approximate because the surviving biographical summaries do not date the ruling. See the biographical account.
ר׳ יום טוב בן משה צהלון travels to Egypt on communal and rabbinic business. The year is an approximate map anchor; the journey, not its precise date, is documented. See Encyclopaedia Judaica.
ר׳ יום טוב בן משה צהלון is active in Constantinople during his wider Ottoman responsa and communal work. The displayed year is approximate. See Encyclopaedia Judaica.
ר׳ יום טוב בן משה צהלון dies around 1619/20; this record uses 1620. Safed is used as his final scholarly centre. See Encyclopaedia Judaica.

ר׳ יואל בן שמואל סירקיש.event: ר׳ יואל בן שמואל סירקיש is born in Lublin in 1561 into a learned family. Encyclopaedia Judaica biography

After early study with ר׳ נפתלי צבי הירש שור, ר׳ יואל סירקיש continues learning at Brest under ר׳ פייבוש, preparing for a career in communal rabbinic leadership. Biographical chronology and cited references
Following early rabbinates in several smaller communities, ר׳ יואל סירקיש serves at Belz and builds a reputation as an authoritative judge and Talmudist. Encyclopaedia Judaica biography
ר׳ יואל סירקיש holds the prestigious rabbinate of Brest-Litovsk, one of the major Torah centres of the Commonwealth. Encyclopaedia Judaica biography
ר׳ יואל סירקיש is appointed av bet din of Kraków and head of its yeshiva, the final and most influential communal post of his career. Encyclopaedia Judaica biography

Publication of בית חדש begins at Kraków. ר׳ יואל סירקיש reconstructs the sources and development of rulings in the ארבעה טורים and challenges over-reliance on abbreviated codes. Encyclopaedia Judaica biography
ר׳ יואל בן שמואל סירקיש dies on 14 March 1640 and is buried in Kraków’s Remuh Cemetery, where his grave survives. Wikimedia Commons grave record

ר׳ יאשיהו בן יוסף פינטו.event: ר׳ יאשיהו בן יוסף פינטו נולד בדמשק למשפחה יהודית ספרדית מבוססת. Jewish Virtual Library
ר׳ יאשיהו בן יוסף פינטו למד בדמשק אצל ר׳ יעקב אבולעפיה, שהסמיך אותו לרבנות; השנה מקורבת לתקופת התגבשותו כתלמיד חכם. אנציקלופדיה יהודית דעת
ר׳ יאשיהו בן יוסף פינטו השלים בדמשק את כסף נבחר, חיבור הדרשות הראשון שלו שנדפס בעיר. Jewish Virtual Library
ר׳ יאשיהו בן יוסף פינטו שהה בירושלים וקיבל שם מר׳ יעקב אבולעפיה סמיכה המשתייכת למסורת הסמיכה הצפתית; התאריך בקירוב. אנציקלופדיה יהודית דעת
ר׳ יאשיהו בן יוסף פינטו פעל תקופה בחלב כדרשן וכמנהיג תורני לפני שחזר לדמשק; מועד השהות המדויק אינו מוסכם. Jewish Virtual Library
ר׳ יאשיהו בן יוסף פינטו עבר לצפת בכוונה להשתקע בה והמשיך שם בעבודתו הספרותית. אנציקלופדיה יהודית דעת
לאחר פטירת בנו הצעיר ר׳ יוסף בצפת שב ר׳ יאשיהו בן יוסף פינטו לדמשק וקיבל את הנהגת הקהילה לאחר ר׳ חיים ויטאל. Jewish Virtual Library
ר׳ יאשיהו בן יוסף פינטו נפטר בדמשק בחודש אדר ת״ח (פברואר–מרץ 1648), לאחר שכיהן כרבה של העיר. Jewish Virtual Library

ר׳ יום טוב ליפמן הלר.event: ר׳ יום טוב ליפמן הלר is born at Wallerstein in 1579; a scholarly Czech reference gives 1578. Encyclopaedia Judaica biography.
As a youth, ר׳ יום טוב ליפמן הלר studies in Friedberg under ר׳ יעקב גינצבורג before continuing to Prague. Jewish Virtual Library.
At about eighteen, ר׳ יום טוב ליפמן הלר, a disciple of ר׳ יהודה ליווא בן בצלאל, is appointed a dayan in Prague and begins twenty-eight years of judicial service. Encyclopaedia Judaica.
ר׳ יום טוב ליפמן הלר begins publishing תוספות יום טוב on the Mishnah in Prague; the first edition appears in parts from 1614 to 1617. Joseph M. Davis, Yom-Tov Lipmann Heller.
ר׳ יום טוב ליפמן הלר is called to the rabbinate of Mikulov in October 1624. Czech Biographical Dictionary.
ר׳ יום טוב ליפמן הלר becomes av bet din of Vienna and helps establish a centralized Jewish community in Leopoldstadt. Encyclopaedia Judaica.
ר׳ יום טוב ליפמן הלר returns as chief rabbi of Prague. Accusations arising from communal conflict and taxation soon place him in grave danger. Czech Biographical Dictionary.
Imperial authorities imprison ר׳ יום טוב ליפמן הלר in Vienna in 1629; his death sentence is commuted, but he pays a heavy fine and loses office. He recounts the ordeal in מגילת איבה. ANU Museum.
After leaving the Habsburg lands, ר׳ יום טוב ליפמן הלר moves into Poland, residing first in Lublin and subsequently in Brest-Litovsk and Nemyriv. Encyclopaedia Judaica.
ר׳ יום טוב ליפמן הלר becomes rabbi of Volodymyr, serving there for approximately a decade. ANU Museum.
ר׳ יום טוב ליפמן הלר is called to Kraków, where he serves as rabbi, revises תוספות יום טוב, and later heads the yeshiva. Encyclopaedia Judaica.
ר׳ יום טוב ליפמן הלר dies in Kraków in 1654 and is buried in the historic Jewish cemetery. Czech Biographical Dictionary.

ר׳ נתן נטע שפירא.event: ר׳ נתן נטע שפירא is born in Kazimierz around 1585 into a prominent rabbinic family. UCL doctoral research.

As a young scholar, ר׳ נתן נטע שפירא becomes associated with the Kraków–Lublin rabbinic world and is traditionally counted among the pupils of ר׳ מאיר בן גדליה מלובלין; the year is approximate. YIVO Encyclopedia.
At about thirty-two, ר׳ נתן נטע שפירא becomes head of the Talmudic academy in Kazimierz and a leading rabbinical judge. Museum of Kraków study.
ר׳ נתן נטע שפירא composes the intricate kabbalistic interpretations later published as מגלה עמוקות; the year is an approximate composition anchor, not a first-edition date. YIVO Encyclopedia.
ר׳ נתן נטע שפירא dies on 20 July 1633 and is buried in the Remuh Cemetery in Kazimierz. Kraków City of Literature.

ר׳ דוד הלוי סגל.event: ר׳ דוד הלוי סגל נולד בקירוב בשנת 1586 בלודמיר (וולודימיר), ווהלין; שנת הלידה והמקום מקובלים אך אינם מתועדים בתעודת לידה. Chabad biography
ר׳ דוד הלוי סגל למד במרכזי התורה של פולין ונעשה חתנו ותלמידו של ר׳ יואל סירקיש, הב״ח; השנה מסמנת בקירוב את ראשית תקופת לימודיו הבוגרת ואינה תאריך אירוע ודאי. Jewish Encyclopedia
ר׳ דוד הלוי סגל כיהן ברבנות פוטליץ בגליציה, אחת ממשרות הרבנות הראשונות המתועדות במסורת הביוגרפית שלו. Electronic Jewish Encyclopedia
ר׳ דוד הלוי סגל עבר לפוזנן ושימש בה בתפקיד רבני; התיארוך בקירוב משום שהמקורות הביוגרפיים אינם אחידים בפרטי כהונותיו המוקדמות. Jewish Encyclopedia
ר׳ דוד הלוי סגל נתמנה לרב ולאב בית דין באוסטרוה, ובה השלים את טורי זהב על יורה דעה. Chabad biography
בעת שישב באוסטרוה ראה ר׳ דוד הלוי סגל את טורי זהב על יורה דעה יוצא לאור בלובלין; מקום הדפוס אינו מוצג כמקום מגוריו. National Library of Israel catalogue
גזרות ת״ח–ת״ט החריבו את הקהילה באוסטרוה ואילצו את ר׳ דוד הלוי סגל לברוח; המקורות אינם מאפשרים מסלול פליטות שנתי מדויק, ולכן הנקודה נשארת בעיר שממנה נעקר. Jewish Encyclopedia
ר׳ דוד הלוי סגל התיישב בלבוב ונבחר לרב הקהילה; העיר נעשתה מרכז פעילותו בשנותיו האחרונות. Electronic Jewish Encyclopedia
ר׳ דוד הלוי סגל נפטר בלבוב בכ״ו בשבט תכ״ז (20 בפברואר 1667) ונקבר בבית העלמין היהודי הישן בעיר. Chabad biography

ר׳ משה רבקש.event: ר׳ משה רבקש is born around 1595; the precise year and birthplace are disputed, and Prague is reported in some modern scholarship. Dovid Katz, Lithuanian Jewish Culture.

By adulthood, ר׳ משה רבקש is established in Vilna, where he becomes a prominent Talmudist; the date marks an approximate early-career anchor rather than a documented arrival. Encyclopaedia Judaica biography.
