The capture and devastation of Vilna in 1655 forces ר׳ משה רבקש to flee together with other leading scholars. Encyclopaedia Judaica biography.

After being blocked near the Prussian frontier and travelling by sea, ר׳ משה רבקש reaches Amsterdam. The Sephardi community, through ר׳ שאול לוי מורטירה and ר׳ יצחק אבוהב דה פונסקה, helps him remain there. Encyclopaedia Judaica biography.
ר׳ משה רבקש participates in correcting the Amsterdam שולחן ערוך and contributes באר הגולה, identifying the legal sources and explaining divergent rulings. Lithuanian Jewish Culture.
After his Amsterdam exile, ר׳ משה רבקש returns to Vilna; the exact return year is not recorded, so 1667 is an approximate late-life map anchor. Encyclopaedia Judaica biography.
ר׳ משה רבקש dies in Vilna around 1671/72. Encyclopaedia Judaica biography.

ר׳ חיים בנבנישתי.event: ר׳ חיים בנבנישתי is born in Constantinople in 1603 into a prominent rabbinic family. Hakham Yomi biography.
In Constantinople, ר׳ חיים בנבנישתי studies under ר׳ יוסף מטראני and develops the broad responsa scholarship that later informs כנסת הגדולה. İzmir Jewish Heritage Project.
ר׳ חיים בנבנישתי is appointed rabbi of Tire near İzmir in 1644. İzmir Jewish Heritage Project.

ר׳ חיים בנבנישתי becomes one of the rabbis of İzmir in 1658. The same year the אורח חיים portion of כנסת הגדולה appears at Livorno; the printing place is not treated as proof of travel. İzmir Jewish Heritage Project.
During the Sabbatean crisis, ר׳ חיים בנבנישתי initially supports שבתאי צבי but reverses course after the apostasy and becomes an opponent of the continuing movement. Hakham Yomi biography.
ר׳ חיים בנבנישתי publishes שיירי כנסת הגדולה on אורח חיים at İzmir in 1671, expanding his digest of halakhic decisions and local customs. İzmir Jewish Heritage Project.
ר׳ חיים בנבנישתי dies in İzmir on 17 Elul 5433 (1673) and is buried there. Hakham Yomi biography.

ר׳ מנשה בן ישראל.event: ר׳ מנשה בן ישראל, born Manoel Dias Soeiro, is born in 1604 to a Portuguese converso family. Lisbon is the conventional map point, although La Rochelle is also reported and the birthplace remains disputed. See Encyclopaedia Judaica and the Nieuw Nederlandsch Biografisch Woordenboek.

Around 1613–1614, the family of ר׳ מנשה בן ישראל settles in Amsterdam and openly returns to Judaism. He studies with ר׳ יצחק עוזיאל and rapidly gains recognition as a preacher and scholar. See Encyclopaedia Judaica.
ר׳ מנשה בן ישראל establishes Amsterdam’s first enduring Hebrew printing press in 1626, helping make the city a major center of Jewish book production. See Encyclopaedia Judaica.
With the first part of El Conciliador, ר׳ מנשה בן ישראל reaches a wide Jewish and Christian scholarly readership and expands his international correspondence. See Encyclopedia.com.
ר׳ מנשה בן ישראל meets the former Swedish queen Christina at Antwerp in 1654 during one of his documented diplomatic and scholarly journeys. See the bibliographic discussion in Encyclopaedia Judaica.

In October 1655, ר׳ מנשה בן ישראל arrives in London, presents his Humble Addresses to Oliver Cromwell and advocates the legal return of Jews to England. The Whitehall Conference debates the proposal in December. See the Dictionary of National Biography.
While remaining in London, ר׳ מנשה בן ישראל publishes Vindiciae Judaeorum, answering anti-Jewish accusations and defending Jewish civic reliability. See the Dictionary of National Biography.

After returning from England following the death of his son Samuel, ר׳ מנשה בן ישראל dies at Middelburg on 20 November 1657. He is subsequently buried at Beth Haim cemetery in Ouderkerk aan de Amstel. See Encyclopaedia Judaica.

ר׳ יעקב ששפורטש.event: ר׳ יעקב ששפורטש is born and educated in Oran in 1610 in a distinguished Sephardi family. Encyclopaedia Judaica biography.
At twenty-four, ר׳ יעקב ששפורטש becomes rabbi of Tlemcen after earlier service on its rabbinical court. Jewish Encyclopedia.
ר׳ יעקב ששפורטש exercises rabbinic authority in Moroccan communities including Fez and Salé; the year is an approximate regional-career anchor. Jewish Encyclopedia.

After imprisonment and conflict with Moroccan authorities, ר׳ יעקב ששפורטש escapes with his family and reaches Amsterdam; sources vary between the late 1640s and early 1650s. Encyclopaedia Judaica biography.
The Moroccan ruler sends ר׳ יעקב ששפורטש on a diplomatic mission to the Spanish court seeking assistance against rebels. Jewish Encyclopedia.
ר׳ יעקב ששפורטש becomes haham of London’s young Portuguese Jewish congregation. Encyclopaedia Judaica biography.
Driven from plague-stricken London, ר׳ יעקב ששפורטש settles in Hamburg. From here he organizes his evidence-based opposition to the rapidly spreading Sabbatean movement. Jewish Encyclopedia.
ר׳ יעקב ששפורטש returns to Amsterdam to head the Keter Torah yeshiva founded by the Pinto brothers. Jewish Encyclopedia.
ר׳ יעקב ששפורטש becomes dayan and head of the yeshiva in Livorno. Jewish Encyclopedia.
ר׳ יעקב ששפורטש returns to Amsterdam and becomes head of the Ets Haim academy. Jewish Encyclopedia.
Following the death of ר׳ יצחק אבוהב דה פונסקה, ר׳ יעקב ששפורטש becomes rabbi of Amsterdam’s Portuguese community. Jewish Encyclopedia.
ר׳ יעקב ששפורטש dies in Amsterdam on 15 April 1698. Encyclopaedia Judaica biography.

ר׳ שמואל אבוהב.event: ר׳ שמואל אבוהב is born in Hamburg in 1610 into a Portuguese converso family active in establishing the city’s Jewish community. Dizionario Biografico degli Italiani.
At thirteen, ר׳ שמואל אבוהב is sent to Venice to study under ר׳ דוד פרנקו; he later marries his teacher’s daughter. Dizionario Biografico degli Italiani.
As a young scholar, ר׳ שמואל אבוהב becomes rabbi of Verona, where he develops an international reputation as a teacher and respondent; the appointment year is approximate. Posen Library biography.
From Verona, ר׳ שמואל אבוהב works to ransom Jews of Kroměříž captured by Swedish forces, illustrating his wider communal and charitable activity. Dizionario Biografico degli Italiani.
ר׳ שמואל אבוהב is called to Venice as av bet din and becomes one of the foremost halakhic authorities of Italian Jewry. Encyclopaedia Judaica biography.
ר׳ שמואל אבוהב helps interrogate נתן העזתי during his visit to Venice and actively opposes the continuing Sabbatean movement. Posen Library biography.

Around the age of eighty, ר׳ שמואל אבוהב leaves Venice temporarily under circumstances that remain unclear; the broad regional coordinate avoids inventing a specific undocumented residence. Dizionario Biografico degli Italiani.
Having returned to Venice, ר׳ שמואל אבוהב dies there on 22 August 1694. Dizionario Biografico degli Italiani.

ר׳ ישראל יעקב בן שמואל חגיז.event: ר׳ ישראל יעקב בן שמואל חגיז is born in Fez in 1620. See the Jewish Encyclopedia.
ר׳ ישראל יעקב בן שמואל חגיז reaches Italy to publish and teach, issuing תחילת חכמה at Verona in 1647. See the Jewish Encyclopedia.
During his Italian period, ר׳ ישראל יעקב בן שמואל חגיז publishes פתיל תכלת in Venice. See the works bibliography.
Supported by the Vega brothers of Livorno, ר׳ ישראל יעקב בן שמואל חגיז establishes the בית יעקב academy in Jerusalem. See the Hebrew biography.
ר׳ ישראל יעקב בן שמואל חגיז emerges as a determined rabbinic opponent of Shabbetai Tzvi and Sabbateanism. See the Jewish Encyclopedia.
ר׳ ישראל יעקב בן שמואל חגיז travels to Constantinople intending to publish לחם הפנים. See the biographical account.
ר׳ ישראל יעקב בן שמואל חגיז dies in Constantinople in 1674 before completing the planned publication. See the Hebrew biography.

ר׳ שבתי בן מאיר הכהן.event: ר׳ שבתי בן מאיר הכהן נולד באמשטיבובה (כיום מסטסיבאווה, בלארוס); מקורות אחדים מציינים את וילנה ולכן מקום הלידה אינו ודאי לחלוטין. Jewish Encyclopedia
ר׳ שבתי בן מאיר הכהן למד בטיקטין אצל ר׳ יהושע השיל בן יוסף, מן הישיבות המרכזיות בפולין־ליטא. Jewish Encyclopedia
ר׳ שבתי בן מאיר הכהן המשיך את לימודיו בקרקוב, ולאחר מכן גם בלובלין; שנת 1638 היא בקירוב בתוך תקופת לימודיו. Posen Library
ר׳ שבתי בן מאיר הכהן התיישב בווילנה לאחר נישואיו, עסק בלימוד ובהוראה ולימים ישב בבית דינו של ר׳ משה לימא. Jewish Encyclopedia
ר׳ שבתי בן מאיר הכהן השלים בווילנה את שפתי כהן על יורה דעה, שיצא בדפוס קרקוב בשנים 1646–1647; מקום הדפוס אינו מוצג כמקום מגוריו. National Library of Israel catalogue
עם כיבוש וילנה במלחמת רוסיה–פולין נמלט ר׳ שבתי בן מאיר הכהן מן העיר; הוא עבר בלובלין בדרכו מערבה. Posen Library
ר׳ שבתי בן מאיר הכהן הגיע לפראג במסגרת נדודיו לאחר נפילת וילנה, לפני שקיבל משרה במורביה. Jewish Encyclopedia
ר׳ שבתי בן מאיר הכהן שימש ברבנות שטרז׳ניצה שבמורביה. Jewish Encyclopedia
ר׳ שבתי בן מאיר הכהן נתמנה לרב הולשוב שבמורביה והנהיג בה ישיבה וקהילה עד פטירתו. Posen Library
ר׳ שבתי בן מאיר הכהן נפטר בהולשוב בכ״א באדר א׳ תכ״ב ונקבר בבית העלמין היהודי בעיר; מקורות הממירים את התאריך באופן שונה מציינים לעיתים 1663. Wikimedia Commons grave record

ר׳ משה זכות.event: ר׳ משה זכות is born around 1625 into Amsterdam’s Portuguese Jewish community and later studies under ר׳ שאול לוי מורטירה. Posen Library biography.

Seeking advanced Talmudic learning, ר׳ משה זכות studies for a period in Poland. The specific town is uncertain, so Poznań is used only as a regional approximation rather than a claimed residence. Jewish Encyclopedia.
ר׳ משה זכות begins a journey intended for the Land of Israel in 1644 but remains in Venice, which becomes the center of his rabbinic, literary and kabbalistic activity. Posen Library biography.
In Venice, ר׳ משה זכות becomes an influential transmitter and editor of Lurianic Kabbalah while serving the community as a rabbi and teacher. Jewish Encyclopedia.
ר׳ משה זכות accepts the rabbinate of Mantua in 1673 and develops a major kabbalistic study circle whose disciples include ר׳ בנימין הכהן ויטאלי and ר׳ אברהם רוויגו. Posen Library biography.
ר׳ משה זכות dies in Mantua on 1 October 1697 after more than two decades of rabbinic and kabbalistic leadership there. Jewish Encyclopedia.

ר׳ מאיר בן יהודה לייב פאפירש.event: ר׳ מאיר בן יהודה לייב פאפירש is born around 1628 into a Kraków family; recent manuscript research corrects older Prague traditions. See the Free University Berlin dissertation.

As a young scholar, ר׳ מאיר בן יהודה לייב פאפירש settles in Jerusalem and studies the manuscript legacy of ר׳ חיים ויטאל with transmitters including ר׳ יעקב צמח; the year is approximate. See the Free University research project.
Around 1649 ר׳ מאיר בן יהודה לייב פאפירש returns to Poland carrying Lurianic manuscripts, helping transmit the Jerusalem tradition to Europe. See the research project account.
ר׳ מאיר בן יהודה לייב פאפירש is again active in Jerusalem, organising Lurianic manuscripts into influential recensions; the year is approximate. See Encyclopedia.com.
ר׳ מאיר בן יהודה לייב פאפירש dies in Jerusalem in 1662. See Encyclopedia.com.

ר׳ אברהם אבלי הלוי גומבינר.event: ר׳ אברהם אבלי הלוי גומבינר is born at Gombin around 1637; sources also preserve an approximate 1635 date. Encyclopaedia Judaica biography.

After the loss of his parents during the era of the Cossack massacres, ר׳ אברהם אבלי הלוי גומבינר continues his studies in Lithuania with his relative ר׳ יעקב יצחק גומבינר. The precise Lithuanian town is not securely identified, so Vilnius is used only as a regional map approximation. Encyclopaedia Judaica biography.
ר׳ אברהם אבלי הלוי גומבינר settles in Kalisz, where he serves as dayan and head of a yeshiva; Encyclopaedia Judaica records service there from 1656. Encyclopaedia Judaica.
By about age thirty, ר׳ אברהם אבלי הלוי גומבינר has prepared the core of his commentary on אורח חיים, originally entitled נר ישראל and later famous as מגן אברהם. Jewish Encyclopedia.
ר׳ אברהם אבלי הלוי גומבינר dies in Kalisz around 1683; a competing chronology gives 5 October 1682. His son later brings מגן אברהם to print. Jewish Encyclopedia.

ר׳ יאיר חיים בכרך.event: ר׳ יאיר חיים בכרך is born in Lipník nad Bečvou in Moravia in 1638 (some sources give 1639). See the Jewish Virtual Library and Posen Library.

Around age twelve, ר׳ יאיר חיים בכרך moves with his family to Worms when his father ר׳ משה שמשון בכרך becomes rabbi of the community. The year follows the standard chronology. See the Posen Library biography.
ר׳ יאיר חיים בכרך is appointed rabbi of Koblenz in 1666 after earlier rabbinic activity associated with Mainz. See the Jewish Encyclopedia and Posen Library.
ר׳ יאיר חיים בכרך returns to Worms, where he teaches and writes, although the community later selects another successor to his father as chief rabbi. See the Posen Library.

After French forces destroy Worms in 1689, ר׳ יאיר חיים בכרך flees with his family to Metz, beginning a prolonged displacement that also takes him through Heidelberg and Frankfurt. See the Jewish Encyclopedia.

ר׳ יאיר חיים בכרך.place: Frankfurt am Main, Holy Roman Empire
ר׳ יאיר חיים בכרך.event: During the years after the destruction of Worms, ר׳ יאיר חיים בכרך lives for periods in Heidelberg and Frankfurt. Frankfurt is shown as a documented center of this unsettled decade; the exact sequence within individual years is not fully secure. See the Jewish Encyclopedia.

The restored Worms community appoints ר׳ יאיר חיים בכרך as its rabbi. In the same year he publishes חוות יאיר at Frankfurt, though the printing location is not treated as a separate journey. See the Posen Library.
ר׳ יאיר חיים בכרך dies in Worms on 1 January 1702 and is buried in the Holy Sands Jewish cemetery. See the Jewish Encyclopedia.

ר׳ שבתי משורר בס.event: ר׳ שבתי משורר בס is born in Kalisz in 1641 to ר׳ יוסף. See the Jewish Encyclopedia, the Posen Library and the POLIN Virtual Shtetl.

After his parents are killed in the 1655 persecutions at Kalisz, the fourteen-year-old ר׳ שבתי משורר בס takes refuge in Prague. He studies Talmud under ר׳ מאיר וֶרטֶרס, learns singing from ר׳ לייב שיר השירים and becomes a bass singer in the Altneuschul, the origin of the surnames Bass, Bassista and משורר. See the Jewish Encyclopedia and Posen Library.

Between 1674 and 1679, ר׳ שבתי משורר בס undertakes a sustained research journey through Jewish centres and libraries in Poland, Germany and Holland. Recorded stops include Glogau, Kalisz, Krotoszyn, Leszno, Poznań, Worms and Amsterdam. This regional marker represents an itinerary, not a permanent residence. See the Jewish Encyclopedia and Posen Library.

In Amsterdam, ר׳ שבתי משורר בס studies the crafts of Hebrew printing and proofreading. In 1680 he publishes שפתי חכמים, his explanation of רש״י on the Torah, and שפתי ישנים, the pioneering bibliography that catalogues more than two thousand Hebrew books. See YIVO Encyclopedia, Posen Library and the National Library of Israel.

After obtaining official permission, ר׳ שבתי משורר בס establishes his Hebrew press at Dyhernfurth. Its first known book appears in August 1689. The enterprise attracts Jewish compositors, correctors and craftsmen and contributes to the formation of a permanent Jewish community. See YIVO Encyclopedia, the POLIN Virtual Shtetl and the Jewish Encyclopedia.
A fire partly destroys the Dyhernfurth press, but ר׳ שבתי משורר בס and his family rebuild the printing enterprise. See the YIVO Encyclopedia.

Jesuit accusations that his publications contain anti-Christian passages lead to the arrest of ר׳ שבתי משורר בס and the confiscation of books from his press. He is ultimately acquitted, but the proceedings seriously disrupt the business. See YIVO Encyclopedia, Posen Library and the Jewish Encyclopedia.

Having returned to Poland, ר׳ שבתי משורר בס dies at Krotoszyn on 21 July 1718, corresponding to 22 Tammuz 5478. His descendants continue the Dyhernfurth printing house, while שפתי חכמים becomes a standard companion to רש״י. See the Jewish Encyclopedia, the Hebrew biographical entry and the POLIN Virtual Shtetl.

ר׳ נפתלי בן יצחק הכהן כ״ץ.event: ר׳ נפתלי בן יצחק הכהן כ״ץ is born in Ostroh around 1648. See the National Library of Israel authority record.
As a youth, ר׳ נפתלי בן יצחק הכהן כ״ץ is captured by Tatars and held for several years before escaping; Ostroh is used as the regional anchor. See the biographical account.
ר׳ נפתלי בן יצחק הכהן כ״ץ is appointed chief rabbi of Poznań. See the standard biography.

ר׳ נפתלי בן יצחק הכהן כ״ץ.place: Frankfurt am Main, Holy Roman Empire
ר׳ נפתלי בן יצחק הכהן כ״ץ.event: ר׳ נפתלי בן יצחק הכהן כ״ץ becomes rabbi of Frankfurt and begins printing סמיכת חכמים. See the first-edition catalogue documentation.

ר׳ נפתלי בן יצחק הכהן כ״ץ.place: Frankfurt am Main, Holy Roman Empire
ר׳ נפתלי בן יצחק הכהן כ״ץ.event: A catastrophic fire begins in the home of ר׳ נפתלי בן יצחק הכהן כ״ץ. He is arrested amid accusations connected with practical Kabbalah, acquitted, and compelled to leave Frankfurt. See the Hebrew biographical account.
After leaving Frankfurt, ר׳ נפתלי בן יצחק הכהן כ״ץ spends time in Prague; the year is approximate. See the biographical chronology.
While journeying toward the Land of Israel, ר׳ נפתלי בן יצחק הכהן כ״ץ dies in Constantinople in 1719. See the National Library of Israel.

ר׳ דוד ניטו.event: ר׳ דוד ניטו is born in Venice on 13 January 1654 to Pinhas Nieto. See the Posen Library biography and Encyclopaedia Judaica summary.

ר׳ דוד ניטו studies medicine at Padua and develops the scientific learning later visible in his calendrical and theological works. The year is an approximate educational marker. See the Posen Library.

In Livorno, ר׳ דוד ניטו works as physician, preacher and rabbinical judge while pursuing astronomy and calendar calculation. The start year is approximate. See Posen Library and Jewish Virtual Library.
ר׳ דוד ניטו is called as Haham of London's Spanish and Portuguese congregation and becomes the first rabbinic leader to serve at the newly built Bevis Marks Synagogue. See the Posen Library.

After controversy over his description of nature as God's governance, ר׳ דוד ניטו receives a vindicating responsum from ר׳ צבי הירש אשכנזי clarifying that his teaching affirms providence rather than independent nature. See Encyclopaedia Judaica.
ר׳ דוד ניטו publishes מטה דן, his dialogical defence of the Oral Torah, in Hebrew and Spanish. See the YIVO Online Exhibition first-edition record.

ר׳ דוד ניטו.place: Velho Jewish Cemetery, Mile End, London
ר׳ דוד ניטו.event: ר׳ דוד ניטו dies in London on 10 January 1728 and is buried in the Spanish and Portuguese congregation's Velho cemetery. See the Wikimedia authority and grave record.

ר׳ יהודה בן שמואל רוזאניס.event: ר׳ יהודה בן שמואל רוזאניס is born in Constantinople in 1657. See the Jewish Virtual Library.
ר׳ יהודה בן שמואל רוזאניס combines advanced Torah study with work in his family’s commercial house; the year is approximate. See Encyclopedia Daat.
ר׳ יהודה בן שמואל רוזאניס signs the communal ban against the Sabbatean propagandist ר׳ נחמיה חייא חיון. See the Jewish Virtual Library.
ר׳ יהודה בן שמואל רוזאניס dies in Constantinople on 13 April 1727; his writings are subsequently prepared for print by ר׳ יעקב כולי. See the Jewish Virtual Library.

ר׳ צבי הירש אשכנזי.event: ר׳ צבי הירש אשכנזי נולד בטרביץ שבמורביה בא׳ באלול תי״ח (30 באוגוסט 1658); מקורות ישנים מציעים גם 1656 או 1660. Hebrew biography
בנעוריו למד ר׳ צבי הירש אשכנזי בבודא אצל סבו ר׳ אפרים הכהן, רב העיר; השנה מציינת בקירוב את תקופת לימודיו. Jewish Encyclopedia
ר׳ צבי הירש אשכנזי למד כשנתיים בסלוניקי אצל ר׳ אליהו קובו, קיבל סמיכה ואימץ את התואר הספרדי חכם. Hebrew biography
לאחר שנמלט מן המצור על בודא התקבל ר׳ צבי הירש אשכנזי לחכם ולרב בסרייבו, ובה כיהן זמן קצר. Jewish Encyclopedia
ר׳ צבי הירש אשכנזי התיישב באלטונה ובהמשך נעשה רב שלוש קהילות אה״ו — אלטונה, המבורג וונדסבק. Jewish Encyclopedia
ר׳ צבי הירש אשכנזי נתמנה לרב הקהילה האשכנזית באמסטרדם והדפיס בעיר את שו״ת חכם צבי. Hebrew biography
ר׳ צבי הירש אשכנזי הוביל את ההתנגדות לנחמיה חייא חיון ולשרידי השבתאות; המחלוקת עם הנהגת הקהילה הביאה לפרישתו. Jewish Encyclopedia
לאחר שעזב את אמסטרדם שהה ר׳ צבי הירש אשכנזי בלונדון כאורח הקהילה הספרדית, שהכירה אותו מפסיקתו לטובת ר׳ דוד ניטו. Hebrew biography
ר׳ צבי הירש אשכנזי התקבל לרב לבוב בחורף 1718 ונפטר בעיר בא׳ באייר תע״ח (3 במאי 1718), לאחר חודשים מעטים בתפקיד. Hebrew biography

ר׳ חזקיה די סילוה.event: ר׳ חזקיה די סילוה is born in Livorno in 1659. Biographical overview.
At about twenty, ר׳ חזקיה די סילוה leaves Livorno for Jerusalem and enters the yeshiva of ר׳ משה גאלנטי, with whom he studies for approximately ten years. Biographical overview.

After the death of ר׳ משה גאלנטי, ר׳ חזקיה די סילוה succeeds him as head of the yeshiva in Jerusalem. His son’s testimony supports the role of teacher rather than the later claim that he was chief rabbi. Biographical overview and source discussion.

Traveling in Europe as a Jerusalem emissary, ר׳ חזקיה די סילוה reaches Amsterdam in 1691, declines an offer to serve its Sephardic community, and begins printing פרי חדש on יורה דעה. Biographical overview.
ר׳ חזקיה די סילוה returns to Jerusalem after his European mission and resumes teaching and halakhic writing. Biographical overview.

ר׳ חזקיה די סילוה.place: Mount of Olives, Jerusalem, Ottoman Empire
ר׳ חזקיה די סילוה.event: ר׳ חזקיה די סילוה dies in Jerusalem in 1698, aged thirty-nine, and is buried on the Mount of Olives. Biographical overview.

ר׳ אהרן אורי פייבוש הארט.event: ר׳ אהרן אורי פייבוש הארט נולד בברסלאו שבשלזיה בשנת 1670. Jewish Encyclopedia
ר׳ אהרן אורי פייבוש הארט למד בצעירותו בישיבה בפולין; מקום הישיבה ושנת ההגעה המדויקים אינם מתועדים, ולכן הנקודה היא אזורית ומשוערת. Dictionary of National Biography
ר׳ אהרן אורי פייבוש הארט התמנה לרב הקהילה האשכנזית בלונדון ושירת בבית הכנסת בדוכס פלייס; מקורות שונים מציבים את תחילת כהונתו בין 1704 ל־1706. Jewish Encyclopedia
ר׳ אהרן אורי פייבוש הארט פרסם את אורים ותומים להגנת פסיקתו במחלוקת גט; זה היה הספר הראשון שנדפס כולו בעברית בלונדון. Dictionary of National Biography
דיוקנו של ר׳ אהרן אורי פייבוש הארט נחרט בידי ג'יימס מקארדל על פי ציור של ברתולומיו דנדרידג', עדות חזותית מתוארכת מתקופת חייו. National Portrait Gallery
ר׳ אהרן אורי פייבוש הארט נפטר בלונדון בשנת 1756 לאחר כחמישה עשורים בהנהגת הקהילה. Jewish Encyclopedia

ר׳ יעקב יהושע פאלק.event: ר׳ יעקב יהושע פאלק is born in Kraków on 19 December 1680. See the Frankfurter Personenlexikon and Jewish Museum Frankfurt METAhub.
After marriage, ר׳ יעקב יהושע פאלק settles in Lviv, where his family and early scholarly career are established. See the ANU Museum database.

A gunpowder explosion destroys the family home, killing the mother, wife and young daughter of ר׳ יעקב יהושע פאלק. Rescued from the ruins, he vows to compose the Talmudic work that becomes פני יהושע. See the Frankfurter Personenlexikon and first-edition description.
ר׳ יעקב יהושע פאלק begins a sequence of local rabbinates in Tarlow, Kurow and Lesko before returning to Lviv. The year is approximate within the documented sequence. See the ANU Museum database.
ר׳ יעקב יהושע פאלק becomes chief rabbi of Lviv, succeeding the scholarly leadership associated with ר׳ צבי אשכנזי. See the ANU Museum database.
ר׳ יעקב יהושע פאלק accepts the Berlin rabbinate after leaving the troubled Lviv community. See the ANU Museum database and German biographical synthesis.
ר׳ יעקב יהושע פאלק becomes rabbi of Metz, serving until his call to Frankfurt. See Jewish Museum Frankfurt METAhub.

ר׳ יעקב יהושע פאלק.place: Frankfurt am Main, Holy Roman Empire
ר׳ יעקב יהושע פאלק.event: ר׳ יעקב יהושע פאלק assumes Frankfurt’s chief rabbinate, one of the most prestigious rabbinic offices in Europe. See Jewish Museum Frankfurt METAhub.

After opposing ר׳ יהונתן אייבשיץ in the amulet controversy and losing political support in Frankfurt, ר׳ יעקב יהושע פאלק leaves the city and stays in Worms. See German biographical synthesis and the ANU Museum database.

ר׳ יעקב יהושע פאלק.place: Offenbach am Main, Holy Roman Empire
ר׳ יעקב יהושע פאלק.event: ר׳ יעקב יהושע פאלק dies in Offenbach on 16 January 1756; he is buried in Frankfurt’s Battonnstraße Jewish cemetery. See the Frankfurter Personenlexikon and documented grave record.

ר׳ נחמן מהורודנקה.event: ר׳ נחמן מהורודנקה נולד בקירוב סביב 1680; מקום הלידה המדויק אינו ודאי, והנקודה בהורודנקה משקפת את הזיקה הגאוגרפית שבכינויו. Encyclopaedia Judaica summary
ר׳ נחמן מהורודנקה נמנה עם תלמידי החכמים של ברודי ובהמשך היה מתלמידיו הקרובים של ר׳ ישראל בעל שם טוב; השנה מציינת בקירוב את תקופת פעילותו המוקדמת. Biography with cited references
ר׳ נחמן מהורודנקה עלה לארץ ישראל בחבורה חסידית והגיע דרך נמל חיפה. Biography with cited references
לאחר הגעתו שהה ר׳ נחמן מהורודנקה בצפת לפני שהתיישב בטבריה. Biography with cited references
ר׳ נחמן מהורודנקה נפטר בטבריה בב׳ בתמוז תקכ״ה, 21 ביוני 1765 לפי המסורת המתוארכת, ונקבר בבית העלמין העתיק. Biography and burial reference

ר׳ יוסף בן עמנואל אירגאס.event: ר׳ יוסף בן עמנואל אירגאס is born in Livorno in 1685 to Sarah and ר׳ עמנואל אירגאס, a community leader. See the Hacham Yomi biography and Jewish Encyclopedia.
As a young scholar, ר׳ יוסף אירגאס studies Kabbalah intensively with ר׳ בנימין הכהן ויטאלי, a disciple of ר׳ משה זכות. The year is approximate within his early education. See Encyclopaedia Judaica.

ר׳ יוסף בן עמנואל אירגאס.place: Neveh Shalom Yeshiva, Pisa, Grand Duchy of Tuscany
ר׳ יוסף בן עמנואל אירגאס.event: After his 1704 marriage, ר׳ יוסף אירגאס settles in Pisa, establishes the Neveh Shalom yeshiva and organizes charities for poor brides and clothing the needy. See Encyclopaedia Judaica and Da'at.
Back in Livorno, ר׳ יוסף אירגאס refuses the Sabbatean ר׳ נחמיה חיון an approbation and has him expelled, beginning a bitter international pamphlet controversy. See Jewish Encyclopedia.
From Livorno, ר׳ יוסף אירגאס answers Hayyun through תוכחת מגולה and הצד נחש. Their London printing is a publication location, not evidence that Ergas travelled there. See Jewish Encyclopedia.

ר׳ יוסף בן עמנואל אירגאס dies in Livorno on 3 Sivan 5490 at about forty-five. His תלמיד ר׳ מלאכי הכהן and other editors publish the responsa and kabbalistic corpus after his death. See the Hacham Yomi biography.

ר׳ דוד אלטשולר.place: Jaworów, Polish–Lithuanian Commonwealth; now Yavoriv, Ukraine
ר׳ דוד אלטשולר.event: ר׳ דוד אלטשולר is born in 1687 at Jaworów, where he later serves as rabbi. ANU Museum biographical record

As rabbi in Jaworów, ר׳ דוד אלטשולר develops a concise explanatory commentary on the Prophets and Writings intended to make the peshat tradition accessible beyond elite libraries. ANU Museum biographical record
ר׳ דוד אלטשולר is associated with Prague as a rabbi and commentator, the source of the common designation “of Prague.” ANU Museum biographical record

ר׳ דוד אלטשולר.place: Žółkiew, Polish–Lithuanian Commonwealth; now Zhovkva, Ukraine
ר׳ דוד אלטשולר.event: The commentary project of ר׳ דוד אלטשולר begins appearing in print on Psalms, Proverbs, and Job. His son ר׳ יחיאל הלל אלטשולר subsequently completes and disseminates the work. Sefaria author and works record
ר׳ דוד אלטשולר dies in 1769. ר׳ יחיאל הלל אלטשולר carries the commentary to completion and presents it as מצודת דוד for verse meaning and מצודת ציון for vocabulary. ANU Museum biographical record

ר׳ נתנאל וייל.event: ר׳ נתנאל וייל is born at Stühlingen in 1687 to ר׳ נפתלי צבי הירש וייל, in a family tracing its rabbinic lineage to ר׳ יעקב וייל (מהרי״ו). His father and a brother are murdered in 1692. See the Jewish Encyclopedia, LEO-BW and the Hebrew biographical account.

At ten, the orphaned ר׳ נתנאל וייל is brought by his mother to Fürth, then a major centre of Jewish learning. He is soon sent onward to Prague to live with his paternal uncle. See the Jewish Encyclopedia and the Hebrew biographical account.

In Prague, ר׳ ליפמן וייל raises his nephew ר׳ נתנאל וייל. The gifted youth is admitted to the yeshiva of ר׳ אברהם ברודא, becomes his outstanding disciple, and in 1708 marries the teacher’s niece פייגלא. See the Jewish Encyclopedia and Encyclopaedia Judaica via Jewish Virtual Library.

ר׳ נתנאל וייל.place: Metz and the western German yeshiva circuit
ר׳ נתנאל וייל.event: After his marriage, ר׳ נתנאל וייל accompanies his teacher ר׳ אברהם ברודא westward and continues studying in his yeshiva. Modern accounts associate this phase with Metz and Frankfurt, while the older Jewish Encyclopedia names Mayence; the marker is therefore deliberately regional and the date approximate. Compare the Encyclopaedia Judaica summary, the Jewish Encyclopedia and the Hebrew biographical account.

Following the death of ר׳ אברהם ברודא, ר׳ נתנאל וייל returns to Prague. He serves as an assistant rabbi, leads advanced Talmud study and teaches a large body of pupils while living on a modest salary. He begins the scholarship that will become קרבן נתנאל. See the Jewish Encyclopedia, LEO-BW and the Hebrew biographical account.

Maria Theresa’s decree expelling the Jews of Prague and Bohemia uproots ר׳ נתנאל וייל. In 1745 he accepts the regional rabbinate of the Black Forest communities, headquartered at Mühringen, and writes much of his commentary on the רא״ש there. See the Jewish Encyclopedia, Encyclopaedia Judaica and Karlsruhe Stadtwiki.

ר׳ נתנאל וייל is appointed chief regional rabbi for the margraviates of Baden-Baden and Baden-Durlach, with his seat in Karlsruhe. He completes קרבן נתנאל and becomes one of the city’s most significant Jewish scholars. See the City of Karlsruhe, LEO-BW and Encyclopaedia Judaica.

ר׳ נתנאל וייל publishes קרבן נתנאל, his commentary on the rulings of ר׳ אשר בן יחיאל for orders מועד and נשים. It is the first Hebrew book printed in Karlsruhe and later enters standard Talmud editions alongside the רא״ש. See Encyclopaedia Judaica, the Jewish Encyclopedia and the history of Karlsruhe’s Jewish community.

ר׳ נתנאל וייל dies at Rastatt on 7 May 1769 (traditionally 30 Nisan 5529) while still serving as Baden’s chief regional rabbi. He is buried in Karlsruhe, where his grave survives, and his son ר׳ ידידיה טיאה וייל continues his rabbinic legacy. See the City of Karlsruhe, Jewish Community of Karlsruhe and Wikimedia Commons documentation of his grave.

ר׳ יעקב כולי.event: ר׳ יעקב כולי is born in Jerusalem around 1689. See the Hebrew biographical account.
By 1714 ר׳ יעקב כולי is in Constantinople, editing the writings of his grandfather ר׳ משה בן חביב and working closely with ר׳ יהודה רוזאניס. See the Jewish Encyclopedia.
ר׳ יעקב כולי begins publishing מעם לועז in Ladino, opening with Genesis. See the Me’am Lo’ez overview.
ר׳ יעקב כולי dies in Constantinople on 19 Av 5492, 9 August 1732, leaving מעם לועז to be continued by later scholars. See the Hebrew biography.

ר׳ יהונתן אייבשיץ.event: ר׳ יהונתן אייבשיץ נולד בשנת 1690 לפי הכרונולוגיה המקובלת; המקורות חלוקים על אתר הלידה המדויק באזור פולין. YIVO Encyclopedia
ר׳ יהונתן אייבשיץ התבסס בפראג כדרשן וכמלמד בישיבה, ובהמשך נעשה מן הסמכויות התורניות הבולטות בעיר. Das Jüdische Hamburg
ר׳ יהונתן אייבשיץ התמנה לדיין בבית הדין של פראג והמשיך להנהיג את ישיבתו. Das Jüdische Hamburg
ר׳ יהונתן אייבשיץ קיבל את רבנות מץ וכיהן בה כשמונה שנים כרב וכראש ישיבה. YIVO Encyclopedia
ר׳ יהונתן אייבשיץ נבחר לרב קהילות אה״ו—אלטונה, המבורג וונדסבק—ומיקם את מרכז הנהגתו באלטונה. YIVO Encyclopedia
באלטונה פרצה מחלוקת הקמעות סביב ר׳ יהונתן אייבשיץ והאשמותיו של ר׳ יעקב עמדין; הוויכוח התפשט ברחבי אירופה. Jewish Encyclopedia
ר׳ יהונתן אייבשיץ נפטר באלטונה ב־18 בספטמבר 1764 ונקבר בבית העלמין היהודי המקומי. Das Jüdische Hamburg

ר׳ אריה לייב גינצבורג.event: ר׳ אריה לייב גינצבורג is born around 1695 in Pinsk to ר׳ אשר גינצבורג, who serves in the Pinsk rabbinate before moving to the Minsk district. The year is approximate: major references give 1695 or 1695/96. See the YIVO Encyclopedia, ANU Museum genealogy record, and Da'at Hebrew encyclopedia.

ר׳ אריה לייב גינצבורג.place: Minsk district, Polish–Lithuanian Commonwealth; date approximate
ר׳ אריה לייב גינצבורג.event: Around 1720 ר׳ אריה לייב גינצבורג begins assisting his father ר׳ אשר after the latter's appointment over the upper Minsk rabbinical district, then encompassing numerous smaller communities. The approximate year follows the Encyclopaedia Judaica chronology. See Encyclopaedia Judaica and Da'at.

ר׳ אריה לייב גינצבורג founds and heads a yeshivah in Minsk in 1733. It attracts students from Belarus and Lithuania, while disagreement with ר׳ יחיאל היילפרין and his school develops over educational method. Later, in his own introduction to שאגת אריה, ר׳ אריה לייב distinguishes classroom sharpening from the search for halakhic truth. See Encyclopaedia Judaica and the YIVO Encyclopedia.

In 1742 ר׳ אריה לייב גינצבורג leaves his Minsk yeshivah amid the prolonged dispute surrounding its method of study. Sources say he settled in a nearby community and continued assisting his aged father, but do not securely identify a precise town; the marker therefore remains at the district centre rather than inventing a location. See Encyclopaedia Judaica and Chabadpedia's Hebrew account.

ר׳ אריה לייב גינצבורג.place: Volozhin, Polish–Lithuanian Commonwealth; now Valozhyn, Belarus
ר׳ אריה לייב גינצבורג.event: ר׳ אריה לייב גינצבורג becomes rabbi of Volozhin in 1750 and establishes a select yeshivah. Among the students associated with this period are ר׳ חיים מוולוז׳ין and his brother ר׳ שמחה. See Encyclopaedia Judaica and Da'at.

While based in Volozhin, ר׳ אריה לייב גינצבורג completes שאגת אריה, his major collection of halakhic inquiries chiefly concerning Orach Chaim. It is first printed at Frankfurt an der Oder in 1755/56. The marker remains in Volozhin because a printing city alone does not prove that the author lived there. See YIVO Encyclopedia, Jewish Encyclopedia, and Encyclopaedia Judaica.

After a period of travel, ר׳ אריה לייב גינצבורג accepts appointment as rabbi and av bet din of Metz in 1765 and heads its important yeshivah; royal confirmation follows in October 1766. A dispute over the placement of Akdamut in the Shavuot Torah reading mars his early relationship with the synagogue leadership, but he remains communal rabbi. See the Jewish Encyclopedia, French Wikipedia's sourced Metz chronology, and the regional history of the Metz rabbinate.

In Metz ר׳ אריה לייב גינצבורג publishes טורי אבן, his novellae on Rosh Hashanah, Chagigah and Megillah. By his later years his sight has failed, yet sources report that he continues lecturing with the assistance of readers and his prodigious memory. See the Jewish Encyclopedia, Encyclopaedia Judaica, and the Jewish Books bibliography.

ר׳ אריה לייב גינצבורג dies in Metz on 23 June 1785 after approximately twenty years as its rabbi. The community holds solemn funeral observances. His burial was associated with the old Jewish cemetery near today's Avenue de Blida; a modern memorial records him after the historic cemetery's destruction and reinterment history. Hebrew sources disagree whether the date was 15 or 25 Tammuz 5545. See the Jewish Encyclopedia, French Wikipedia, and the report on the old Metz cemetery memorial.

ר׳ חיים בן עטר (אור החיים הקדוש).event: ר׳ חיים בן עטר is born in Salé to ר׳ משה בן עטר and receives his earliest Torah education from his grandfather, ר׳ חיים בן עטר הזקן. See Encyclopaedia Judaica and Posen Library.

Political persecution forces the family from Salé to Meknes. The young ר׳ חיים בן עטר continues his education and learns the jewelry trade while the household stays with ר׳ משה די אבילה. See the Daily Sage archive.
After roughly three years in Meknes, the family returns to Salé, where ר׳ חיים בן עטר develops as a teacher in the Ben Attar study-house tradition. See Encyclopaedia Judaica and the Daily Sage.

Following his father-in-law's death, ר׳ חיים בן עטר faces worsening financial and legal pressures while continuing to teach. Sources vary on family details and exact timing; see Posen Library and Encyclopaedia Judaica.

While based in Morocco, ר׳ חיים בן עטר brings his Talmudic novellae חפץ ה׳ to print in Amsterdam. The publication is recorded by the Jewish Encyclopedia; the marker does not imply a documented Amsterdam visit.

Amid famine and instability, ר׳ חיים בן עטר teaches in Fez and is associated with the academy of ר׳ שמואל אלבז while preparing to leave Morocco. See the Daily Sage and Institute for Jewish Ideas and Ideals.
ר׳ חיים בן עטר passes through Algiers after leaving Morocco, an intermediate stage toward Italy and the Land of Israel. See the Daily Sage biography and scholarly overview.
ר׳ חיים בן עטר reaches Livorno, where patrons support his academy, publications and planned aliyah; he gathers the fellowship that will accompany him. See Posen Library and Encyclopaedia Judaica.

The commentary אור החיים is prepared for its Venice printing as ר׳ חיים בן עטר organizes departure from Italy. The 1742 edition is documented by the Jewish Encyclopedia. His precise physical stay in Venice is not securely dated.

ר׳ חיים בן עטר, his wives and approximately thirty disciples arrive by sea at Acre. Epidemics affecting Jaffa and Jerusalem lead the group to remain in the north. See Posen Library and the Institute for Jewish Ideas and Ideals.

During the delay in northern Palestine, ר׳ חיים בן עטר and his fellowship study among Galilean Jewish communities before moving to Jerusalem. Sources agree on an approximately year-long northern sojourn but vary over individual stops, so this marker is regional. See Posen Library.

ר׳ חיים בן עטר settles in Jerusalem and establishes מדרש כנסת ישראל for advanced revealed Torah and kabbalistic study. ר׳ חיים יוסף דוד אזולאי is among the scholars associated with his academy. See Posen Library and the Daily Sage.
ר׳ חיים בן עטר dies on 15 Tammuz 5503 (7 July 1743), aged about forty-seven, and is buried on the Mount of Olives. See Posen Library and Da'at Encyclopedia.

ר׳ יעקב ישראל עמדין.event: ר׳ יעקב ישראל עמדין is born at Altona on 4 June 1697 to ר׳ צבי הירש אשכנזי and Sarah. See the Metzler Lexicon biography and Posen Library.

ר׳ יעקב עמדין studies under his father ר׳ צבי הירש אשכנזי while the family lives in Amsterdam, absorbing his father's textual independence and opposition to Sabbateanism. See the biographical chronology.
After marriage, ר׳ יעקב עמדין lives in Brody and studies in its renowned kloyz, entering the Galician rabbinic scholarly network. See the Posen Library biography.
ר׳ יעקב עמדין becomes rabbi of Emden, the only sustained official rabbinate of his career and the source of the surname by which he is known. See the Metzler Lexicon.

ר׳ יעקב עמדין resigns the Emden rabbinate and returns to Altona as an independent scholar. He later establishes a private press, allowing him to publish without holding communal office. See Posen Library.

ר׳ יעקב עמדין begins his public campaign alleging Sabbatean formulas in amulets attributed to ר׳ יהונתן אייבשיץ, igniting a trans-European controversy. See the Posen Library and Encyclopaedia Judaica.
ר׳ יעקב ישראל עמדין dies at Altona on 19 April 1776 and is buried in the Königstraße Jewish cemetery. See the Wikimedia Commons grave record.

ר׳ ישראל בן אליעזר בעל שם טוב.place: Okopy, Podolia, Polish–Lithuanian Commonwealth; now Okopy, Ukraine
ר׳ ישראל בן אליעזר בעל שם טוב.event: According to Hasidic tradition, ר׳ ישראל בן אליעזר בעל שם טוב is born on 18 Elul 5458 (1698) at Okopy, a small fortified settlement in Podolia. Modern scholarship accepts Okopy as the likely birthplace but dates the birth only to about 1700; the displayed year is traditional, not documentarily certain. See Moshe Rosman, YIVO Encyclopedia, the National Library of Israel and the traditional Da'at entry.

During his early adult years, ר׳ ישראל בן אליעזר בעל שם טוב works in several Podolian communities, reportedly as an elementary teacher, ritual slaughterer and circumciser, while acquiring knowledge of rabbinic literature, Kabbalah and herbal remedies. The source does not provide a secure year-by-year itinerary, so 1720 is an approximate career marker rather than a claimed date of relocation. See YIVO Encyclopedia.

ר׳ ישראל בן אליעזר בעל שם טוב.place: Kuty and the southeastern Podolian–Carpathian region; date approximate
ר׳ ישראל בן אליעזר בעל שם טוב.event: In the southeastern Podolian–Carpathian region, ר׳ ישראל בן אליעזר בעל שם טוב associates with mystical and ascetic practitioners including ר׳ משה מקיטוב and learns practical as well as contemplative Kabbalah and medicinal remedies. His wife Chana is the sister of ר׳ אברהם גרשון מקיטוב. The date is approximate because the biographical source establishes the relationships but not an exact move. See YIVO Encyclopedia.

By the 1730s, while active in Podolian towns including Tłuste, ר׳ ישראל בן אליעזר בעל שם טוב is using the title baal shem or baal shem tov and gaining a reputation as a healer and spiritual intermediary. Later tradition describes a public 'revelation' around this period, but the contemporary evidence supports a gradual emergence rather than one precisely documented ceremony. See Moshe Rosman, YIVO Encyclopedia and the National Library of Israel.

ר׳ ישראל בן אליעזר בעל שם טוב.place: Medzhybizh, Podolia, Polish–Lithuanian Commonwealth; now Ukraine
ר׳ ישראל בן אליעזר בעל שם טוב.event: ר׳ ישראל בן אליעזר בעל שם טוב settles in Medzhybizh after the Jewish communal leadership provides him a house free of rent and tax. Czartoryski estate documents identify the privileged resident as a kabbalist in 1740 and subsequently as a baal shem and 'baal shem doctor,' supplying rare contemporary evidence for his residence and communal function. See YIVO Encyclopedia biography and the YIVO Medzhybizh entry.

In the famous narrative later preserved as אגרת הקודש, ר׳ ישראל בן אליעזר בעל שם טוב reports a Rosh Hashanah visionary ascent and a messianic answer linking redemption to the spread of his teachings. The text was transmitted and printed only after his death, so this event is presented as an influential attributed testimony rather than a fully secure autograph record. See Encyclopaedia Judaica and the National Library of Israel.

At Medzhybizh, ר׳ ישראל בן אליעזר בעל שם טוב leads a learned mystical circle and attracts visiting disciples including ר׳ יעקב יוסף מפולנאה, ר׳ דב בער ממזריטש, ר׳ פנחס מקוריץ and ר׳ נחמן מהורודנקה. His teachings circulate orally through this network and later appear in students' books, especially תולדות יעקב יוסף. See YIVO Encyclopedia and the Hebrew Da'at study.

ר׳ ישראל בן אליעזר בעל שם טוב dies in Medzhybizh in 1760 and is buried in its Jewish cemetery. Hasidic tradition places his death on Shavuot, usually 6 Sivan 5520; the securely documented point is the year and town. His disciples subsequently turn the Medzhybizh circle into the expanding Hasidic movement. See YIVO Encyclopedia, the National Library of Israel and the geolocated Wikimedia Commons cemetery record.

ר׳ מלאכי בן יעקב הכהן.place: Livorno, Grand Duchy of Tuscany; approximate
ר׳ מלאכי בן יעקב הכהן.event: ר׳ מלאכי בן יעקב הכהן was born in Livorno between about 1695 and 1700; the project uses 1700 as its canonical approximate year. See biographical chronology and Daat.
In Livorno, ר׳ מלאכי בן יעקב הכהן became a principal disciple of ר׳ יוסף אירגאס and studied both rabbinic law and Kabbalah. The year is approximate. See Daat’s Hebrew biography.

A responsum dated Nisan 1732 documents ר׳ מלאכי בן יעקב הכהן participating in the wider Italian halakhic network. Its reference to a Roman civil dispute is not treated as proof that he moved to Rome. See biographical and bibliographic summary.
ר׳ מלאכי בן יעקב הכהן composed שבחי תודה for a communal fast observed in Livorno on 22 Shevat. See work chronology.
The first edition of יד מלאכי, ר׳ מלאכי בן יעקב הכהן’s systematic guide to Talmudic and halakhic methodology, appeared in Livorno in 1766–1767. See Daat and bibliographic summary.

ר׳ מלאכי בן יעקב הכהן died in 1772 according to a contemporary eulogy. The precise death and burial locations are not securely known; Livorno is retained only as his last documented centre. See source discussion.

ר׳ יהודה בן שמעון אשכנזי.place: Frankfurt am Main, Holy Roman Empire; year approximate
ר׳ יהודה בן שמעון אשכנזי.event: ר׳ יהודה בן שמעון אשכנזי is born in Frankfurt am Main around 1700. The place is recorded by Encyclopaedia Judaica, but no exact birth year survives; 1700 is a transparent approximation. See Encyclopaedia Judaica and Da'at.

ר׳ יהודה בן שמעון אשכנזי.place: Tykocin, Polish–Lithuanian Commonwealth; now Poland; year approximate
ר׳ יהודה בן שמעון אשכנזי.event: By the first half of the eighteenth century ר׳ יהודה בן שמעון אשכנזי serves as a dayan in Tykocin. The appointment year is not preserved, so 1730 is an approximate career marker. See the National Library of Israel authority record and Encyclopaedia Judaica.

While serving at Tykocin, ר׳ יהודה בן שמעון אשכנזי sees his באר היטב on Orach Chaim printed at Amsterdam in 1742. The map remains at his documented residence because printing in Amsterdam does not prove physical presence there. See Encyclopaedia Judaica.

ר׳ יהודה בן שמעון אשכנזי dies in 1743 after serving as dayan and producing the digests known as באר היטב. Later printers combine his Orach Chaim and Even HaEzer work with similarly titled works by other authors. See the recorded 8 Tammuz yahrzeit and Encyclopaedia Judaica.

ר׳ יצחק ניטו.event: ר׳ יצחק ניטו נולד בלונדון בשנת 1702 כבנו של ר׳ דוד ניטו, חכם הקהילה הספרדית־פורטוגלית. National Library of Israel authority record
ר׳ יצחק ניטו התמנה לחכם קהל שער השמים בבית הכנסת בוויס מרקס. Biography citing the Jewish Encyclopedia and Bevis Marks history
ר׳ יצחק ניטו התפטר מתפקיד החכם ועזב את לונדון לתקופה; יעד מסעו אינו מתועד בבירור. Biography citing the Jewish Encyclopedia
ר׳ יצחק ניטו חזר ללונדון ועבד כנוטריון לאחר שובו. Biography citing the Jewish Encyclopedia
ר׳ יצחק ניטו הגיע מלונדון לגיברלטר, נעשה רבה הראשון של הקהילה והנהיג את קהל שער השמים; תאריך הקמת המבנה הקדום שנוי במחלוקת. Great Synagogue history and references
ר׳ יצחק ניטו שב ללונדון והתמנה אב בית דין של הקהילה הספרדית־פורטוגלית. Biography citing the Jewish Encyclopedia
ר׳ יצחק ניטו התפטר מבית הדין לאחר מחלוקת פנימית על סמכויות ותארים. Biography citing the Jewish Encyclopedia
ר׳ יצחק ניטו נפטר בלונדון בשנת 1774. National Library of Israel authority record

ר׳ דוב בער ממזריטש.place: Lokachi, Volhynian Voivodeship, Polish–Lithuanian Commonwealth; now Ukraine
ר׳ דוב בער ממזריטש.event: ר׳ דוב בער ממזריטש is born at Lokachi in Volhynia, probably around 1704, to ר׳ אברהם, a poor teacher. His birth year is not securely known: scholarly and Hasidic sources variously propose 1698, 1704 and about 1710. See the Encyclopedia of Religion and the uncertainty survey by Bar-Ilan University's Chair for Hasidism.

ר׳ דוב בער ממזריטש.place: Lwów, Polish–Lithuanian Commonwealth; now Lviv, Ukraine
ר׳ דוב בער ממזריטש.event: According to established Hasidic biographical tradition, the gifted young ר׳ דוב בער ממזריטש is sent to the Lwów yeshivah of ר׳ יעקב יהושע פאלק, author of פני יהושע. The approximate year is a map aid rather than a documented enrollment date. See the Hebrew biographical account maintained by Bar-Ilan University's Chair for Hasidism.

By early adulthood, ר׳ דוב בער ממזריטש has married at Turchyn and works as a teacher in a nearby village before serving as the town's maggid. He deepens his study of Kabbalah and adopts the severe ascetic disciplines characteristic of his early religious life. The date is approximate because the surviving sources establish the sequence but not a precise year. See Bar-Ilan's Hebrew biography and the Encyclopedia of Religion.

ר׳ דוב בער ממזריטש.place: Korets and Rivne, Volhynia; now Ukraine
ר׳ דוב בער ממזריטש.event: During the period before his Hasidic leadership, ר׳ דוב בער ממזריטש serves successively as a maggid in Korets and Rivne. His preaching ability and advanced Talmudic and kabbalistic learning become central to his public identity. The date is approximate and represents an attested career phase rather than a securely dated appointment. See Bar-Ilan University's Chair for Hasidism.

ר׳ דוב בער ממזריטש.place: Medzhybizh, Podolia, Polish–Lithuanian Commonwealth; now Ukraine
ר׳ דוב בער ממזריטש.event: Around the middle of the eighteenth century, the physically frail and intensely ascetic ר׳ דוב בער ממזריטש travels to Medzhybizh and becomes a disciple of ר׳ ישראל בעל שם טוב. The precise first-visit year is unknown. The encounter redirects his religious path toward divine immanence, joy, transformation of material life and devekut rather than bodily mortification. See the scholarly interpretation in the Encyclopedia of Religion and the Hebrew biography from Bar-Ilan University.

ר׳ דוב בער ממזריטש.place: Mezhirichi, Volhynia, Polish–Lithuanian Commonwealth; now Velyki Mezhyrichi, Ukraine
ר׳ דוב בער ממזריטש.event: After the 1760 death of ר׳ ישראל בעל שם טוב and a period of unsettled succession, ר׳ דוב בער ממזריטש becomes the central leader of most of the emerging Hasidic movement at Mezhirichi. His court trains an elite fellowship and sends disciples into Volhynia, Podolia, Poland, Galicia, Lithuania and White Russia, transforming a regional revival into a networked movement. See the Encyclopedia of Religion and YIVO's history of Mezhyrichi.

ר׳ דוב בער ממזריטש.place: Hannopil, Volhynia, Polish–Lithuanian Commonwealth; now Ukraine
ר׳ דוב בער ממזריטש.event: During the 1772 epidemic at Mezhirichi, ר׳ דוב בער ממזריטש relocates with his household to Hannopil with assistance from his disciple ר׳ משולם זושא מאניפולי. He dies there on 19 Kislev 5533—4 December Old Style / 15 December 1772 New Style—and is buried in the Hannopil Jewish cemetery. His death coincides with the first major communal bans against Hasidism. See the death chronology in the Encyclopedia of Religion, the epidemic tradition summarized in French Wikipedia, and the verified Wikimedia tomb record.

ר׳ מאיר מרגליות.event: ר׳ מאיר מרגליות is born around 1707 into the Margolies rabbinic family. The exact town and year remain uncertain, and catalogues range from about 1700 to 1708. See the Hebrew biographical synthesis and the first-edition bibliographic description.

By the early phase of his career, ר׳ מאיר מרגליות serves rabbinic communities in the Galician–Podolian region and belongs to the early circle of ר׳ ישראל בעל שם טוב. The year is approximate. See the Hebrew biography.

ר׳ מאיר מרגליות serves within Lviv's rabbinical judiciary and becomes known beyond the region through halakhic correspondence. The precise appointment sequence varies in later accounts. See the Hebrew reference biography.

A decree of King Stanisław August Poniatowski recognizes ר׳ מאיר מרגליות as rabbi of Bratslav and a wider Ukrainian rabbinic district within the Commonwealth. See the document-based Hebrew chronology.
ר׳ מאיר מרגליות assumes the Ostroh rabbinate, from which he exercises broad halakhic authority during the final years of his life. See the Meir Netivim first-edition description.
ר׳ מאיר מרגליות dies on 10 Iyar 5550 and is buried in Ostroh near ר׳ שמואל אליעזר הלוי איידלס. His sons arrange the printing of מאיר נתיבים in 1791–92. See the Hebrew biographical record.

ר׳ משה חיים לוצאטו.event: ר׳ משה חיים לוצאטו נולד בגטו פדובה בשנת 1707 וקיבל חינוך תורני וכללי רחב. Treccani
ר׳ משה חיים לוצאטו החל לתעד גילויים מיסטיים של מגיד וללמד חוג צעירים, אירוע שהצית את הפולמוס סביב פעילותו הקבלית. Jewish Encyclopedia
בלחץ רבני ונציה התחייב ר׳ משה חיים לוצאטו שלא לפרסם או ללמד את כתביו הקבליים ללא אישור ר׳ ישעיהו באסאן וסמכויות נוספות. Jewish Encyclopedia
ר׳ משה חיים לוצאטו עזב את איטליה והתיישב באמסטרדם, שם התפרנס כלוטש יהלומים והמשיך בכתיבה. Treccani
ר׳ משה חיים לוצאטו הדפיס באמסטרדם את מסילת ישרים, חיבורו המוסרי הידוע ביותר. Jewish Encyclopedia
ר׳ משה חיים לוצאטו עלה עם משפחתו לארץ ישראל והתיישב בעכו. Treccani
ר׳ משה חיים לוצאטו ובני משפחתו נפטרו בעכו במגפה, בכ״ו באייר תק״ו (16 במאי 1746); מסורת מקום קבורתו אינה ודאית. Treccani

ר׳ חיים שמואל יעקב פאלק.event: ר׳ חיים שמואל יעקב פאלק is born around 1708, probably at Fürth, although Pidhaytsi in Podolia is an important competing tradition. See the source-linked biography and Jewish Encyclopedia.

After legal danger elsewhere in Westphalia, ר׳ חיים שמואל יעקב פאלק receives protection from Count Alexander von Rantzau and performs kabbalistic and alchemical demonstrations observed at Holzminden. See the documented biographical account.
ר׳ חיים שמואל יעקב פאלק settles in London's East End and becomes known as the Baal Shem of London or Doctor Falckon. See the London biographical account.

At Wellclose Square, ר׳ חיים שמואל יעקב פאלק maintains a household and practical-kabbalistic circle. His surviving diary documents ritual activity and finances more securely than later miracle stories. See the bibliographical biography.

ר׳ חיים שמואל יעקב פאלק.place: Alderney Road Jewish Cemetery, Mile End, London
ר׳ חיים שמואל יעקב פאלק.event: ר׳ חיים שמואל יעקב פאלק dies in London on 17 April 1782 and is buried at Alderney Road. His will supports the Great Synagogue and leaves ritual objects to the community. See the biographical chronology.

ר׳ יעקב יוסף הכהן מפולנאה.place: Podolia; exact birthplace unknown (marker anchored at Shargorod)
ר׳ יעקב יוסף הכהן מפולנאה.event: ר׳ יעקב יוסף הכהן מפולנאה is born around 1710. Neither the exact year nor birthplace is securely documented; the marker uses Shargorod, his earliest documented rabbinic post, rather than claiming a birth house. See Posen Library.

While serving as rabbi of Shargorod, ר׳ יעקב יוסף הכהן מפולנאה embraces Hasidism under ר׳ ישראל בעל שם טוב; his new allegiance reportedly leads to his removal from office. The year marks the earliest securely bounded phase, not an exact conversion date. See Posen Library and Daat.
ר׳ יעקב יוסף הכהן מפולנאה begins his long period as preacher and communal rabbi in Nemyriv, lasting until 1770. See the YIVO Encyclopedia.
ר׳ יעקב יוסף הכהן מפולנאה becomes rabbi of Polonne and makes the town his final home. See Posen Library and the YIVO Encyclopedia.

His תולדות יעקב יוסף appears in print, the first printed Hasidic book and a foundational record of teachings attributed to ר׳ ישראל בעל שם טוב. The marker remains at the author’s documented residence rather than implying that he lived at the printing press. See Posen Library.
ר׳ יעקב יוסף הכהן מפולנאה dies in Polonne. Posen Library dates the death to 1783; variant dates in later references are retained in the record’s date note. See Posen Library.

ר׳ יחזקאל הלוי לנדא.event: ר׳ יחזקאל הלוי לנדא is born at Opatów on 18 Heshvan 5474 (7 November 1713) to ר׳ יהודה הלוי לנדא and חיה. He studies first with his father and local teachers. See the Jewish Museum in Prague and Daʿat.

Shortly after marrying at about eighteen, ר׳ יחזקאל הלוי לנדא enters the elite kloyz at Brody, an important center of Talmudic and kabbalistic scholarship. In 1733 he becomes head judge of one of Brody's four Jewish courts and remains in its learned circle for about thirteen years. See the YIVO Encyclopedia and Daʿat.

ר׳ יחזקאל הלוי לנדא becomes chief rabbi and head of the Talmudic academy at Yampol in Volhynia. His sermons, responsa and communal judgments establish his wider reputation. This is Yampil in present-day Khmelnytskyi Oblast, correcting the former coordinate near Lviv. See YIVO and the Jewish Museum in Prague.

From Yampol, ר׳ יחזקאל הלוי לנדא writes אגרת השלום, proposing a settlement of the divisive amulet controversy between ר׳ יעקב עמדין and ר׳ יהונתן אייבשיץ while challenging procedural defects in the testimony. See YIVO Encyclopedia and Daʿat.

Following his election in late 1754, ר׳ יחזקאל הלוי לנדא assumes office as chief rabbi of Prague in 1755 and heads its prominent yeshivah. He guides the community through the Seven Years' War, Habsburg centralization and religious controversy. See the Jewish Museum in Prague and Oxford Academic.

At Prague, ר׳ יחזקאל הלוי לנדא publishes the first edition of נודע ביהודה, named in memory of his father ר׳ יהודה. It organizes decisions from his Brody, Yampol and Prague periods. See the Jewish Museum in Prague and the original title information at Wikisource.

ר׳ יחזקאל הלוי לנדא dies in Prague on 17 Iyar 5553 (29 April 1793). In accordance with his written wishes, his grave bears a restrained stone rather than an elaborate ohel; he is buried in the Jewish cemetery on Fibichova Street in Žižkov. See Daʿat, the Jewish Museum, and the Prague cemetery guide.

ר׳ יחיא צאלח.event: ר׳ יחיא צאלח is born in Sana’a in 1713 into a learned rabbinic family. Some later summaries give 1715, but national-library authority data and the traditional chronology support 1713. See the National Library of Israel and HaMichlol’s sourced Hebrew biography.

As a young scholar, ר׳ יחיא צאלח studies with his grandfather and leading Sana’a rabbis while supporting himself as a silversmith and then a manuscript scribe. The displayed year is approximate. See HaMichlol.
Around 1756–1757 ר׳ יחיא צאלח is appointed head of Sana’a’s rabbinical court and great yeshiva, becoming Yemenite Jewry’s leading halakhic authority. See HaMichlol and the National Library of Israel.

During the 1761 persecution in which most Sana’a synagogues are demolished, ר׳ יחיא צאלח preserves communal leadership and textual tradition under pressure. See the documented overview of Yiḥyah Salaḥ and its cited Yemenite sources.
From Sana’a, ר׳ יחיא צאלח arranges for his halakhic work זבח תודה to be sent toward printing in Calcutta; this is a publication initiative, not evidence that he traveled to India. See HaMichlol.
ר׳ יחיא צאלח dies in Sana’a on 28 Nisan 5565 (27 April 1805), leaving the central halakhic and liturgical corpus of the Baladi tradition. See the National Library of Israel and HaMichlol.

ר׳ אלימלך מליז׳נסק.event: ר׳ אלימלך מליז׳נסק is born in 1717 at Łopuchowo, a small village near Tykocin in Podlasie, to ר׳ אליעזר ליפמן and his wife. Some modern summaries give Tykocin itself; the village-level identification is preserved here while acknowledging that the surviving biography is largely based on later Hasidic sources. See the Hebrew biographical study at Daʿat, the regional summary from the Foundation for the Preservation of Jewish Heritage in Poland, and the Łopuchowo geographic record.

By the mid-eighteenth century, ר׳ אלימלך מליז׳נסק and his brother ר׳ משולם זושא מאניפולי undertake a voluntary wandering exile marked by poverty, ascetic disciplines and efforts to inspire repentance. The itinerary and dates are not securely documented, so this map point represents their home region rather than an invented route. The tradition and its evidentiary limits are discussed in the Hebrew scholarly account at Daʿat.

Around the 1760s, through the influence of his brother ר׳ משולם זושא מאניפולי, ר׳ אלימלך מליז׳נסק joins the circle of ר׳ דוב בער ממזריטש at Mezhirichi. He becomes one of the Maggid's important disciples and absorbs the teaching that would underlie his later model of Hasidic leadership. The year is approximate because the sources establish the relationship but not a precise arrival date. See YIVO Encyclopedia, the Polish Jewish Heritage route, and the Hebrew study at Daʿat.

After the death of ר׳ דוב בער ממזריטש in 1772, ר׳ אלימלך מליז׳נסק settles at Leżajsk in Galicia and emerges as the central organizer of early Hasidism in Poland and Galicia. His modest court attracts disciples whom he trains to lead communities across the region, while his teaching develops the tsaddik's responsibility for both the spiritual and material needs of followers. See the scholarly entry in the YIVO Encyclopedia and the Hebrew biography at Daʿat.

ר׳ אלימלך מליז׳נסק dies at Leżajsk on 21 Adar 5547 (11 March 1787) and is buried in the town's Jewish cemetery. His son ר׳ אלעזר succeeds him locally and helps prepare his teachings for publication. The ohel over the burial place remains an identified pilgrimage site. See YIVO Encyclopedia, the Hebrew Daʿat encyclopedia, and the geotagged Wikimedia ohel record.

ר׳ משולם זושא מאניפולי.place: Galicia; exact birthplace unknown (traditional marker at Tarnów)
ר׳ משולם זושא מאניפולי.event: ר׳ משולם זושא מאניפולי is born around 1718. The exact place is not securely documented; Tarnów is used only as a traditional geographic anchor. See Posen Library.

ר׳ משולם זושא מאניפולי.place: Polish–Lithuanian Commonwealth; itinerant phase, marker at Leżajsk
ר׳ משולם זושא מאניפולי.event: ר׳ משולם זושא מאניפולי and his brother ר׳ אלימלך מליז׳נסק are remembered as travelling preachers. The route and dates are not recoverable, so this point is an approximate narrative anchor rather than a claimed residence. See Posen Library.
ר׳ משולם זושא מאניפולי studies in the circle of ר׳ דוב בער המגיד ממזריטש. The year is approximate because the sources establish the relationship but not its precise beginning. See Posen Library.
Following the death of ר׳ דוב בער המגיד ממזריטש, ר׳ משולם זושא מאניפולי settles in Hanipol and teaches there. See Posen Library.

ר׳ משולם זושא מאניפולי joins ר׳ יהודה לייב הכהן of Hanipol in an approbation for Tanya by ר׳ שניאור זלמן מליאדי, illustrating his standing among the senior Hasidic masters. See the text and date of the approbations.
ר׳ משולם זושא מאניפולי dies in Hanipol in 1800 and is buried near ר׳ דוב בער המגיד ממזריטש. See Posen Library.

ר׳ אליהו בן שלמה זלמן מווילנה.place: Sialiec near Brest, Polish–Lithuanian Commonwealth; now Belarus
ר׳ אליהו בן שלמה זלמן מווילנה.event: ר׳ אליהו בן שלמה זלמן is born on 15 Nisan 5480 (23 April 1720) at Sialiec near Brest. See the National Library of Israel and the Vilna Gaon Museum.

ר׳ אליהו בן שלמה זלמן מווילנה.place: Great Synagogue area, Vilna, Polish–Lithuanian Commonwealth
ר׳ אליהו בן שלמה זלמן מווילנה.event: As a child, ר׳ אליהו demonstrates exceptional command of rabbinic texts and delivers a public discourse in Vilna. Later miracle-like elaborations are not needed to establish the securely remembered fact of his precocity. See the National Library biography.

ר׳ אליהו studies for a period in Kėdainiai and enters a wider Lithuanian scholarly network. Lithuanian library research places him there in 1738–45, alongside years of travel. See the Wroblewski Library of the Lithuanian Academy of Sciences.

After youthful travel, ר׳ אליהו בן שלמה זלמן settles in Vilna and devotes himself to study and a small circle of disciples. He never serves as the city's official rabbi, judge or yeshiva head. See the Vilna Gaon Museum historical correction.

ר׳ אליהו בן שלמה זלמן מווילנה.place: Great Synagogue quarter, Vilna, Polish–Lithuanian Commonwealth
ר׳ אליהו בן שלמה זלמן מווילנה.event: After emissaries of the emerging Hasidic movement fail to obtain a meeting, ר׳ אליהו מווילנה becomes the authority behind organized communal bans against Hasidism. See the YIVO Encyclopedia and the National Library of Israel.

ר׳ אליהו מווילנה sets out toward the Land of Israel but turns back while still in Europe, explaining that he lacks permission from Heaven. The proposed date varies from c.1760 to 1778 or 1782; 1782 is retained only as an approximate map marker. See the National Library of Israel and the source-linked chronology of the disputed date.

Having abandoned the journey, ר׳ אליהו מווילנה returns to his family and disciples in Vilna. Later migrations of the Perushim were undertaken after his death and are therefore not plotted as his movements. See the National Library biography.

ר׳ אליהו בן שלמה זלמן מווילנה dies on 19 Tishrei 5558 (9 October 1797). His sons and disciples begin editing a vast posthumous corpus from notes and teachings. See the National Library of Israel and Vilna Gaon Museum.

ר׳ שלום מזרחי שרעבי.place: Sharʿab region, Yemen Eyalet, Ottoman Empire
ר׳ שלום מזרחי שרעבי.event: ר׳ שלום מזרחי שרעבי is born in the Sharʿab region of Yemen around 1720. A later Bet El tradition gives 1723, but international library authority records use 1720. See the National Library of Israel authority record and Encyclopaedia Judaica.

On his journey from Yemen toward Jerusalem, ר׳ שלום שרעבי passes through commercial and scholarly centres remembered as India and Baghdad. Exact dates are not documented; 1738 is an approximate route marker, not a claim of permanent residence. See the biographical tradition.

ר׳ שלום שרעבי continues through Damascus, where tradition associates him with Torah study and a halakhic discussion before his arrival in Jerusalem. The year is approximate. See the Rashash biography.

ר׳ שלום מזרחי שרעבי.place: Bet El Yeshiva, Jewish Quarter, Jerusalem
ר׳ שלום מזרחי שרעבי.event: By about 1740, ר׳ שלום שרעבי reaches Jerusalem and joins Bet El, founded in 1737 by ר׳ גדליה חיון. Devotional accounts say he first works anonymously as the caretaker while concealing his expertise. See Encyclopaedia Judaica and Bet El's institutional history.

ר׳ שלום מזרחי שרעבי.place: Bet El Yeshiva, Jewish Quarter, Jerusalem
ר׳ שלום מזרחי שרעבי.event: The Bet El fellowship binds itself through a covenant of mutual spiritual responsibility, and ר׳ שלום שרעבי emerges as the academy's central interpreter and, after ר׳ גדליה חיון, its head. See Encyclopaedia Judaica.

ר׳ שלום שרעבי signs alongside Jerusalem communal leaders on a letter authorizing emissaries to western Europe, documentary evidence of his public standing beyond the study house. See the Encyclopaedia Judaica account.

ר׳ שלום מזרחי שרעבי.place: Mount of Olives Jewish Cemetery, Jerusalem
ר׳ שלום מזרחי שרעבי.event: ר׳ שלום מזרחי שרעבי dies on 10 Shevat 5537 (18 January 1777) and is buried on the Mount of Olives. See the National Library authority record and the Wikimedia tomb record.

ר׳ צבי הירש בן אריה ליב לוין.event: ר׳ צבי הירש בן אריה ליב לוין is born in Rzeszów to ר׳ אריה ליב בן שאול and Miriam, daughter of ר׳ צבי הירש אשכנזי. See Deutsche Biographie and Jewish Encyclopedia.
ר׳ צבי הירש לוין publicly supports his uncle ר׳ יעקב עמדין in the controversy with ר׳ יהונתן אייבשיץ. See Jewish Encyclopedia.

ר׳ צבי הירש בן אריה ליב לוין.place: Great Synagogue, Duke's Place, City of London
ר׳ צבי הירש בן אריה ליב לוין.event: After election in 1756, ר׳ צבי הירש לוין arrives to lead London's principal German and Polish congregation and becomes known as Hart Lyon. See the Dictionary of National Biography.
Following a London dispute over sheḥitah supervision and the congregation's refusal to permit a public answer, ר׳ צבי הירש לוין resigns and accepts the Halberstadt rabbinate. See Jewish Encyclopedia.
ר׳ צבי הירש לוין moves to the Mannheim rabbinate before being called to Berlin. See Deutsche Biographie.
ר׳ צבי הירש לוין becomes Berlin's chief rabbi. His tenure coincides with difficult negotiations between rabbinic law, communal elites, the Haskalah and the Prussian state. See Deutsche Biographie.

The controversy over new educational proposals places ר׳ צבי הירש לוין under opposing pressures from traditional authorities and Berlin intellectuals. He attempts to resign but remains in office. See Jewish Encyclopedia.
ר׳ צבי הירש בן אריה ליב לוין dies in Berlin on 26 August 1800 after nearly three decades as chief rabbi. See the German national biographical authority.

ר׳ חיים יוסף דוד אזולאי.event: ר׳ חיים יוסף דוד אזולאי is born in Jerusalem in 1724 to ר׳ יצחק זרחיה אזולאי and Sarah, into a family descended from ר׳ אברהם אזולאי. See the National Library of Israel and the CET Hebrew biography.

As a young scholar, ר׳ חיים יוסף דוד אזולאי studies Talmud, halakhah and Kabbalah with leading Jerusalem sages, including ר׳ יונה נבון, ר׳ חיים בן עטר, ר׳ יצחק הכהן רפפורט and ר׳ שלום שרעבי. The year is a representative educational marker. See the CET and the biographical overview.

On 9 January 1753, ר׳ חיים יוסף דוד אזולאי leaves as an emissary for the Hebron community, beginning a five-year fundraising and scholarly journey. After travelling through Egypt, he sails from Alexandria toward Livorno. See the modern study of his diary and identity in Mediterranean Historical Review.

During his first mission, ר׳ חיים יוסף דוד אזולאי reaches Livorno, the port and Hebrew-printing centre that becomes the hub of his European travels and later life. From Italy he proceeds through German lands, Holland, England and France. See the scholarly journey reconstruction and Jewish Virtual Library.

ר׳ חיים יוסף דוד אזולאי.place: Frankfurt am Main, Holy Roman Empire
ר׳ חיים יוסף דוד אזולאי.event: On the German stage of his first mission, ר׳ חיים יוסף דוד אזולאי meets ר׳ יעקב יהושע פאלק, the פני יהושע, who recognizes him from earlier correspondence. See the referenced biographical synthesis and Da'at's Hebrew encyclopedia.

ר׳ חיים יוסף דוד אזולאי visits London during the west-European circuit of his first mission, raising support and examining books and manuscripts. The exact months are less secure than the overall 1753–58 journey. See the CET's Hebrew account.

After completing the first mission, ר׳ חיים יוסף דוד אזולאי returns to Jerusalem in spring 1758 with extensive notes on Jewish communities, manuscripts and libraries. See the documented journey summary in the Chida bibliographical study.

By 1764, ר׳ חיים יוסף דוד אזולאי is in Egypt; sources associate this middle period with several years of communal rabbinic service before his return to Hebron. Exact beginning and end dates vary. See the referenced biography and CET.

ר׳ חיים יוסף דוד אזולאי accepts a second major emissary mission for Hebron in 1772–73, leaving the Land of Israel for North Africa and Europe. The precise departure year is reported as 1772 or early 1773. See Jewish Virtual Library and the scholarly journey study.

On the North African leg, ר׳ חיים יוסף דוד אזולאי spends substantial time in Tunis, fundraising, teaching and recording local scholars and books. Here he learns of his first wife's death. See the bibliographical biography and referenced biography.

Arriving at Livorno in 1774, ר׳ חיים יוסף דוד אזולאי is held in quarantine for forty days and writes שם הגדולים largely from memory. He then prints its first part and the first part of ברכי יוסף. See the National Library of Israel and the first-edition record.

ר׳ חיים יוסף דוד אזולאי reaches Paris during the final west-European portion of his second mission and examines important manuscript collections. See the referenced travel chronology and the biographical overview.

ר׳ חיים יוסף דוד אזולאי.place: Pisa and Livorno, Grand Duchy of Tuscany
ר׳ חיים יוסף דוד אזולאי.event: After visiting Holland, ר׳ חיים יוסף דוד אזולאי marries his second wife Rachel in Pisa on 28 October 1778 and settles permanently in Livorno, devoting himself to writing and publication. See the documented biography and the Livorno account.

ר׳ חיים יוסף דוד אזולאי dies in Livorno on 1 March 1806 after nearly three decades of scholarship and publishing there. His 1960 reinterment in Jerusalem is posthumous and therefore not used as a lifetime map movement. See the National Library of Israel and the Wikimedia authority data.

ר׳ פינחס שפירא מקוריץ.event: ר׳ פינחס שפירא מקוריץ is born in Shklov, conventionally dated to 1726. See Encyclopaedia Judaica-derived biography.

His family relocates to Miropol, bringing the young ר׳ פינחס שפירא מקוריץ into the region where Hasidism was developing. The year is approximate because the surviving biographical tradition does not fix the move precisely. See Daat.

ר׳ פינחס שפירא מקוריץ becomes associated with Koretz and the circle of ר׳ ישראל בעל שם טוב. The year is only a map anchor for an inadequately dated formative period. See Encyclopaedia Judaica-derived biography and Korets memorial history.
After leaving Koretz during the 1770s, ר׳ פינחס שפירא מקוריץ settles in Ostroh. See the Korets memorial history.
While preparing to journey to the Land of Israel, ר׳ פינחס שפירא מקוריץ falls ill and dies in Shepetivka on 10 Elul 5551. See Daat and the Korets memorial history.

ר׳ שמואל שמלקה הלוי הורוביץ מניקלשבורג.event: ר׳ שמואל שמלקה הלוי הורוביץ מניקלשבורג is born in Chortkiv in 1726. See the Hebrew biographical synthesis and Chabad biography.
Together with his brother ר׳ פינחס הלוי הורוביץ, ר׳ שמואל שמלקה הלוי הורוביץ מניקלשבורג enters the circle of ר׳ דוב בער המגיד ממזריטש. The date is approximate. See Jewish Encyclopedia.
ר׳ שמואל שמלקה הלוי הורוביץ מניקלשבורג begins serving as rabbi of Ryczywół. See the Hebrew biographical synthesis.
ר׳ שמואל שמלקה הלוי הורוביץ מניקלשבורג assumes the rabbinate of Sieniawa. See the Hebrew biographical synthesis.
ר׳ שמואל שמלקה הלוי הורוביץ מניקלשבורג is appointed rabbi of Nikolsburg and introduces a visible Hasidic devotional presence there. See Jewish Encyclopedia and Nikolsburg community history.
ר׳ שמואל שמלקה הלוי הורוביץ מניקלשבורג serves as chief rabbi of Moravia, combining regional communal authority with Hasidic teaching. See Jewish Encyclopedia.
ר׳ שמואל שמלקה הלוי הורוביץ מניקלשבורג dies in Nikolsburg on 28 April 1778. See Jewish Encyclopedia and the POLIN Virtual Shtetl biography.

ר׳ יחיאל מיכל מזלוטשוב.event: ר׳ יחיאל מיכל מזלוטשוב is born in Brody, conventionally in 1726, to ר׳ יצחק מדרוהוביץ. See the Encyclopaedia Judaica-derived biography and Zolochiv memorial history.
ר׳ יחיאל מיכל מזלוטשוב joins the circle of ר׳ ישראל בעל שם טוב. The relationship is well attested, but the first visit is not precisely dated. See the Encyclopaedia Judaica-derived biography.

After the death of ר׳ ישראל בעל שם טוב, ר׳ יחיאל מיכל מזלוטשוב accepts the leadership of ר׳ דוב בער המגיד ממזריטש while preaching in Brody and participating in its celebrated kloiz. See the Encyclopaedia Judaica-derived biography.

ר׳ יחיאל מיכל מזלוטשוב serves as preacher in Zolochiv and becomes permanently identified as its Maggid. The appointment date is approximate. See the Encyclopaedia Judaica-derived biography and Zolochiv memorial history.

Toward the end of his life, ר׳ יחיאל מיכל מזלוטשוב settles in Yampil, where he leads disciples and where his sermons are later remembered as those of the Maggid Meisharim of Yampil. See the Encyclopaedia Judaica-derived biography.
ר׳ יחיאל מיכל מזלוטשוב dies in Yampil on 25 Elul 5546 according to the principal local and dynastic chronology. See Zolochiv memorial history and the Electronic Jewish Encyclopedia.

ר׳ דוד בן חסין.event: ר׳ דוד בן חסין is born in Meknes in 1727 to Aaron ben Hassin. See Encyclopaedia Judaica and the National Library of Israel.
At about seventeen, ר׳ דוד בן חסין begins מגדל לדוד, evidence of his early engagement with biblical exegesis. See the Da'at Hebrew biography.
ר׳ דוד בן חסין studies with ר׳ מרדכי בירדוגו and marries his daughter. The year is approximate because the relationship is secure but the exact date is not. See the National Library of Israel.

During journeys among Moroccan communities and to Gibraltar, ר׳ דוד בן חסין presents and circulates his poems. The precise year is not established, so this is an approximate mid-career marker. See the referenced biography and Jewish Encyclopedia.
The disorder accompanying Moulay Yazid's reign enters ר׳ דוד בן חסין's poetry alongside drought, mortality and pleas for redemption. See the National Library of Israel.
ר׳ דוד בן חסין dies in Meknes on 10 Tammuz 5552. His poems continue in manuscripts and performance before תהלה לדוד is printed in Amsterdam in 1807. See Encyclopaedia Judaica.

ר׳ יוסף תאומים.event: ר׳ יוסף תאומים is born in 1727 at Shchyrets, a town southwest of Lviv, to ר׳ מאיר תאומים. Older summaries sometimes simplify the birthplace to Lemberg, but modern biographical accounts distinguish Shchyrets from the family's subsequent residence in Lviv. See the National Library of Israel authority record and the German biographical account.

ר׳ יוסף תאומים.place: Lviv, Polish–Lithuanian Commonwealth; now Ukraine; year approximate
ר׳ יוסף תאומים.event: During his childhood ר׳ יוסף תאומים moves with his family to Lviv, where his father ר׳ מאיר תאומים serves as dayan, preacher and head of a yeshivah. He studies principally under his father and, while still young, contributes novellae to one of his father's books. The precise migration year is not preserved, so 1735 is an approximate map point within his childhood. See Encyclopaedia Judaica and the Jewish Encyclopedia.

ר׳ יוסף תאומים.place: Komarno, Polish–Lithuanian Commonwealth; now Ukraine; year approximate
ר׳ יוסף תאומים.event: Around age twenty ר׳ יוסף תאומים marries and settles in Komarno. He spends more than a decade there in intensive study and writing while also working as a melamed. The year 1747 follows his stated age and is approximate rather than a documented day of relocation. See the Encyclopaedia Judaica biography and the sourced English chronology.

By 1767 ר׳ יוסף תאומים is studying and teaching in Berlin in the renowned beit midrash maintained by ר׳ דניאל יפה, where he concentrates on preparing and printing his writings. The National Library dates this phase to 1767–1770; another major encyclopedia describes a later Berlin stay beginning in 1772, so the exact span remains disputed. See the National Library of Israel and Encyclopaedia Judaica.

In 1774 ר׳ יוסף תאומים returns to Lviv to succeed his late father as preacher and halakhic instructor; he later serves as a dayan. He remains there for approximately seven years. See Encyclopaedia Judaica and the National Library authority record.

ר׳ יוסף תאומים.place: Frankfurt an der Oder, Kingdom of Prussia; now Germany
ר׳ יוסף תאומים.event: ר׳ יוסף תאומים accepts appointment as rabbi and av bet din of Frankfurt an der Oder in 1781. He stipulates that the community support a group of yeshivah students, making advanced Torah study part of his communal office. Some summaries date the formal appointment to 1782; the contemporary Hebrew year תקמ״א begins in 1780 and spans 1781, while major scholarly reference works use 1781. See Encyclopaedia Judaica and the Jewish Encyclopedia.

ר׳ יוסף תאומים.place: Frankfurt an der Oder, Kingdom of Prussia
ר׳ יוסף תאומים.event: While serving in Frankfurt an der Oder, ר׳ יוסף תאומים publishes the first edition of פרי מגדים on Orach Chaim in 1787. Together with the earlier Yoreh De'ah portion, its component supercommentaries—משבצות זהב, אשל אברהם and שפתי דעת—establish his lasting authority in practical halakhah. See the National Library of Israel bibliographic record and the Jewish Encyclopedia.

ר׳ יוסף תאומים.place: Frankfurt an der Oder, Kingdom of Prussia
ר׳ יוסף תאומים.event: ר׳ יוסף תאומים dies at Frankfurt an der Oder on 4 Iyar 5552 (26 April 1792) after approximately eleven years leading the community. He is buried in its historic Jewish cemetery. His finite numeric death year ensures that his map marker ends in 1792 rather than persisting for centuries. See the National Library of Israel and the Jewish Encyclopedia.

ר׳ מנחם מנדל מוויטבסק.event: ר׳ מנחם מנדל מוויטבסק is born around 1730 in Vitebsk. See Posen Library.

ר׳ מנחם מנדל מוויטבסק.place: Vitebsk and Horodok region; year approximate
ר׳ מנחם מנדל מוויטבסק.event: After studying under ר׳ דוב בער המגיד ממזריטש, ר׳ מנחם מנדל מוויטבסק becomes a central Hasidic teacher in the Vitebsk–Horodok region. The year is an approximate midpoint in his pre-1772 leadership. See YIVO Encyclopedia and Posen Library.
ר׳ מנחם מנדל מוויטבסק and ר׳ שניאור זלמן מליאדי attempt to meet ר׳ אליהו מווילנה to ease the conflict surrounding Hasidism, but the meeting does not take place. See Posen Library.
Opposition and persecution force ר׳ מנחם מנדל מוויטבסק and his circle to leave Minsk. See Posen Library.
ר׳ מנחם מנדל מוויטבסק leads roughly three hundred Hasidim to Ottoman Palestine and initially settles in Safed with ר׳ אברהם מקאליסק. See YIVO Encyclopedia and Daat.

ר׳ מנחם מנדל מוויטבסק.place: Tiberias, Ottoman Palestine; transfer date approximate
ר׳ מנחם מנדל מוויטבסק.event: The Hasidic community led by ר׳ מנחם מנדל מוויטבסק establishes its principal centre in Tiberias after difficulties in Safed; the exact transfer unfolded over several years. See YIVO Encyclopedia.
ר׳ מנחם מנדל מוויטבסק dies in Tiberias and is buried in the city’s old Jewish cemetery. See Posen Library and YIVO Encyclopedia.

ר׳ מנחם נחום טברסקי מצ׳רנוביל.place: Norynsk, Volhynia, Polish–Lithuanian Commonwealth; modern identification approximate
ר׳ מנחם נחום טברסקי מצ׳רנוביל.event: ר׳ מנחם נחום טברסקי מצ׳רנוביל is born in 1730 in Norynsk in Volhynia. Historical sources vary between the related forms Norynsk, Norinsk and Garinsk; the coordinate is regional and should not be read as a house-level identification.
