See the Electronic Jewish Encyclopedia and Hebrew Daat encyclopedia.

As a young scholar ר׳ מנחם נחום טברסקי מצ׳רנוביל joins the circle of ר׳ ישראל בעל שם טוב at Medzhybizh. The precise first visit is unknown, so 1755 is approximate. See the Electronic Jewish Encyclopedia and biographical study.

ר׳ מנחם נחום טברסקי מצ׳רנוביל.place: Mezhirichi, Volhynia, Polish–Lithuanian Commonwealth; year approximate
ר׳ מנחם נחום טברסקי מצ׳רנוביל.event: After the death of ר׳ ישראל בעל שם טוב, ר׳ מנחם נחום טברסקי מצ׳רנוביל becomes a disciple of ר׳ דוב בער המגיד ממעזריטש and helps spread Hasidism through Ukraine. The year is approximate. See the Electronic Jewish Encyclopedia.
ר׳ מנחם נחום טברסקי מצ׳רנוביל establishes his own Hasidic court at Chernobyl, preaching humility, moral refinement and charity. See the biographical study and Electronic Jewish Encyclopedia.

ר׳ מנחם נחום טברסקי מצ׳רנוביל dies at Chernobyl on 11 Cheshvan 5558 (31 October 1797). His son ר׳ מרדכי טברסקי succeeds him. See the National Library of Israel authority record and dated biographical chronology.

The disciples of ר׳ מנחם נחום טברסקי מצ׳רנוביל publish מאור עיניים and ישמח לב posthumously at Slavuta. This publication marker intentionally occurs after his death and does not extend his lifespan on the map. See the National Library of Israel catalogue and first-edition description.

ר׳ פנחס הלוי הורוויץ.event: ר׳ פנחס הלוי הורוויץ is born around 1730 into the rabbinic Horowitz family, a son of ר׳ צבי הירש הורוויץ. Chortkiv is the conventional birthplace, although a Frankfurt museum biography gives Lachowicze; the exact location is therefore not certain. See the Deutsche Biographie authority record and Jewish Museum Frankfurt's account.

By the mid-1750s, ר׳ פנחס הלוי הורוויץ serves in his first known rabbinate at Witków. The exact appointment year is not preserved and 1755 is an approximate career marker. See the Kedem bibliographical account and Encyclopaedia Judaica-derived biography.
ר׳ פנחס הלוי הורוויץ subsequently serves as rabbi of Lachowicze. The year is approximate because the sequence of offices is firmer than their precise dates. See the reference biography.

Together with his brother ר׳ שמואל שמלקה הורוויץ, ר׳ פנחס הלוי הורוויץ studies in the circle of ר׳ דב בער ממזריטש. The relationship is well attested in Hasidic tradition, but 1769 is only a representative late-1760s date. See the bibliographical biography accompanying first editions.

ר׳ פנחס הלוי הורוויץ.place: Frankfurt am Main, Holy Roman Empire
ר׳ פנחס הלוי הורוויץ.event: The Frankfurt community elects ר׳ פנחס הלוי הורוויץ chief rabbi and av beit din. He leads its yeshiva and communal judiciary; his pupils include ר׳ משה סופר. See the Jewish Museum Frankfurt.

ר׳ פנחס הלוי הורוויץ.place: Frankfurt am Main, Holy Roman Empire
ר׳ פנחס הלוי הורוויץ.event: While serving in Frankfurt, ר׳ פנחס הלוי הורוויץ brings ספר כתובה — הפלאה to print in nearby Offenbach. The printing location does not imply relocation. See the work-by-work reference account.

ר׳ פנחס הלוי הורוויץ.place: Frankfurt am Main, Holy Roman Empire
ר׳ פנחס הלוי הורוויץ.event: ר׳ פנחס הלוי הורוויץ publishes המקנה in Offenbach while continuing to head the Frankfurt rabbinate and yeshiva. See the Encyclopaedia Judaica-derived bibliography.

ר׳ פנחס הלוי הורוויץ.place: Frankfurt am Main, Holy Roman Empire
ר׳ פנחס הלוי הורוויץ.event: ר׳ פנחס הלוי הורוויץ dies in Frankfurt on 1 July 1805 and is buried in the old Jewish cemetery on Battonnstraße. See the Jewish Encyclopedia and Jewish Museum Frankfurt.

ר׳ רפאל חיים יצחק קאריגל.event: ר׳ רפאל חיים יצחק קאריגל is born in Hebron on 15 October 1733 according to the Newport/Yale chronology. The National Library's older authority heading gives 1729, a documented conflict. See the Yale Beinecke catalogue of the Stiles papers and the National Library authority record.

At about seventeen, ר׳ רפאל חיים יצחק קאריגל receives rabbinic ordination in Hebron; he names ר׳ דוד מלמד among his teachers. The year follows his reported age and is approximate. See the Jewish Encyclopedia.
ר׳ רפאל חיים יצחק קאריגל begins his international emissary career and spends approximately 1754–56 in Constantinople. See the itinerary preserved in the Jewish Encyclopedia.

From about 1761 to 1763, ר׳ רפאל חיים יצחק קאריגל lives in Curaçao and appears to undertake rabbinic duties, although surviving congregational records do not prove a formal incumbency. See the cautious account in the Jewish Encyclopedia.
ר׳ רפאל חיים יצחק קאריגל returns to Hebron for approximately four years, maintaining the home community from which his Atlantic emissary identity derived. See the documented itinerary.

From 1768 to 1771, ר׳ רפאל חיים יצחק קאריגל teaches in a London bet midrash and reports receiving an annual salary of £100. The exact building has not been securely identified, so the point avoids claiming a particular synagogue. See the Jewish Encyclopedia.

ר׳ רפאל חיים יצחק קאריגל spends roughly a year in Jamaica before travelling into the North American colonies. Kingston is the cautious community anchor because the surviving summary does not securely name a more precise Jamaican site. See the itinerary source.

ר׳ רפאל חיים יצחק קאריגל.place: New York and Philadelphia, British North America
ר׳ רפאל חיים יצחק קאריגל.event: During 1772–73, ר׳ רפאל חיים יצחק קאריגל travels through the North American colonies, spending time in New York and Philadelphia before his best-documented Newport residence. The map uses New York as a representative first colonial stage rather than asserting a full route. See the Jewish Encyclopedia.

ר׳ רפאל חיים יצחק קאריגל.place: Yeshuat Israel (Touro Synagogue), Newport, Rhode Island
ר׳ רפאל חיים יצחק קאריגל.event: From March to July 1773, ר׳ רפאל חיים יצחק קאריגל lives among Newport's Jewish community, officiates at Yeshuat Israel and meets Ezra Stiles repeatedly for Hebrew and rabbinic study. On 28 May he delivers the Shavuot sermon later printed as The Salvation of Israel. See the National Library of Israel, Touro Synagogue and the Folger catalogue of the sermon.
On 21 July 1773, ר׳ רפאל חיים יצחק קאריגל sails from Newport to Suriname and remains there for more than seven months. See the Encyclopaedia Judaica-derived biography.
By 1775, ר׳ רפאל חיים יצחק קאריגל is serving the Nidhe Israel community in Barbados as hakham. See the reference biography and Touro Synagogue's discussion of his Barbados correspondence.

ר׳ רפאל חיים יצחק קאריגל dies in Barbados in May 1777 and is buried in the Nidhe Israel cemetery, where his trilingual gravestone survives. See the reference biography and the National Library authority record.

ר׳ אהרן הגדול מקרלין.place: Janów, Polish–Lithuanian Commonwealth; identification traditionally associated with present-day Ivanava, Belarus
ר׳ אהרן הגדול מקרלין.event: ר׳ אהרן הגדול מקרלין is born in Janów in 1736 to ר׳ יעקב and Perl. Because several towns bore the name Janów, the coordinate follows the Karlin tradition's association with Ivanava rather than claiming a house-level location. See the sourced biographical account and Hebrew Yeshiva encyclopedia.

ר׳ אהרן הגדול מקרלין.place: Mezhirichi, Volhynia, Polish–Lithuanian Commonwealth; year approximate
ר׳ אהרן הגדול מקרלין.event: As a young man ר׳ אהרן הגדול מקרלין becomes a prominent disciple of ר׳ דוב בער ממזריטש. The precise first year is not preserved, so 1755 is an approximate study-stage marker. See Yeshiva's Hebrew biography.

ר׳ אהרן הגדול מקרלין.place: Karlin, Pinsk, Polish–Lithuanian Commonwealth; now Belarus; year approximate
ר׳ אהרן הגדול מקרלין.event: By about 1760 ר׳ אהרן הגדול מקרלין establishes an influential Hasidic centre at Karlin near Pinsk. His fiery preaching and ecstatic prayer help spread Hasidism throughout the region. See the Jewish Telegraphic Agency and biographical synthesis.

ר׳ אהרן הגדול מקרלין.place: Karlin, Pinsk, Polish–Lithuanian Commonwealth; year approximate
ר׳ אהרן הגדול מקרלין.event: In his mature Karlin period ר׳ אהרן הגדול מקרלין composes the Sabbath hymn יה אכסוף. Its exact date is unknown; 1770 is used only as a defensible late-life map point. See Hebrew Yeshiva encyclopedia.

ר׳ אהרן הגדול מקרלין.place: Karlin, Pinsk, Polish–Lithuanian Commonwealth; now Belarus
ר׳ אהרן הגדול מקרלין.event: ר׳ אהרן הגדול מקרלין dies in Karlin on 19 Nisan 5532 at age thirty-six and is buried in the Karlin cemetery. His disciple ר׳ שלמה מקרלין succeeds him, while his descendants later lead Karlin-Stolin. See the JTA report on the gravesite tradition and sourced biography.

ר׳ ישראל הופשטיין מקוז׳ניץ.event: ר׳ ישראל הופשטיין מקוז׳ניץ is born around 1737 in Opatów. See the YIVO Encyclopedia and National Library authority data.
ר׳ ישראל הופשטיין מקוז׳ניץ studies in the circle of ר׳ דוב בער המגיד ממזריטש, after earlier association with ר׳ שמואל שמלקה מניקלשבורג. The year is approximate. See the YIVO Encyclopedia.
ר׳ ישראל הופשטיין מקוז׳ניץ becomes a leading disciple of ר׳ אלימלך מליז׳נסק, whose model of the tsaddik strongly shapes his later leadership. See the YIVO Encyclopedia.

ר׳ ישראל הופשטיין מקוז׳ניץ establishes his court at Kozienice, creating an influential centre of Polish Hasidism. The exact beginning of the court is not securely dated. See Daat and the YIVO Encyclopedia.

During Napoleon’s Russian campaign, ר׳ ישראל הופשטיין מקוז׳ניץ joins ר׳ יעקב יצחק הלוי הורוביץ מלובלין and ר׳ מנחם מנדל מרימנוב in prayer linked to hopes that the war might advance Jewish redemption. See the YIVO account of the episode.
ר׳ ישראל הופשטיין מקוז׳ניץ dies at Kozienice in 1814. His son ר׳ משה אליקים בריעה הופשטיין succeeds him. See the YIVO Encyclopedia and Daat.

ר׳ שלמה מקרלין.event: ר׳ שלמה מקרלין is born in Tulchyn in 1738 to ר׳ מאיר. See the Chabad biographical study.
After encountering ר׳ אהרן הגדול מקרלין, ר׳ שלמה מקרלין travels to study under ר׳ דוב בער המגיד ממזריטש. The year is approximate. See the Chabad biographical study.
Following the death of ר׳ אהרן הגדול מקרלין, ר׳ שלמה מקרלין succeeds him and leads the Karlin Hasidic community. See the Chabad biography and sourced Karlin chronology.

Sustained opposition to Hasidism forces ר׳ שלמה מקרלין to leave Karlin for Ludmir, where he establishes a new centre and attracts important disciples. See the Chabad biography and Shtetl Routes historical guide.
During Polish–Russian fighting, ר׳ שלמה מקרלין is struck by a bullet and dies from the wound six days later, on 22 Tammuz 5552 (12 July 1792). See the dated biographical account.

ר׳ לוי יצחק מברדיצ׳ב.event: ר׳ לוי יצחק מברדיצ׳ב is born in Husaków, Galicia, in 1740 into a rabbinic family. See the YIVO Encyclopedia of Jews in Eastern Europe and the Posen Library.
In the early 1760s, ר׳ לוי יצחק מברדיצ׳ב takes an early rabbinic post in Ryczywół. The precise appointment date is approximate, but the sequence precedes Żelechów. See the YIVO biography.

ר׳ לוי יצחק מברדיצ׳ב becomes rabbi of Żelechów and openly teaches Hasidic ideas. Opposition to the new movement makes his position increasingly difficult. See the YIVO Encyclopedia and the scholarly study of his Żelechów leadership in Zippi Kauffman's article.

Through ר׳ שמואל שמלקה הורוויץ, ר׳ לוי יצחק מברדיצ׳ב enters the circle of ר׳ דב בער ממזריטש and becomes a major disseminator of the Maggid's Hasidic teaching. The year is representative rather than a precisely documented arrival. See the YIVO Encyclopedia.

ר׳ לוי יצחק מברדיצ׳ב is appointed rabbi of Pinsk. He promotes Hasidic practice and preaching there, meeting sustained communal resistance that eventually ends his tenure. See the YIVO biography and My Jewish Learning's reference overview.

After leaving Pinsk, ר׳ לוי יצחק מברדיצ׳ב becomes rabbi of Berdychiv in 1785. He remains here for the rest of his life, and the city becomes inseparable from his identity and teachings. See the YIVO Encyclopedia.

While based in Berdychiv, ר׳ לוי יצחק מברדיצ׳ב publishes the first portion of קדושת לוי in Slavuta, devoted to Hanukkah and Purim. The printer's city is not treated as a relocation. See the YIVO work history and the Posen Library's dated text record.

ר׳ לוי יצחק מברדיצ׳ב dies in Berdychiv in 1809 and is buried in the city's Jewish cemetery. His sons subsequently publish the expanded Torah commentary in 1811. See the YIVO Encyclopedia and the biographical overview.

ר׳ נתן הכהן אדלר.place: Frankfurt am Main, Holy Roman Empire
ר׳ נתן הכהן אדלר.event: ר׳ נתן הכהן אדלר is born in Frankfurt on 16 December 1741. See the Jewish Encyclopedia.

ר׳ נתן הכהן אדלר.place: Frankfurt am Main, Holy Roman Empire
ר׳ נתן הכהן אדלר.event: At about twenty ר׳ נתן הכהן אדלר establishes a yeshiva and private devotional circle; future leaders including ר׳ משה סופר study under him. See the Jewish Encyclopedia.

ר׳ נתן הכהן אדלר.place: Frankfurt am Main, Holy Roman Empire
ר׳ נתן הכהן אדלר.event: Conflict intensifies between the kabbalistic private congregation of ר׳ נתן הכהן אדלר and Frankfurt’s established communal leadership, which issues restrictions against the circle. See the Jewish Museum Frankfurt METAhub.
ר׳ נתן הכהן אדלר leaves Frankfurt with students, including ר׳ משה סופר, and accepts the rabbinate of Boskovice. See the Jewish Encyclopedia and Jewish Museum Frankfurt.

ר׳ נתן הכהן אדלר.place: Frankfurt am Main, Holy Roman Empire
ר׳ נתן הכהן אדלר.event: After difficulties in Boskovice, ר׳ נתן הכהן אדלר returns to Frankfurt and resumes teaching and kabbalistic practice in a more private setting. See the Jewish Encyclopedia.

ר׳ נתן הכהן אדלר.place: Battonnstraße Jewish Cemetery, Frankfurt am Main
ר׳ נתן הכהן אדלר.event: ר׳ נתן הכהן אדלר dies in Frankfurt on 17 September 1800 and is buried in the Battonnstraße cemetery. See the Jewish Museum Frankfurt METAhub.

ר׳ משולם פייבוש הלר.event: ר׳ משולם פייבוש הלר was born around 1742 into a rabbinic family descended from ר׳ יום טוב ליפמן הלר. The exact birthplace and year are not securely documented, so the marker is regional. See Encyclopaedia Judaica.

ר׳ משולם פייבוש הלר became a principal disciple of ר׳ יחיאל מיכל מזלוטשוב. The year is approximate and marks a documented intellectual relationship rather than a precisely dated move. See Daat and Encyclopaedia Judaica.
During his formative years, ר׳ משולם פייבוש הלר also encountered the teaching circle of ר׳ דוב בער ממזריטש. The date is approximate and does not claim permanent residence. See Daat’s biography.
At Zbarazh, ר׳ משולם פייבוש הלר wrote the first epistle that became יושר דברי אמת, explaining the inward discipline of Hasidic prayer and devekut. See the text on Sefaria and chronology.

The two epistles of ר׳ משולם פייבוש הלר were first printed anonymously in the Lviv anthology ליקוטים יקרים. The marker remains at his residence rather than treating the printshop as a move. See Encyclopaedia Judaica.
ר׳ משולם פייבוש הלר died at Zbarazh on 20 Kislev 5555 (12 December 1794) and was buried there. See the biographical chronology.

ר׳ אריה לייב הכהן הלר.event: ר׳ אריה לייב הכהן הלר is born in Kalush around 1745 to ר׳ יוסף הכהן הלר. See the YIVO Encyclopedia and the Galicia-Bukovina community history.

ר׳ אריה לייב הכהן הלר.place: Tysmenytsia, Polish–Lithuanian Commonwealth; now Ukraine; year approximate
ר׳ אריה לייב הכהן הלר.event: As a young scholar ר׳ אריה לייב הכהן הלר studies under ר׳ משולם איגרא in Tysmenytsia. The year is approximate because sources preserve the relationship but not its exact beginning. See the YIVO Encyclopedia.

ר׳ אריה לייב הכהן הלר.place: Rozhniativ, Habsburg Galicia; now Ukraine; year approximate
ר׳ אריה לייב הכהן הלר.event: Before reaching Stryi, ר׳ אריה לייב הכהן הלר serves as rabbi of Rozhniativ. The office is attested, but its opening year is uncertain; 1775 is an approximate midpoint rather than a false precise appointment date. See the Hebrew biographical summary.
ר׳ אריה לייב הכהן הלר becomes rabbi of Stryi in 1788 and publishes the first part of קצות החושן. He remains the city's rabbi for the rest of his life. See the YIVO Encyclopedia.
In Stryi ר׳ אריה לייב הכהן הלר publishes שב שמעתתא in 1804, presenting seven sustained conceptual investigations begun in his youth. See the YIVO Encyclopedia and the Hebrew biography.

ר׳ אריה לייב הכהן הלר dies in Stryi on 19 Tevet 5573, in late December 1812. Some references label the corresponding civil year 1813; the project follows the explicit 1812 civil chronology while recording the discrepancy. See the YIVO Encyclopedia and sourced biography.

ר׳ מנחם מנדל מרימנוב.event: ר׳ מנחם מנדל מרימנוב is born in Nowe Miasto in 1745 to ר׳ יוסף חריף. See Daat and the YIVO Encyclopedia.
During a period of study in Nikolsburg, ר׳ מנחם מנדל מרימנוב encounters Hasidism and adopts its devotional path. The date is approximate. See Daat.
ר׳ מנחם מנדל מרימנוב joins the court of ר׳ אלימלך מליז׳נסק and becomes one of his principal disciples. See Daat and the YIVO Encyclopedia.

After the death of ר׳ אלימלך מליז׳נסק, ר׳ מנחם מנדל מרימנוב develops an independent court eventually centred at Rymanów, attracting disciples from across Galicia. The precise beginning of residence is uncertain. See the YIVO Encyclopedia and Daat.

During Napoleon’s Russian campaign, ר׳ מנחם מנדל מרימנוב joins ר׳ יעקב יצחק הלוי הורוביץ מלובלין and ר׳ ישראל הופשטיין מקוז׳ניץ in prayer linked to hopes for political and messianic deliverance. See the YIVO Encyclopedia.
ר׳ מנחם מנדל מרימנוב dies at Rymanów on 19 Iyar 5575 (29 May 1815) and is buried there. See the YIVO Encyclopedia and sourced chronology.

ר׳ שניאור זלמן מלאדי.place: Liozna, Polish–Lithuanian Commonwealth; now Liozna, Belarus
ר׳ שניאור זלמן מלאדי.event: ר׳ שניאור זלמן מלאדי is born at Liozna in 1745 according to the accepted chronology. See the YIVO Encyclopedia and Chabad biography.

ר׳ שניאור זלמן מלאדי.place: Mezhirichi, Volhynia, Polish–Lithuanian Commonwealth; now Ukraine; year approximate
ר׳ שניאור זלמן מלאדי.event: At about twenty ר׳ שניאור זלמן מלאדי joins the circle of ר׳ דוב בער ממזריטש and develops the teachings that become Chabad. The precise first-visit year varies in traditional accounts. See the YIVO Encyclopedia and Da'at.

ר׳ שניאור זלמן מלאדי serves as maggid in Liozna and begins building a regional Hasidic following; at the Maggid's request he also begins the halakhic project later known as שולחן ערוך הרב. See the YIVO Encyclopedia.
Following denunciations by opponents, ר׳ שניאור זלמן מלאדי is arrested and imprisoned in Saint Petersburg; he is released on 19 Kislev after investigation. See the Jewish Encyclopedia and Da'at.
After a second investigation and final release, ר׳ שניאור זלמן מלאדי establishes his court at Liadi, from which his enduring geographical title derives. See the YIVO Encyclopedia and Da'at.

ר׳ שניאור זלמן מלאדי.place: Pena, Kursk Governorate, Russian Empire; now Pen, Russia
ר׳ שניאור זלמן מלאדי.event: During the French invasion ר׳ שניאור זלמן מלאדי evacuates Liadi with his family, supports the Russian cause and dies at Pena on 24 Tevet 5573 while travelling east. See The Last Journey and the YIVO Encyclopedia.

ר׳ שניאור זלמן מלאדי.place: Hadiach, Poltava Governorate, Russian Empire; now Ukraine
ר׳ שניאור זלמן מלאדי.event: After his death at Pena, ר׳ שניאור זלמן מלאדי is taken to Hadiach for burial; his gravesite becomes a major Chabad pilgrimage place. See the sourced biographical record.

ר׳ יעקב יצחק הלוי הורוביץ.event: ר׳ יעקב יצחק הלוי הורוביץ is born around 1745 into a rabbinic family in the Lublin region. Sources variously name Łuków, Józefów or Szczebrzeszyn, so the marker is regional rather than falsely precise. See the YIVO Encyclopedia and Rachel Elior’s scholarly study.
As a young Hasid, ר׳ יעקב יצחק הלוי הורוביץ studies in the circle of ר׳ דוב בער ממזריטש. The date is approximate and does not claim continuous residence. See YIVO and Daat’s Hebrew biography.

After the Maggid’s death, ר׳ יעקב יצחק הלוי הורוביץ becomes a close disciple of ר׳ אלימלך מליז׳נסק, whose model of the tsaddik deeply shapes him. The year is approximate. See YIVO and Hebrew scholarship.
With the blessing of ר׳ אלימלך מליז׳נסק, ר׳ יעקב יצחק הלוי הורוביץ begins leading an independent Hasidic circle at Łańcut around 1785. See Rachel Elior’s historical study and the Hebrew biography.

After intermediate stages including Czechosław/Czechów, ר׳ יעקב יצחק הלוי הורוביץ establishes his enduring court in Lublin, which becomes the central school of Polish Hasidism. The exact settlement year is uncertain. See the YIVO Encyclopedia and Bar-Ilan University’s research project.

ר׳ יעקב יצחק הלוי הורוביץ falls from a window under circumstances that later Hasidic memory and Maskilic satire interpret differently; he remains seriously ill. See the YIVO bibliography, which cites David Assaf’s source-critical study of the event.
ר׳ יעקב יצחק הלוי הורוביץ dies in Lublin on 9 Av 5575, 15 August 1815, and is buried in the Old Jewish Cemetery. See the National Library authority record and Hebrew chronology.

ר׳ רפאל בירדוגו.event: ר׳ רפאל בירדוגו is born in Meknes to ר׳ מרדכי בירדוגו, within a rabbinic family whose earlier leaders included ר׳ משה בירדוגו. See the Encyclopaedia Judaica family entry and the Brill scholarly study.

After his father's death, the adolescent ר׳ רפאל בירדוגו continues advanced study in straitened circumstances. Later family memory emphasizes both his early learning and prolonged poverty; the year is approximate. See the Jewish Encyclopedia.

ר׳ רפאל בירדוגו.place: Rabbinical court, Mellah of Meknes, Morocco
ר׳ רפאל בירדוגו.event: By the late 1770s ר׳ רפאל בירדוגו serves as a dayan in Meknes. His surviving decisions establish him as both a courtroom jurist and an interpreter of local takkanot. See the peer-reviewed study of his legal reasoning.

During the violent reign of Moulay Yazid, Meknes Jewry suffers plunder, displacement and economic crisis. ר׳ רפאל בירדוגו provides legal and communal leadership in this setting; his writings should be read against these disruptions rather than as abstract jurisprudence. See the Meknes historical overview and Brill.

As the leading judge of Meknes, ר׳ רפאל בירדוגו helps frame communal regulations and decisions involving inheritance, marriage, debt and expenditure. His willingness to oppose powerful householders and other judges is visible in the responsa. See Jewish Encyclopedia and the modern legal study.

ר׳ רפאל בירדוגו dies in Meknes on Hoshana Rabbah 5582. His manuscripts and responsa pass into the custody of the Berdugo scholarly family and become authoritative sources for later Moroccan decisors. See the Encyclopaedia Judaica entry.

ר׳ אברהם דנציג.event: ר׳ אברהם דנציג is born in Danzig, now Gdańsk, to ר׳ יחיאל מיכל. Modern authorities normally give 1748, while several summaries allow 1747. See Encyclopaedia Judaica and the National Library of Israel catalogue.

At approximately fourteen, ר׳ אברהם דנציג enters the Prague yeshiva and studies with ר׳ יחזקאל לנדא and ר׳ יוסף ליברמן. His father reportedly required him to guard his traditional formation amid the city’s changing intellectual culture. See Encyclopaedia Judaica and My Jewish Learning.

After roughly four years of study in Prague, ר׳ אברהם דנציג settles in Vilna. Although qualified for rabbinic office, he follows his family principle of not deriving income from Torah and supports himself as a merchant. See Jewish Encyclopedia and Encyclopaedia Judaica.

During his decades in commerce, ר׳ אברהם דנציג periodically travels from Vilna to the major Leipzig fairs while continuing intensive Torah study. His writings refer to these journeys, but their individual dates are not securely recorded; 1780 is a representative map marker only. See the Jewish Encyclopedia biography.

ר׳ אברהם דנציג also frequents the commercial fairs of Königsberg, an experience that helps explain the practical, household-centered orientation of his later codes. The surviving sources do not date particular trips; this representative year is approximate. See the Jewish Encyclopedia.

ר׳ אברהם דנציג begins issuing חיי אדם, his practical reorganization of the laws of אורח חיים for educated householders. Later expanded editions incorporate further correction and analysis, and organized חיי אדם study societies emerge in many communities. See the primary text on Sefaria and the publication history and cited references.

A military gunpowder-magazine explosion devastates ר׳ אברהם דנציג’s courtyard and home, kills thirty-one people and injures members of his family, who nevertheless survive. He establishes 15–16 Kislev as an annual family פולווער־פורים of fasting, thanksgiving, charity and a festive meal. Contemporary calendar conversion creates a 1803/1804 dating variation. See his account cited by the Jewish Encyclopedia and Simcha Fishbane’s modern study Beyond a Code of Jewish Law.

After the explosion contributes to the loss of his commercial fortune, ר׳ אברהם דנציג accepts service as a dayan in Vilna. His precise appointment year is not uniformly recorded, so 1804 is an approximate transition marker. See the Jewish Encyclopedia and Encyclopaedia Judaica.

An expanded Vilna edition of חיי אדם appears alongside its learned companion נשמת אדם. The combination makes practical rules accessible while preserving the deeper argumentation needed by scholars. See the bibliographic description of the 1809–1810 editions and נשמת אדם on Sefaria.

ר׳ אברהם דנציג publishes שערי צדק, systematizing laws dependent on the Land of Israel. In its introduction he connects the project to his vow and unrealized hope to settle in Jerusalem. See the Jewish Encyclopedia bibliography and the discussion in Beyond a Code of Jewish Law.

The mature חכמת אדם and its analytical companion בינת אדם circulate in Vilna, extending ר׳ אברהם דנציג’s codification principally to יורה דעה. Edition dates vary between 1812 and 1815. See חכמת אדם on Sefaria, the Jewish Encyclopedia bibliography and Encyclopaedia Judaica.

ר׳ אברהם דנציג dies in Vilna on 4 Tishrei 5581 (12 September 1820). His codes remain central sources for later practical halakhah, while בית אברהם, his ethical testament, is published posthumously in 1821. See Encyclopaedia Judaica, the National Library of Israel and My Jewish Learning.

ר׳ אברהם יהושע השל מאפטא.event: ר׳ אברהם יהושע השל מאפטא is born in Żmigród in 1748 according to the standard dynastic chronology; some Hebrew references give 1755. See the Hebrew biographical overview and Daat.
ר׳ אברהם יהושע השל מאפטא studies under ר׳ אלימלך מליז׳נסק and also receives influence from ר׳ יחיאל מיכל מזלוטשוב. The year is approximate. See Daat.
ר׳ אברהם יהושע השל מאפטא assumes his first documented rabbinate at Kolbuszowa, where followers begin gathering around him. See Daat and the Hebrew biographical overview.
ר׳ אברהם יהושע השל מאפטא becomes rabbi of Opatów and is thereafter universally known as the Apter Rav, even after later moves. See Daat.
ר׳ אברהם יהושע השל מאפטא accepts the rabbinate of Iași. His tenure ends amid sharp communal opposition, after which he leaves Moldavia. See Daat.
ר׳ אברהם יהושע השל מאפטא settles in Medzhybizh, where he becomes a senior Hasidic leader and devotes himself to teaching rather than formal communal office. See Daat.
ר׳ אברהם יהושע השל מאפטא dies in Medzhybizh on 5 Nisan 5585 and is buried there. See Daat and the dated gravesite record.

ר׳ משה חיים אפרים מסדילקוב.event: ר׳ משה חיים אפרים מסדילקוב was born in Medzhybizh to Udl, daughter of ר׳ ישראל בעל שם טוב, and ר׳ יחיאל מיכל אשכנזי. Some traditions give 1742 or about 1750. See the biographical overview and Jewish Encyclopedia.

ר׳ משה חיים אפרים מסדילקוב.place: Mezhirichi and Polonne; approximate study period
ר׳ משה חיים אפרים מסדילקוב.event: After the death of the בעל שם טוב, ר׳ משה חיים אפרים מסדילקוב studied in the circles of ר׳ דוב בער ממזריטש and ר׳ יעקב יוסף מפולנאה. The marker represents a formative study period, not continuous residence. See biographical overview.
ר׳ משה חיים אפרים מסדילקוב settled in Sudilkov and served as a maggid, composing and delivering teachings later preserved in דגל מחנה אפרים. See biographical chronology.
Around 1785, ר׳ משה חיים אפרים מסדילקוב returned to Medzhybizh. Some sources place the return several years later, so the year is approximate. See Daat and the modern chronology.
ר׳ משה חיים אפרים מסדילקוב died on 17 Iyar 5560 (12 May 1800) and was buried in Medzhybizh near ר׳ ישראל בעל שם טוב. See the biographical record.

The author’s son ר׳ יעקב יחיאל published דגל מחנה אפרים at Korets in 1810. The marker remains at the author’s final centre rather than implying that he travelled after death. See the Jewish Encyclopedia and first-edition catalogue.

ר׳ חיים איצקוביץ מוולוז׳ין.place: Volozhin, Polish–Lithuanian Commonwealth; now Valozhyn, Belarus
ר׳ חיים איצקוביץ מוולוז׳ין.event: ר׳ חיים איצקוביץ מוולוז׳ין is born on ז׳ בסיוון תק״ט (24 May 1749) in Volozhin to ר׳ יצחק בן חיים, a communal leader, and Rivka daughter of Yosef Rapoport. See the Hebrew biographical entry and the National Library authority page.

As a young student, ר׳ חיים איצקוביץ מוולוז׳ין studies for about two years with ר׳ רפאל זיסקינד הכהן, then rabbi of Minsk and later of Hamburg. The sources preserve the stage but not a secure starting year, so 1761 is approximate. See Hebrew Wikiyeshiva and the Idra source study.

In adolescence ר׳ חיים איצקוביץ מוולוז׳ין studies under the town’s rabbi ר׳ אריה לייב גינצבורג, author of שאגת אריה. This relationship is well attested, although the exact year is reconstructed from later biographical accounts. See Hebrew Wikiyeshiva and the Idra study.

By the late 1760s or early 1770s, ר׳ חיים איצקוביץ מוולוז׳ין begins travelling to Vilna to learn from ר׳ אליהו בן שלמה זלמן. Later sources variously place his beginning at age nineteen or twenty-five; the relationship is certain but 1770 is an approximate map anchor. See YIVO Encyclopedia and Hebrew Wikiyeshiva.

By 1782 ר׳ חיים איצקוביץ מוולוז׳ין is formally appointed to the Volozhin rabbinate; surviving appointment letters from 1782 and 1785 provide firmer evidence than later claims assigning the office to 1774. See the description of the two appointment documents.

Around age forty, ר׳ חיים איצקוביץ מוולוז׳ין accepts the rabbinate of Vilkomir (modern Ukmergė). Opposition within the community leads him to return to Volozhin after about one year. The move is attested, but 1789 is approximate. See Hebrew Wikiyeshiva and the document catalogue.

ר׳ חיים איצקוביץ מוולוז׳ין circulates אגרת החיים, a public appeal asking communities to send capable students and finance a permanent centre of advanced Torah learning. See the National Library catalogue and Hebrew historical overview.

ר׳ חיים איצקוביץ מוולוז׳ין.place: Yeshivat Etz Chaim, Volozhin, Russian Empire
ר׳ חיים איצקוביץ מוולוז׳ין.event: Around 1803 ר׳ חיים איצקוביץ מוולוז׳ין founds Yeshivat Etz Chaim. It recruits advanced students beyond the local community, supports them materially and maintains continuous study, becoming the institutional model for later Lithuanian yeshivot. See the YIVO Encyclopedia and Yeshivat Har Etzion.

A fire in 1815 destroys many responsa manuscripts belonging to ר׳ חיים איצקוביץ מוולוז׳ין. The surviving legal material later printed in חוט המשולש is therefore only part of his halakhic output. See the Daf Yomi biographical dictionary and cross-reference.

ר׳ חיים איצקוביץ מוולוז׳ין.place: Volozhin, Russian Empire; now Valozhyn, Belarus
ר׳ חיים איצקוביץ מוולוז׳ין.event: ר׳ חיים איצקוביץ מוולוז׳ין dies in Volozhin on י״ד בסיוון תקפ״א (14 June 1821) and is buried there. His son ר׳ יצחק מוולוז׳ין succeeds him as head of the yeshivah and publishes נפש החיים in 1824. See the National Library authority page, the Hebrew biography, and the documented gravestone photograph.

ר׳ משה טייטלבוים מאוהעל.event: ר׳ משה טייטלבוים מאוהעל is born in Przemyśl in 1759. See the Teitelbaum family history.
ר׳ משה טייטלבוים מאוהעל begins serving as rabbi in Sieniawa around age twenty-five. See the biographical profile.
After encountering Hasidism, ר׳ משה טייטלבוים מאוהעל becomes a disciple of ר׳ יעקב יצחק הורוביץ, the חוזה מלובלין; the year is approximate. See the biographical account.
ר׳ משה טייטלבוים מאוהעל is appointed rabbi of Sátoraljaújhely and establishes a major centre of Hungarian Hasidism. See the standard biography.
ר׳ משה טייטלבוים מאוהעל dies in Sátoraljaújhely on 17 July 1841 and is buried there. See the Teitelbaum family history.

ר׳ אבא בר איבו.event: ר׳ אבא בר איבו נולד בקירוב בשנת 175 בכפרי שבבבל; המקום הקדום לא זוהה בוודאות ולכן הנקודה היא עוגן אזורי בלבד. Encyclopedia of World Biography
ר׳ אבא בר איבו עלה לארץ ישראל ולמד אצל דודו ר׳ חייא ובבית מדרשו של ר׳ יהודה הנשיא בציפורי; השנה מקורבת לתקופת לימודיו. Jewish Encyclopedia
ר׳ אבא בר איבו חזר לבבל בשנת 219 ופעל תחילה בנהרדעא לצד ר׳ שמואל בר אבא; מיקום העיר הקדומה משוער. Biographical synthesis with Talmudic references
ר׳ אבא בר איבו עבר לסורא והקים בה ישיבה שיטתית סביב המשנה והמסורת הארץ־ישראלית, יסוד למרכז התורה הבבלי. Encyclopedia of World Biography
בישיבת סורא לימד ר׳ אבא בר איבו קהל תלמידים רחב; מחלוקותיו עם ר׳ שמואל בר אבא נעשו תשתית מרכזית של ההלכה האמוראית. Jewish Encyclopedia
ר׳ אבא בר איבו נפטר בבבל בקירוב בשנת 247; ישיבת סורא ותלמידיו המשיכו את מפעלו והפכו את בבל למרכז לימוד התורה. Encyclopedia of World Biography

ר׳ חיים טירר.event: ר׳ חיים טירר was born near Buchach. The National Library uses 1760, while other traditions give different approximate years. See the National Library catalogue.
ר׳ חיים טירר studied in the circle of ר׳ יחיאל מיכל מזלוטשוב, the formative teacher repeatedly associated with him. The year is approximate. See Daat’s Hebrew biography.
ר׳ חיים טירר served as a communal rabbi in Mohyliv-Podilskyi, one of several documented rabbinates before Chernivtsi. The date is approximate. See Daat.

By the late eighteenth century, ר׳ חיים טירר was serving as rabbi of Chernivtsi, the office with which his name became permanently associated. The opening year is approximate. See Hebrew biographical chronology.

After leaving the Chernivtsi rabbinate amid conflict with Austrian authorities, ר׳ חיים טירר passed through Moldavia and served in Botoșani and later Chișinău while preparing to reach the Land of Israel. See Hebrew chronology and Daat.
ר׳ חיים טירר reached Safed and joined its Hasidic community. The precise arrival year varies in later accounts, so 1813 is approximate. See Daat.
ר׳ חיים טירר died in Safed on 27 Kislev 5578 and was buried in the old cemetery. See the National Library authority-linked catalogue.

ר׳ אפרים זלמן מרגליות.place: Brody, Kingdom of Galicia and Lodomeria; now Ukraine
ר׳ אפרים זלמן מרגליות.event: ר׳ אפרים זלמן מרגליות is born in Brody on 27 November 1760 to ר׳ מנחם מניש מרגליות. Some older English references give 1762, but National Library and modern scholarly authority records support 1760. See the National Library of Israel and YIVO.

ר׳ אפרים זלמן מרגליות publishes his early responsa בית חדש החדשות in 1785, demonstrating a reputation that soon brings questions from other communities. See the Jewish Encyclopedia biography and bibliography.

Brody’s rabbis recognize ר׳ אפרים זלמן מרגליות among their number. Financial independence from his successful commercial house enables him to maintain a yeshiva at home and serve as a scholar of the kloyz without relying on a salaried pulpit. See the Jewish Encyclopedia and Orthodox Union biography.

From Brody, ר׳ אפרים זלמן מרגליות publishes the first volumes titled בית אפרים in Lemberg in 1809–1810. The map remains at his evidenced residence rather than incorrectly treating the printing city as a relocation. See YIVO’s bibliography.

The four-part responsa collection שו״ת בית אפרים establishes ר׳ אפרים זלמן מרגליות as a major authority across the divisions of Shulchan Aruch. He continues commercial activity, teaching and extensive rabbinic correspondence from Brody. See YIVO and the Hebrew biography.

ר׳ אפרים זלמן מרגליות.place: Brody, with works printed in Dubno
ר׳ אפרים זלמן מרגליות.event: ר׳ אפרים זלמן מרגליות issues יד אפרים on Orach Chaim and שערי אפרים on public Torah reading in 1820. The books are printed in Dubno, but Brody remains his biographically supported location. See the bibliographical record.

ר׳ אפרים זלמן מרגליות dies in Brody on 4 August 1828, 24 Av 5588. His manuscripts and already influential rulings continue to appear in posthumous editions, most famously מטה אפרים. See the National Library authority record and YIVO.

ר׳ עקיבא איגר.event: ר׳ עקיבא איגר is born in Eisenstadt on 8 November 1761 to ר׳ משה גינז. See YIVO Encyclopedia and the City of Poznań.

As a youth, ר׳ עקיבא איגר studies in Mattersdorf before continuing his advanced training in Breslau. The year is an approximate educational marker, not a claimed enrollment date. See the City of Poznań biographical profile.
ר׳ עקיבא איגר studies in Breslau under ר׳ וולף אייבשיץ and gains recognition as a young Talmudic scholar. See the City of Poznań.
Following his marriage, ר׳ עקיבא איגר settles in Lissa, supported by his family while devoting himself to study and teaching. See the City of Poznań profile.
ר׳ עקיבא איגר becomes rabbi of Märkisch Friedland, leads a yeshiva and begins the long rabbinic correspondence later preserved in his responsa. See YIVO Encyclopedia.
ר׳ עקיבא איגר accepts the rabbinate of Posen, the office he holds for the remainder of his life. See YIVO Encyclopedia and the City of Poznań.

While serving Posen, ר׳ עקיבא איגר sees his concise notes begin appearing in the Prague Talmud of 1830–1835; these become the canonical גליון הש״ס. Printing in Prague is not treated as a relocation. See bibliographical summary and YIVO Encyclopedia.
ר׳ עקיבא איגר dies in Posen on 12 October 1837 after twenty-two years as the city's rabbi and is buried in its Jewish cemetery. See the City of Poznań.

ר׳ שלמה הירשל.event: ר׳ שלמה הירשל is born in London on 12 February 1762 while his father ר׳ צבי הירש לוין serves the Great Synagogue. See the Jewish Encyclopedia.

As a small child, ר׳ שלמה הירשל leaves England with his father, who resigns the London rabbinate and takes office in Halberstadt. He is subsequently educated in Germany and Poland. See the Jewish Encyclopedia.
ר׳ שלמה הירשל becomes rabbi of Prenzlau, where he serves for approximately nine years before his return to London. See the Dictionary of National Biography.

ר׳ שלמה הירשל.place: Great Synagogue, Duke's Place, City of London
ר׳ שלמה הירשל.event: The Great Synagogue appoints ר׳ שלמה הירשל as its rabbi in 1802. His authority is soon recognized across Britain's Ashkenazi communities, making him the first officeholder whose imperial Chief Rabbinate is effectively unquestioned. See the official History of the Chief Rabbinate.

ר׳ שלמה הירשל.place: Great Synagogue, Duke's Place, City of London
ר׳ שלמה הירשל.event: During ר׳ שלמה הירשל's tenure, the Great Synagogue receives a formal visit from three royal dukes in 1809; he also pioneers English-language preaching and national orders of service. See the official Chief Rabbinate history.

ר׳ שלמה הירשל.place: Great Synagogue, Duke's Place, City of London
ר׳ שלמה הירשל.event: Near the end of his rabbinate, ר׳ שלמה הירשל strongly opposes the newly formed West London Synagogue and its religious reforms, helping define the institutional separation of British Reform Judaism from the established Ashkenazi rabbinate. See the Jewish Encyclopedia.
ר׳ שלמה הירשל dies in London on 31 October 1842 and is buried in Brady Street Cemetery on 2 November. See the Dictionary of National Biography and Jewish Encyclopedia.

ר׳ שמחה בונים בונהרד מפשיסחה.event: ר׳ שמחה בונים בונהרד מפשיסחה is born in Wodzisław in 1765. See YIVO Encyclopedia.
As a young scholar, ר׳ שמחה בונים בונהרד מפשיסחה studies in the Central European yeshiva world, including Nikolsburg; the year is approximate. See the biographical chronology.
After periods in commerce and pharmacy, ר׳ שמחה בונים בונהרד מפשיסחה settles into the circle of the יהודי הקדוש at Przysucha; the year is approximate. See YIVO Encyclopedia.
Following the death of the יהודי הקדוש, ר׳ שמחה בונים בונהרד מפשיסחה becomes leader of the Peshischa movement. See YIVO Encyclopedia.
ר׳ שמחה בונים בונהרד מפשיסחה dies in Przysucha on 4 September 1827 and is buried there. See Encyclopedia Daat.

ר׳ נחמן מברסלב.event: ר׳ נחמן מברסלב is born in Medzhybizh on 1 Nisan 5532 (4 April 1772) to ר׳ שמחה and פייגא, a granddaughter of ר׳ ישראל בעל שם טוב. His paternal grandfather is ר׳ נחמן מהורודנקה. See the Oxford Bibliographies overview and YIVO Encyclopedia.

Shortly after turning thirteen, ר׳ נחמן מברסלב marries Sashia, daughter of ר׳ אפרים, and lives near her family for about five years while pursuing an unusually intense private devotional life. The broad sequence is documented by Oxford Bibliographies; the exact village identification varies in English transliteration, so the coordinates are regional.
ר׳ נחמן מברסלב moves to Medvedivka and begins functioning publicly as a Hasidic teacher, gradually attracting his first circle of followers. See the Encyclopaedia Judaica biography.

Traveling with ר׳ שמעון toward the Land of Israel, ר׳ נחמן מברסלב spends a difficult and deliberately inconspicuous interval in Ottoman Istanbul before securing passage onward. The journey is preserved in early Breslov sources and assessed in the National Library of Israel reconstruction.

ר׳ נחמן מברסלב lands at Haifa shortly before Rosh Hashanah 5559. He later treats setting foot in the Land of Israel as a transformative rupture in his spiritual development. See the National Library of Israel and Sefaria author profile.

In Tiberias, ר׳ נחמן מברסלב is received by ר׳ אברהם מקאליסק and spends much of his approximately three-and-a-half-month stay among the northern Hasidic community. He also visits the grave of his grandfather, ר׳ נחמן מהורודנקה. See the National Library account.

ר׳ נחמן מברסלב visits Safed and sacred sites in the Upper Galilee during his northern sojourn. Later devotional narratives elaborate these visits, but the broad itinerary is supported by the National Library of Israel reconstruction.

As Napoleon's campaign reaches the coast, ר׳ נחמן מברסלב reaches Acre amid an exodus of civilians and leaves aboard an Ottoman vessel on 17 March, two days before the siege begins. See the dated reconstruction by the National Library of Israel.

After mistakenly boarding a military rather than merchant vessel, ר׳ נחמן מברסלב and ר׳ שמעון endure a hazardous voyage and reach Rhodes, where the Jewish community helps redeem them from their predicament. See the National Library narrative.

Returning through Istanbul and the Black Sea, ר׳ נחמן מברסלב lands at Galați and continues overland home after further storms. The route is summarized by the National Library of Israel; details ultimately derive from Breslov travel traditions recorded by ר׳ נתן שטרנהרץ.

After returning from the Land of Israel, ר׳ נחמן מברסלב settles briefly in Zlatopil. His challenge to the condition of contemporary Hasidism contributes to a fierce dispute with ר׳ אריה לייב משפולה. See YIVO Encyclopedia.

ר׳ נחמן מברסלב moves to Bratslav and forms the distinctive community that takes the town's name. Here ר׳ נתן שטרנהרץ becomes his closest disciple and principal recorder, preserving teachings, stories and conversations. See YIVO on ר׳ נחמן and YIVO on ר׳ נתן שטרנהרץ.
Suffering from tuberculosis, ר׳ נחמן מברסלב travels to Lviv to consult physicians and remains there for several months before returning to Bratslav. See the Encyclopaedia Judaica biography.

The first part of ליקוטי מוהר״ן, the central collection of ר׳ נחמן מברסלב's discourses, is printed at Ostroh under the editorial care of his disciples. Its date and significance are documented by YIVO Encyclopedia; read the work on Sefaria.

Knowing his illness is terminal, ר׳ נחמן מברסלב moves to Uman, tells several of his major tales, teaches the ten-Psalm תיקון הכללי, and chooses burial near Jews killed in the 1768 massacre. He dies of tuberculosis on 18 Tishrei 5571 (16 October 1810) and is buried there. See Oxford Bibliographies, YIVO Encyclopedia and Sefaria.

ר׳ שלום רוקח מבעלזא.event: ר׳ שלום רוקח מבעלזא is born in Brody in 1779. See Encyclopedia Daat.
After being orphaned, ר׳ שלום רוקח מבעלזא is raised and educated in Sokal by his uncle ר׳ ישכר דב רמרז; the year is approximate. See the Belz dynasty history.
ר׳ שלום רוקח מבעלזא studies under ר׳ יעקב יצחק הורוביץ, the חוזה מלובלין; the year is approximate. See Encyclopedia Daat.
ר׳ שלום רוקח מבעלזא becomes rabbi of Belz and emerges as the first Belzer Rebbe. See the Belz dynasty history.
ר׳ שלום רוקח מבעלזא completes and dedicates the great Belz synagogue after personally directing its construction. See the World of Belz history.
ר׳ שלום רוקח מבעלזא dies in Belz on 10 September 1855 and is buried there. See the Belz institutional history.

ר׳ נתן שטרנהרץ מברסלב.event: ר׳ נתן שטרנהרץ is born in Nemyriv on 15 Shevat 5540 (22 January 1780) to ר׳ נפתלי הרץ in a prosperous, learned family opposed to early Hasidism. See YIVO Encyclopedia and the YIVO history of Nemyriv.

As a young teenager, ר׳ נתן שטרנהרץ marries Esther Shaindel, daughter of the prominent scholar ר׳ דוד צבי אוירבך, and continues intensive Talmudic and halakhic study. The exact domestic locations in early biographies vary; the marker represents his wife's family region. The autobiographical framework is preserved in ימי מוהרנ״ת, while his family and intellectual background are summarized by YIVO.
After unsatisfying visits to other Hasidic courts, ר׳ נתן שטרנהרץ meets ר׳ נחמן מברסלב in Bratslav and becomes his disciple despite family opposition. See YIVO Encyclopedia.

Traveling repeatedly between nearby Nemyriv and Bratslav, ר׳ נתן שטרנהרץ becomes the meticulous recorder and editor on whom ר׳ נחמן מברסלב increasingly relies for preservation of his discourses. See YIVO and the Breslov corpus on Sefaria.

ר׳ נתן שטרנהרץ helps bring the first part of ר׳ נחמן מברסלב's ליקוטי מוהר״ן to print at Ostroh, an early landmark in his lifelong editorial mission. The publication is discussed in the YIVO biography of ר׳ נחמן; the text is available on Sefaria.

ר׳ נתן שטרנהרץ attends ר׳ נחמן מברסלב during his final period in Uman and assumes responsibility for safeguarding the teachings after his death on 18 Tishrei 5571. He becomes the community's informal leader but never claims the title of rebbe. See YIVO Encyclopedia.

ר׳ נתן שטרנהרץ organizes the first annual Breslov Rosh Hashanah gathering at the grave of ר׳ נחמן מברסלב, establishing Uman as the movement's enduring pilgrimage focus. YIVO identifies him as the movement's post-1810 leader; the first gathering is also summarized in the YIVO profile and later pilgrimage historiography.

At Ostroh, ר׳ נתן שטרנהרץ publishes סיפורי מעשיות, preserving the symbolic tales told by ר׳ נחמן מברסלב in Hebrew and Yiddish. His editorial and publishing role is documented by YIVO; YIVO's history of Yiddish literature places the early edition in 1815–1816.

On his own hazardous pilgrimage to the Land of Israel, ר׳ נתן שטרנהרץ travels through Ottoman Istanbul during the Greek–Ottoman war. The trip is narrated firsthand in ימי מוהרנ״ת; its historical setting is summarized by the Breslov Research Institute.

ר׳ נתן שטרנהרץ reaches Ottoman Palestine during his 1822 pilgrimage and enters through Acre before visiting Jewish communities and sacred sites. The route is reconstructed primarily from his own ימי מוהרנ״ת; the Breslov Research Institute confirms the 1822 pilgrimage.

In the Galilee, ר׳ נתן שטרנהרץ visits Tiberias, Safed and graves associated with earlier kabbalists and Hasidic immigrants, interpreting the journey through the teachings of ר׳ נחמן מברסלב. These stages derive principally from his travel memoir ימי מוהרנ״ת, so the marker is regional rather than a claim of continuous residence.

ר׳ נתן שטרנהרץ reaches Jerusalem during the central phase of his pilgrimage, praying at holy places and recording the spiritual meaning of the visit. His firsthand source is ימי מוהרנ״ת; the date is corroborated by the Breslov Research Institute.

As the Rosh Hashanah gathering expands, ר׳ נתן שטרנהרץ raises funds for a dedicated prayer hall in Uman and composes prayers for use at the grave of ר׳ נחמן מברסלב. His role in developing the pilgrimage follows the scholarly overview in YIVO Encyclopedia and the movement's documented publication history.

During the anti-Breslov campaign led by ר׳ משה צבי מסאווראן, ר׳ נתן שטרנהרץ is denounced to the authorities, briefly arrested, restricted and forced away from Bratslav to Nemyriv. YIVO dates the most severe campaign to 1835–1839 and records his Nemyriv residence in 1835–1838; see YIVO on ר׳ נתן and YIVO on Nemyriv.

ר׳ נתן שטרנהרץ returns to Bratslav, rebuilds the embattled community and continues printing and circulating Breslov teachings with a press acquired for that mission. His leadership and publishing program are described by YIVO Encyclopedia.

ר׳ נתן שטרנהרץ dies in Bratslav on 10 Tevet 5605 (20 December 1844) and is buried in the Jewish cemetery there. He leaves Breslov without a successor-rebbe but with a durable textual, liturgical and pilgrimage infrastructure. See YIVO Encyclopedia.

ר׳ יצחק בן מאיר הכהן.event: ר׳ יצחק בן מאיר הכהן, later identified as the ritual slaughterer of Livorno and author of זבחי כהן, is born in 1780 according to the National Library of Israel authority record. See the National Library catalogue.

By adulthood ר׳ יצחק בן מאיר הכהן serves as shochet of Livorno’s Jewish community. The displayed year is approximate because no appointment document has been located; the office is stated on his book’s title page. See the digitized זבחי כהן catalogue record.

ר׳ יצחק בן מאיר הכהן publishes זבחי כהן in Livorno, recording local rules and traditions of shechita with bilingual terminology and anatomical and bird illustrations. See the National Library of Israel and the specialist study of kosher-species traditions.

ר׳ יצחק בן מאיר הכהן dies in 1849. The available authority record supplies the lifespan but no more precise death location; Livorno is used because it is his only securely documented centre of activity. See the National Library catalogue.

ר׳ ישראל בן גדליה ליפשיץ.place: Obersitzko, Kingdom of Prussia (present-day Obrzycko, Poland)
ר׳ ישראל בן גדליה ליפשיץ.event: ר׳ ישראל בן גדליה ליפשיץ is born in 1782 at Obersitzko in the Posen region to ר׳ גדליה ליפשיץ and Keila. See Encyclopaedia Judaica and the German biographical summary.
ר׳ ישראל בן גדליה ליפשיץ serves as rabbi in Wronki by 1821, the first securely dated office in the standard reference chronology. See Encyclopaedia Judaica.
By 1826, ר׳ ישראל בן גדליה ליפשיץ holds rabbinic office in Dessau and the surrounding district; references also associate part of the 1826–37 period with Colmar. See Encyclopaedia Judaica and דעת.
During his Dessau period, ר׳ ישראל בן גדליה ליפשיץ begins publishing portions of his Mishnah commentary תפארת ישראל; installments appear across roughly 1830–1850. See Yeshivat Har Etzion.

ר׳ ישראל בן גדליה ליפשיץ.place: Danzig, Kingdom of Prussia (present-day Gdańsk, Poland)
ר׳ ישראל בן גדליה ליפשיץ.event: ר׳ ישראל בן גדליה ליפשיץ becomes rabbi of Danzig in 1837 and remains the city's rabbinic leader for the rest of his life. See Encyclopaedia Judaica.

By about 1850, the principal installments of תפארת ישראל have appeared, establishing ר׳ ישראל בן גדליה ליפשיץ as a major modern commentator on the Mishnah. The commentary combines the concise יכין with longer analytical discussions called בעז. See Yeshivat Har Etzion and דעת.

ר׳ ישראל בן גדליה ליפשיץ dies in Danzig on 19 September 1860 (3 Tishrei 5621). Family tradition records that he died after synagogue prayers while still wrapped in tallit and tefillin. See the Hebrew study by Yeshivat Har Etzion and the German biographical record.

ר׳ צבי אלימלך שפירא.event: ר׳ צבי אלימלך שפירא was born at Jawornik Polski. The project uses 1783, while YIVO gives 1785. See the National Library authority record and YIVO Encyclopedia.

ר׳ צבי אלימלך שפירא.place: Rymanów and Lublin; approximate study period
ר׳ צבי אלימלך שפירא.event: As a young scholar, ר׳ צבי אלימלך שפירא entered the circles of ר׳ מנחם מנדל מרימנוב and ר׳ יעקב יצחק הלוי הורוביץ מלובלין; the displayed year is approximate and does not assert uninterrupted residence. See YIVO and Daat.

After earlier rabbinic service in small Galician communities, ר׳ צבי אלימלך שפירא served as rabbi of Strzyżów. Exact appointment dates are not securely established, so this marker is approximate. See Daat’s Hebrew biography.
ר׳ צבי אלימלך שפירא became rabbi of Munkács, where his resistance to religious modernisation generated communal conflict. The appointment year is approximate. See YIVO Encyclopedia.
After leaving Munkács, ר׳ צבי אלימלך שפירא returned to Dynów and developed the Hasidic court from which the Dinov dynasty emerged. See biographical overview and YIVO.
ר׳ צבי אלימלך שפירא died at Dynów on 18 Tevet 5601 (11 January 1841) and was buried there. See the National Library of Israel.

ר׳ אליעזר פאפו.event: ר׳ אליעזר פאפו is born in Sarajevo to ר׳ יצחק פאפו. Modern authorities differ between 1784, 1785 and 1786; this map uses the conventional 1785 birth year. See National Library of Israel and HaChacham HaYomi.

At approximately age twenty-seven, ר׳ אליעזר פאפו leaves Sarajevo for Ottoman Bulgaria and establishes the principal setting of his later rabbinic career. The exact month and intermediate route are not documented, so the marker uses Silistra rather than inventing an itinerary. See Orthodox Union biography.
ר׳ אליעזר פאפו briefly serves the Sephardi community of Bucharest before returning to Silistra. See HaChacham HaYomi.
ר׳ אליעזר פאפו begins serving as rabbi and head of the rabbinical court of Silistra, directing charity, adjudication and communal reconciliation. See HaChacham HaYomi.

While leading Silistra, ר׳ אליעזר פאפו brings his alphabetically organized ethical guide פלא יועץ to publication in Constantinople. The printing city does not imply that he relocated there. See Jewish Encyclopedia and National Library of Israel.

ר׳ אליעזר פאפו dies in Silistra on 20 Tishrei 5588 after ministering during an epidemic and is buried there. Some catalogues render the civil year as 1827; the Hebrew date used by HaChacham HaYomi falls in 1828. See HaChacham HaYomi.

ר׳ יעקב צבי מקלנבורג.event: ר׳ יעקב צבי מקלנבורג נולד בליסה בשנת 1785 למשפחת ר׳ גמליאל, בעיר שהייתה מרכז תורה חשוב. Encyclopaedia Judaica biography
ר׳ יעקב צבי מקלנבורג למד בליסה אצל ר׳ זכריה מנדל, בנו של ר׳ דוד טעבלי ומקורבו של ר׳ עקיבא איגר; השנה מקורבת. Etz Hayim commentator biography
ר׳ יעקב צבי מקלנבורג בחר תחילה במסחר לצד לימודו ולא ביקש משרת רבנות; תאריך ההתחלה משוער. Encyclopaedia Judaica biography
לאחר כישלון עסקיו קיבל ר׳ יעקב צבי מקלנבורג את רבנות קניגסברג, ובה כיהן ברציפות עד מותו. Encyclopaedia Judaica biography
ר׳ יעקב צבי מקלנבורג פרסם בקניגסברג את המהדורה הראשונה של הכתב והקבלה, פירוש שנועד לבסס את אחדות התורה שבכתב ושבעל פה. National Library of Israel authority and editions
מקניגסברג הצטרף ר׳ יעקב צבי מקלנבורג להתנגדות הרבנית לאספת הרפורמה בבראונשווייג; מקום הכינוס אינו מוצג כמקום מגוריו. YU Torah biographical study
ר׳ יעקב צבי מקלנבורג נפטר בקניגסברג בשנת 1865 לאחר שלושים וארבע שנות רבנות, וביקש בצוואתו שלא יינשאו עליו הספדים. Encyclopaedia Judaica biography

ר׳ מנחם מנדל שניאורסון.event: ר׳ מנחם מנדל שניאורסון is born in Liozna on 20 September 1789. See the Bibliothèque nationale de France authority record and Chabad biography.
The young ר׳ מנחם מנדל שניאורסון, raised in the household of his grandfather ר׳ שניאור זלמן מלאדי, moves with that court from Liozna to Liadi. See the Chabad biography.

After the upheaval of 1812 and the succession of his father-in-law ר׳ דוב בער שניאורי, ר׳ מנחם מנדל שניאורסון settles in Lubavitch and devotes years to study and writing. The displayed year reflects the court’s postwar establishment. See Chabad.org.
After initially refusing the role following ר׳ דוב בער שניאורי’s death, ר׳ מנחם מנדל שניאורסון formally accepts leadership of Chabad in 1831. See Chabad’s documented chronology.

ר׳ מנחם מנדל שניאורסון attends the government-called rabbinical conference in Saint Petersburg, opposing coercive educational reforms and enduring repeated detention during the proceedings. See Chabad biography.

Back in Lubavitch, ר׳ מנחם מנדל שניאורסון supports Jewish agricultural settlement and helps establish the colony of Shchedrin, while continuing to lead a rapidly growing Hasidic movement. See Chabad biography.
ר׳ מנחם מנדל שניאורסון dies in Lubavitch on 29 March 1866 (17 March Old Style) and is buried there. See the BnF authority record.

ר׳ יהודה אריה ליאון ביבאס.event: ר׳ יהודה אריה ליאון ביבאס נולד בקירוב בשנת 1789 בגיברלטר למשפחה ספרדית שמוצאה מתטואן. Jewish Community of Hebron biography
לאחר מות אביו עבר ר׳ יהודה אריה ליאון ביבאס לבית סבו בליבורנו, ובה רכש השכלה תורנית וכללית והוכשר כרב וכרופא; השנה מקורבת. Hebron biography
ר׳ יהודה אריה ליאון ביבאס ביקר בלונדון ופגש את משה מונטיפיורי, שעמו עמד בהמשך בקשר סביב חיזוק היישוב בארץ ישראל. Hebron biography
ר׳ יהודה אריה ליאון ביבאס חזר לגיברלטר והקים בה ישיבה שמשכה תלמידים מאנגליה, מאיטליה ומצפון אפריקה; השנה מקורבת. Hebron biography
ר׳ יהודה אריה ליאון ביבאס נתמנה לרבה הראשי של קורפו ושימש בה מנהיג רוחני במשך כשני עשורים. Encyclopaedia Judaica on Corfu
במסע הסברה בין קהילות אירופה פגש ר׳ יהודה אריה ליאון ביבאס בזמון את ר׳ יהודה אלקלעי והשפיע על תפיסתו בדבר עלייה מאורגנת ותחייה לאומית. Hebron biography
לאחר מות אשתו עלה ר׳ יהודה אריה ליאון ביבאס לארץ ישראל בשנת 1852 והתקבל ביפו בידי תלמידיו בדרכו לחברון. Hebron biography
ר׳ יהודה אריה ליאון ביבאס התיישב בחברון עם ספרייתו, נפטר בי״ז בניסן תרי״ב (6 באפריל 1852) ונקבר בבית העלמין היהודי העתיק. Hebron biography and tomb history

ר׳ יצחק ברנייס.event: ר׳ יצחק ברנייס is born at Weisenau near Mainz on 29 September 1792. See Das Jüdische Hamburg and the Deutsche Biographie.

ר׳ יצחק ברנייס studies at the University of Würzburg while learning Talmud under ר׳ אברהם בינג, making him one of the early German rabbis to unite university and advanced traditional study. See Das Jüdische Hamburg.
After Würzburg, ר׳ יצחק ברנייס works briefly in Munich as a private tutor in the Hirsch household. The year is approximate. See the Jewish Encyclopedia.
ר׳ יצחק ברנייס returns to the Mainz area as a private scholar before his call to Hamburg. See the Jewish Encyclopedia.

The German-Israelite community of Hamburg appoints ר׳ יצחק ברנייס its chief rabbinic authority. He accepts only with broad responsibility for religious and educational institutions and takes the title חכם. See Das Jüdische Hamburg and the Jewish Encyclopedia.

Under ר׳ יצחק ברנייס, Hamburg’s Talmud Torah school begins a major reform that adds German and general subjects while retaining traditional Jewish education. The historical Elbstraße site no longer survives, so the coordinate marks its former Neustadt vicinity. See Das Jüdische Hamburg’s institutional history.
ר׳ יצחק ברנייס issues a public halakhic declaration against the revised Hamburg Temple prayer book, arguing that its users do not fulfill the basic obligation of prayer. See Das Jüdische Hamburg.
ר׳ יצחק ברנייס dies of a stroke in Hamburg on 1 May 1849. He was buried at the Grindel cemetery; his gravestone was later transferred to Ohlsdorf. See Das Jüdische Hamburg.

ר׳ חיים הלברשטאם.event: ר׳ חיים הלברשטאם was born in Tarnogród in 1793 according to the common Polish chronology; some catalogues use 1797. See Wirtualny Sztetl and the National Library authority record.

ר׳ חיים הלברשטאם.place: Lublin and Galician study circles; approximate
ר׳ חיים הלברשטאם.event: As a young scholar, ר׳ חיים הלברשטאם encountered the circle of ר׳ יעקב יצחק הלוי הורוביץ מלובלין and later attached himself especially to ר׳ נפתלי צבי הורוביץ מרופשיץ. The year is approximate. See Wirtualny Sztetl.
Following his marriage, ר׳ חיים הלברשטאם studied with his father-in-law ר׳ ברוך פרנקל־תאומים, rabbi of Lipník and author of ברוך טעם. The year is approximate. See biographical overview.
ר׳ חיים הלברשטאם received his first communal rabbinate at Rudnik nad Sanem. The exact appointment year is uncertain. See Polish biographical record.
ר׳ חיים הלברשטאם became rabbi of Nowy Sącz, founded a major yeshiva and developed the Hasidic court that became the Sanz dynasty. See Wirtualny Sztetl.
While leading Sanz, ר׳ חיים הלברשטאם published the legal sections of דברי חיים on divorce documents and ritual baths. See the Wikimedia bibliographic image.
The principal responsa volumes of דברי חיים appeared during ר׳ חיים הלברשטאם’s final year, consolidating his standing as a leading Galician posek. See German bibliographic chronology.

ר׳ חיים הלברשטאם died in Nowy Sącz on 25 Nisan 5636 (19 April 1876) and was buried in the Jewish cemetery on Rybacka Street. His Torah discourses appeared posthumously as דברי חיים in 1877. See Wirtualny Sztetl and bibliographic chronology.

ר׳ שמואל בן יוסף שטראשון (הרש״ש).event: ר׳ שמואל בן יוסף שטראשון is born in Zaskevichi on 18 Heshvan 5554 (24 October 1793), according to the modern documentary reconstruction; older encyclopedias commonly print 1794. He is initially known as Zaskovitzer after his birthplace. The marker uses modern Zaskavichy, Belarus, the geographical identification supplied by gazetteers. See The Lost Library, YIVO Encyclopedia and the National Library of Israel authority record.

At approximately thirteen, ר׳ שמואל בן יוסף שטראשון marries Sarah, daughter of ר׳ דוד שטראשון, and joins her family in their village near Vilna. He takes the surname שטראשון; the precise modern identification of the village is uncertain, so this marker is a regional Vilna anchor rather than a claimed building location. See the Jewish Encyclopedia and Encyclopaedia Judaica. The year is approximate.

During Napoleon's invasion of 1812, the French army wrecks the distillery belonging to the family of ר׳ דוד שטראשון. The extended household moves into Vilna, where ר׳ שמואל בן יוסף שטראשון becomes permanently rooted. Commercial activity supports his study while his wife takes a leading role in managing the business. See the Jewish Encyclopedia and YIVO Encyclopedia.

In the study house founded by his father-in-law, ר׳ שמואל בן יוסף שטראשון devotes himself to intensive learning and studies with ר׳ אברהם דנציג, who cites him in בינת אדם and חכמת אדם under the name Zaskovitzer. The year is a representative early-Vilna marker, not a precisely dated commencement. See Encyclopaedia Judaica.

ר׳ שמואל בן יוסף שטראשון joins other scholars in establishing Yeshivat ha-Arba'im, an ambitious but short-lived Vilna institution. He continues the rigorous Lithuanian scholarly culture associated with the circle and legacy of ר׳ אליהו מווילנה. See the YIVO Encyclopedia of Jews in Eastern Europe.

By the 1840s, ר׳ שמואל בן יוסף שטראשון is delivering crowded daily Talmud lectures without payment at the synagogue on Popławska Street. Discussion in these sessions helps generate the notes later printed as הגהות הרש״ש. In 1843 his father-in-law dies, but Sarah and other relatives continue operating the family business so he can maintain his scholarly life. The exact synagogue building has not been securely identified, so the coordinate marks the historical district only. See the Jewish Encyclopedia and Encyclopaedia Judaica.

Vilna editions of Midrash Rabbah issued in 1843–1845 publish annotations by ר׳ שמואל בן יוסף שטראשון; further notes appear in 1855. His reputation spreads through both print and rabbinic correspondence, while he remains a communal leader and refuses the offered rabbinate of Suwałki. See the Jewish Encyclopedia and the National Library of Israel bibliography.

ר׳ שמואל בן יוסף שטראשון dies in Vilna on 21 March 1872 (11 Adar II 5632). His glosses on almost the entire Talmud and Mishnah are subsequently absorbed into standard Vilna-style editions, making הגהות הרש״ש part of everyday advanced Talmud study. See the Jewish Encyclopedia, YIVO Encyclopedia and the National Library of Israel.

ר׳ צבי הירש קלישר.event: ר׳ צבי הירש קלישר is born in Lissa on 24 March 1795 and later studies under ר׳ יעקב לורברבוים and ר׳ עקיבא איגר. See the Jewish Encyclopedia and Deutsche Biographie.
After marriage, ר׳ צבי הירש קלישר settles in Thorn, where he serves without salary as acting rabbi for the rest of his life. See Encyclopaedia Judaica and the Toruń city history.

During his Thorn rabbinate, ר׳ צבי הירש קלישר publishes אבן בוחן, beginning the major printed phase of his halakhic and philosophical work. Printing at Krotoschin does not imply residence there. See the Jewish Encyclopedia.

From Thorn, ר׳ צבי הירש קלישר promotes a colonization society for Palestine and sustained fundraising, agricultural and political preparation. The marker remains at his documented residence rather than falsely placing him in Palestine. See the detailed historical account.

ר׳ צבי הירש קלישר publishes דרישת ציון, arguing that Jewish restoration can begin through natural action, settlement and agriculture before miraculous redemption. See the scholarly monograph and Jewish Encyclopedia.
ר׳ צבי הירש קלישר dies in Thorn on 16 October 1874 and is buried locally after approximately fifty years of communal service. See the Deutsche Biographie and German biographical account.

ר׳ ישראל פרידמן מרוז׳ין.event: ר׳ ישראל פרידמן מרוז׳ין is born at Pohrebyshche on 5 October 1796. See the National Library of Israel.
After the death of his elder brother, the young ר׳ ישראל פרידמן מרוז׳ין assumes Hasidic leadership. See Encyclopedia Daat.
ר׳ ישראל פרידמן מרוז׳ין establishes his celebrated court at Ruzhyn; the year is approximate. See the YIVO Encyclopedia.
Russian authorities imprison ר׳ ישראל פרידמן מרוז׳ין on an unsubstantiated murder allegation. See the YIVO Encyclopedia.
After release and escape from Russia, ר׳ ישראל פרידמן מרוז׳ין re-establishes his court at Sadigura in Bukovina. See the YIVO Encyclopedia.
ר׳ ישראל פרידמן מרוז׳ין dies at Sadigura on 9 October 1850 and is buried there. See the National Library of Israel.

ר׳ יעקב יוקב עטלינגר.event: ר׳ יעקב יוקב עטלינגר is born in Karlsruhe on 17 March 1798 to ר׳ אהרן עטלינגר. See the Hebrew encyclopedia biography.
ר׳ יעקב יוקב עטלינגר studies in the yeshiva of ר׳ אברהם בינג while also attending Würzburg University. See the German biography.
ר׳ יעקב יוקב עטלינגר returns to Karlsruhe as a teacher at the Elias Wormser study house. See the German chronology.
ר׳ יעקב יוקב עטלינגר becomes primator of the Lemle-Moses Klaus in Mannheim, where ר׳ שמשון רפאל הירש studies under him. See the Leo Baeck Institute record.
ר׳ יעקב יוקב עטלינגר becomes chief rabbi and av bet din in Altona and establishes an influential yeshiva. See the career biography.
In response to Reform controversies, ר׳ יעקב יוקב עטלינגר establishes Der treue Zionswächter and its Hebrew supplement Shomer Tziyon HaNe'eman. See the publication history.
ר׳ יעקב יוקב עטלינגר dies in Altona on 7 December 1871 and is buried there. See the epigraphic grave record.

ר׳ מרדכי יוסף ליינר.event: ר׳ מרדכי יוסף ליינר is born in Tomaszów Lubelski around 1800. Sources vary between 1800, 1801 and 1802; this record follows YIVO’s chronology. See the YIVO Encyclopedia and Hartman Institute.
As a young man, ר׳ מרדכי יוסף ליינר joins the Hasidic school of ר׳ שמחה בונים מפשיסחה. The year is approximate. See peer-reviewed scholarship and Hartman Institute.

After the death of ר׳ שמחה בונים, ר׳ מרדכי יוסף ליינר follows ר׳ מנחם מנדל מקוצק and becomes a central disciple charged with guiding fellow Hasidim. The year is approximate. See peer-reviewed research.

Following a dramatic break with ר׳ מנחם מנדל מקוצק in 1839–1840, ר׳ מרדכי יוסף ליינר begins leading an independent circle, initially in Tomaszów. The exact cause and dating are disputed. See YIVO and Hartman Institute.

ר׳ מרדכי יוסף ליינר establishes his court in Izbica, founding the dynasty later known as Izbica–Radzyn and teaching disciples including ר׳ יהודה לייב איגר and ר׳ צדוק הכהן מלובלין. See YIVO and POLIN Virtual Shtetl.
ר׳ מרדכי יוסף ליינר dies in Izbica in 1854, traditionally on 7 Tevet 5614, and is buried in the local Jewish cemetery. See the YIVO Encyclopedia and the documented cemetery guide.

ר׳ שמואל דוד לוצאטו.event: ר׳ שמואל דוד לוצאטו is born in Trieste on 22 August 1800 to Hezekiah Luzzatto and Miriam Regina Lolli Cormons. See the Dizionario Biografico degli Italiani.

Still a teenager in Trieste, ר׳ שמואל דוד לוצאטו completes מאמר הניקוד after years of Hebrew poetry, grammar and biblical study pursued largely through self-education. See the documented early chronology.

While teaching privately in Trieste, ר׳ שמואל דוד לוצאטו publishes the first volume of כינור נעים and contributes philological and exegetical studies to Hebrew periodicals. See the Encyclopaedia Judaica-derived biography.

ר׳ שמואל דוד לוצאטו is appointed professor at the newly founded rabbinical college in Padua, where he teaches Bible, Hebrew philology, history and theology for the remainder of his life. See the Istituto Veneto biography and Treccani.

From Padua, ר׳ שמואל דוד לוצאטו publishes בתולת בת יהודה, helping restore scholarly attention to the Hebrew poetry of ר׳ יהודה הלוי while maintaining a vast European correspondence. See the biographical and bibliographical account.

ר׳ שמואל דוד לוצאטו begins publishing his Italian translation and Hebrew commentary on Isaiah, integrating philology, Masorah, ancient versions and a defense of prophetic unity. See the Treccani biography.

ר׳ שמואל דוד לוצאטו dies in Padua at the end of September 1865 after more than three decades of teaching. Italian institutional sources give 29 September, while some biographies give 30 September. See the Istituto Veneto record and Treccani.

ר׳ נתן מרקוס הכהן אדלר.event: ר׳ נתן מרקוס הכהן אדלר נולד בהנובר ב־15 בינואר 1803 לר׳ מרדכי אדלר. Jewish Encyclopedia
ר׳ נתן מרקוס הכהן אדלר קיבל סמיכה מר׳ אברהם בינג בווירצבורג ודוקטורט מאוניברסיטת ארלנגן, בשילוב הכשרה תורנית ואקדמית. Jewish Encyclopedia
ר׳ נתן מרקוס הכהן אדלר נתמנה לרב הראשי של הנובר ופעל להסדרת החינוך והקהילות במחוז. Jewish Encyclopedia
לאחר בחירה שכללה קהילות לונדון והפרובינציה נכנס ר׳ נתן מרקוס הכהן אדלר לתפקיד הרב הראשי של בריטניה והאימפריה. Office of the Chief Rabbi
ר׳ נתן מרקוס הכהן אדלר דחק במנהיגי בתי הכנסת הגדולים בלונדון להתאחד במסגרת ארגונית אחת. Office of the Chief Rabbi
האיחוד שקידם ר׳ נתן מרקוס הכהן אדלר הוכר בחוק כאיחוד הקהילות, וחיזק את מוסדות הרבנות, הכשרות והקבורה המשותפים. United Synagogue history
בעקבות ירידה בבריאותו העביר ר׳ נתן מרקוס הכהן אדלר חלק ניכר מתפקידיו לבנו ר׳ הרמן אדלר, שמונה לסגן הרב הראשי. Office of the Chief Rabbi
ר׳ נתן מרקוס הכהן אדלר נפטר בברייטון ב־21 בינואר 1890 ונקבר בבית העלמין של איחוד הקהילות בווילסדן. Jewish Encyclopedia

ר׳ שלמה הכהן רבינוביץ.event: ר׳ שלמה הכהן רבינוביץ was born at Włoszczowa around 1803. Some traditions give 1800 or 1801. See the YIVO Encyclopedia and ANU family record.
As a youth, ר׳ שלמה הכהן רבינוביץ studied in Piotrków under ר׳ אברהם צבי פצנובסקי and ר׳ דוד חריף. The displayed year is approximate. See the biographical account.
After marriage, ר׳ שלמה הכהן רבינוביץ lived in Przedbórz and worked as a Torah teacher. He also drew close to ר׳ ישכר בער מרדושיץ and later ר׳ משה בידרמן מלעלוב. See the biographical account.
ר׳ שלמה הכהן רבינוביץ was appointed communal rabbi of Radomsko, beginning the association that made the town a major Hasidic centre. See YIVO.
Following the death of ר׳ ישכר בער מרדושיץ, many followers accepted ר׳ שלמה הכהן רבינוביץ as rebbe; this marks the foundation of the Radomsk Hasidic dynasty. See YIVO Encyclopedia.

ר׳ שלמה הכהן רבינוביץ died in Radomsko on 29 Adar 5626 (16 March 1866) and was buried in the local Jewish cemetery. His teachings began appearing posthumously as תפארת שלמה in 1867. See the Radomsko memorial history and Encyclopaedia Judaica/JVL.

ר׳ שלמה גאנצפריד.event: ר׳ שלמה גאנצפריד is born in 1804 at Ungvár, today Uzhhorod in Ukraine, to ר׳ יוסף. The National Library catalogue preserves an 1802 authority variant, while modern scholarly references and standard biographies use 1804. See Encyclopaedia Judaica, Sefaria and the National Library record.

After his father dies when he is eight, the gifted ר׳ שלמה גאנצפריד comes under the guardianship of Ungvár’s rabbi and rosh yeshiva, ר׳ צבי הירש הלר. See the Encyclopaedia Judaica biography and the biographical synthesis.

At approximately fifteen, ר׳ שלמה גאנצפריד follows his guardian and teacher ר׳ צבי הירש הלר to Bonyhád. He remains in the yeshiva for nearly a decade, continuing intensive Talmud study until ordination and marriage. See the biographical account and the Jewish Encyclopedia.

After marriage and rabbinic ordination, ר׳ שלמה גאנצפריד briefly pursues commerce, including the wine trade, first around Homonna (Humenné) and then Ungvár. The year is approximate; the episode explains his later sensitivity to practical business law and the needs of working Jews. See the Jewish Encyclopedia and the modern biography.

Leaving an unsuccessful commercial career, ר׳ שלמה גאנצפריד accepts the rabbinate of Brezovica. He serves the community until 1849 and develops his program of clear, practical halakhic instruction. See the Encyclopaedia Judaica and the Jewish Encyclopedia.

While serving in Brezovica, ר׳ שלמה גאנצפריד publishes קסת הסופר, his practical code for scribes. ר׳ משה סופר endorses the book as essential knowledge for anyone receiving certification to write Torah scrolls, tefillin and mezuzot. See קסת הסופר on Sefaria and Encyclopaedia Judaica.

ר׳ שלמה גאנצפריד returns to his native Ungvár as a dayan on its rabbinical court. Serving in the Orthodox leadership associated with ר׳ מאיר אייזנשטטר, he sees the need to equip ordinary households with reliable knowledge of practical halakhah. See the Encyclopaedia Judaica, Sefaria and the biographical synthesis.

ר׳ שלמה גאנצפריד first publishes קיצור שולחן ערוך at Ungvár in 1864. Its concise Hebrew presents the laws of daily life to non-specialists; repeated editions, translations and classroom use rapidly make it one of the most influential Ashkenazi halakhic manuals. See Evyatar Marienberg’s peer-reviewed study, The 19th-century Kitzur Shulhan Arukh, Sefaria and the National Library collection.

At the 1869 Hungarian Jewish Congress in Budapest, ר׳ שלמה גאנצפריד acts as a leading spokesman for Orthodox Jewry during the dispute over national communal organization and the relationship with the Neolog movement. See Encyclopaedia Judaica and the Jewish Encyclopedia.

ר׳ שלמה גאנצפריד dies in Ungvár on 30 July 1886, traditionally 28 Tammuz 5646, after serving its rabbinical court for nearly four decades. His קיצור שולחן ערוך continues to shape household practice and Jewish religious education internationally. See the Jewish Encyclopedia, Encyclopaedia Judaica and Chabad’s author reference.

ר׳ צבי הירש חיות.place: Brody, Kingdom of Galicia and Lodomeria, Habsburg monarchy
ר׳ צבי הירש חיות.event: ר׳ צבי הירש חיות is born in Brody on 20 November 1805 (28 Marḥeshvan 5566) into the prosperous scholarly family of ר׳ מאיר חיות. Brody provides the setting for both his intensive rabbinic education and unusually broad general learning. See the YIVO Encyclopedia of Jews in Eastern Europe and the National Library of Israel authority record.

ר׳ צבי הירש חיות.place: Brody, Kingdom of Galicia and Lodomeria; education period approximate
ר׳ צבי הירש חיות.event: During his youth in Brody, ר׳ צבי הירש חיות studies with Galician authorities including ר׳ אפרים זלמן מרגליות and develops competence in languages, history, philosophy, and contemporary scholarship. His later intellectual circle includes ר׳ נחמן קרוכמל and ר׳ שלמה יהודה רפפורט. The year is representative because surviving biographies do not provide a semester-by-semester itinerary. See YIVO and the biographical summary in Encyclopaedia Judaica.

ר׳ צבי הירש חיות.place: Żółkiew (Zhovkva), Kingdom of Galicia and Lodomeria
ר׳ צבי הירש חיות.event: ר׳ צבי הירש חיות is appointed rabbi of the Żółkiew district in 1829 while still in his twenties. He remains there for more than twenty years, serving as communal rabbi while producing studies that combine traditional halakhic commitments with historical analysis of rabbinic literature. See the YIVO Encyclopedia.

ר׳ צבי הירש חיות.place: Żółkiew (Zhovkva), Kingdom of Galicia and Lodomeria
ר׳ צבי הירש חיות.event: While serving Żółkiew, ר׳ צבי הירש חיות publishes תורת נביאים, an early statement of his approach to tradition, rabbinic authority, and Talmudic method. Its appearance marks the growth of his reputation as a scholar who used modern organization and historical questions without abandoning halakhic authority. See Encyclopaedia Judaica.

ר׳ צבי הירש חיות.place: Żółkiew (Zhovkva), Kingdom of Galicia and Lodomeria
ר׳ צבי הירש חיות.event: ר׳ צבי הירש חיות publishes מבוא התלמוד, his best-known independent work, offering a structured account of the Oral Torah, halakhah, aggadah, interpretation, enactments, and the composition of rabbinic literature. Publication is attached to his secure Żółkiew rabbinate rather than to later printing locations. See the National Library of Israel catalogue and YIVO.

ר׳ צבי הירש חיות.place: Lwów (Lviv), Kingdom of Galicia and Lodomeria
ר׳ צבי הירש חיות.event: To comply with Austrian rules requiring district rabbis to demonstrate formal general education, ר׳ צבי הירש חיות travels to Lwów in the summer of 1846, passes external university examinations, and receives official permission to serve in the rabbinate. The evidence supports an examination certificate, not the doctorate sometimes claimed in popular accounts. See the YIVO Encyclopedia.

ר׳ צבי הירש חיות.place: Żółkiew (Zhovkva), Kingdom of Galicia and Lodomeria
ר׳ צבי הירש חיות.event: From Żółkiew, ר׳ צבי הירש חיות helps lead a circle of Galician rabbis and maskilim opposing the Reform rabbinical conferences in Germany and publishes מנחת קנאות. In the same period his responsa engage modern religious innovations while arguing from within traditional jurisprudence. See YIVO.

ר׳ צבי הירש חיות is elected rabbi of Kalisz in 1852. The move gives him a major Polish communal post, but his tenure is marked by opposition from sections of the local community; he remains for approximately three years. See the YIVO Encyclopedia and Encyclopaedia Judaica.

ר׳ צבי הירש חיות.place: Lwów (Lviv), Kingdom of Galicia and Lodomeria; final return
ר׳ צבי הירש חיות.event: After becoming seriously ill in 1855, ר׳ צבי הירש חיות leaves Kalisz and returns to Galicia. He dies in Lwów on 12 October 1855, aged forty-nine. This follows YIVO’s account of his return and the Galician biographical tradition; some popular summaries instead list Kalisz as the death place. See YIVO and the Hebrew reference entry at Da’at.

ר׳ יצחק אייזיק אייכנשטיין מזידיטשוב.event: ר׳ יצחק אייזיק אייכנשטיין מזידיטשוב is born in Galicia around 1805; the precise birthplace remains uncertain, so Sambir is used only as the family’s regional anchor. See the National Library catalogue.
As a young man, ר׳ יצחק אייזיק אייכנשטיין מזידיטשוב becomes a close disciple of his uncle ר׳ צבי הירש מזידיטשוב; the year is approximate. See the biographical account.
ר׳ יצחק אייזיק אייכנשטיין מזידיטשוב studies with and visits ר׳ שלום רוקח of Belz; the year is approximate. See the biographical summary.
After the death of the שר שלום, ר׳ יצחק אייזיק אייכנשטיין מזידיטשוב formally accepts leadership as Rebbe at Zidichov. See the Hebrew dynasty history.
ר׳ יצחק אייזיק אייכנשטיין מזידיטשוב dies at Zhydachiv on 4 June 1873 and is buried there. See the manuscript and biographical catalogue.

ר׳ שמשון רפאל הירש.event: ר׳ שמשון רפאל הירש is born in Hamburg on 20 June 1808. See the Neue Deutsche Biographie.
He studies Talmud and halakhah in Mannheim under ר׳ יעקב יוקב עטלינגר, who later ordains him. See the Neue Deutsche Biographie.
ר׳ שמשון רפאל הירש studies classical languages, history and philosophy at Bonn while preparing for public rabbinic leadership. See the Neue Deutsche Biographie.
