He becomes Landesrabbiner of Oldenburg, where he writes The Nineteen Letters and Horeb. See the Neue Deutsche Biographie.
He takes office as district rabbi based in Emden, serving the Aurich and Osnabrück districts and developing Jewish education. See the Neue Deutsche Biographie.
He becomes chief rabbi of Moravia and Austrian Silesia, based in Nikolsburg, and participates in political advocacy for Jewish civil rights. See the Neue Deutsche Biographie.
ר׳ שמשון רפאל הירש accepts the call of the Israelitische Religionsgesellschaft and builds its synagogue, schools and communal institutions. See the Frankfurter Personenlexikon.
He campaigns for Austritt, the legal right of Orthodox Jews to leave the general religious community while remaining Jewish citizens. See the Frankfurter Personenlexikon.
ר׳ שמשון רפאל הירש dies in Frankfurt on 31 December 1888 and is buried in the community cemetery on Rat-Beil-Straße. See the Frankfurter Personenlexikon.

ר׳ מאיר ליבוש בן יחיאל מיכל וייזר (המלבי.event: ר׳ מאיר ליבוש בן יחיאל מיכל וייזר is born in Volochysk on 19 Adar II 5569 (7 March 1809). After his father ר׳ יחיאל מיכל dies during his childhood, he is educated by his stepfather ר׳ לייב מוולוצ'יסק and by ר׳ משה הלוי הורוויץ. See YIVO Encyclopedia and ויקיפדיה העברית.

At approximately thirteen, ר׳ מאיר ליבוש בן יחיאל מיכל וייזר travels to Warsaw for advanced rabbinic study and becomes known as the ‘Volhynian prodigy.’ His early marriage and later divorce belong to this formative period; exact intermediate dates remain uncertain. See ויקיפדיה העברית and YIVO Encyclopedia.

In 1834, ר׳ מאיר ליבוש בן יחיאל מיכל וייזר travels through European centers including Pressburg, Trieste, Amsterdam and Breslau to present the manuscript of ארצות החיים and obtain approbations. Breslau is used for this map stage because it became the work's publication center in 1837; the event does not imply continuous residence there. See YIVO Encyclopedia and the National Library of Israel.

With the recommendation of ר׳ שלמה זלמן טיקטין, ר׳ מאיר ליבוש בן יחיאל מיכל וייזר receives his first communal rabbinate at Wreschen around 1837–1839. He publishes ארצות השלום in 1839 but experiences financial strain and communal friction. See YIVO Encyclopedia and ויקיפדיה העברית.

Around 1841, ר׳ מאיר ליבוש בן יחיאל מיכל וייזר becomes rabbi of the larger Kempen community, serving for approximately seventeen years and acquiring the sobriquet ‘the Kempener.’ In response to the 1844 Reform conference at Brunswick, he develops the program that becomes התורה והמצוה. See YIVO Encyclopedia and ויקיפדיה העברית.

In 1859, ר׳ מאיר ליבוש בן יחיאל מיכל וייזר becomes chief rabbi and preacher of Bucharest. He strengthens kashrut supervision, education, Hebrew printing and the eruv, while opposing liturgical and institutional reforms promoted by sections of the communal elite. See YIVO Encyclopedia and ויקיפדיה העברית.

On 18 March 1864, Romanian authorities arrest ר׳ מאיר ליבוש בן יחיאל מיכל וייזר, take him through Giurgiu and expel him across the Danube to Ruse after accusations by his opponents. In Ruse he is hosted by ר׳ אברהם בן ישראל רוזאניס. See ויקיפדיה העברית and the Jewish Encyclopedia.

After his expulsion, ר׳ מאיר ליבוש בן יחיאל מיכל וייזר petitions the Ottoman authorities in Constantinople without obtaining reinstatement, then spends roughly six months in Paris seeking diplomatic and communal assistance. The coordinate marks Paris, his longer documented stop. See Jewish Encyclopedia and ויקיפדיה העברית.

In spring 1865, ר׳ מאיר ליבוש בן יחיאל מיכל וייזר accepts the Łęczyca rabbinate formerly held by his father-in-law ר׳ חיים אוירבך. Opposition from both modernizing and Hasidic constituencies makes this another short tenure. See ויקיפדיה העברית and Jewish Encyclopedia.

After leaving Łęczyca, ר׳ מאיר ליבוש בן יחיאל מיכל וייזר serves for a short period as rabbi in Kherson. The precise starting year is not consistently reported; 1867 is an approximate map marker between his 1865 appointment and his move to Mogilev in 1870. See the Jewish Encyclopedia and YIVO Encyclopedia.

ר׳ מאיר ליבוש בן יחיאל מיכל וייזר (המלבי.place: Mogilev on the Dnieper, Russian Empire
ר׳ מאיר ליבוש בן יחיאל מיכל וייזר (המלבי.event: In 1870, ר׳ מאיר ליבוש בן יחיאל מיכל וייזר becomes rabbi of Mogilev on the Dnieper. Conflict with affluent modernizers leads to denunciation as a political offender and an official order expelling him from the city. See the Jewish Encyclopedia and the Russian Jewish Encyclopedia.

By approximately 1875, ר׳ מאיר ליבוש בן יחיאל מיכל וייזר serves as rabbi of Königsberg's Russian and Polish Jewish community. He remains there for about four years, continuing his writing amid further tensions with German Jewish reformers. See Russian Jewish Encyclopedia and Jewish Encyclopedia.

In 1879, ר׳ מאיר ליבוש בן יחיאל מיכל וייזר visits Vilna and is considered for its rabbinate after the death of ר׳ יצחק אליהו לנדא. The governor blocks his appointment because of the earlier political accusation attached to his Mogilev expulsion. See the Jewish Encyclopedia and ויקיפדיה העברית.

While traveling to accept the Kremenchuk rabbinate, ר׳ מאיר ליבוש בן יחיאל מיכל וייזר becomes ill and dies in Kyiv on 1 Tishrei 5640 (18 September 1879), the first day of Rosh Hashanah. He is buried in Kyiv. See the Jewish Encyclopedia, ויקיפדיה העברית and the National Library of Israel.

ר׳ ישראל ליפקין מסלנט.event: ר׳ ישראל ליפקין מסלנט is born in Žagarė to ר׳ זאב וולף ליפקין. See the Vilna Jewish history profile.
After marrying Esther Fega Eisenstein, ר׳ ישראל ליפקין מסלנט settles in Salant and studies under ר׳ צבי הירש ברוידא and ר׳ יוסף זונדל מסלנט. See the Hebrew biographical study.
ר׳ ישראל ליפקין מסלנט leads Meile's yeshiva and subsequently teaches independently in Zarzecze, developing the educational method later called Musar. See the Vilna profile.
After refusing leadership of the government rabbinical school, ר׳ ישראל ליפקין מסלנט leaves Vilna for Kovno and establishes a Musar-focused yeshiva. See the documented chronology.
ר׳ ישראל ליפקין מסלנט moves west and initially stays with the Hirsch brothers in Halberstadt while recovering his health. See the biographical account.
ר׳ ישראל ליפקין מסלנט establishes himself for a period in Memel and teaches across Prussia and Germany. See Jews in East Prussia.
From Königsberg ר׳ ישראל ליפקין מסלנט publishes the Hebrew halakhic and ethical journal Tevunah. See the publication history.
ר׳ ישראל ליפקין מסלנט spends about two years organising communal life among Russian Jewish immigrants in Paris. See the biographical manuscript description.
ר׳ ישראל ליפקין מסלנט dies in Königsberg on 2 February 1883; his grave was positively relocated in 2007. See the death and burial account.

ר׳ אברהם צבי הירש אייזנשטט.event: ר׳ אברהם צבי הירש אייזנשטט is probably born in Białystok in 1812 (תקע"ב) to ר׳ יעקב אשר אייזנשטט and Rachel. Later sources often give 1813, but a source-critical comparison with the contemporary report of his age at death favors 1812. He descends from ר׳ מאיר אייזנשטט, author of פנים מאירות. See Hanan Yitzhaki's specialist study and ויקיפדיה העברית.

At approximately fifteen, ר׳ אברהם צבי הירש אייזנשטט marries Yenta Reizel, daughter of Yehuda Leib HaKohen of Grodno, and remains in Białystok. She manages a stationery and paper-goods business while he studies in the beit midrash of ר׳ יחיאל נעכעס alongside ר׳ שמואל הלוי, author of בגדי ישע, and ר׳ גרשון חן טוב, author of מנחה חדשה. See המעין / מכון שלמה אומן and the cross-referenced English biography.

ר׳ אברהם צבי הירש אייזנשטט.place: Grodno, Russian Empire; now Hrodna, Belarus
ר׳ אברהם צבי הירש אייזנשטט.event: Around the early 1830s, after government offices that had patronized the family stationery business relocate, ר׳ אברהם צבי הירש אייזנשטט and his household move from Białystok to Grodno. When the business fails there, he accepts service as a dayan to support his family. The year is necessarily approximate because the surviving biography says only that this occurred several years before his 1836 rabbinate. See Hanan Yitzhaki's biographical reconstruction.

ר׳ אברהם צבי הירש אייזנשטט.place: Bristovitz, Grodno Governorate; now Vyalikaya Byerastavitsa, Belarus
ר׳ אברהם צבי הירש אייזנשטט.event: ר׳ אברהם צבי הירש אייזנשטט is appointed rabbi of Bristovitz in 1836. In the same year, following recovery from a serious illness, he publishes the first edition of פתחי תשובה on Yoreh De'ah in Vilna. The printing location documents publication, while Bristovitz is his evidenced residence and rabbinic post. See המעין and the contemporary-reference synthesis in the Jewish Encyclopedia.

ר׳ אברהם צבי הירש אייזנשטט.place: Utyan, Kovno Governorate; now Utena, Lithuania
ר׳ אברהם צבי הירש אייזנשטט.event: In 1856 (תרט"ז), ר׳ אברהם צבי הירש אייזנשטט accepts the Utyan community's invitation to become its rabbi and av beit din. He remains associated with Utyan through the rest of his working life while continuing the expansion of פתחי תשובה. See the dated appointment in Hanan Yitzhaki's study and the historical entry in the Jewish Encyclopedia.

ר׳ אברהם צבי הירש אייזנשטט.place: Königsberg, Kingdom of Prussia; now Kaliningrad, Russia
ר׳ אברהם צבי הירש אייזנשטט.event: During the winter of 5628, the seriously ill ר׳ אברהם צבי הירש אייזנשטט travels from Utyan to Königsberg for medical treatment. He dies there on Friday, 3 Elul 5628 (21 August 1868), aged approximately fifty-six, and is buried in the Königsberg Jewish cemetery near ר׳ יהודה אשכנזי of Tykocin and ר׳ יעקב צבי מקלנבורג. The 1868 date is confirmed by a contemporary Ha-Maggid notice and his son's family record, correcting a mistaken reading of the gravestone as 1865. See the documentary date analysis and ויקיפדיה העברית.

ר׳ עבדאללה סומך.event: ר׳ עבדאללה סומך, also known by the Hebrew name ר׳ עובדיה אברהם יוסף סומך, is born in Baghdad in 1813 to ר׳ אברהם יוסף יחזקאל and Khatun. His family traced its ancestry to ר׳ נסים גאון. See the National Library of Israel authority record and the Hebrew biographical account.

ר׳ עבדאללה סומך.place: Baghdad, Ottoman Iraq; educational year approximate
ר׳ עבדאללה סומך.event: As a youth in Baghdad, ר׳ עבדאללה סומך studies under ר׳ יעקב בר יוסף הרופא, who later calls him his distinguished and discerning pupil, and under ר׳ משה חיים. The displayed year is an approximate educational marker because the sources do not provide an enrollment date. See the contemporary-oriented Jewish Encyclopedia and the Hebrew Wikiyeshiva biography.

ר׳ עבדאללה סומך.place: Midrash Abu Menashi, later Midrash Beit Zilkha, Jewish quarter of Baghdad
ר׳ עבדאללה סומך.event: After leaving commerce to teach young scholars without payment, ר׳ עבדאללה סומך receives the support of Ezekiel Reuben Manasseh, who purchases a courtyard and establishes Midrash Abu Menashi in 1840. The institution develops into Midrash Beit Zilkha, which ר׳ עבדאללה סומך heads until his death. The exact historic building coordinates are not securely published, so this marker uses Baghdad's former Jewish-quarter area rather than claiming a surviving building footprint. See the institutional history and Encyclopaedia Judaica.

ר׳ עבדאללה סומך.place: Midrash Beit Zilkha, Baghdad; representative mid-career year
ר׳ עבדאללה סומך.event: By the middle decades of the nineteenth century, ר׳ עבדאללה סומך directs Baghdad's principal advanced rabbinic academy. Among the scholars formed in his circle are ר׳ יוסף חיים, ר׳ אליהו מני, ר׳ אברהם הלל, ר׳ יצחק מג׳לד, ר׳ ששון שמוחה and ר׳ שלמה בכור חוצין. The year marks a long teaching career rather than a single appointment. See the Hebrew biography and student list and the Jewish Encyclopedia.

A contemporary 1887 report describes ר׳ עבדאללה סומך as heavily occupied with questions sent to Baghdad from Persia and Central Asia, especially in divorce and marriage law. His responsa also reached Baghdadi communities in India and addressed the practical consequences of modernization. See the cited contemporary report and analysis in the Hebrew biography and the scholarly article on his halakhic response to change in Pe'amim.

During the 1889 cholera epidemic, ר׳ עבדאללה סומך falls ill while staying in a village near Baghdad and is brought back into the city for treatment. He dies in Baghdad on 18 Elul 5649 (13 September 1889). The village name appears in variant forms and cannot be geolocated securely, so no fabricated village marker is used. See the detailed Hebrew account and Encyclopaedia Judaica.

ר׳ עבדאללה סומך.place: Traditional shrine of Joshua the High Priest and Jewish cemetery, Baghdad
ר׳ עבדאללה סומך.event: Because epidemic regulations close the regular cemetery, ר׳ עבדאללה סומך is first buried, with gubernatorial permission, in the courtyard traditionally associated with Joshua the High Priest, west of the Tigris. Local opposition triggers a violent confrontation, arrests of Jewish leaders and wider anti-Jewish attacks. After official intervention, his remains are transferred about three months later to Baghdad's Jewish cemetery. Exact nineteenth-century grave coordinates are uncertain, so the marker is placed only at Baghdad level. See the near-contemporary Jewish Encyclopedia and the full Hebrew burial narrative.

ר׳ נפתלי צבי יהודה ברלין.event: ר׳ נפתלי צבי יהודה ברלין is born in Mir on 20 November 1816. See the YIVO Encyclopedia.
At fourteen he marries Rayna Batya, daughter of ר׳ יצחק מוולוז׳ין, and joins the scholarly household surrounding Volozhin Yeshiva. See the YIVO Encyclopedia.
ר׳ נפתלי צבי יהודה ברלין begins teaching regularly in the yeshiva and emerges as a candidate for its leadership. See the YIVO Encyclopedia.
He becomes principal rosh yeshiva of Volozhin, beginning approximately four decades of institutional leadership. See the YIVO Encyclopedia.
He participates in a Hovevei Zion conference and is chosen for an advisory role, lending rabbinic support to settlement in the Land of Israel. See the biographical chronology.
The Russian authorities close Volozhin Yeshiva amid conflict over state demands; ר׳ נפתלי צבי יהודה ברלין leaves the institution he led for decades. See the YIVO Encyclopedia.
ר׳ נפתלי צבי יהודה ברלין dies in Warsaw on 10 August 1893 and is buried in the Jewish cemetery on Okopowa Street. See the death and burial chronology.

ר׳ יצחק אלחנן ספקטור.event: ר׳ יצחק אלחנן ספקטור is born in Ros in the Grodno region in 1817 and first studies with his father ר׳ ישראל איסר. See the Jewish Encyclopedia.
After marrying at thirteen, he settles with his wife’s family in Vawkavysk and studies under ר׳ בנימין דיסקין, from whom he receives semikhah. See the Jewish Encyclopedia.
He accepts his first rabbinic appointment in Izabelin, beginning a succession of communal posts. See the Russian Jewish Encyclopedia.
ר׳ יצחק אלחנן ספקטור becomes rabbi of Biaroza. See the Jewish Encyclopedia.
He is appointed rabbi of Nyasvizh, where his growing reputation attracts halakhic inquiries. See the Jewish Encyclopedia.
He moves to the rabbinate of Novogrudok and remains there until 1864. See the Jewish Encyclopedia.
ר׳ יצחק אלחנן ספקטור becomes rabbi of Kovno, the office from which he emerges as a foremost authority of Russian Jewry. See the YIVO Encyclopedia.

Following anti-Jewish violence, he participates in conferences of Jewish communal leaders in Saint Petersburg and presses traditional Jewish concerns before the authorities. See the Jewish Encyclopedia.
ר׳ יצחק אלחנן ספקטור dies in Kovno on 6 March 1896 after thirty-two years as its rabbi. See the YIVO Encyclopedia.

ר׳ עזריאל הילדסהיימר.event: ר׳ עזריאל הילדסהיימר is born in Halberstadt on 11 May 1820. See Neue Deutsche Biographie and the National Library of Israel.
As an adolescent, ר׳ עזריאל הילדסהיימר studies at the Altona yeshiva of ר׳ יעקב עטלינגר while also acquiring classical languages. The year is approximate. See the Da’at Hebrew biography.

ר׳ עזריאל הילדסהיימר matriculates at the University of Berlin in 1843, studying Semitic languages, history, philosophy and mathematics alongside continuing Torah study. See the Neue Deutsche Biographie and German Wikipedia’s sourced chronology.
At Halle, ר׳ עזריאל הילדסהיימר completes doctoral studies in philosophy and Semitic scholarship in 1844. See the history of the Berlin Rabbinical Seminary.

ר׳ עזריאל הילדסהיימר becomes rabbi of Eisenstadt in 1851 and establishes a yeshiva and school combining rigorous Talmud study with languages and general education. See Neue Deutsche Biographie and the Da’at biography.

Invited by Berlin Orthodox Jews who reject Abraham Geiger’s appointment, ר׳ עזריאל הילדסהיימר becomes rabbi of the emerging Adass Jisroel community in 1869. See the documented Hebrew survey of German rabbis.

ר׳ עזריאל הילדסהיימר opens the Orthodox Rabbinical Seminary in Berlin in 1873, institutionalizing his synthesis of yeshiva learning, academic Jewish studies and preparation for communal leadership. See the seminary history and Da’at’s Berlin community history.
ר׳ עזריאל הילדסהיימר dies in Berlin on 12 June 1899 and is buried in the Adass Jisroel cemetery. See Neue Deutsche Biographie and Wikimedia authority data.

ר׳ יוסף דובער הלוי סולובייצ׳יק.place: Nesvizh, Minsk Governorate, Russian Empire; now Belarus
ר׳ יוסף דובער הלוי סולובייצ׳יק.event: ר׳ יוסף דובער הלוי סולובייצ׳יק is born around 1820 in Nesvizh to ר׳ יצחק זאב הלוי סולובייצ׳יק and Rivka. His maternal ancestry connects him to ר׳ חיים מוולוז׳ין. The exact day is unknown. See the Hebrew biography and genealogical source study.

ר׳ יוסף דובער הלוי סולובייצ׳יק.place: Volozhin, Minsk Governorate, Russian Empire; date approximate
ר׳ יוסף דובער הלוי סולובייצ׳יק.event: As a boy of about ten, ר׳ יוסף דובער הלוי סולובייצ׳יק is sent to Volozhin for private study and then enters the yeshivah, developing the textual mastery that shapes his career. The year is approximate. See the Hebrew biographical account and bibliographic record for the scholarly biography.

While still a young scholar, ר׳ יוסף דובער הלוי סולובייצ׳יק teaches in Minsk, associated in later accounts with Bluma’s kloyz and with replacing the local lecturer ר׳ גרשון תנחום. The episode is secure in the biographical tradition, but its precise year is not. See the genealogical-biographical study.

After the death of ר׳ אליעזר יצחק פריד, ר׳ יוסף דובער הלוי סולובייצ׳יק joins ר׳ נפתלי צבי יהודה ברלין in leading the Volozhin Yeshiva. He serves as the Netziv’s deputy and delivers advanced Talmudic instruction until leaving in 1865. See the cross-referenced biography and the Hebrew rabbinic dictionary.

ר׳ יוסף דובער הלוי סולובייצ׳יק becomes rabbi of Slutsk in 1865. He teaches advanced students including ר׳ יוסף רוזין and ר׳ זלמן סנדר שפירא, and communal accounts credit him with arranging meals for impoverished schoolchildren. See the biographical synthesis and the Hebrew biography.

ר׳ יוסף דובער הלוי סולובייצ׳יק.place: Warsaw, Congress Poland; transition dated approximately
ר׳ יוסף דובער הלוי סולובייצ׳יק.event: After conflict with communal modernizers and Slutsk leaders, ר׳ יוסף דובער הלוי סולובייצ׳יק resigns and moves to Warsaw, where he lives without a formal rabbinate and experiences financial hardship. Accounts date the resignation to 1874 or 1875; this map uses 1874 while preserving the uncertainty. See the biographical synthesis and Hebrew collected biography.

After ר׳ יהושע לייב דיסקין leaves Brisk for Jerusalem, the community appoints ר׳ יוסף דובער הלוי סולובייצ׳יק as its rabbi. Sources place the beginning in 1877–1879; 1878 is a midpoint marker rather than a claimed exact inauguration year. He serves Brisk for the remainder of his life. See the Hebrew biography and cross-reference.

ר׳ יוסף דובער הלוי סולובייצ׳יק.place: Brisk/Brest-Litovsk, Russian Empire; now Brest, Belarus
ר׳ יוסף דובער הלוי סולובייצ׳יק.event: ר׳ יוסף דובער הלוי סולובייצ׳יק dies in Brisk on ד׳ באייר תרנ״ב (1 May 1892) and is buried in the city’s Jewish cemetery. Contemporary reporting described the community’s public mourning; his son ר׳ חיים הלוי סולובייצ׳יק succeeds him. See the Hebrew article quoting the funeral report and the Wikimedia portrait record.

ר׳ צדוק הכהן מלובלין.event: ר׳ צדוק הכהן מלובלין is born on 23 Shevat 5583 (4 February 1823) in Kreuzburg, now Krustpils in Latvia, to the Lithuanian rabbi ר׳ יעקב הכהן. See YIVO Encyclopedia and Encyclopaedia Judaica.

Orphaned as a young child, ר׳ צדוק הכהן מלובלין is raised and educated by his uncle ר׳ יוסף בן אשר, a student of ר׳ חיים מוולוז׳ין. His early reputation gives rise to the designation 'the prodigy of Krynki.' See Encyclopaedia Judaica. The coordinates are regional because the surviving reference does not establish a precise residence.

ר׳ צדוק הכהן מלובלין marries young into a wealthy family, allowing him to continue intensive study. A subsequent marital crisis leads him to seek an exceptional heter me'ah rabbanim from one hundred rabbis. YIVO and Encyclopaedia Judaica report the episode, but exact dates, allegations and itinerary are not secure; this is intentionally a regional marker.

During travels through Poland seeking rabbinic authorization, ר׳ צדוק הכהן מלובלין reaches the Lublin region and encounters Hasidic teachers. This journey marks his transition from a Lithuanian non-Hasidic formation toward Hasidism. See Encyclopaedia Judaica; the year is approximate.

ר׳ צדוק הכהן מלובלין becomes a disciple of ר׳ מרדכי יוסף ליינר מאיזביצה, whose radical exploration of providence, will, sin and divine purpose permanently reshapes his thought. See YIVO Encyclopedia, Encyclopaedia Judaica and his Sefaria author profile. The first year of discipleship is approximate.

After ר׳ מרדכי יוסף ליינר dies, ר׳ צדוק הכהן מלובלין supports his friend ר׳ יהודה לייב איגר as leader of the Lublin Hasidic circle. For more than thirty years ר׳ צדוק studies, writes and lives in relative seclusion rather than claiming leadership. See YIVO and Encyclopaedia Judaica.

Following the death of ר׳ יהודה לייב איגר, ר׳ צדוק הכהן מלובלין reluctantly accepts leadership of the Lublin Hasidim. His public sermons from this final period are later collected in פרי צדיק. See YIVO Encyclopedia, Encyclopaedia Judaica and the digitized work.

In his final years, ר׳ צדוק הכהן מלובלין continues teaching and writing but declines to publish most manuscripts during his lifetime, while indicating that they should appear after his death. Many unpublished manuscripts will later be lost in the Lublin ghetto. See Encyclopaedia Judaica and the National Library of Israel catalogue.

ר׳ צדוק הכהן מלובלין dies on 9 Elul 5660 (3 September 1900) in Lublin. Posthumous publication begins almost immediately: פרי צדיק starts appearing in 1901 and צדקת הצדיק in 1902. See YIVO, Encyclopaedia Judaica and צדקת הצדיק on Sefaria.

ר׳ שמחה זיסל זיו.event: ר׳ שמחה זיסל זיו was born in Kelmė, Lithuania, then in the Russian Empire, into the Broida family. JewAge biography
In Kovno, ר׳ שמחה זיסל זיו became a leading disciple of ר׳ ישראל סלנטר and committed himself to the emerging Musar programme. The year is approximate. Kelm Yizkor Book
Returning to Kelmė, ר׳ שמחה זיסל זיו founded the Kelm Talmud Torah, whose disciplined curriculum made the town a major centre of Musar education. JewAge biography; Kelm Yizkor Book
After official pressure on the Kelm school, ר׳ שמחה זיסל זיו transferred the institution to Grobiņa in Courland. JewAge biography
Poor health compelled ר׳ שמחה זיסל זיו to return to Kelmė. He continued directing a select Musar circle there while the Grobiņa branch survived until 1886. JewAge biography
From Kelmė, ר׳ שמחה זיסל זיו encouraged a group of disciples to settle in Ottoman Palestine, extending the Kelm Musar network. JewAge biography
ר׳ שמחה זיסל זיו died in Kelmė on 26 July 1898, the eve of Tisha B’Av. JewAge biography; Kelm Yizkor Book

ר׳ יחיאל מיכל הלוי אפשטיין.event: ר׳ יחיאל מיכל הלוי אפשטיין is born in Bobruisk on 24 January 1829. See the YIVO Encyclopedia and Oxford Bibliographies.
As a young teenager he studies briefly at Volozhin Yeshiva under ר׳ יצחק מוולוז'ין. See Encyclopaedia Judaica’s biography.
He returns to Bobruisk, studies under ר׳ אליהו גולדברג, works for a time in commerce and later assists the local rabbinical court. See Oxford Bibliographies.
He accepts his first communal rabbinate in Novozybkov, serving a town containing both Chabad Hasidim and non-Hasidim. See My Jewish Learning.
ר׳ יחיאל מיכל הלוי אפשטיין becomes rabbi of Novogrudok and remains its principal halakhic authority for the rest of his life. See the YIVO Encyclopedia.
The first volume of Aruch HaShulchan, on Choshen Mishpat, appears while he is serving in Novogrudok; later divisions are printed through 1907. See the scholarly history of the work.
ר׳ יחיאל מיכל הלוי אפשטיין dies in Novogrudok in 1908 after more than three decades as its rabbi. See the YIVO Encyclopedia.

ר׳ חיים חזקיהו מדיני.event: ר׳ חיים חזקיהו מדיני is born in Jerusalem on 7 Cheshvan 5593 (1832) to ר׳ רפאל אשר אליהו מדיני and Kalu Vida. Older sources variously print 1833 or 1834, but the National Library authority record and Encyclopaedia Judaica use 1832. See the National Library of Israel, Encyclopaedia Judaica and the Hebrew HaChacham HaYomi biography.

ר׳ חיים חזקיהו מדיני.place: Jerusalem, Ottoman Palestine; educational date approximate
ר׳ חיים חזקיהו מדיני.event: As a young Jerusalem scholar, ר׳ חיים חזקיהו מדיני studies under ר׳ יצחק קובו and ר׳ יוסף נסים בורלא. He marries Rivka at eighteen and receives rabbinic ordination at approximately nineteen; 1848 is an approximate educational marker because the references do not give a full year-by-year study record. See Encyclopaedia Judaica and the Jewish Encyclopedia.

ר׳ חיים חזקיהו מדיני.place: Constantinople, Ottoman Empire; now Istanbul, Türkiye
ר׳ חיים חזקיהו מדיני.event: Following his father's sudden death, ר׳ חיים חזקיהו מדיני moves with his wife, widowed mother and two sisters from Jerusalem to Constantinople. He supports the household partly by tutoring, teaches publicly without payment and devotes himself to study and writing during a fourteen-year residence. See Encyclopaedia Judaica and HaChacham HaYomi.

While living in Constantinople, ר׳ חיים חזקיהו מדיני publishes his first work, מכתב לחזקיהו, containing Talmudic novellae and responsa. The book was printed in Smyrna, but the printing place is not treated as a personal move. See the Jewish Encyclopedia and the National Library of Israel catalogue.

ר׳ חיים חזקיהו מדיני.place: Karasubazar, Crimea, Russian Empire; now Bilohirsk, Ukraine
ר׳ חיים חזקיהו מדיני.event: ר׳ חיים חזקיהו מדיני accepts the rabbinate of Karasubazar in Crimea. During thirty-two years of leadership he establishes schools and yeshivot, introduces communal regulations, corrects practices he considers mistaken and works closely with the Krymchak Jewish community. See Encyclopaedia Judaica and the Jewish Encyclopedia.

From Karasubazar, ר׳ חיים חזקיהו מדיני begins issuing volumes of שדי חמד, the encyclopedic halakhic project he has assembled through extensive reading and correspondence. Thirteen of its eighteen volumes appear during his lifetime; Warsaw is a printing location, not evidence that he relocated there. See Encyclopaedia Judaica, the Hebrew text at Wikisource and the National Library catalogue.

After more than three decades in Crimea, ר׳ חיים חזקיהו מדיני returns to Jerusalem in 1899 and remains there for approximately two years. When his name is advanced for the Sephardi chief rabbinate, he seeks a quieter setting in which to continue his scholarship. See Encyclopaedia Judaica and the Jewish Community of Hebron biography.

ר׳ חיים חזקיהו מדיני moves to Hebron in 1901, hoping to study and complete his writings away from public office. He teaches from Beit Romano, where his study and library become a scholarly centre. See the Jewish Community of Hebron and Encyclopaedia Judaica.

After the deaths of Hebron's leading rabbis ר׳ אליהו מני and ר׳ חיים רחמים יוסף פרנקו, ר׳ חיים חזקיהו מדיני reluctantly accepts communal leadership and serves as Hebron's rabbi until his death. The references place his Hebron move and ensuing rabbinate in 1901, without securely dating the interval between them more precisely. See Encyclopaedia Judaica and the Jewish Community of Hebron biography.

ר׳ חיים חזקיהו מדיני.place: Ancient Jewish cemetery, Hebron, Ottoman Palestine
ר׳ חיים חזקיהו מדיני.event: ר׳ חיים חזקיהו מדיני dies in Hebron on 24 Kislev 5665 (1904) and is buried in the city's ancient Jewish cemetery. His library and correspondence dispersed after his death, while remaining portions and later editions of שדי חמד continued to appear. See the National Library of Israel, HaChacham HaYomi and the Hebron community biography.

ר׳ יוסף חיים מבגדאד.event: ר׳ יוסף חיים מבגדאד is born in Baghdad in 1835 to ר׳ אליהו חיים, in a family central to the city’s rabbinic leadership. See the National Library of Israel authority record and NLI biography catalogue.

Around age ten ר׳ יוסף חיים מבגדאד begins advanced study with his uncle ר׳ דוד חי בן מאיר and later learns in the academy of ר׳ עבדאללה סומך. The year marks the documented childhood transition approximately. See the sourced biography.

After his father’s death, ר׳ יוסף חיים מבגדאד assumes Baghdad’s principal weekly preaching role, addressing large audiences for roughly fifty years without taking a salaried chief-rabbinic office. See the documentary biography and contemporary material.

In 1869 ר׳ יוסף חיים מבגדאד makes a pilgrimage from Baghdad to Jerusalem, Hebron and sacred sites, meeting local scholars and strengthening his connection with the Land of Israel before returning home. See the NLI-catalogued scholarly biography.

The teachings of ר׳ יוסף חיים מבגדאד are published as בן איש חי, arranging practical halakhah and kabbalistic exposition by the weekly Torah portions; the book gives him his best-known title. See Sefaria’s work description.
On 30 August 1909 ר׳ יוסף חיים מבגדאד dies after more than half a century of public teaching and is buried in Baghdad. See the National Library account and contemporary obituary material.

ר׳ ישראל מאיר הכהן קגן.event: ר׳ ישראל מאיר הכהן קגן is born in Zhetel in 1838. See the National Library of Israel bibliography and biographical chronology.
After his father’s death, the young ר׳ ישראל מאיר הכהן קגן moves to Vilna and continues intensive Torah study. See the Oxford Bibliographies survey.
Following marriage, he settles in Radin, the small town that remains the centre of his teaching and writing for most of his life. See the National Library of Israel bibliography.
ר׳ ישראל מאיר הכהן קגן helps establish the Radin Yeshiva, which develops into an important centre of Torah and mussar study. See the Radin Yeshiva history.
During the First World War, the Radin yeshiva community is displaced eastward; ר׳ ישראל מאיר הכהן קגן spends part of the wartime exile in Smilovichi. See the yeshiva chronology.
After wartime displacement, he returns to Radin and resumes leadership, writing and public advocacy. See the Radin Yeshiva history.
ר׳ ישראל מאיר הכהן קגן dies in Radin on 15 September 1933 and is buried there. See the National Library of Israel bibliography.

ר׳ אברהם בורנשטיין.event: ר׳ אברהם בורנשטיין was born in Będzin in Congress Poland to ר׳ זאב נחום בורנשטיין. Some popular chronologies give 1838, while Encyclopaedia Judaica gives 1839. Encyclopaedia Judaica/JVL
As a young scholar, ר׳ אברהם בורנשטיין joined the Kotsk circle, becoming a close disciple and eventually son-in-law of ר׳ מנחם מנדל מורגנשטרן. The year is approximate. Biographical chronology
After the death of ר׳ מנחם מנדל מורגנשטרן, ר׳ אברהם בורנשטיין accepted the rabbinate of Parczew, the first of his documented communal posts. Encyclopaedia Judaica/JVL
ר׳ אברהם בורנשטיין became rabbi of Krośniewice, continuing to teach the analytical method later expressed in his responsa. Encyclopaedia Judaica/JVL
ר׳ אברהם בורנשטיין assumed the rabbinate of Nasielsk, where his growing following combined Kotsk Hasidism with advanced halakhic study. Encyclopaedia Judaica/JVL
ר׳ אברהם בורנשטיין became rabbi of Sochaczew, founded a major yeshiva, and emerged as the first Sochatchover Rebbe. Fundacja Brama Cukermana; Encyclopaedia Judaica/JVL

From Sochaczew, ר׳ אברהם בורנשטיין sent his son and son-in-law to Ottoman Palestine to investigate land for an observant agricultural colony; Ottoman rules prevented the purchase. Because he did not travel personally, this remains a Sochaczew event. Encyclopaedia Judaica/JVL
In Sochaczew, ר׳ אברהם בורנשטיין published אגלי טל, his systematic study of the Sabbath labours. Encyclopaedia Judaica/JVL
ר׳ אברהם בורנשטיין died in Sochaczew and was buried in the Jewish cemetery there. His son ר׳ שמואל בורנשטיין succeeded him as second rebbe. Encyclopaedia Judaica/JVL

ר׳ נפתלי צבי הירש הכהן אדלר.event: ר׳ נפתלי צבי הירש הכהן אדלר is born in Hanover on 30 May 1839 to ר׳ נתן מרקוס אדלר. See the Jewish Encyclopedia.
The Adler family moves to London after ר׳ נתן מרקוס אדלר becomes chief rabbi; ר׳ נפתלי צבי הירש הכהן אדלר later attends University College School and University College. See the German biography.
ר׳ נפתלי צבי הירש הכהן אדלר undertakes rabbinical study in Prague and receives authorisation from ר׳ שלמה יהודה ליב רפפורט. See the contemporary encyclopedia account.
ר׳ נפתלי צבי הירש הכהן אדלר receives his doctorate from Leipzig University. See the biographical chronology.
ר׳ נפתלי צבי הירש הכהן אדלר becomes principal of Jews' College and the next year minister of Bayswater Synagogue. See the Jewish Encyclopedia.
ר׳ נפתלי צבי הירש הכהן אדלר begins his long ministry at Bayswater Synagogue. See the office history.
ר׳ נפתלי צבי הירש הכהן אדלר succeeds his father as Chief Rabbi of the British Empire. See the Jewish Encyclopedia.
ר׳ נפתלי צבי הירש הכהן אדלר dies in London on 18 July and is buried at Willesden Jewish Cemetery. See the Jewish Communities and Records biography.

ר׳ מאיר שמחה הכהן מדווינסק.event: ר׳ מאיר שמחה הכהן מדווינסק is born in Butrimonys in 1843. See the Jewish Virtual Library biography.
After marriage at about seventeen, ר׳ מאיר שמחה הכהן מדווינסק settles in Białystok and continues intensive independent study while his wife supports the family. See the biographical chronology.

He becomes rabbi of Dvinsk’s non-Hasidic community and serves there for nearly four decades, alongside ר׳ יוסף רוזין of the Hasidic community. See the Association of Latvian and Estonian Jews archive.

During the First World War and the severe disruption surrounding Dvinsk, he remains a central communal authority involved in sustaining Jewish religious and relief life. See the Latvian Jewish historical archive.
ר׳ מאיר שמחה הכהן מדווינסק dies in Riga on 14 August 1926 while seeking medical treatment; he is subsequently buried in Dvinsk. See the biographical chronology.

ר׳ יהודה אריה ליב אלתר.event: ר׳ יהודה אריה ליב אלתר is born in Warsaw on 15 April 1847, 29 Nisan 5607, to ר׳ אברהם מרדכי אלתר and Esther Landsztajn. See the Hebrew Daat biography and referenced chronology.

Orphaned of both parents, ר׳ יהודה אריה ליב אלתר moves into the household of his grandfather ר׳ יצחק מאיר אלתר in Góra Kalwaria and receives his formative education there. The year follows his father’s death when he was about eight. See the biographical chronology and the Hebrew profile.

Around age ten, ר׳ יהודה אריה ליב אלתר accompanies his grandfather to ר׳ מנחם מנדל מקוצק, an encounter remembered as spiritually formative. The displayed year is approximate. See the referenced biography.
ר׳ יהודה אריה ליב אלתר marries Yocheved Rivka, daughter of ר׳ יהודה ליב Kaminer. To avoid sharing his father-in-law’s exact name, Aryeh is added to his own. See the documented family chronology.

ר׳ יהודה אריה ליב אלתר.place: Góra Kalwaria and Aleksandrów Łódzki, Congress Poland
ר׳ יהודה אריה ליב אלתר.event: After the death of ר׳ יצחק מאיר אלתר, ר׳ יהודה אריה ליב אלתר declines the Ger leadership and accepts ר׳ חנוך העניך הכהן לוין of Aleksander as rebbe. Góra Kalwaria remains his home base. See the Hebrew historical profile.

Following the death of ר׳ חנוך העניך הכהן לוין, the twenty-three-year-old ר׳ יהודה אריה ליב אלתר accepts leadership of Ger Hasidism. He also serves as av beit din and teaches the discourses later collected as שפת אמת. See Daat and the scholarly history of Ger leadership.

Yocheved Rivka, the first wife of ר׳ יהודה אריה ליב אלתר, dies in 1901. He later marries Reyzl, daughter of ר׳ ברוך הלברשטאם of Gorlice, while continuing to lead the expanding Ger community. See the Hebrew biography.

During the Russo-Japanese War, ר׳ יהודה אריה ליב אלתר corresponds with and supports Hasidim conscripted into the Russian army. His final illness is remembered in Ger tradition as aggravated by anguish over their fate. See the Encyclopaedia Judaica-derived biography.

ר׳ יהודה אריה ליב אלתר dies in Ger on 11 January 1905, 5 Shevat 5665, and is buried beside his grandfather. His son ר׳ אברהם מרדכי אלתר succeeds him; the first volume of his posthumous Torah discourses appears that year. See Daat and the first-edition description.

ר׳ יוסף יוזל הורביץ.event: ר׳ יוסף יוזל הורביץ is born in Plungė (Plungyan), Lithuania, into the family of ר׳ שלמה זלמן זיו הורביץ. His birth year is reported variously as 1847, 1848 or 1850; this map uses the well-attested 1847 chronology. See the Posen Library biography and the National Library of Israel authority record.

As an adolescent, ר׳ יוסף יוזל הורביץ receives an intensive traditional education associated with Kurtuvėnai and the Kelmė milieu and is already teaching by about sixteen. His father served in Kurtuvėnai. The displayed year is an approximate educational marker. See the Posen Library and biographical synthesis with cited references.

At about eighteen, ר׳ יוסף יוזל הורביץ marries the daughter of ר׳ יעקב שטיין and assumes responsibility for his father-in-law’s prosperous textile business in Švėkšna. The year follows the approximate age given in the surviving biography. See the documented biographical summary.

Around age twenty-seven, ר׳ יוסף יוזל הורביץ meets ר׳ ישראל סלנטר in Memel. The encounter persuades him to leave commercial life and devote himself to Torah and mussar, the decisive turn in his biography. The year is approximate. See the biographical account and Novardok Research Center overview.

ר׳ יוסף יוזל הורביץ enters the Kovno Kollel Perushim and studies in the circle of ר׳ יצחק בלאזר, ר׳ נפתלי אמסטרדם and ר׳ אברהם שנקר. Following his first wife’s death, he also undertakes an extended period of seclusion and mussar discipline in Kovno. See the biographical synthesis and Novardok Research Center; the year is approximate.

Seeking sustained self-scrutiny away from public honor, ר׳ יוסף יוזל הורביץ establishes a simple retreat in woodland near Dzyatlava and spends long periods there over roughly twelve years. Sources preserve the retreat more securely than its exact beginning; both the year and regional coordinate are approximate. See the biographical account.

ר׳ שמחה זיסל זיו urges ר׳ יוסף יוזל הורביץ to redirect his intense private discipline toward public education. He consequently begins establishing kollelim and yeshivot across the region. The early 1890s date is supported by the Posen Library; see also the Novardok Research Center.

ר׳ יוסף יוזל הורביץ establishes the yeshiva at Navahrudak that becomes the central institution and namesake of his mussar movement. Its students combine demanding Torah study with organized ethical work, radical bitachon and exercises intended to break dependence on social approval. See the Novardok Yeshiva history, Posen Library and Novardok Research Center.

ר׳ יוסף יוזל הורביץ.place: Navahrudak and the western Russian Empire
ר׳ יוסף יוזל הורביץ.event: From the Navahrudak center, ר׳ יוסף יוזל הורביץ develops an unusually expansive network of Novardok yeshivot and kollelim, with institutions reported in cities including Dvinsk, Minsk, Warsaw, Berdychiv, Odessa and Lida. This is a representative network marker, not a claim that every foundation occurred in 1908. See the Posen Library and Novardok Research Center.

The First World War displaces the Novardok network eastward. ר׳ יוסף יוזל הורביץ regroups students in Homel and continues founding and sustaining yeshivot despite hunger, epidemic and military disruption. Sources variously place the move in 1914 or 1915; this map uses 1915. See the biographical account and Novardok Research Center.

ר׳ יוסף יוזל הורביץ reaches Kyiv amid revolution and civil war and establishes additional centers for displaced students. Accounts describe four yeshivot created in the city; the exact transition from Homel is variously dated 1917–1918. See the biographical synthesis and Novardok Research Center.

After personally tending students during a typhus epidemic, ר׳ יוסף יוזל הורביץ contracts the disease and dies in Kyiv on 17 Kislev 5680 (9 December 1919). His teachings are subsequently preserved by disciples in מדרגת האדם. His remains were reinterred at Har HaMenuchot in Jerusalem in 1963, a posthumous fact deliberately kept out of the movement chronology. See the biographical account, the National Library of Israel and the catalogued biography by ר׳ דב כץ.

ר׳ נתן צבי פינקל (הסבא מסלבודקה).place: Raseiniai, Kovno Governorate, Russian Empire; now Lithuania
ר׳ נתן צבי פינקל (הסבא מסלבודקה).event: ר׳ נתן צבי פינקל is born in Raseiniai to ר׳ משה פינקל and Miriam. Orphaned while young, he is raised among relatives, including a period in Vilna. See the National Library of Israel authority record and the Hebrew Daat biography.

ר׳ נתן צבי פינקל (הסבא מסלבודקה).place: Kelmė, Kovno Governorate, Russian Empire; now Lithuania
ר׳ נתן צבי פינקל (הסבא מסלבודקה).event: As a young man, ר׳ נתן צבי פינקל marries Gittel, a granddaughter of Kelm’s rabbi, and enters the educational orbit of ר׳ שמחה זיסל זיו. The displayed year is approximate because surviving biographies do not securely date the beginning of this formative relationship. See Daat and Encyclopaedia Judaica.

ר׳ נתן צבי פינקל organizes a kollel for advanced scholars in Kovno, an institutional precursor to his later Slabodka enterprise. Sources date the beginnings of this work to 1876–1877, so 1877 is used as an approximate map marker. See the Hebrew biography.

ר׳ נתן צבי פינקל establishes and shapes Yeshivat Knesses Yisrael in Slabodka. Under his supervision it becomes the principal institutional expression of the Slabodka Musar school and its doctrine of גדלות האדם. See the referenced biography and the Hebrew historical study of Lithuanian Musar yeshivot.

To extend the Slabodka educational network, ר׳ נתן צבי פינקל establishes a yeshiva in Slutsk, sending students and appointing ר׳ איסר זלמן מלצר to lead it, while ר׳ משה מרדכי אפשטיין remains a principal leader in Slabodka. See the Hebrew biographical chronology.

After the First World War reaches Lithuania, ר׳ נתן צבי פינקל and the Slabodka yeshiva leave their home and begin a wartime exile through the Russian interior, initially regrouping in Minsk. See the sourced institutional chronology.

During the prolonged wartime displacement, ר׳ נתן צבי פינקל continues directing the Slabodka community in Kremenchuk. The route is represented only at securely recurring institutional stations, not as a complete travel diary. See the yeshiva history.
Following war and revolution, ר׳ נתן צבי פינקל returns with the yeshiva to Slabodka and rebuilds its Lithuanian centre. See the historical study and the Hebrew chronology.

Lithuanian requirements for secular studies and the associated threat of conscription lead ר׳ נתן צבי פינקל and the yeshiva leadership to establish a major branch in Mandatory Palestine rather than abandon the institution’s curriculum. See the Hebrew biography.

ר׳ נתן צבי פינקל (הסבא מסלבודקה).place: Knesses Yisrael–Slabodka Yeshiva, Hebron, Mandatory Palestine
ר׳ נתן צבי פינקל (הסבא מסלבודקה).event: After an advance group establishes the Hebron branch, ר׳ נתן צבי פינקל immigrates and joins it in 1925, providing spiritual leadership alongside ר׳ משה מרדכי אפשטיין. See Encyclopaedia Judaica and the Hebron community history.

ר׳ נתן צבי פינקל (הסבא מסלבודקה).place: Jerusalem; burial on the Mount of Olives
ר׳ נתן צבי פינקל (הסבא מסלבודקה).event: ר׳ נתן צבי פינקל dies in Jerusalem on 1 February 1927, 29 Shevat 5687, and is buried on the Mount of Olives. His death precedes the 1929 destruction of the Hebron community. See the National Library authority record and biographical chronology.

ר׳ ישעיה שטיינר מקרסטיר.place: Zboró, Kingdom of Hungary; now Zborov, Slovakia
ר׳ ישעיה שטיינר מקרסטיר.event: ר׳ ישעיה שטיינר מקרסטיר is born in 1851 at Zboró to ר׳ משה and Hentsha Miriam Steiner. The coordinate is settlement-level. See the Hebrew biographical account and sourced English biography.

ר׳ ישעיה שטיינר מקרסטיר.place: Olaszliszka, Kingdom of Hungary; now Hungary; year approximate
ר׳ ישעיה שטיינר מקרסטיר.event: As a youth ר׳ ישעיה שטיינר מקרסטיר enters the household and court of ר׳ צבי הירש פרידמן מליסקא, becoming his close attendant and disciple. The exact first year is not preserved, so 1865 is approximate. See the Hebrew biography.

ר׳ ישעיה שטיינר מקרסטיר.place: Bodrogkeresztúr, Kingdom of Hungary; year approximate
ר׳ ישעיה שטיינר מקרסטיר.event: Following the death of ר׳ צבי הירש פרידמן מליסקא and a disputed succession, ר׳ ישעיה שטיינר מקרסטיר establishes his own Hasidic centre at Kerestir. His home becomes known for feeding visitors and assisting the poor. The year marks the transition approximately. See the Hebrew account and sourced biography.

ר׳ ישעיה שטיינר מקרסטיר dies at Kerestir on 27 April 1925, 3 Iyar 5685, and is buried there. His son ר׳ אברהם שטיינר succeeds him. See the Hebrew biography, National Library of Israel archive record and Commons authority category.

ר׳ שמעון אהרן אגסי.event: ר׳ שמעון אהרן אגסי is born in Baghdad in 1852 into a prosperous merchant family whose forebears had migrated from Persia. See the National Library of Israel archive description.

As a young scholar, ר׳ שמעון אהרן אגסי studies at Midrash Bet Zilkha under ר׳ שמואל מג׳לד and ר׳ נסים הלוי, while beginning the study of Kabbalah. The year is an approximate educational anchor rather than a documented enrolment date. See the National Library of Israel.
ר׳ שמעון אהרן אגסי marries Rachel (Tchahla), daughter of ר׳ עבדאללה בן אליה בחר, in 1879. See the detailed family biography in the National Library of Israel archive.

By the turn of the century, ר׳ שמעון אהרן אגסי is teaching, preaching and corresponding with ר׳ יוסף חיים. He establishes a yeshiva for future rabbis and dayanim and the תומכי תורה society to sustain its students; the displayed year is approximate. See the Hebrew National Library archive description.
ר׳ שמעון אהרן אגסי dies in Baghdad during a plague epidemic on 8 Av 5674 (31 July 1914), only days after the First World War begins. See the National Library of Israel and its archive feature.

ר׳ חיים הלוי סולובייצ׳יק.event: ר׳ חיים הלוי סולובייצ׳יק was born in Volozhin on 25 March 1853 while his father ר׳ יוסף דוב הלוי סולובייצ׳יק taught at its yeshiva. Posen Library; Biographical chronology
During his youth, ר׳ חיים הלוי סולובייצ׳יק lived and studied in Slutsk after his father assumed its rabbinate. The year is approximate. Biographical chronology
After marrying Lifsha, daughter of ר׳ רפאל שפירא, ר׳ חיים הלוי סולובייצ׳יק returned to Volozhin and pursued advanced study there. Encyclopaedia Judaica
ר׳ חיים הלוי סולובייצ׳יק joined the Volozhin yeshiva faculty and began publicly developing the conceptual analytical method later called the Brisker derekh. Posen Library; Centenary study
After the Russian government closed the Volozhin yeshiva, ר׳ חיים הלוי סולובייצ׳יק moved to Brest-Litovsk and succeeded his father as rabbi of Brisk. Posen Library
While seeking medical treatment, ר׳ חיים הלוי סולובייצ׳יק died in Otwock on 30 July 1918, 21 Av 5678. Biographical chronology
ר׳ חיים הלוי סולובייצ׳יק was buried in the Okopowa Street Jewish Cemetery in Warsaw, near ר׳ נפתלי צבי יהודה ברלין. Burial record

ר׳ שמואל בורנשטיין.event: ר׳ שמואל בורנשטיין was born on 4 Cheshvan 5616 (16 October 1855) in Kock, in the home of his maternal grandfather ר׳ מנחם מנדל מורגנשטרן. His father ר׳ אברהם בורנשטיין was then supported in his father-in-law’s household. Some modern summaries misconvert the Hebrew year as 1856. Sochaczew memorial book; Sochaczew municipal history

At approximately eight years old, ר׳ שמואל בורנשטיין moved with his family to Parczew when his father ר׳ אברהם בורנשטיין accepted the town’s rabbinate. He received his education chiefly from his father and remained closely attached to him throughout their later moves. Hebrew biography; Sochaczew memorial book

ר׳ שמואל בורנשטיין accompanied his father’s household to Krośniewice, another of the rabbinates in which his youth and intensive study under ר׳ אברהם בורנשטיין unfolded. The precise year is approximate because accessible biographical summaries establish the sequence more securely than the date. Sochaczew memorial book; Polish-Jewish historical guide

ר׳ שמואל בורנשטיין, by then married to Yuta Leah Litmanowicz, moved with his father’s household to Nasielsk when ר׳ אברהם בורנשטיין assumed its rabbinate. His son and eventual successor ר׳ דוד בורנשטיין was born there. Sochaczew memorial book; Chronology of the father’s rabbinates

ר׳ שמואל בורנשטיין settled with his family in Sochaczew when ר׳ אברהם בורנשטיין became the city’s rabbi. He lived in a separate house near his father, taught disciples, and participated in the yeshiva and emerging Sochatchov court. Sochaczew memorial book; City of Sochaczew

Acting for his father, ר׳ שמואל בורנשטיין travelled to Ottoman Palestine to investigate purchasing land for an observant agricultural settlement. The mission failed because Ottoman rules prevented the proposed acquisition by foreign subjects. The available account establishes travel to the Land of Israel but not every stop, so the marker is regional to Jerusalem rather than tied to an invented parcel. Herzog College pedagogy article

Following the death of ר׳ אברהם בורנשטיין, ר׳ שמואל בורנשטיין was installed as the second Sochatchover Rebbe and assumed leadership of the Sochaczew yeshiva. He initially hesitated because communal leadership would reduce his uninterrupted study, but senior disciples pressed him to succeed his father. Hebrew biography; City of Sochaczew

After wartime detention in Germany as a Russian subject and the German army’s destruction of Sochaczew, ר׳ שמואל בורנשטיין could not restore his court in the devastated city and re-established it in Łódź. The unknown German detention site is not plotted as a separate movement. Hebrew biographical study; Dynastic chronology

Finding crowded industrial Łódź burdensome to his health and study, ר׳ שמואל בורנשטיין moved his court to nearby Zgierz. The Sochatchov centre followed him there, and he established a study hall and later a yeshiva while continuing to hope for a return to Sochaczew. Polish-Jewish historical guide; Sochaczew municipal history

Because of declining health, ר׳ שמואל בורנשטיין was taken to the resort town of Otwock, where he died on 24 Tevet 5686 (10 January 1926). His body was then returned to Sochaczew for burial beside his father; this marker represents the place of death. Hebrew biography; Sochaczew memorial book

ר׳ שמואל בורנשטיין was buried in the Bornsztain ohel in the Jewish cemetery on Sierpniowa Street, Sochaczew, beside ר׳ אברהם בורנשטיין. The cemetery and ohel were devastated during the Holocaust; the ohel was reconstructed in the early 1990s. The marker is cemetery-level rather than an asserted grave-level point. ESJF cemetery survey; International Jewish Cemetery Project

ר׳ משה גסטר.event: ר׳ משה גסטר is born in Bucharest on 17 September 1856, the eldest son of Abraham Emanuel Gaster and Phina Judith Rubinstein. See the AIM25 archival biography.
After completing his Bucharest baccalaureate, ר׳ משה גסטר studies at the University of Leipzig and earns a doctorate in 1877. See the AIM25 catalogue.
ר׳ משה גסטר continues rabbinical study at the Jewish Theological Seminary of Breslau and receives his rabbinical diploma in 1881. See Encyclopaedia Judaica.

Returning to Bucharest, ר׳ משה גסטר lectures on Romanian language, literature and comparative mythology from 1881 to 1885 while publishing foundational studies of Romanian popular literature. See the AIM25 archival biography.

The Romanian government expels ר׳ משה גסטר in 1885 after his advocacy against the persecution and civic exclusion of Romanian Jews. He settles in England and lectures at Oxford in 1886. See Encyclopaedia Judaica and UCL Special Collections.
ר׳ משה גסטר is appointed Haham of the Spanish and Portuguese Jews and rabbi of Bevis Marks Synagogue in 1887. See UCL Special Collections.
ר׳ משה גסטר becomes principal of the Judith Lady Montefiore College at Ramsgate in 1890, resigning in 1896 after disputes over its management. See the AIM25 catalogue.

During the First World War, ר׳ משה גסטר remains a senior Zionist advocate; his London home hosts discussions between Zionist representatives and British officials in the period preceding the Balfour Declaration. See the AIM25 biographical record.
Failing eyesight leads ר׳ משה גסטר to retire from the Hahamship in 1918–19, although he continues scholarly and communal activity. See the AIM25 archive catalogue.
ר׳ משה גסטר dies near Abingdon on 5 March 1939, leaving a major archive and manuscript collection now divided among several institutions. See UCL's Moses Gaster Papers.

ר׳ יוסף רוזין.event: ר׳ יוסף רוזין was born in Rogachev, now Belarus, into a Kapust-Chabad Hasidic family. Encyclopaedia Judaica/JVL; Hebrew biography
At about thirteen, ר׳ יוסף רוזין went to Slutsk and studied under ר׳ יוסף דוב הלוי סולובייצ׳יק alongside ר׳ חיים הלוי סולובייצ׳יק. JewAge biography
ר׳ יוסף רוזין continued his studies in Shklov under ר׳ יהושע לייב דיסקין. The exact opening year is approximate. Encyclopaedia Judaica/JVL
ר׳ יוסף רוזין became rabbi of Dvinsk’s Hasidic community, serving in parallel and cordial cooperation with ר׳ מאיר שמחה הכהן. Encyclopaedia Judaica/JVL
While serving in Dvinsk, ר׳ יוסף רוזין issued early volumes of צפנת פענח on the Mishneh Torah of ר׳ משה בן מימון; the physical printing in Piotrków is not treated as a residence. First-edition record
During the First World War evacuation of Dvinsk, ר׳ יוסף רוזין relocated to Petrograd and continued answering halakhic questions there. Latvian Jewish history
ר׳ יוסף רוזין returned from Petrograd to Dvinsk and resumed his communal rabbinate and prolific correspondence. Latvian Jewish history
After travelling to Vienna for unsuccessful surgery, ר׳ יוסף רוזין died there on 5 March 1936. Tzafnat Pane’ach Institute; Contemporary JTA report
The body of ר׳ יוסף רוזין was returned to Dvinsk, where a large funeral took place and he was buried in the Jewish cemetery. Jewish Telegraphic Agency, 11 March 1936

ר׳ ברוך הלוי אפשטיין.event: ר׳ ברוך הלוי אפשטיין was born in Bobruisk to ר׳ יחיאל מיכל הלוי אפשטיין. He was raised principally in Novogrudok after his father became its rabbi. Encyclopaedia Judaica
As a youth, ר׳ ברוך הלוי אפשטיין studied at the Volozhin yeshiva under his uncle ר׳ נפתלי צבי יהודה ברלין. Jewish Virtual Library

After marrying the daughter of Pinsk rabbi ר׳ אלעזר משה הורוויץ, ר׳ ברוך הלוי אפשטיין settled in Pinsk, where he worked in banking while sustaining intensive Torah study. The year is approximate. Jewish Virtual Library; Pinsk Yizkor Book
In Pinsk, ר׳ ברוך הלוי אפשטיין published תורה תמימה, composed there circa 1898–1902. Sefaria text record
ר׳ ברוך הלוי אפשטיין travelled to New York seeking opportunities to publish his writings and obtain a suitable post; he served for a period as director of Ezras Torah. Biographical chronology
After three years in the United States, ר׳ ברוך הלוי אפשטיין returned to Pinsk and resumed his writing there. Biographical chronology

Following the German entry into Pinsk in July 1941, the elderly and ill ר׳ ברוך הלוי אפשטיין was taken to the Jewish hospital and died two days later. Some major references instead give 1942. Detailed biographical account; Alternative 1942 dating

ר׳ שמעון יהודה שקופ.event: ר׳ שמעון יהודה שקופ was born in Turets, near Karelichy in present-day Belarus. This corrects the old file’s confusion with modern Torez in eastern Ukraine. YIVO Encyclopedia
At about twelve, ר׳ שמעון יהודה שקופ entered the Mir yeshiva for advanced Talmudic study. YIVO Encyclopedia
ר׳ שמעון יהודה שקופ moved to Volozhin, where he studied under ר׳ נפתלי צבי יהודה ברלין and became closely associated with ר׳ חיים סולובייצ׳יק. YIVO Encyclopedia
ר׳ אליעזר גורדון appointed ר׳ שמעון יהודה שקופ to teach at the Telz yeshiva. His seventeen-year tenure helped define a rigorous conceptual approach. YIVO Encyclopedia
After leaving Telz during its Musar controversy, ר׳ שמעון יהודה שקופ became rabbi of Maltsh and established a yeshiva there. YIVO Encyclopedia
ר׳ שמעון יהודה שקופ accepted the rabbinate of Brańsk, continuing to formulate his distinctive method. YIVO Encyclopedia
ר׳ שמעון יהודה שקופ became rosh yeshiva of Shaar HaTorah in Grodno, rebuilding it into a major interwar institution. YIVO Encyclopedia
In Grodno, ר׳ שמעון יהודה שקופ published שערי יושר, the systematic expression of his conceptual approach to Talmudic law. YIVO Encyclopedia
During a fundraising mission in New York, ר׳ שמעון יהודה שקופ briefly taught at RIETS before choosing to return to Grodno. YIVO Encyclopedia
ר׳ שמעון יהודה שקופ returned to Grodno and resumed leadership of Shaar HaTorah. YIVO Encyclopedia
ר׳ שמעון יהודה שקופ died in Grodno shortly after the Soviet occupation and was buried in the city’s Jewish cemetery. YIVO Encyclopedia

ר׳ שלום דובער שניאורסון.event: ר׳ שלום דובער שניאורסון is born in Lyubavichi on 20 Cheshvan 5621 to ר׳ שמואל שניאורסון and Rivkah. See Chabad.org’s biography.
At fifteen ר׳ שלום דובער שניאורסון marries Shterna Sarah, granddaughter of ר׳ מנחם מנדל שניאורסון. See the Chabad biography.

After the death of his father ר׳ שמואל שניאורסון, ר׳ שלום דובער שניאורסון begins delivering original discourses and guiding Hasidim while initially declining the formal title of rebbe. See Chabad.org’s detailed chronology.
ר׳ שלום דובער שניאורסון fully assumes public leadership as the fifth Chabad rebbe. See the institutional chronology.
ר׳ שלום דובער שניאורסון founds Yeshivat Tomchei Temimim, integrating intensive Talmudic and Chabad study with contemplative prayer. See Chabad’s illustrated institutional history.
ר׳ שלום דובער שניאורסון begins the monumental sequence known as המשך תרס״ו, exemplifying his systematic exposition of Chabad theology. See the teaching survey.
As the First World War reaches the region, ר׳ שלום דובער שניאורסון relocates the Chabad court from Lyubavichi to Rostov-on-Don. See Chabad.org.
From Rostov, ר׳ שלום דובער שניאורסון responds to revolutionary suppression by organizing the defence of Jewish education and observance, work continued by ר׳ יוסף יצחק שניאורסון. See the biography.
ר׳ שלום דובער שניאורסון dies in Rostov on 2 Nisan 5680 and is buried there; his son ר׳ יוסף יצחק שניאורסון succeeds him. See Chabad.org’s biography.

ר׳ ברוך בער ליבוביץ.event: ר׳ ברוך בער ליבוביץ is born near Slutsk around 1862. Library authority records also preserve an 1866 chronology, so the year is explicitly qualified. See the National Library archive and sourced biography.
As a young scholar, ר׳ ברוך בער ליבוביץ studies at Volozhin and becomes a devoted disciple of ר׳ חיים הלוי סולובייצ׳יק. The year is approximate. See the sourced biography.
ר׳ ברוך בער ליבוביץ becomes head of Knesset Beit Yitzchak in Slabodka, shaping generations of students through the Brisk method. See the NLI institutional summary.
The First World War forces ר׳ ברוך בער ליבוביץ and his yeshiva eastward through Minsk and then Kremenchug. Minsk is used as the first documented displacement point. See the biographical chronology.
After revolutionary upheaval, ר׳ ברוך בער ליבוביץ re-establishes Knesset Beit Yitzchak in Vilna; surviving letters document him there in 1923. See the National Library autograph archive.
ר׳ ברוך בער ליבוביץ relocates the yeshiva to Kamianets, where it grows into a premier academy known widely as the Kamenitz Yeshiva. See the sourced institutional history.
ר׳ ברוך בער ליבוביץ visits the United States with ר׳ ראובן גרוזובסקי to raise funds for Kamenitz. New York is used as the campaign’s principal documented centre. See the sourced biography.
After Germany invades Poland, ר׳ ברוך בער ליבוביץ flees with the yeshiva into Lithuania, becomes ill and dies in Vilna on 17 November 1939. See the sourced death account and Wikimedia authority data.

ר׳ חיים עוזר גרודזינסקי.place: Iwye, Vilna Governorate, Russian Empire; now Iŭje, Belarus
ר׳ חיים עוזר גרודזינסקי.event: ר׳ חיים עוזר גרודזינסקי is born on 9 Elul 5623 (24 August 1863) in Iwye. His father, ר׳ דוד שלמה גרודזינסקי, serves as the town’s rabbi for more than forty years, following an earlier family tradition of local rabbinic leadership. See the Association of Jews of Vilna biography, National Library of Israel authority record and Volozhin Yeshiva biography.

ר׳ חיים עוזר גרודזינסקי.place: Eishyshok, Vilna Governorate, Russian Empire; now Eišiškės, Lithuania
ר׳ חיים עוזר גרודזינסקי.event: At about twelve, ר׳ חיים עוזר leaves Iwye to study with the perushim, the advanced scholars of Eishyshok, and celebrates his bar mitzvah there. The move marks his entry into the wider Lithuanian Torah-study network. See the Association of Jews of Vilna and the Volozhin Yeshiva biography.

ר׳ חיים עוזר גרודזינסקי.place: Volozhin Yeshiva, Volozhin, Russian Empire; now Belarus
ר׳ חיים עוזר גרודזינסקי.event: At fifteen, ר׳ חיים עוזר enters the Volozhin Yeshiva. He studies in the circle of ר׳ נפתלי צבי יהודה ברלין and is accepted into the advanced shiur of ר׳ חיים הלוי סולובייצ׳יק, whose conceptual method profoundly shapes his later responsa. See the Volozhin Yeshiva biography and the Association of Jews of Vilna.

ר׳ חיים עוזר גרודזינסקי.place: Vilna, Russian Empire; now Vilnius, Lithuania
ר׳ חיים עוזר גרודזינסקי.event: Around age twenty, ר׳ חיים עוזר marries Leah, daughter of Vilna dayan ר׳ אליהו אליעזר גרודזינסקי and granddaughter of ר׳ ישראל מסלנט. He settles in Vilna and enters its dense network of batei midrash, rabbinical courts and charitable institutions. See the Association of Jews of Vilna biography and the Hebrew biographical compilation.

Following the sudden death of his father-in-law, ר׳ חיים עוזר joins the Vilna beit din as a dayan at roughly twenty-three. He eventually becomes its dominant halakhic authority, although Vilna’s fragmented communal structure makes the simplified title ‘chief rabbi’ historically imprecise. See the Association of Jews of Vilna and the CET–Yad Vashem educational biography.

ר׳ חיים עוזר establishes an advanced scholars’ kibbutz at the Gaon’s kloyz and supports the Ramailes Yeshiva. After the death of ר׳ יצחק אלחנן ספקטור, his role increasingly extends from local adjudication to international responsa and Russian Jewish communal policy. See the Hebrew biographical compilation and the Vilna Jewish association.

ר׳ חיים עוזר participates in Orthodox organizational discussions in Hamburg that precede the creation of Agudath Israel. The meeting reflects his effort to coordinate traditional communities across imperial borders amid Zionist, socialist and modernizing movements. See the Association of Jews of Vilna biography.

ר׳ חיים עוזר גרודזינסקי.place: Kattowitz, German Empire; now Katowice, Poland
ר׳ חיים עוזר גרודזינסקי.event: At Agudath Israel’s founding conference, ר׳ חיים עוזר becomes a central member of its Moetzes Gedolei HaTorah. His participation gives the new transnational organization Lithuanian rabbinic standing, though he continues to act through Vilna’s own institutions. See the Association of Jews of Vilna and the National Library of Israel.

The first volume of שו״ת אחיעזר appears in Vilna. Published volumes through 1939 establish ר׳ חיים עוזר as a major twentieth-century decisor, applying rigorous Talmudic analysis to ritual, civil, family and communal questions. See the Otzar HaHochma bibliographic catalogue, bibliographic record for אחיעזר and the Vilna biography.

ר׳ חיים עוזר גרודזינסקי.place: Grodno, Second Polish Republic; now Hrodna, Belarus
ר׳ חיים עוזר גרודזינסקי.event: At a rabbinical convention in Grodno, ר׳ חיים עוזר and ר׳ ישראל מאיר הכהן sponsor the Vaad Hayeshivot. He is appointed its leader, and its Vilna office coordinates fundraising, grants and oversight for dozens of yeshivot across the eastern Polish provinces. See the YIVO Archives finding aid and the Vaad Hayeshivot collection description.

After the Nazi takeover in Germany, ר׳ חיים עוזר issues an appeal describing the unprecedented danger and raising assistance for German Jewish refugees. His surviving letters document aid to individuals and communities as well as yeshiva finance. See his 21 November 1933 Call for the Assistance of the Refugees from Germany and the National Library of Israel archive description.

ר׳ חיים עוזר גרודזינסקי.place: Vilna, successively Polish, Soviet-occupied and Lithuanian territory
ר׳ חיים עוזר גרודזינסקי.event: Following the German and Soviet invasion of Poland, ר׳ חיים עוזר urges yeshivot trapped in occupied eastern Poland to gather in Vilna, anticipating its transfer to neutral Lithuania. Thousands of refugees arrive; he and the Vaad distribute students among communities and organize food, lodging and institutional support. See the YIVO Vaad Hayeshivot records, the CET–Yad Vashem biography and the Vilna Jewish association.

As Soviet rule closes or threatens religious institutions, ר׳ חיים עוזר insists that yeshiva study continue and remains involved in refugee relief despite illness. He dies on 5 Av 5700 (9 August 1940) and is buried in Vilna’s new Jewish cemetery. See the CET–Yad Vashem educational biography, National Library of Israel and the Association of Jews of Vilna.

ר׳ אברהם מרדכי אלתר.event: ר׳ אברהם מרדכי אלתר is born in Góra Kalwaria on 25 December 1865 to ר׳ יהודה אריה ליב אלתר and Yocheved Rivka Kaminer. See the National Library authority record and sourced biography.
After the death of his father, ר׳ אברהם מרדכי אלתר becomes the third Gerrer Rebbe and oversees Ger’s rapid institutional expansion. See the sourced biography.
War conditions force ר׳ אברהם מרדכי אלתר from Ger to Warsaw, which becomes his principal base for leadership, education and Agudath Israel activity. See Jewish Observer historical profile.

ר׳ אברהם מרדכי אלתר makes the first of several visits to Mandatory Palestine, meeting communities and strengthening Gerrer settlement and institutions. The Jerusalem point represents the documented itinerary’s main centre. See the sourced overview.
After the German invasion, ר׳ אברהם מרדכי אלתר is targeted by the Nazis and hidden at changing Warsaw addresses while supporters seek an escape route. See the sourced wartime account.
Rescued from occupied Poland, ר׳ אברהם מרדכי אלתר reaches Mandatory Palestine and re-establishes the Gerrer court in Jerusalem. See the historical profile and biography.

ר׳ אברהם מרדכי אלתר dies in besieged Jerusalem on Shavuot, 13 June 1948. With the Mount of Olives inaccessible, he is buried in the yeshiva courtyard. See the burial account and the Wikimedia memorial documentation.

ר׳ אברהם יצחק הכהן קוק.place: Grīva, beside Dvinsk; now Daugavpils, Latvia
ר׳ אברהם יצחק הכהן קוק.event: ר׳ אברהם יצחק הכהן קוק is born on 16 Elul 5625 (7 September 1865) in Grīva, across the Daugava from Dvinsk, to ר׳ שלמה זלמן קוק and Perel Zlata Felman. See the National Library of Israel and Rav Kook chronology.

ר׳ אברהם יצחק הכהן קוק.place: Volozhin, Russian Empire; now Valozhyn, Belarus
ר׳ אברהם יצחק הכהן קוק.event: At about eighteen, ר׳ אברהם יצחק הכהן קוק enters the Volozhin yeshivah and studies for roughly eighteen months under ר׳ נפתלי צבי יהודה ברלין. See the Rav Kook chronology and Yeshivat Har Etzion.
ר׳ אברהם יצחק הכהן קוק marries Batsheva, daughter of the Panevėžys rabbi ר׳ אליהו דוד רבינוביץ׳-תאומים (the Aderet), and continues advanced study near his new family. See the Rav Kook chronology.

ר׳ אברהם יצחק הכהן קוק accepts his first communal rabbinate in Žeimelis and launches the rabbinic periodical עיטור סופרים. After Batsheva dies in 1889, he later marries Raiza-Rivka, daughter of the Aderet’s twin brother ר׳ צבי יהודה רבינוביץ׳-תאומים. See the National Library archive and Yeshivat Har Etzion.

ר׳ אברהם יצחק הכהן קוק becomes rabbi of Bauska and remains there until his 1904 aliyah. His rulings and correspondence establish him as a distinctive halakhic and spiritual voice. See Yeshivat Har Etzion and the National Library of Israel.

In May 1904 ר׳ אברהם יצחק הכהן קוק arrives in Jaffa as rabbi of the city and the surrounding Jewish agricultural settlements. He founds a yeshivah and develops rulings for renewed agricultural life in the Land of Israel. See the National Library archive and Yeshivat Har Etzion.

ר׳ אברהם יצחק הכהן קוק.place: Galilee agricultural settlements; representative marker at Merhavia
ר׳ אברהם יצחק הכהן קוק.event: ר׳ אברהם יצחק הכהן קוק joins the first rabbinic tour of Jewish agricultural settlements, travelling through Galilee and the valleys to connect the rabbinate with largely secular pioneers. This marker represents a multi-stop journey, not a residence. See the National Library archive.

Travelling to Europe for the planned Agudat Israel conference, ר׳ אברהם יצחק הכהן קוק is stranded by the First World War. Unable to return to Ottoman Palestine as a Russian subject, he spends the first phase of exile in St Gallen. See Mercaz HaRav and Yeshivat Har Etzion.

ר׳ אברהם יצחק הכהן קוק.place: Machzike Hadath, Brick Lane and Fournier Street, Spitalfields, London
ר׳ אברהם יצחק הכהן קוק.event: ר׳ אברהם יצחק הכהן קוק becomes rav of Machzike Hadath, the Spitalfields Great Synagogue, serving until 1919 on condition that he may return to Jaffa after the war. He advocates publicly for a Jewish national home during the period of the Balfour Declaration. See the congregation’s official history and Encyclopaedia Judaica.
After the war, ר׳ אברהם יצחק הכהן קוק returns to the Land of Israel and becomes Ashkenazi chief rabbi of Jerusalem. See the Rav Kook chronology and National Library of Israel.

ר׳ אברהם יצחק הכהן קוק helps establish the Chief Rabbinate and becomes the first Ashkenazi chief rabbi of Mandatory Palestine, serving alongside Sephardi chief rabbi ר׳ יעקב מאיר. See the Rav Kook chronology and a National Library archival record.

ר׳ אברהם יצחק הכהן קוק.place: Beit HaRav, 9 HaRav Kook Street, Jerusalem
ר׳ אברהם יצחק הכהן קוק.event: ר׳ אברהם יצחק הכהן קוק moves into Beit HaRav, which serves as his home, study hall and public headquarters from 1923 until his death. See the Beit HaRav–HaOrot foundation and site history.

At Beit HaRav, ר׳ אברהם יצחק הכהן קוק founds the Central Universal Yeshivah, soon known as Mercaz HaRav, joining advanced Torah learning, Hebrew revival and preparation for religious national leadership. See the official Mercaz HaRav biography.

ר׳ אברהם יצחק הכהן קוק.place: Jerusalem and Mount of Olives Cemetery
ר׳ אברהם יצחק הכהן קוק.event: ר׳ אברהם יצחק הכהן קוק dies in Jerusalem on 3 Elul 5695 (1 September 1935) and is buried in the Jewish cemetery on the Mount of Olives. His students continue publishing his notebooks, responsa and correspondence. See the Rav Kook chronology and National Library of Israel.

ר׳ יחיא יצחק הלוי.event: ר׳ יחיא יצחק הלוי is born in Sana’a around 1867 to Musa Yitzhak Halevi and begins learning with his maternal grandfather ר׳ שלום מנצורה. See HaChacham HaYomi and the Bar-Ilan scholarly study.

As a young scholar, ר׳ יחיא יצחק הלוי studies Talmud and halakhah in the Maharitz synagogue and at night in the study house of ר׳ חיים קורח; he also qualifies in ritual slaughter. See the sourced biographical account.

Community leaders appoint ר׳ יחיא יצחק הלוי av beit din of Sana’a after the death of the preceding court head, beginning three decades of authority across Yemen’s Jewish communities. See the Bar-Ilan University study and NLI documentary collection.

During the siege and catastrophic famine, ר׳ יחיא יצחק הלוי assumes wider leadership as hakham bashi and chief rabbi, then works to reconstruct a community reduced by starvation and disease. See HaChacham HaYomi and the scholarly study of his relations with Imam Yahya.
Famine and siege force ר׳ יחיא יצחק הלוי to leave Sana’a temporarily for Al Mahwit after his first wife dies during the crisis. See the HaChacham HaYomi chronology.
During the same famine-driven displacement, ר׳ יחיא יצחק הלוי continues from Al Mahwit to Dhamar before returning to lead the reconstructed Sana’a community. See the HaChacham HaYomi biography.

ר׳ יחיא יצחק הלוי initially supports a new Jewish school combining religious and general studies, but later disputes curricular and ritual reforms associated with fellow dayan ר׳ יחיא קאפח; both continue serving on the court. See the documented account and Hebrew biography.

The court headed by ר׳ יחיא יצחק הלוי answers questions sent by ר׳ אברהם יצחק הכהן קוק, illustrating his legal authority and international correspondence. See the biographical documentation and Bar-Ilan research on his responsa.

As chief rabbi and communal representative, ר׳ יחיא יצחק הלוי provides visiting geographer Carl Rathjens a tax-roll list recording hundreds of Yemenite Jewish settlements; he also continues supervising courts, slaughterers, taxation and orphan-rescue efforts. See the sourced account and scholarly article.

ר׳ יחיא יצחק הלוי dies in Sana’a on 11 Sivan 5692 after nearly thirty years at the head of its court and is succeeded by ר׳ יחיא אל-אביץ׳. See HaChacham HaYomi and the National Library memorial collection.

ר׳ יוסף צבי דושינסקי.event: ר׳ יוסף צבי דושינסקי is born at Paks in 1867 to ר׳ ישראל and Sarah Elka Dushinsky. Some catalogues give 1868; the project follows the Hebrew chronology. See the National Library of Israel authority page and Hebrew historical study.

ר׳ יוסף צבי דושינסקי.place: Galanta, Kingdom of Hungary; now Slovakia
ר׳ יוסף צבי דושינסקי.event: ר׳ יוסף צבי דושינסקי is appointed rabbi of Galanta after his Hungarian yeshiva education and ordination. See the scholarly Jerusalem history and Encyclopaedia Judaica-derived entry.
ר׳ יוסף צבי דושינסקי becomes rabbi of Khust and leads its important Orthodox community and yeshiva. See the scholarly account.

ר׳ יוסף צבי דושינסקי.place: Yeshivat Beit Yosef Tzvi, 54 Shmuel HaNavi Street, Jerusalem
ר׳ יוסף צבי דושינסקי.event: Invited to succeed ר׳ יוסף חיים זוננפלד, ר׳ יוסף צבי דושינסקי settles in Jerusalem and establishes his home, synagogue and Yeshivat Beit Yosef Tzvi near 54 Shmuel HaNavi Street. See the location-specific scholarly history and Hebrew study.

As גאב״ד of the Edah HaChareidis, ר׳ יוסף צבי דושינסקי presents its position to the United Nations Special Committee on Palestine. The hearing occurred in Jerusalem and is not mapped as foreign travel. See the scholarly historical study.

During the siege and worsening illness ר׳ יוסף צבי דושינסקי briefly recuperates in Bat Yam, then dies on 17 October 1948 and is buried in Jerusalem's temporary Shaare Zedek cemetery. See the detailed Hebrew study and sourced biography.

ר׳ חיים אלעזר שפירא.event: ר׳ חיים אלעזר שפירא is born in Strzyżów on 17 December 1868 into the Munkács Spira dynasty. See the sourced biography and Wikimedia authority data.

By the 1890s, ר׳ חיים אלעזר שפירא is established in Munkács alongside his father ר׳ צבי הירש שפירא, studying, teaching and assisting the dynasty’s institutions. The year is approximate. See the biographical chronology.
ר׳ חיים אלעזר שפירא becomes chief dayan of the Munkács rabbinical court while serving alongside his father. See the sourced biography.
After his father’s death, ר׳ חיים אלעזר שפירא succeeds as chief rabbi and Munkács Rebbe, expanding traditional schools and the Darchei Teshuva yeshiva. See the Yad Vashem community exhibition.

ר׳ חיים אלעזר שפירא visits Mandatory Palestine, spending significant time in Jerusalem and meeting ר׳ שלמה אליעזר אלפנדרי; the journey is documented in מסעות ירושלים. See Yad Vashem and the historic journey volume.

The wedding of the only daughter of ר׳ חיים אלעזר שפירא, Chaya Fruma Rivka, to ר׳ ברוך יהושע ירחמיאל רבינוביץ draws tens of thousands and becomes a landmark event in interwar Jewish Munkács. See the Yad Vashem exhibition.
ר׳ חיים אלעזר שפירא dies in Munkács on 13 May 1937 and is buried there; thousands join the funeral. See Yad Vashem and the contemporary memorial photograph.

ר׳ איסר זלמן מלצר.event: ר׳ איסר זלמן מלצר was born in Mir, then in the Russian Empire and now Belarus. The marker uses the historic town centre, correcting the former record’s erroneous Vilnius coordinates. Jewish Virtual Library
As a teenager, ר׳ איסר זלמן מלצר entered the Volozhin yeshiva, studying under ר׳ נפתלי צבי יהודה ברלין and especially ר׳ חיים סולובייצ׳יק. Jewish Virtual Library
After additional study in Radin under ר׳ ישראל מאיר הכהן, ר׳ איסר זלמן מלצר married Beila Hinda Frank and joined the Slabodka scholarly circle. Jewish Virtual Library
ר׳ איסר זלמן מלצר founded and headed the Slutsk yeshiva; in 1903 he also became rabbi of Slutsk. The institution became an important centre of Lithuanian learning. Jewish Virtual Library
Following Bolshevik repression and imprisonment, ר׳ איסר זלמן מלצר crossed into Poland and rejoined his displaced yeshiva in Kletsk. Kletsk Yizkor Book
ר׳ איסר זלמן מלצר immigrated to Mandatory Palestine and became rosh yeshiva of Etz Chaim in Jerusalem, then based beside the Mahane Yehuda area on Jaffa Road. Jewish Virtual Library
In Jerusalem, ר׳ איסר זלמן מלצר issued the first volume of אבן האזל, his influential analysis of the Mishneh Torah of ר׳ משה בן מימון. Jewish Virtual Library
ר׳ איסר זלמן מלצר died in Jerusalem on 10 Kislev 5714 and was buried on Har HaMenuchot. Jewish Virtual Library

ר׳ משה רוזן.place: Brańsk, Grodno Governorate, Russian Empire; now Poland
ר׳ משה רוזן.event: ר׳ משה רוזן, later known as בעל נזר הקודש, is born in Brańsk in 1870 to ר׳ יהודה אריה. See the sourced identity biography.

ר׳ משה רוזן.place: Bielsk Podlaski and Ruzhin, Russian Empire
ר׳ משה רוזן.event: During his formative years ר׳ משה רוזן studies in Bielsk under ר׳ אריה ליב ילין and in Ruzhin under ר׳ מרדכי גימפל יפה before prolonged independent learning. The point is placed at Bielsk and the year is approximate. See the biographical account.
ר׳ משה רוזן studies in the Kovno kollel and receives ordination from ר׳ יצחק אלחנן ספקטור and ר׳ משה דנישבסקי. The displayed year is approximate. See the sourced biography.
ר׳ משה רוזן becomes rabbi of Kvėdarna, where he develops his Kodashim scholarship and friendship with ר׳ אברהם ישעיהו קרליץ. See the cemetery biography and scholarly recollections.
While serving Kvėdarna, ר׳ משה רוזן publishes נזר הקודש on Zevahim; printing location alone is not treated as a move. See the works chronology.

ר׳ משה רוזן.place: Mesivta Torah Vodaath, Brooklyn, New York
ר׳ משה רוזן.event: ר׳ משה רוזן immigrates to the United States and teaches during the early development of Torah Vodaath’s advanced beit midrash. See Kevarim’s biography.
ר׳ משה רוזן assumes a Brooklyn congregational rabbinate and continues writing and publishing נזר הקודש. See the biographical essay on his Brownsville years.
ר׳ משה רוזן dies on 12 October 1957 and is buried at Mount Judah Cemetery in Queens. See the cemetery record.

ר׳ יעקב חיים סופר.event: ר׳ יעקב חיים סופר is born in Baghdad around 1870 to ר׳ יצחק ברוך סופר and Esther. The displayed year follows the majority modern dating; the National Library authority allows 1869 or 1870, and some later traditions give 1867. See the National Library of Israel authority record and the German biographical summary.
