ר׳ יעקב חיים סופר.place: Beit Zilkha Yeshivah, Baghdad, Ottoman Iraq; year approximate
ר׳ יעקב חיים סופר.event: In Baghdad, the young ר׳ יעקב חיים סופר studies at Beit Zilkha under ר׳ עבדאללה סומך and is shaped by the teaching and customs of ר׳ יוסף חיים, the Ben Ish Chai. The sources establish these teachers but not a precise enrollment year, so 1885 is an approximate educational marker. See the Hebrew Yeshiva biography and biographical references collected here.

ר׳ יעקב חיים סופר.place: Beit El Synagogue, Old City of Jerusalem, Ottoman Palestine
ר׳ יעקב חיים סופר.event: ר׳ יעקב חיים סופר travels from Iraq to Ottoman Palestine with Iraqi colleagues, visits holy sites and decides to settle permanently in Jerusalem. He joins the kabbalistic study circle at Beit El and is also associated with Rehovot HaNahar under ר׳ חיים שאול דוויק הכהן. See the biographical account and the study of the Ben Ish Chai's circle.

ר׳ יעקב חיים סופר.place: Shoshanim LeDavid Synagogue and Yeshivah, 46 Rabbi Sonnenfeld Street, Jerusalem
ר׳ יעקב חיים סופר.event: ר׳ יעקב חיים סופר moves his principal study and teaching to the Iraqi synagogue and yeshivah Shoshanim LeDavid. He writes his major works here and serves as a leading scholar of Jerusalem's Babylonian community. The marker is placed on the building at 46 Rabbi Sonnenfeld Street. See the synagogue history and coordinates and his biography.

The first complete volume of כף החיים, covering Orach Chayim 1–88, appears in Jerusalem. Further Orach Chayim volumes follow in 1913, 1915, 1920, 1924, 1928, 1931 and 1933, making the work a sustained Jerusalem publishing project rather than a single-date publication. See the first-edition bibliographic description.

ר׳ יעקב חיים סופר publishes the first Yoreh De'ah volume of כף החיים. He dies before completing the next volume; it is later issued from his manuscript with a concluding section supplied by ר׳ עובדיה יוסף. See the edition record and the manuscript discussion.

ר׳ יעקב חיים סופר.place: Mount of Olives Jewish Cemetery, Jerusalem
ר׳ יעקב חיים סופר.event: ר׳ יעקב חיים סופר dies in Jerusalem on 9 Sivan 5699 (27 May 1939), aged about sixty-nine, and is buried on the Mount of Olives. See the Hebrew biographical entry and the National Library authority record.

ר׳ עמרם קורח.event: ר׳ עמרם קורח is born in Sana'a on 27 May 1871 to ר׳ יחיא קורח. See the National Library of Israel and HaChacham HaYomi.

As a young adult, ר׳ עמרם קורח serves as secretary of the rabbinical court under ר׳ סלימאן קארה, later administers the heqdesh treasury and heads the Al-Kessar synagogue. The year is an approximate career marker. See the biographical introduction summarized by Amram Qorah biography.
ר׳ עמרם קורח is selected as an assistant to chief rabbi ר׳ יחיא אל-אביץ׳, following the death of ר׳ יחיא יצחק הלוי. See HaChacham HaYomi.

After the death of ר׳ יחיא אל-אביץ׳, ר׳ עמרם קורח becomes chief rabbi and head of Sana'a’s rabbinical court, the last holder of the unified office. See HaChacham HaYomi and the National Library of Israel.

ר׳ עמרם קורח resigns the chief rabbinate after approximately two years amid communal conflict, but continues as arbitrator, ritual slaughterer and liaison with Yemen’s government. See the detailed biographical synthesis based on the introduction to סערת תימן.
ר׳ עמרם קורח acts as a principal intermediary between Yemenite Jewry and the Jewish Agency during preparations for mass emigration. See biographical documentation.
On the eve of Yom Kippur 1950, ר׳ עמרם קורח immigrates during Operation On Eagles’ Wings and settles in Jerusalem. See HaChacham HaYomi.

ר׳ עמרם קורח dies in Jerusalem on 3 October 1952 and is buried in Sanhedria Cemetery. The exact date corrects older references that list 1953. See the National Library of Israel and biographical references.

ר׳ יוסף צבי הרץ.event: ר׳ יוסף צבי הרץ is born on 25 September 1872 in Rebrény, now Zemplínska Široká in Slovakia. See the Chief Rabbinate history.
The Hertz family emigrates to New York, where ר׳ יוסף צבי הרץ receives Jewish and general education. See the Encyclopaedia Judaica biography.
ר׳ יוסף צבי הרץ becomes the first rabbinical graduate of the Jewish Theological Seminary of America. See the biographical chronology.
ר׳ יוסף צבי הרץ begins his first pulpit at Congregation Adath Jeshurun, serving until 1898. See the Jewish Encyclopedia.
ר׳ יוסף צבי הרץ becomes rabbi of the Witwatersrand Old Hebrew Congregation and later teaches philosophy at Transvaal University College. See the Jewish Encyclopedia.
Returning to New York, ר׳ יוסף צבי הרץ serves Congregation Orach Chayim until his election to the British chief rabbinate. See the Encyclopaedia Judaica biography.
ר׳ יוסף צבי הרץ is elected Chief Rabbi of the United Hebrew Congregations of the British Empire, an office he holds for thirty-three years. See the official history.
ר׳ יוסף צבי הרץ begins his Imperial pastoral tour through South Africa, Rhodesia, Australasia and Canada. See the tour chronology.
During the Imperial tour, ר׳ יוסף צבי הרץ visits Jewish communities in Australia and New Zealand. See the tour chronology.
ר׳ יוסף צבי הרץ concludes the Canadian stage of his Imperial tour before returning to Britain. See the tour chronology.
During the war, ר׳ יוסף צבי הרץ additionally serves as acting principal of Jews’ College and advocates for European Jewry. See the Encyclopaedia Judaica biography.
ר׳ יוסף צבי הרץ helps found the Council of Christians and Jews to oppose antisemitism and promote cooperation. See the Council history.
ר׳ יוסף צבי הרץ dies in office on 14 January 1946 and is buried at Willesden Jewish Cemetery. See the Chief Rabbinate history.

ר׳ אלחנן בונם וסרמן.event: ר׳ אלחנן בונם וסרמן was born in Biržai, then in the Kovno Governorate of the Russian Empire, to Naftali Beinish and Sheina Rakhel. Biographical chronology
After his family moved to Bauska, ר׳ אלחנן בונם וסרמן entered the Telz yeshiva, studying under ר׳ אליעזר גורדון and ר׳ שמעון יהודה שקופ. Biographical chronology
ר׳ אלחנן בונם וסרמן moved to Brest-Litovsk and studied for two years under ר׳ חיים הלוי סולובייצ׳יק, whom he regarded as his principal teacher in analytical learning. Biographical chronology
After marrying Michla, daughter of ר׳ מאיר אטלס, ר׳ אלחנן בונם וסרמן settled in Salantai and devoted himself to study in his father-in-law’s household. Biographical chronology
ר׳ אלחנן בונם וסרמן and ר׳ יואל ברנצ׳יק founded a mesivta in Mstislavl, establishing his reputation as an educator. Biographical chronology
ר׳ אלחנן בונם וסרמן joined the Kodashim kollel of ר׳ ישראל מאיר הכהן in Radin, studying intensively there until 1910. Biographical chronology
At the encouragement of ר׳ ישראל מאיר הכהן, ר׳ אלחנן בונם וסרמן became rosh yeshiva of the Brest mesivta, leading it until war closed the school in 1914. Biographical chronology
During the First World War exile, ר׳ אלחנן בונם וסרמן assumed leadership of the displaced Radin yeshiva group in Smilavichy. Biographical chronology
ר׳ אלחנן בונם וסרמן settled in Baranovichi and became rosh yeshiva of Ohel Torah, which grew under him into a leading interwar yeshiva. Ohel Torah history

ר׳ אלחנן בונם וסרמן began a seventeen-month fundraising tour through the United States on behalf of Ohel Torah. New York represents the principal documented hub rather than every stop. American journey chronology
ר׳ אלחנן בונם וסרמן returned to Baranovichi and his students shortly before the German invasion of Poland. American journey chronology
War and occupation forced ר׳ אלחנן בונם וסרמן to Vilna, where he continued teaching refugees and students. Holocaust chronology
On 6 July 1941, ר׳ אלחנן בונם וסרמן was seized in Kovno and murdered with other rabbis at the Seventh Fort by Lithuanian collaborators. Holocaust chronology

ר׳ ירוחם הלוי ליבוביץ.event: ר׳ ירוחם הלוי ליבוביץ was born in Lyuban, in the Minsk region of the Russian Empire. Sources divide between approximately 1875 and 1873. English biography; Hebrew biography and alternative dating
As a young student, ר׳ ירוחם הלוי ליבוביץ entered Slabodka and came under the influence of ר׳ נתן צבי פינקל. The year is approximate. Kelm and Musar background; Biographical summary

ר׳ ירוחם הלוי ליבוביץ continued his formation at the Kelm Talmud Torah, absorbing the method of ר׳ שמחה זיסל זיו and studying for years with ר׳ נפתלי טרופ. The opening year is approximate. Kelm historical account; Jewish Observer biography
After advanced study in the Kodashim kollel at Radin, ר׳ ירוחם הלוי ליבוביץ became mashgiach of the Radin yeshiva. Jewish Observer biography; Hebrew chronology
ר׳ ירוחם הלוי ליבוביץ left Radin and joined the Mir yeshiva as mashgiach, bringing the disciplined Kelm approach into Mir’s educational programme. Hebrew chronology; History of Lithuanian yeshivot

The First World War separated ר׳ ירוחם הלוי ליבוביץ from the Mir yeshiva’s exile in Poltava; he returned to his family in Užventis and later assisted other displaced Lithuanian yeshivot. Hebrew chronology
During the postwar reconstruction, ר׳ ירוחם הלוי ליבוביץ served for a period at the Ponevezh yeshiva in Panevėžys. Hebrew chronology
ר׳ ירוחם הלוי ליבוביץ helped direct the restored Slabodka yeshiva while ר׳ נתן צבי פינקל was absent. Hebrew chronology
ר׳ ירוחם הלוי ליבוביץ returned permanently to Mir as mashgiach, beginning the period remembered as the yeshiva’s spiritual golden age. Mir Yeshiva institutional history
ר׳ ירוחם הלוי ליבוביץ died in Mir on 18 Sivan 5696 after complications from a stroke and was buried in the town’s Jewish cemetery. Biographical record; Extended memorial biography

ר׳ אליהו לופיאן.place: Grajewo, Łomża Governorate, Russian Empire; now Poland
ר׳ אליהו לופיאן.event: ר׳ אליהו לופיאן is born in Grajewo to Yaakov and Frida Lopian. The National Library authority record and most published biographies use 1876; an alternative tradition argues for 1872, so no exact civil birth date is asserted. The coordinate is town-level because the family home has not been securely identified. See the National Library of Israel authority record and ויקיפדיה העברית.

ר׳ אליהו לופיאן.place: Łomża, Łomża Governorate, Russian Empire; now Poland
ר׳ אליהו לופיאן.event: When his family emigrates to the United States, the young ר׳ אליהו לופיאן chooses to remain in Łomża so that he can continue intensive Torah study. He studies first in the junior framework and then in the main Łomża yeshiva under ר׳ אליעזר שולביץ, enduring serious poverty. Sources variously say he was nine or ten, so 1886 is an approximate marker. See ויקישיבה and ויקיפדיה העברית.

ר׳ אליהו לופיאן.place: Kelmė, Kovno Governorate, Russian Empire; now Lithuania
ר׳ אליהו לופיאן.event: ר׳ אליהו לופיאן enters the Kelm Talmud Torah and studies the disciplined Mussar method under ר׳ שמחה זיסל זיו and ר׳ יצחק בלאזר. Since sources say that he studied with ר׳ שמחה זיסל for more than a year before the latter's death in 1898, 1897 is an approximate but evidence-based marker. He also marries Sarah Leah, daughter of ר׳ יצחק דוד רוטמן, a Kelm disciple. See ויקיפדיה העברית and Encyclopaedia Judaica's biographical entry.

During the First World War, ר׳ אליהו לופיאן remains in Kelm with students and continues teaching while much of the population disperses. After the war he travels among Lithuanian towns to give Mussar talks and persuade former students to return, helping re-establish the Kelm institution that he had led with ר׳ יוסף לייב ננדיק. See ויקיפדיה העברית and ויקישיבה.

ר׳ אליהו לופיאן.place: Etz Chaim Yeshiva, Thrawl Street, Whitechapel, London
ר׳ אליהו לופיאן.event: ר׳ אליהו לופיאן settles in London and joins Etz Chaim Yeshiva as its Mussar educator and senior rabbinic leader, working alongside ר׳ נחמן שלמה גרינשפן. Sources disagree over whether his appointment/arrival should be dated 1926 or 1928; the institution's Thrawl Street premises were consecrated in 1926, and reference works date his appointment to that year, while the standard English biography gives immigration in 1928. The marker is placed on Thrawl Street rather than at a generic London coordinate. See the Orthodox Union biography, Encyclopaedia Judaica, and the surviving 1940 Etz Chaim magazine.

ר׳ אליהו לופיאן immigrates from Britain to Israel in 1950 and initially settles in Jerusalem. He delivers influential Mussar talks at the Zikhron Moshe and Kelilat Shaul synagogues and is associated with Kamenitz Yeshiva; contemporary newspaper notices also record his teaching activity in Jerusalem and Tel Aviv. See ויקיפדיה העברית and the surviving visa correspondence.

ר׳ אליהו לופיאן.place: Knesses Chizkiyahu Yeshiva, Zikhron Ya'akov, Israel
ר׳ אליהו לופיאן.event: At approximately seventy-five, ר׳ אליהו לופיאן accepts appointment as mashgiach ruchani of Knesses Chizkiyahu in Zikhron Ya'akov. Before accepting, he consults ר׳ אברהם ישעיהו קרליץ, whose blessing 'עוד ינובון בשיבה' encourages him to continue public teaching in old age. See Dirshu's account and ויקיפדיה העברית.

ר׳ אליהו לופיאן.place: Knesses Chizkiyahu Yeshiva, Kfar Hasidim–Rekhasim, Israel
ר׳ אליהו לופיאן.event: When Knesses Chizkiyahu transfers from Zikhron Ya'akov to its new campus beside Kfar Hasidim in April 1955, ר׳ אליהו לופיאן moves with the yeshiva and continues as its revered spiritual director. After the sudden death of rosh yeshiva ר׳ נח שימונוביץ, he helps stabilize the institution and supports the appointment of ר׳ אליהו מישקובסקי. The coordinate follows the documented yeshiva location, not the center of Haifa. See the institutional history and ויקישיבה.

In his final years, ר׳ אליהו לופיאן lives in Jerusalem's Bayit VeGan neighborhood with his daughter Chaya Ita and son-in-law ר׳ קלמן עזריאל פינסקי, while remaining closely identified with Knesses Chizkiyahu. The year is approximate because the source describes his last years without supplying a moving date. See ויקיפדיה העברית.

ר׳ אליהו לופיאן.place: Jerusalem and the Mount of Olives Jewish Cemetery
ר׳ אליהו לופיאן.event: ר׳ אליהו לופיאן dies in Jerusalem on 21 September 1970, corresponding to 20 Elul 5730, aged about ninety-four under the canonical 1876 chronology. He is buried in the Jewish cemetery on the Mount of Olives. See the National Library of Israel authority record, the Hebrew biography and contemporary newspaper reference, and the English biographical record.

ר׳ פינחס דוד הלוי הורוביץ.event: ר׳ פינחס דוד הלוי הורוביץ is born in Jerusalem in 1876 (some civil records give 15 July 1877), into a Nikolsburg-Lelov Hasidic family. The coordinate is neighbourhood-level, not a claimed birth house. See the Encyclopaedia Judaica-derived entry and sourced biography.

ר׳ פינחס דוד הלוי הורוביץ.place: Mea Shearim, Jerusalem, Ottoman Empire; year approximate
ר׳ פינחס דוד הלוי הורוביץ.event: After his father’s death, ר׳ פינחס דוד הלוי הורוביץ studies under his uncle ר׳ דוד בידרמן מלעלוב and supports early rabbinic activity through architectural work, including expansion associated with Mea Shearim. The year is approximate. See the specialist encyclopedia entry and biographical sketch.

ר׳ פינחס דוד הלוי הורוביץ.place: Europe and Russian Empire; mission route not precisely recoverable
ר׳ פינחס דוד הלוי הורוביץ.event: The Jerusalem community sends ר׳ פינחס דוד הלוי הורוביץ to Europe as its representative in a rabbinic dispute. The First World War prevents his return; no speculative city-to-city route is plotted. See the Encyclopaedia Judaica-derived biography.

ר׳ פינחס דוד הלוי הורוביץ arrives in Boston to collect charity and forms a Hasidic court, giving rise to the Boston dynasty. He strengthens traditional observance, education and communal kashrut. See the history of the Boston dynasty and biographical account.

ר׳ פינחס דוד הלוי הורוביץ.place: Williamsburg, Brooklyn, New York, United States
ר׳ פינחס דוד הלוי הורוביץ.event: ר׳ פינחס דוד הלוי הורוביץ moves his court from Boston to Williamsburg and opens a Bostoner beth midrash there. See the sourced biography and dynastic history.

ר׳ פינחס דוד הלוי הורוביץ.place: Williamsburg, Brooklyn, New York, United States
ר׳ פינחס דוד הלוי הורוביץ.event: ר׳ פינחס דוד הלוי הורוביץ dies in Williamsburg on 28 November 1941. His sons ר׳ משה הורוביץ and ר׳ לוי יצחק הורוביץ continue the dynasty; his remains are later reinterred in Jerusalem. See the sourced biography and German biographical account.

ר׳ אברהם ישעיהו קרליץ.event: ר׳ אברהם ישעיהו קרליץ is born in Kosava on 7 November 1878 to the town’s rabbi ר׳ שמריהו יוסף קרליץ and Rasha Leah Katzenelbogen. See the biographical summary.
After marriage ר׳ אברהם ישעיהו קרליץ settles in Kvidan, where his wife supports the household and he concentrates on study and writing. See the scholarly biography.
ר׳ אברהם ישעיהו קרליץ anonymously publishes the first volume of Chazon Ish, the title by which he becomes known. See the publication history.
War displacement brings ר׳ אברהם ישעיהו קרליץ to Stowbtsy; he subsequently spends time in Minsk before returning. See the scholarly life study.
ר׳ אברהם ישעיהו קרליץ settles in Vilna, studies and writes in relative anonymity, and develops ties with ר׳ חיים עוזר גרודזנסקי. See the biographical account.

ר׳ אברהם ישעיהו קרליץ immigrates to the Land of Israel and settles in Bnei Brak, where he becomes a central halakhic and communal authority without accepting formal office. See the documented migration.

ר׳ אברהם ישעיהו קרליץ.place: Chazon Ish home and Shomrei Shabbos Cemetery, Bnei Brak
ר׳ אברהם ישעיהו קרליץ.event: ר׳ אברהם ישעיהו קרליץ dies at his Bnei Brak home on 24 October 1953 and is buried in the Shomrei Shabbos cemetery. See the death record.

ר׳ אליעזר יהודה פינקל.event: ר׳ אליעזר יהודה פינקל is born in Kelm to ר׳ נתן צבי פינקל and Gittel Wolpert. Sources disagree between 1877 and 1879; the standard 1879 chronology is used here. See the National Library authority record and Encyclopaedia Judaica biography.
The family of ר׳ אליעזר יהודה פינקל moves to Slabodka, where his father develops Yeshivat Knesset Yisrael and gives him his early education. See the Hebrew biographical account.
After study at Telz, ר׳ אליעזר יהודה פינקל studies in Brisk under ר׳ חיים הלוי סולובייצ׳יק, a major influence on his Talmudic method. See the Hebrew chronology.
ר׳ אליעזר יהודה פינקל is among the students sent to strengthen the new Slutsk yeshiva of ר׳ יעקב דוד וילובסקי, before further study at Halusk, Radin and Mir. See the Hebrew biography.
ר׳ אליעזר יהודה פינקל marries Malka Kamai, daughter of rosh yeshiva ר׳ אליהו ברוך קמאי, and joins Mir’s leadership shortly afterward. See the sourced biography.
Following the death of ר׳ אליהו ברוך קמאי, ר׳ אליעזר יהודה פינקל becomes rosh yeshiva of Mir while the institution is displaced by the First World War. See the manuscript catalogue biography.
ר׳ אליעזר יהודה פינקל returns to Mir as its chief spiritual and institutional leader; enrollment grows into an international student body during the interwar period. See the encyclopedic account.
Having travelled to Palestine seeking visas and a future refuge for Mir students, ר׳ אליעזר יהודה פינקל remains there after war prevents return to Europe. See the Mir Yeshiva institutional history.
ר׳ אליעזר יהודה פינקל opens the Jerusalem Mir with ten students, initially in Meah Shearim and then in Beit Yisrael near the present campus. See the institutional chronology and Mir memorial history.
ר׳ אליעזר יהודה פינקל dies in Jerusalem on 19 July 1965 and is buried on Har HaMenuchot. See the National Library record and biography.

ר׳ משה סולובייצ׳יק.event: ר׳ משה סולובייצ׳יק is born in Volozhin in 1879 to ר׳ חיים סולובייצ׳יק and studies with him until the Volozhin yeshiva closes in 1892. See the official RIETS history.
After Volozhin closes, ר׳ משה סולובייצ׳יק moves with his family to Brisk, where his father develops the analytical method the son will later transmit abroad. See the RIETS institutional biography.
At about twenty-three ר׳ משה סולובייצ׳יק marries Pesya, daughter of ר׳ אליהו פיינשטיין, and lives for several years in Pruzhany. See the RIETS history.
In 1910 ר׳ משה סולובייצ׳יק becomes rabbi of Raseiniai and establishes a yeshiva there. See the RIETS biography.
In 1913 ר׳ משה סולובייצ׳יק is appointed rabbi of Khislavichi in the Smolensk region, serving there through the upheavals of war and revolution. See the RIETS history.

In 1921 ר׳ משה סולובייצ׳יק accepts the Mizrachi movement’s invitation to lead Talmud studies at Tachkemoni in Warsaw after declining to displace his brother ר׳ יצחק זאב סולובייצ׳יק in Brisk. See the official RIETS account.

ר׳ משה סולובייצ׳יק.place: RIETS, Washington Heights, New York City
ר׳ משה סולובייצ׳יק.event: In 1929 ר׳ משה סולובייצ׳יק immigrates to New York and joins RIETS as rosh yeshiva, bringing the Brisker method into the center of American Orthodox higher learning. See the Yeshiva University history.
On 31 January 1941 ר׳ משה סולובייצ׳יק dies in New York after more than a decade at RIETS; his teaching continues through his students and sons. See the RIETS institutional biography.

ר׳ צבי הירש פרבר.event: ר׳ צבי הירש פרבר is born in Slabodka beside Kovno in approximately 1878 or 1879. Encyclopaedia Judaica and manuscript catalogues use 1879; JCR-UK gives 18 September 1878. See Encyclopaedia Judaica, the JCR-UK minister profile and the National Library archive.

As a young scholar, ר׳ צבי הירש פרבר studies in the Lithuanian yeshiva world. Biographical and manuscript sources connect him with ר׳ יצחק אלחנן ספקטור, ר׳ יצחק בלאזר and ר׳ נפתלי אמסטרדם; the displayed year is an approximate educational marker rather than a documented enrollment date. See the specialist Kedem manuscript description.

After migrating to Britain in 1910 or 1911, ר׳ צבי הירש פרבר teaches Talmud in Manchester and is associated with the foundation or early leadership of its yeshiva. Encyclopaedia Judaica dates his settlement in England to 1911, while the National Library and manuscript sources use 1910. See Encyclopaedia Judaica, Kedem and the JCR-UK profile.

In July 1913, ר׳ צבי הירש פרבר becomes rabbi of the West End Talmud Torah Synagogue in Soho, later known as the West End Great Synagogue. He will serve this immigrant congregation for more than forty years. See JCR-UK and Encyclopaedia Judaica.

During the First World War years in London, ר׳ צבי הירש פרבר forms a close relationship with ר׳ אברהם יצחק הכהן קוק. Their surviving correspondence reflects rabbinic cooperation and friendship; a 1921 recommendation from ר׳ אברהם יצחק הכהן קוק is preserved in the archive. See the National Library of Israel archive description.

While serving in London, ר׳ צבי הירש פרבר begins publishing כרם הצבי, his principal halakhic and aggadic commentary on the Torah. The first volume was printed in Vienna, but that publication location is not evidence that he personally relocated there. The Torah series continued through 1938. See Encyclopaedia Judaica and the description of his autograph manuscript at Kedem.

ר׳ צבי הירש פרבר publishes בירור הלכה, addressing the halakhic consequences of civil marriage and divorce. Archival papers preserve the rabbinic controversy generated by the work, making this an unusually well-documented episode in his legal career. See the National Library of Israel archive.

Around 1947, ר׳ צבי הירש פרבר drafts צהלת הצבי; portions are later printed in ספר המועדים (London, 1950). Surviving autograph leaves, drafts and letters reveal an active working scholar rather than only a public preacher. See the manuscript description and dating.

After more than four decades at the West End congregation, ר׳ צבי הירש פרבר retires in 1954 or 1955. The one-year discrepancy reflects differing institutional summaries, not a second appointment. See Encyclopaedia Judaica and the JCR-UK profile.

ר׳ צבי הירש פרבר dies in London in November 1966 after a career joining Lithuanian rabbinic learning to the institutions of immigrant British Orthodoxy. Encyclopaedia Judaica and manuscript specialists give 1966; the National Library authority heading's 1967 endpoint is retained as a catalogue variant in this record's date note. See Encyclopaedia Judaica, Kedem and the National Library archive.

ר׳ יוסף יצחק שניאורסון.event: ר׳ יוסף יצחק שניאורסון is born on 12 Tammuz 5640 in Lyubavichi. See the Chabad chronology.
After his marriage, ר׳ יוסף יצחק שניאורסון is appointed to direct Tomchei Temimim and increasingly represents his father in communal affairs. See the Chabad chronology.
The Lubavitch court relocates to Rostov, where ר׳ יוסף יצחק שניאורסון continues educational and relief work. See the extended biography.
Following his father’s death, ר׳ יוסף יצחק שניאורסון becomes the sixth Lubavitcher Rebbe and organizes underground religious life. See the Chabad chronology.
Forced from Rostov, ר׳ יוסף יצחק שניאורסון establishes his headquarters in Leningrad and directs a clandestine religious network. See the Chabad biography.
Soviet police arrest ר׳ יוסף יצחק שניאורסון; his death sentence is commuted to exile and then cancelled after international intervention. See the documented chronology.
In October, ר׳ יוסף יצחק שניאורסון leaves the Soviet Union and establishes his court in Riga. See the Chabad biography.
ר׳ יוסף יצחק שניאורסון visits Jerusalem and Hebron before continuing to the United States. See the Chabad chronology.
ר׳ יוסף יצחק שניאורסון transfers the Chabad center to Poland and settles at Otwock. See the extended biography.
The German invasion traps ר׳ יוסף יצחק שניאורסון in Warsaw; an unusual rescue negotiated through American officials escorts him out. See the USHMM account.
On 19 March, ר׳ יוסף יצחק שניאורסון reaches New York and establishes Chabad headquarters at 770 Eastern Parkway. See the Chabad biography.
ר׳ יוסף יצחק שניאורסון dies on 10 Shevat 5710 and is buried at Montefiore Cemetery. See the Wikimedia authority record.

ר׳ יחיאל יעקב ויינברג.event: ר׳ יחיאל יעקב ויינברג is born in Ciechanowiec, now Poland; this corrects the former record’s erroneous Ivye birthplace. See the National Library of Israel biography.
ר׳ יחיאל יעקב ויינברג studies at the Mir yeshiva before continuing to Slabodka; the year is approximate. See the biographical overview.
ר׳ יחיאל יעקב ויינברג studies at Knesset Yisrael under ר׳ נתן צבי פינקל; the year is approximate. See the biographical overview.
After marrying Esther Levine, ר׳ יחיאל יעקב ויינברג becomes communal and crown rabbi of Pilviškiai for about seven years. See the biographical overview.
At the outbreak of war, ר׳ יחיאל יעקב ויינברג moves to Germany and pursues university study at Giessen, earning a doctorate. See the Deutsche Biographie.
ר׳ יחיאל יעקב ויינברג joins the Berlin seminary faculty and later becomes its final rector. See the Posen Library biography.
After leaving Nazi Germany, ר׳ יחיאל יעקב ויינברג becomes trapped in Warsaw and assists communal life under occupation. See the National Library biography.

The Germans transfer ר׳ יחיאל יעקב ויינברג, a Soviet citizen, from the Warsaw Ghetto to Wülzburg detention camp, where he remains until April 1945. See the National Library summary of Marc B. Shapiro’s study.
His student ר׳ שאול ויינגורט brings ר׳ יחיאל יעקב ויינברג to Montreux, where he spends his final two decades writing and corresponding. See the National Library biography.
ר׳ יחיאל יעקב ויינברג dies on 24 January 1966 and is buried at Har HaMenuchot in Jerusalem. See the Deutsche Biographie.

ר׳ אריה לוין.place: Orla near Białystok, Russian Empire; now Poland
ר׳ אריה לוין.event: ר׳ אריה לוין is born on 22 March 1885 in Orla near Białystok to Binyamin Beinush and Ethel. The town then lay in the Pale of Settlement of the Russian Empire and is now in Poland. See the Aryeh Levin Heritage Center, the Lehi Heritage Association biography, and the National Library archival record.

ר׳ אריה לוין.place: Hlyusk, Minsk Governorate, Russian Empire; date approximate
ר׳ אריה לוין.event: After periods of study in Slutsk, Slonim, Brest and Pinsk, the young ר׳ אריה לוין studies in Hlyusk under ר׳ ברוך דב ליבוביץ. The source establishes his sequence of yeshivot but not a complete year-by-year itinerary, so 1899 is an approximate map marker. See the Aryeh Levin Heritage Center biography.

ר׳ אריה לוין.place: Volozhin, Russian Empire; now Valozhyn, Belarus
ר׳ אריה לוין.event: Having initially been refused because of his youth, ר׳ אריה לוין is accepted into the Volozhin yeshivah and studies under ר׳ רפאל שפירא. The exact admission year is not supplied by the heritage biography, making 1901 an approximate marker. See the Aryeh Levin Heritage Center.

ר׳ אריה לוין immigrates to Ottoman Palestine in 1905 and lands at Jaffa. There he meets ר׳ אברהם יצחק הכהן קוק, beginning a close relationship that shapes his religious and communal life. See the Aryeh Levin Heritage Center and the Lehi Heritage Association.

Soon after arriving, ר׳ אריה לוין settles in Jerusalem, studies at Yeshivat Torat Chaim and marries Tzipora Chana, daughter of ר׳ דוד שפירא. Jerusalem remains his home for the rest of his life. See the Aryeh Levin Heritage Center and the Da'at biographical entry.
ר׳ אריה לוין receives rabbinic ordination from ר׳ חיים ברלין, ר׳ שמואל סלנט and ר׳ אברהם יצחק הכהן קוק. See the Aryeh Levin Heritage Center and the Da'at biography.

ר׳ אריה לוין becomes mashgiaḥ and spiritual educator at the Etz Chaim Talmud Torah, a position he retains until his death. His work centres on children, including pupils from impoverished homes, rather than pursuit of a prestigious communal rabbinate. See the Aryeh Levin Heritage Center and the Lehi Heritage Association.

By the late 1920s, ר׳ אריה לוין regularly walks to Jerusalem's Central Prison on Sabbaths and festivals to pray with Jewish inmates, listen to them and maintain contact with their families. The work begins with criminal prisoners and later embraces imprisoned members of the Haganah, Irgun and Lehi, earning him the title אבי האסירים. See the Aryeh Levin Heritage Center and the Israel Ministry of Defense Underground Prisoners Museum.

ר׳ אריה לוין.place: Jerusalem hospitals and leprosy hospital in Talbiya
ר׳ אריה לוין.event: Alongside his prison ministry, ר׳ אריה לוין regularly visits patients across Jerusalem, including people isolated in the leprosy hospital in Talbiya; he also visits the related institution in Bethlehem. The displayed year represents a long-running practice, not its documented beginning. See the Aryeh Levin Heritage Center and the Lehi Heritage Association.

ר׳ אריה לוין.place: Jerusalem; identification of the Lamed-Heh remains
ר׳ אריה לוין.event: After the remains of the Lamed-Heh convoy are returned for burial and twelve cannot be conventionally distinguished, ר׳ צבי פסח פרנק asks ר׳ אריה לוין to conduct the traditional גורל הגר״א procedure. Its results are accepted by the bereaved families, the army and state authorities. This was a religious ritual accepted in its historical context, not modern forensic identification. See the Aryeh Levin Heritage Center.

After the establishment of Israel, ר׳ אריה לוין establishes Yeshivat Beit Aryeh in the courtyard of his modest Jerusalem home and appoints his son-in-law ר׳ אליעזר פלצינסקי to lead it. The precise opening year is not given, so 1950 is an approximate post-independence marker. See the Aryeh Levin Heritage Center.

ר׳ אריה לוין.place: Hadassah Medical Center and Sanhedria Cemetery, Jerusalem
ר׳ אריה לוין.event: ר׳ אריה לוין dies at Hadassah Medical Center on Friday, 28 March 1969, immediately before Shabbat HaGadol, and is buried that afternoon in Sanhedria Cemetery. The timing permits fulfillment of his request that no eulogies be delivered. See the Aryeh Levin Heritage Center and the National Library archival authority record.

ר׳ איסר יהודה אונטרמן.event: ר׳ איסר יהודה אונטרמן is born in Brest-Litovsk on 19 April 1886. See the National Library authority record and Encyclopaedia Judaica biography.
At twelve, ר׳ איסר יהודה אונטרמן joins the founding group of the Etz Chaim branch in Maltsh and studies under ר׳ זלמן סנדר כהנא שפירא and later ר׳ שמעון שקופ. See the Hebrew biographical chronology.
ר׳ איסר יהודה אונטרמן studies in the Volozhin kollel and receives semikhah from ר׳ רפאל שפירא; he also receives ordination from ר׳ שמחה זליג ריגר in Brest. See the encyclopedic biography.
At about twenty-four, ר׳ איסר יהודה אונטרמן establishes and leads a yeshiva in Vishneva before serving a succession of Lithuanian communities. See the Encyclopaedia Judaica account.
ר׳ איסר יהודה אונטרמן becomes rabbi of Grodno, his final Eastern European office, and assists in rebuilding communal and yeshiva life after war. See the encyclopedic biography.

ר׳ איסר יהודה אונטרמן is appointed rabbi of Liverpool, where he develops communal education, creates an academy for Torah study and becomes a prominent British Mizrachi leader. See JCR-UK’s documented rabbinical profile.
ר׳ איסר יהודה אונטרמן arrives to serve as Ashkenazi chief rabbi of Tel Aviv–Jaffa, later founding a kollel and a special agunah court. See the contemporary biographical record and sourced chronology.
ר׳ איסר יהודה אונטרמן is elected Ashkenazi Chief Rabbi of Israel and president of the Great Rabbinical Court, serving until 1972. See the documented election chronology.
ר׳ איסר יהודה אונטרמן dies in Jerusalem on 26 January 1976 and is buried on the Mount of Olives. See the Government Press Office portrait record and biography.

ר׳ יחזקאל אברמסקי.place: Dashkovichy, Grodno Governorate, Russian Empire; now Belarus
ר׳ יחזקאל אברמסקי.event: ר׳ יחזקאל אברמסקי is born on 7 February 1886 at Dashkovichy in the Grodno region. The coordinate is village-level because no birth building is documented. See the Russian Jewish Encyclopedia and sourced biography.

ר׳ יחזקאל אברמסקי.place: Telšiai, Russian Empire; now Lithuania; year approximate
ר׳ יחזקאל אברמסקי.event: During his advanced yeshiva education ר׳ יחזקאל אברמסקי studies at Telz and other Lithuanian academies before learning at Brisk under ר׳ חיים הלוי סולובייצ׳יק. The year is approximate and avoids inventing undocumented annual moves. See the biographical account.

ר׳ יחזקאל אברמסקי.place: Smolyan, Mogilev Governorate, Russian Empire; now Smalyany, Belarus
ר׳ יחזקאל אברמסקי.event: ר׳ יחזקאל אברמסקי begins serving the Smolyan community, the first securely dated stage of his rabbinic career. See the Russian Jewish Encyclopedia.

ר׳ יחזקאל אברמסקי.place: Smalyavichy, Minsk Governorate, Russian Empire; now Belarus
ר׳ יחזקאל אברמסקי.event: ר׳ יחזקאל אברמסקי becomes rabbi of Smalyavichy, serving through the revolutionary upheavals and early Soviet period. See the Russian Jewish Encyclopedia.

ר׳ יחזקאל אברמסקי assumes the Slutsk rabbinate. He maintains religious institutions under persecution and later helps ר׳ שלמה יוסף זוין publish Yagdil Torah. See the Slutsk memorial history and Russian Jewish Encyclopedia.

ר׳ יחזקאל אברמסקי.place: Soviet prison and Siberian forced labour; precise camp coordinate uncertain
ר׳ יחזקאל אברמסקי.event: Soviet authorities arrest ר׳ יחזקאל אברמסקי for his religious leadership and send him to forced labour. The map uses a broad regional point because the surviving summaries disagree or do not securely identify a precise camp. See the sourced biography and Russian Jewish Encyclopedia.
After his 1931 release and departure from the Soviet Union, ר׳ יחזקאל אברמסקי settles in London and serves the Machzike Hadath community in the East End. See the biographical account.

ר׳ יחזקאל אברמסקי.place: London Beth Din, London, United Kingdom
ר׳ יחזקאל אברמסקי.event: ר׳ יחזקאל אברמסקי joins and then leads the London Beth Din, serving for seventeen years and enhancing its international halakhic authority. The coordinate is central-London institutional rather than a claim about one permanent historic building. See the sourced biography.

ר׳ יחזקאל אברמסקי retires from the London Beth Din and settles in Jerusalem, where he continues teaching and writing. In 1956 he receives the Israel Prize for rabbinic literature. See the biographical account.
ר׳ יחזקאל אברמסקי dies in Jerusalem on 19 September 1976 and is buried at Har HaMenuchot. See the sourced biography.

ר׳ יצחק זאב הלוי סולובייצ׳יק.place: Volozhin, Russian Empire; now Valozhyn, Belarus
ר׳ יצחק זאב הלוי סולובייצ׳יק.event: ר׳ יצחק זאב הלוי סולובייצ׳יק is born in Volozhin on 20 Tishrei 5647 (19 October 1886) to ר׳ חיים הלוי סולובייצ׳יק and Lifsha, daughter of ר׳ רפאל שפירא. His father is then teaching at the Volozhin yeshivah. See Encyclopaedia Judaica, the National Library of Israel and Sefaria's authority record.

ר׳ יצחק זאב הלוי סולובייצ׳יק.place: Brisk, Grodno Governorate, Russian Empire; now Brest, Belarus
ר׳ יצחק זאב הלוי סולובייצ׳יק.event: When ר׳ חיים הלוי סולובייצ׳יק becomes rabbi of Brisk, the young ר׳ יצחק זאב הלוי סולובייצ׳יק moves with the family to the city that will define his public identity. He studies principally under his father and absorbs the analytic method later called the Brisker derekh. See Encyclopaedia Judaica and the scholarly bibliography at the National Library of Israel.

ר׳ יצחק זאב הלוי סולובייצ׳יק.place: Brisk, reborn Polish state; now Brest, Belarus
ר׳ יצחק זאב הלוי סולובייצ׳יק.event: Following the death of ר׳ חיים הלוי סולובייצ׳יק, ר׳ יצחק זאב הלוי סולובייצ׳יק succeeds his father as rabbi and av beit din of Brisk; surviving communal correspondence documents his authority by 1920. He combines the rabbinate with highly selective Talmudic teaching. See Encyclopaedia Judaica and the 1920 signed communal letter.

ר׳ יצחק זאב הלוי סולובייצ׳יק and his brothers publish their father ר׳ חיים הלוי סולובייצ׳יק's חידושי רבנו חיים הלוי על הרמב״ם in Brisk. The painstaking editorial process and introductory statement become key documents of the family's approach to exact formulation. See the first-edition description and the National Library bibliography.

The German invasion finds ר׳ יצחק זאב הלוי סולובייצ׳יק away from Brisk at the health resort of Krynica. He and his son ר׳ יוסף דוב reach Warsaw but cannot return home; this begins the wartime flight that permanently separates him from Brisk and from family members later murdered in the Holocaust. See the documented chapter summary of The Brisker Rav and the historical account in Mishpacha.

From Warsaw, ר׳ יצחק זאב הלוי סולובייצ׳יק escapes to Vilna, which has become a crowded refuge for Polish and Lithuanian yeshivot and rabbis. He teaches a small selected group while seeking a route out of Europe and receives certificates for entry to Mandatory Palestine. See The Brisker Rav, Mishpacha's historical account and the Kedem biographical note.

ר׳ יצחק זאב הלוי סולובייצ׳יק reaches Mandatory Palestine with several of his children in 1941 and settles in Jerusalem. His wife Alte Hendel and children unable to escape from Brisk are later murdered. In Jerusalem he teaches a selected circle in his home rather than immediately founding a conventional public yeshivah. See Encyclopaedia Judaica, The Brisker Rav and a surviving telegram bearing his Press Street address.

During the formation of the State of Israel, ר׳ יצחק זאב הלוי סולובייצ׳יק becomes an influential leader of Jerusalem's anti-Zionist Lithuanian Haredi public. He opposes incorporation of independent Torah institutions into state structures and intervenes through letters on education, conscription, Jerusalem and religious autonomy. See the scholarly Haredi Society Research Group bibliography and his documented 1947 Jerusalem letter.

ר׳ יצחק זאב הלוי סולובייצ׳יק dies at his Jerusalem home on 9 Tishrei 5720 (11 October 1959), immediately before Yom Kippur, and is buried at Har HaMenuchot. Contemporary reporting records the death and public mourning; his sons and students subsequently publish his writings and institutionalize several Jerusalem Brisk yeshivot. See the contemporary JTA obituary, the National Library catalogue and Sefaria.

ר׳ יוסף שלמה כהנמן.event: ר׳ יוסף שלמה כהנמן is born in Kuliai on 2 June 1886 to Yehuda Leib and Ita Leah Kahaneman. See the YIVO Encyclopedia and Hebrew biography.
At fourteen, ר׳ יוסף שלמה כהנמן enters Telz Yeshiva, studying for six years under ר׳ אליעזר גורדון and ר׳ שמעון שקופ before continuing at Novardok and Radin. See the sourced educational chronology.
ר׳ יוסף שלמה כהנמן studies at Radin under ר׳ ישראל מאיר הכהן and ר׳ נפתלי טרופ after a short period at Novardok. See the biographical account and historical profile.
ר׳ יוסף שלמה כהנמן marries Feige Rubin, becomes rabbi of Vidzy and establishes a yeshiva. See the YIVO Encyclopedia.
ר׳ יוסף שלמה כהנמן becomes rabbi of Panevėžys and develops its yeshiva, schools and orphanage into a major Lithuanian Torah centre. See the YIVO biography.

As a member of the Lithuanian Seimas from 1923 to 1925, ר׳ יוסף שלמה כהנמן represents Jewish communal interests while continuing to lead institutions in Panevėžys. The national parliament met in Kaunas. See the YIVO Encyclopedia.

The outbreak of war catches ר׳ יוסף שלמה כהנמן during a visit to Palestine. Soviet occupation prevents his return to Lithuania, and he begins rescue and rebuilding efforts from Palestine. See the YIVO chronology.

ר׳ יוסף שלמה כהנמן re-establishes Ponevezh Yeshiva in Bnei Brak with a small first group of students, beginning the wider Kiryat HaYeshiva and Batei Avot complex. See the Encyclopaedia Judaica-derived account and YIVO Encyclopedia.
ר׳ יוסף שלמה כהנמן dies on 3 September 1969 after transforming Ponevezh into a central institution of postwar Torah life. See the National Library portrait record and Hebrew biography.

ר׳ יהודה מאיר שפירא.event: ר׳ יהודה מאיר שפירא נולד בז׳ באדר תרמ״ז (3 במרץ 1887) בשאץ שבבוקובינה. YIVO Encyclopedia
לאחר נישואיו למלכה טובה ברייטמן עבר ר׳ יהודה מאיר שפירא לטרנופול, המשיך בלימוד ובהוראה והחל להתפרסם כעילוי משאץ. JewishHistory.org biography
ר׳ יהודה מאיר שפירא קיבל את משרת הרבנות הראשונה שלו בגלינה, הקים מסגרות חינוך ופעל לשיקום הקהילה. YIVO Encyclopedia
ר׳ יהודה מאיר שפירא נתמנה לרבה של סאנוק לאחר מלחמת העולם הראשונה והרחיב בה את פעילותו הציבורית והתורנית. YIVO Encyclopedia
ר׳ יהודה מאיר שפירא נבחר לסיים הפולני מטעם אגודת ישראל ושימש בו עד 1927 כנציג האורתודוקסיה היהודית. YIVO Encyclopedia
בכנסייה הגדולה של אגודת ישראל בווינה הציע ר׳ יהודה מאיר שפירא את לימוד הדף היומי; המחזור העולמי הראשון החל בראש השנה תרפ״ד, 11 בספטמבר 1923. D.A.F. history of Daf Yomi
ר׳ יהודה מאיר שפירא נעשה רבה של פיוטרקוב, ובה המשיך בפעילותו הציבורית והדפיס את שו״ת אור המאיר בשנת 1926. National Library of Israel
ר׳ יהודה מאיר שפירא חנך את הבניין החדש של ישיבת חכמי לובלין והיה לראש הישיבה ולרבה של לובלין. YIVO Encyclopedia
ר׳ יהודה מאיר שפירא נפטר בלובלין בז׳ בחשוון תרצ״ד (27 באוקטובר 1933) ונקבר בעיר; עצמותיו הועברו לירושלים ב־1958. Contemporary JTA obituary

ר׳ יואל טייטלבוים.event: ר׳ יואל טייטלבוים is born in Sighet on 26 Tevet 5647 (13 January 1887). See the YIVO Encyclopedia and detailed chronology.
ר׳ יואל טייטלבוים becomes rabbi of Irshava and establishes a yeshiva. See the biographical chronology.
ר׳ יואל טייטלבוים assumes the rabbinate of Carei, where his court and yeshiva expand. See the YIVO Encyclopedia.
After years of disputed elections, ר׳ יואל טייטלבוים formally assumes the Satu Mare rabbinate. See the YIVO Encyclopedia.
After the German occupation of Hungary, ר׳ יואל טייטלבוים is taken to the Cluj ghetto and included among the Kastner train passengers. See the USHMM history.
The Kastner group, including ר׳ יואל טייטלבוים, is detained at Bergen-Belsen before release to Switzerland in December. See the USHMM history.
After recuperating in Switzerland, ר׳ יואל טייטלבוים reaches Jerusalem in September 1945. See the biographical chronology.
ר׳ יואל טייטלבוים settles in Williamsburg and rebuilds Satmar around Congregation Yetev Lev and a broad institutional network. See the YIVO Encyclopedia.

While based in Brooklyn, ר׳ יואל טייטלבוים becomes president and gaon av beit din of the Edah HaChareidis; this marker records institutional leadership, not permanent relocation. See the YIVO Encyclopedia.
The purpose-built Satmar settlement of Kiryas Joel is established and named for ר׳ יואל טייטלבוים. See the municipal history.
ר׳ יואל טייטלבוים dies on 19 August 1979 and is buried in Kiryas Joel. See the YIVO Encyclopedia.

ר׳ יצחק אייזיק הלוי הרצוג.event: ר׳ יצחק אייזיק הלוי הרצוג is born in Łomża on 3 December 1888. This corrects the former record’s Irish birth coordinate. See the National Library collection biography.
ר׳ יצחק אייזיק הלוי הרצוג moves with his family to Leeds, where his father ר׳ יואל הרצוג holds rabbinic office and his son combines Torah and general studies. See the Jewish Agency biography.
ר׳ יצחק אייזיק הלוי הרצוג becomes rabbi of Belfast after completing advanced academic and rabbinic studies. See the Dictionary of Irish Biography.
ר׳ יצחק אייזיק הלוי הרצוג is appointed rabbi in Dublin and later becomes the first chief rabbi of the Irish Free State. See the Irish Jewish Museum.
Elected to succeed ר׳ אברהם יצחק הכהן קוק, ר׳ יצחק אייזיק הלוי הרצוג becomes Ashkenazi chief rabbi of Mandatory Palestine and settles in Jerusalem. See the National Library archive.

ר׳ יצחק אייזיק הלוי הרצוג tours European countries seeking Jewish child survivors hidden or sheltered during the Holocaust and arranging their Jewish rehabilitation. Brussels represents one documented centre of the wider mission. See Yad Vashem and the Rescue Children archive.

With statehood, ר׳ יצחק אייזיק הלוי הרצוג becomes Israel’s Ashkenazi chief rabbi and president of the Great Rabbinical Court, addressing law, army, conversion and religion-state questions. See the National Library authority record.
ר׳ יצחק אייזיק הלוי הרצוג dies in Jerusalem on 25 July 1959 and is buried in Sanhedria Cemetery. See the National Library record.

ר׳ קלונימוס קלמיש שפירא.event: ר׳ קלונימוס קלמיש שפירא is born in 1889 in Grodzisk Mazowiecki to ר׳ אלימלך שפירא and Chana Bracha Sternfeld. See the YIVO Encyclopedia and Warsaw Ghetto Museum biography.
As a teenager ר׳ קלונימוס קלמיש שפירא studies under ר׳ ירחמיאל משה הופשטיין of Kozhnitz and marries his daughter Rachel Chaya Miriam. The year is approximate. See the Herzog scholarly biography.
In 1913 ר׳ קלונימוס קלמיש שפירא is elected rabbi of Piaseczno, the office from which his enduring title derives. See the Warsaw Ghetto Museum and YIVO.
During the First World War ר׳ קלונימוס קלמיש שפירא moves his principal residence to Warsaw while retaining his association with Piaseczno. See the Herzog biography.
In 1923 ר׳ קלונימוס קלמיש שפירא founds Yeshivat Da’at Moshe in Warsaw, named for his teacher and father-in-law; by the 1930s it has roughly three hundred students. See the Herzog research profile.

After Germany invades Poland, ר׳ קלונימוס קלמיש שפירא returns from Piaseczno to his students in Warsaw. His home at 5 Dzielna Street becomes a center of worship, teaching, refuge and food relief. See the Warsaw Ghetto Museum biography.

From 1939 through 1942 ר׳ קלונימוס קלמיש שפירא delivers and repeatedly revises sermons responding to escalating persecution. He hides the manuscript with the Oneg Shabbat archive; it is recovered after the war and published as אש קודש in 1960. See the YIVO Encyclopedia.
Deported from Warsaw to Trawniki in spring 1943, ר׳ קלונימוס קלמיש שפירא is shot there on 3 November during Aktion Erntefest. See the Warsaw Ghetto Museum and YIVO.

ר׳ ראובן מרגליות.place: Lemberg, Galicia, Austria-Hungary; now Lviv, Ukraine
ר׳ ראובן מרגליות.event: ר׳ ראובן מרגליות is born in Lemberg on 7 Kislev 5650, corresponding to 30 November 1889, to Moshe and Miriam Margolies. See ויקיפדיה העברית and the Encyclopedia of the Founders and Builders of Israel.

At approximately eleven, ר׳ ראובן מרגליות writes an early booklet on Choshen Mishpat. Although he studies with ר׳ משה זאב מזוזה and ר׳ דוד טוניס, his education becomes predominantly self-directed in the Zidichov Hasidic study house. The year is derived from his reported age. See ויקיפדיה העברית.

After his father dies when he is fourteen, ר׳ ראובן מרגליות leaves full-time formal study to manage the family shop while continuing intensive independent learning and beginning to publish in Hebrew periodicals. The year is approximate, based on his age. See ויקיפדיה העברית.

ר׳ ראובן מרגליות publishes his first book, תולדות אדם, a biography and study of ר׳ שמואל אליעזר איידלס. The book inaugurates a publishing career that will exceed fifty volumes. See English Wikipedia's bibliography and the National Library of Israel authority record.

At twenty-four, ר׳ ראובן מרגליות receives rabbinic ordination from ר׳ מאיר אריק and ר׳ משה באב״ד. He nevertheless declines to make a salaried rabbinate his profession and develops a book business that becomes a scholarly meeting place. See ויקיפדיה העברית.

During the First World War, ר׳ ראובן מרגליות flees Lemberg for Vienna. After receiving an Austro-Hungarian conscription order, he hides for roughly two years and composes נפש חיה under severe conditions, sometimes studying by the glow of a stove to avoid detection. The displayed year is approximate within the wartime period. See his account as reproduced by ויקיפדיה העברית.

Back in Lwów, ר׳ ראובן מרגליות combines publishing and bookselling with leadership in Mizrachi and Zionist activity in Eastern Galicia, including religious-national education and Jewish National Fund work. He publishes קוי אור and טל תחיה, considering Jewish law in relation to renewed Jewish public life in the Land of Israel. See the contemporary Ha-Mitzpeh newspaper record and ויקיפדיה העברית.

Following the death of his first wife, ר׳ ראובן מרגליות immigrates to Mandatory Palestine in Tevet 5695 and settles in Tel Aviv. Although ר׳ מאיר שפירא, ר׳ אברהם יצחק הכהן קוק and ר׳ בן ציון מאיר חי עוזיאל had proposed a communal rabbinate, he chooses scholarship and library work. See ויקיפדיה העברית and David Tidhar's contemporary biographical encyclopedia.

ר׳ ראובן מרגליות.place: Rambam Library, Tel Aviv, Mandatory Palestine
ר׳ ראובן מרגליות.event: From the period of his immigration, ר׳ ראובן מרגליות directs Tel Aviv's Rambam Library. During his tenure it grows from a very small collection into a research library of approximately 54,000 volumes, while he continues editing and publishing rabbinic works. The precise administrative start is sometimes described simply as 1934; 1935 marks his first full year in the country. See ויקיפדיה העברית and the National Library of Israel.

ר׳ ראובן מרגליות receives the Israel Prize for rabbinic literature, principally recognizing his pioneering annotated editions and comparative research on the Zoharic corpus. He donates the prize money to Mossad Harav Kook. See contemporary coverage in Davar and the detailed award account in ויקיפדיה העברית.

ר׳ ראובן מרגליות retires after more than three decades directing the Rambam Library and receives the key to the city of Tel Aviv. ר׳ עזריאל הילדסהיימר succeeds him at the library. See the contemporary Ma'ariv report and ויקיפדיה העברית.

ר׳ ראובן מרגליות dies at Ichilov Hospital on 7 Elul 5731, 28 August 1971, aged eighty-one. His funeral leaves his home at 3 Yavne Street, and he is buried in Nahalat Yitzhak Cemetery. See the following day's obituary in Davar and the National Library authority record.

ר׳ ישראל אבוחצירא.event: ר׳ ישראל אבוחצירא is born on 26 September 1889 at Rissani in the Tafilalt. See the authority record and Israeli Ministry of Education biography.
After intensive study in the family yeshiva, ר׳ ישראל אבוחצירא assumes increasing teaching and communal responsibilities; the year is approximate. See the detailed Hebrew biography.
After French forces execute his brother ר׳ דוד אבוחצירא, ר׳ ישראל אבוחצירא relocates and leads communal life chiefly from Boudenib. See the Hebrew chronology.
ר׳ ישראל אבוחצירא becomes av beit din and leading rabbinic authority in Erfoud. See the detailed Hebrew biography.
ר׳ ישראל אבוחצירא immigrates to Israel and initially stays in Jerusalem; he later travels through France and Tunisia and returns to Morocco. See the Ministry of Education biography.
Returning permanently to Israel, ר׳ ישראל אבוחצירא resides first in Yavne and then Ashkelon. See the Ministry of Education biography.
ר׳ ישראל אבוחצירא settles in Netivot, where his home becomes a destination for counsel, prayer and blessing; the exact year is approximate. See the Hebrew chronology.
ר׳ ישראל אבוחצירא dies on 4 Shevat 5744 (8 January 1984) and is buried in Netivot, where his grave becomes a major pilgrimage center. See the authority record.

ר׳ אברהם חיים נאה.event: ר׳ אברהם חיים נאה is born in Hebron on 3 May 1890 to ר׳ מנחם מנדל נאה, head of Magen Avot. See HaChacham HaYomi.

ר׳ אברהם חיים נאה.place: Torat Chaim Yeshiva, Old City of Jerusalem
ר׳ אברהם חיים נאה.event: After his family moves to Jerusalem, ר׳ אברהם חיים נאה studies at Ohel Moshe and then Torat Chaim. The displayed year is approximate. See the Hebrew biography.
As a Chabad emissary, ר׳ אברהם חיים נאה serves and teaches Bukharan Jewry in Samarkand. See HaChacham HaYomi.

Expelled from Ottoman Palestine as a Russian subject during the First World War, ר׳ אברהם חיים נאה reaches Alexandria, establishes Yeshivat Eretz Yisrael for exiles and writes practical halakhic guidance. See the Hebrew biographical account.
After the war ר׳ אברהם חיים נאה returns to Jerusalem and becomes court scribe and close assistant to ר׳ יוסף חיים זוננפלד. See Chabadpedia’s sourced biography.
Serving the Bukharan Quarter and teaching at Musayof, ר׳ אברהם חיים נאה begins publishing קצות השולחן. See the Chabad Library account.
ר׳ אברהם חיים נאה publishes his mature system of halakhic measurements in שיעורי תורה, making traditional quantities usable in modern units. See the works survey.
ר׳ אברהם חיים נאה dies on 21 July 1954 and is buried at Har HaMenuchot. See HaChacham HaYomi.

ר׳ יעקב קמינצקי.event: ר׳ יעקב קמינצקי is born in Kalushkove on 28 February 1891; his family is also closely associated with nearby Dolhinov. The village-level coordinate is approximate because the historic locality is not securely geocoded. See Encyclopaedia Judaica via JVL.

ר׳ יעקב קמינצקי.place: Slabodka, Kaunas, Russian Empire; now Lithuania
ר׳ יעקב קמינצקי.event: As a young scholar, ר׳ יעקב קמינצקי studies for many years at Slabodka under ר׳ משה מרדכי אפשטיין and ר׳ נתן צבי פינקל. The displayed year is an approximate study-period marker. See the Encyclopaedia Judaica biography.
ר׳ יעקב קמינצקי accepts his first communal rabbinate in Tytuvėnai, serving there until 1937. See the biographical chronology.
Leaving Europe, ר׳ יעקב קמינצקי serves briefly at Seattle’s Bikur Cholim Congregation. See the Encyclopaedia Judaica biography.
Later in 1937 ר׳ יעקב קמינצקי moves to Toronto, where he serves Congregation Toras Emes and leads a yeshivah. See the biographical account.

ר׳ יעקב קמינצקי.place: Mesivta Torah Vodaath, Brooklyn, New York
ר׳ יעקב קמינצקי.event: ר׳ יעקב קמינצקי joins the faculty of Torah Vodaath; by 1948 he shares leadership with ר׳ גדליה שור. The coordinate marks the yeshivah’s Brooklyn campus. See Encyclopaedia Judaica.

After retiring from daily yeshivah leadership, ר׳ יעקב קמינצקי settles in Monsey and continues teaching, writing and advising individuals and institutions from his home. See the documented Monsey house history.

ר׳ יעקב קמינצקי.place: Baltimore, Maryland; burial in Queens, New York
ר׳ יעקב קמינצקי.event: ר׳ יעקב קמינצקי dies in Baltimore on 10 March 1986 and is buried at Mount Judah Cemetery in Queens. See the contemporary JTA obituary and cemetery record.

ר׳ צבי יהודה הכהן קוק.event: ר׳ צבי יהודה הכהן קוק is born on Passover eve 1891 in Žeimelis, where his father ר׳ אברהם יצחק הכהן קוק is rabbi. See Mercaz HaRav’s institutional biography.
The Kook family moves to Bauska, where ר׳ צבי יהודה הכהן קוק studies Torah with tutors and his father. See Mercaz HaRav.
ר׳ צבי יהודה הכהן קוק immigrates with his family and reaches Jaffa on 28 Iyar 1904. See the Hebrew institutional biography.

ר׳ צבי יהודה הכהן קוק.place: Torat Chaim Yeshiva, Old City of Jerusalem
ר׳ צבי יהודה הכהן קוק.event: ר׳ צבי יהודה הכהן קוק studies at Torat Chaim under ר׳ זרח אפשטיין before returning to learn principally with his father. See Da’at’s Hebrew biography.
ר׳ צבי יהודה הכהן קוק teaches Torah in Halberstadt; war brings brief detention because he is classified as a Russian enemy subject. See Da’at.
Released from Germany, ר׳ צבי יהודה הכהן קוק joins his parents in Switzerland during the First World War and studies closely with his father. See the concise Hebrew chronology.
While travelling for Degel Yerushalayim, ר׳ צבי יהודה הכהן קוק marries Chava Leah, daughter of ר׳ יהודה לייב הוטנר, in Warsaw. See Mercaz HaRav.
Returning to Jerusalem, ר׳ צבי יהודה הכהן קוק becomes administrative director of Mercaz HaRav and a principal editor of his father’s writings. See the sourced chronology.
After the death of ר׳ יעקב משה חרל״פ, ר׳ צבי יהודה הכהן קוק becomes rosh yeshiva and builds Mercaz HaRav into the central academy of Religious Zionism. See Mercaz HaRav.

ר׳ צבי יהודה הכהן קוק.place: Jerusalem and Mount of Olives, Israel
ר׳ צבי יהודה הכהן קוק.event: ר׳ צבי יהודה הכהן קוק dies in Jerusalem on 9 March 1982 and is buried on the Mount of Olives. See the contemporary JTA obituary.

ר׳ אהרן קוטלר.place: Svislach, then Russian Empire; now Belarus
ר׳ אהרן קוטלר.event: ר׳ אהרן קוטלר, originally Aharon Pines, is born in Svislach in 1892 to ר׳ שניאור זלמן פינס קוטלר, the local rabbi. He later uses the surname Kotler, reportedly adopted from a relative to avoid Russian military conscription. The marker is town-level because the family home is not securely identified. See the National Library of Israel authority record and the Hebrew Yeshiva biography.

At about eleven, the orphaned ר׳ אהרן קוטלר is sent to Krynki to study under ר׳ זלמן סנדר כהנא שפירא. The year is approximate, calculated from the age reported by the source. See the Hebrew Yeshiva biography.

ר׳ אהרן קוטלר.place: Slabodka, Kovno; now Vilijampolė, Kaunas, Lithuania
ר׳ אהרן קוטלר.event: After a period with relatives in Minsk, where ר׳ רפאל ראובן גרוזובסקי encourages him to attend Slabodka, ר׳ אהרן קוטלר enters Yeshivat Knesset Yisrael at about thirteen. He studies in the environment shaped by ר׳ נתן צבי פינקל and ר׳ משה מרדכי אפשטיין and rapidly gains a reputation as an exceptional scholar. The year is approximate. See the Hebrew Yeshiva biography.

After marrying Chana Perel, daughter of ר׳ איסר זלמן מלצר, ר׳ אהרן קוטלר joins the faculty of Yeshivat Etz Chaim in Slutsk. The marriage is placed at about age twenty-two; from 1917 he is documented as a regular maggid shiur. See the Da'at biographical entry and the Hebrew Yeshiva biography.

ר׳ אהרן קוטלר.place: Kletsk, Second Polish Republic; now Belarus
ר׳ אהרן קוטלר.event: Facing Soviet repression, ר׳ אהרן קוטלר leads a substantial group of the Slutsk yeshiva across the frontier to Kletsk. He develops the institution into one of interwar Poland's important Lithuanian yeshivot; ר׳ איסר זלמן מלצר joins it in 1923 before emigrating to Jerusalem in 1925. See the Da'at Jewish Encyclopedia.

ר׳ אהרן קוטלר.place: London and New York; fundraising journey
ר׳ אהרן קוטלר.event: ר׳ אהרן קוטלר travels through England and the United States to raise funds for the Kletsk yeshiva. His American stay lasts many months and exposes him directly to the possibilities and limitations of advanced Torah study in the United States. This marker represents the London stage of a documented transatlantic journey. See the Hebrew Yeshiva biography and Da'at.

After the destruction of independent Poland, the Kletsk yeshiva regroups first in Vilna and then in Jonava. ר׳ אהרן קוטלר continues teaching under Soviet rule until the authorities close the yeshiva in early 1941. The marker is placed in Vilna, the best-documented initial refuge and coordinating center. See the Hebrew Yeshiva biography.

After traveling through Siberia and Japan, ר׳ אהרן קוטלר reaches the United States in 1941. Rather than mapping an undocumented Japanese building, this marker records his secure destination. He becomes a leading member of Vaad Hatzalah, working to rescue rabbis and yeshiva students trapped in Europe; the Yeshiva University archive preserves correspondence from his later chairmanship. See the Hebrew Yeshiva biography, the Yeshiva University Vaad Hatzala archive, and the JDC wartime records guide.

ר׳ אהרן קוטלר.place: Beth Medrash Govoha, 617 Sixth Street, Lakewood, New Jersey
ר׳ אהרן קוטלר.event: ר׳ אהרן קוטלר opens Beth Medrash Govoha in Lakewood with a small founding group, deliberately creating a setting for intensive full-time Torah study away from New York City's distractions. The coordinate is centered on the historic 617 Sixth Street campus nucleus, not merely on Lakewood town center. See the Hebrew Yeshiva biography and the BMG institutional catalogue.

ר׳ אהרן קוטלר.place: Lakewood and New York; support for Torah education in Israel
ר׳ אהרן קוטלר.event: ר׳ אהרן קוטלר helps establish and becomes a principal American advocate and fundraiser for Chinuch Atzmai, founded in Israel in 1953. Because the evidence establishes organizational leadership but not his physical presence at a specific Israeli founding meeting, the marker remains at his Lakewood base rather than inventing a Jerusalem journey. See the history of the Independent Education System and the National Library authority record.

ר׳ אהרן קוטלר.place: Columbia-Presbyterian Medical Center, New York City
ר׳ אהרן קוטלר.event: ר׳ אהרן קוטלר dies in New York on 29 November 1962, not in Lakewood as the former project record stated. Contemporary reporting identifies New York as the place of death. See the Jewish Telegraphic Agency death report and the contemporary Haaretz report in the National Library.

After major funeral observances in the United States, the remains of ר׳ אהרן קוטלר are flown to Israel and buried on Har HaMenuchot in Jerusalem. Contemporary JTA reporting records the Jerusalem burial and the large attendance. See the Jewish Telegraphic Agency burial report.

ר׳ אליהו אליעזר דסלר.place: Homel, Russian Empire; now Gomel, Belarus
ר׳ אליהו אליעזר דסלר.event: ר׳ אליהו אליעזר דסלר is born in Homel in 1892. This corrects the former map coordinate, which incorrectly placed Homel in Moscow. See the sourced biography.
ר׳ אליהו אליעזר דסלר enters the Kelm Talmud Torah, absorbing its rigorous mussar method. See Nechama’s Hebrew biographical profile.
ר׳ אליהו אליעזר דסלר moves to England and begins teaching in London’s East End while establishing himself economically. See the biographical chronology.
Joined by his family, ר׳ אליהו אליעזר דסלר teaches and builds a local Torah-learning circle in Dalston. See the sourced biography.
ר׳ אליהו אליעזר דסלר becomes a founder and senior spiritual force of the Gateshead Kollel, helping rebuild advanced Torah study in wartime Britain. See the career account.

ר׳ אליהו אליעזר דסלר.place: Ponovezh Yeshiva, Bnei Brak, Mandatory Palestine
ר׳ אליהו אליעזר דסלר.event: At the invitation of ר׳ יוסף שלמה כהנמן, ר׳ אליהו אליעזר דסלר becomes mashgiach of Ponovezh Yeshiva. See the Hebrew biographical study.
ר׳ אליהו אליעזר דסלר dies in Bnei Brak on 31 December 1953 and is buried in the city. His teachings are subsequently edited as מכתב מאליהו. See the National Library catalogue record.

ר׳ אהרן ראטה.event: ר׳ אהרן ראטה is born at Ungvár in 1894 to ר׳ שמואל יעקב and Yenta Roth. The coordinate is town-level. See the National Library of Israel authority record and Commons authority category.

ר׳ אהרן ראטה forms the fellowship that becomes Shomrei Emunim at Satu Mare, demanding disciplined prayer, modesty, ritual purity and mutual responsibility. See the Hebrew history of Toldot Aharon and sourced biography.

During an early period in Jerusalem, ר׳ אהרן ראטה gathers disciples among the Old Yishuv before returning to Transcarpathia. Sources establish the period but not a precise first-year building, so the date and point are approximate. See the biographical synthesis.

ר׳ אהרן ראטה.place: Berehovo, Czechoslovakia; now Ukraine; year approximate
ר׳ אהרן ראטה.event: ר׳ אהרן ראטה leads a Hasidic community at Berehovo during the 1930s and publishes works of devotional discipline, including טהרת הקודש. See the sourced biography and Commons authority record.

ר׳ אהרן ראטה settles permanently in Jerusalem and establishes the Shomrei Emunim court, centred in the religious neighbourhoods of the Old Yishuv. See the first-edition biographical description and sourced biography.

ר׳ אהרן ראטה publishes שומר אמונים, his defining work on faith, providence and spiritual endurance amid the catastrophe overtaking European Jewry. See the National Library of Israel catalogue and bibliographical account.

ר׳ אהרן ראטה dies in Jerusalem on 6 Nisan 5707. His movement divides between the Shomrei Emunim leadership of his son ר׳ אברהם חיים ראטה and the Toldot Aharon leadership of his son-in-law ר׳ אברהם יצחק קאהן. See the sourced biography and Hebrew dynastic history.

ר׳ ישראל ברודי.event: ר׳ ישראל ברודי is born in Newcastle upon Tyne on 10 May 1895 to Aaron Brode and Jane Magid, Lithuanian Jewish immigrants. See the Australian Dictionary of Biography.

ר׳ ישראל ברודי.place: Jews’ College and University College London, London
ר׳ ישראל ברודי.event: ר׳ ישראל ברודי enrols at both Jews’ College and University College London, graduating in 1915 with first-class honours in Hebrew, Aramaic and Syriac before continuing at Balliol College, Oxford. See the Australian Dictionary of Biography.
Studies interrupted, ר׳ ישראל ברודי serves as a British Army Jewish chaplain in France from 1917 to 1919. See the Australian Dictionary of Biography.

ר׳ ישראל ברודי becomes minister of Melbourne Hebrew Congregation and head of the Victorian Beth Din. The congregation moves from Bourke Street to its Toorak Road synagogue in 1930. See the Australian Dictionary of Biography.

ר׳ ישראל ברודי becomes founding president of the Zionist Federation of Australia, advocating Zionism and cooperation among Australian Jewish communities until 1937. See the Australian Dictionary of Biography.

Serving again as an army chaplain, ר׳ ישראל ברודי is among the last evacuees from Dunkirk; he later serves with the RAF in the Middle East and becomes senior Jewish chaplain in 1944. See the Australian Dictionary of Biography.
ר׳ ישראל ברודי is appointed principal of Jews’ College in 1946 after his wartime service. See the Australian Dictionary of Biography.
ר׳ ישראל ברודי succeeds ר׳ יוסף הרמן הרץ as chief rabbi of Great Britain and the Commonwealth, serving until 1965. See the Australian Dictionary of Biography.

The refusal of ר׳ ישראל ברודי to approve ר׳ לואיס ג׳ייקובס for the principalship of Jews’ College becomes the defining institutional conflict of his later chief rabbinate. See the documented overview.
Four years after retiring, ר׳ ישראל ברודי is knighted in 1969—not in 1965 as the former record stated—for his public and communal service. See the Australian Dictionary of Biography.

ר׳ ישראל ברודי.place: Lambeth and Willesden Jewish Cemetery, London
ר׳ ישראל ברודי.event: ר׳ ישראל ברודי dies in Lambeth on 13 February 1979 and is buried at Willesden Jewish Cemetery. See the Australian Dictionary of Biography and burial record.

ר׳ משה פיינשטיין.place: Uzda, Minsk Governorate, Russian Empire; now Belarus
ר׳ משה פיינשטיין.event: ר׳ משה פיינשטיין is born on 7 Adar 5655 (3 March 1895) in Uzda, where his father ר׳ דוד פיינשטיין serves as rabbi. He receives his earliest Torah education from his father. See the Orthodox Union biography, contemporary JTA obituary and Encyclopaedia Judaica.

ר׳ משה פיינשטיין.place: Starobin, Minsk Governorate, Russian Empire; now Belarus; date approximate
ר׳ משה פיינשטיין.event: When ר׳ דוד פיינשטיין transfers from Uzda to the rabbinate of Starobin, the young ר׳ משה פיינשטיין moves with his family and continues studying under his father. Sources document the family stage but do not uniformly date the move, so 1907 is retained as an approximate map marker. See the JTA obituary and the Orthodox Union biography.

ר׳ משה פיינשטיין.place: Shklov, Mogilev Governorate, Russian Empire; now Belarus
ר׳ משה פיינשטיין.event: After studying in the Slutsk yeshivah world, ר׳ משה פיינשטיין joins the yeshivah led by ר׳ פסח פרוסקין in Shklov. He later consistently regards ר׳ פסח פרוסקין as his principal rebbe; ר׳ איסר זלמן מלצר and his uncle ר׳ יעקב קנטרוביץ also influence his formation. See JTA, the Orthodox Union and the scholarly Hebrew Kotar study.

ר׳ משה פיינשטיין.place: Mstislavl, Mogilev Governorate, Russian Empire; now Belarus
ר׳ משה פיינשטיין.event: ר׳ משה פיינשטיין continues with ר׳ פסח פרוסקין's yeshivah after its transfer from Shklov to Mstislavl. The event corrects the former map coordinate, which placed Shklov at longitude 0.29 rather than in Belarus. See the biographical synthesis in the Orthodox Union profile and the JTA obituary.

After marrying Shima Kustanovich in 1920, ר׳ משה פיינשטיין becomes rabbi of Lyuban in 1921. For sixteen years he maintains communal religious life and answers halakhic questions under increasingly restrictive Soviet rule. See Encyclopaedia Judaica, the Orthodox Union and the Hebrew biographical study.

ר׳ משה פיינשטיין.place: Mesivtha Tifereth Jerusalem, 145–147 East Broadway, New York City
ר׳ משה פיינשטיין.event: In January 1937, ר׳ משה פיינשטיין, Shima and their children leave the Soviet Union and settle on New York's Lower East Side. He joins Mesivtha Tifereth Jerusalem to develop its advanced beit midrash and semikhah programme and becomes rosh yeshivah after ר׳ יוסף אדלר's death in 1938. See the JTA obituary, the New York Jewish Week institutional history and the Orthodox Union.

ר׳ משה פיינשטיין.place: Mesivtha Tifereth Jerusalem, New York City
ר׳ משה פיינשטיין.event: ר׳ משה פיינשטיין publishes the first volumes of אגרות משה in New York. The expanding responsa collection records answers sent to students, rabbis, institutions and individuals on ritual, marriage, medicine, technology, commerce and American communal conditions. See the University of California Berkeley library record, the National Library of Israel and the Hebrew Kotar study.

By the 1960s, ר׳ משה פיינשטיין is chairing Agudath Israel of America's Moetzes Gedolei HaTorah and serving in senior leadership of the Union of Orthodox Rabbis while advising Torah Umesorah and Chinuch Atzmai. The year is a representative marker for responsibilities extending over decades, not a single appointment date. See the contemporary JTA obituary and the Orthodox Union biography.

ר׳ משה פיינשטיין.place: Mesivtha Tifereth Jerusalem, New York City
ר׳ משה פיינשטיין.event: ר׳ משה פיינשטיין dies in New York on 13 Adar II 5746 (23 March 1986), aged ninety-one. More than 20,000 mourners gather around MTJ on East Broadway for the New York funeral before his coffin is flown to Israel. See the JTA obituary, the contemporary Los Angeles Times report and the New York Jewish Week photograph and history.

After transfer from New York, ר׳ משה פיינשטיין is buried at Har HaMenuchot in Jerusalem near his teacher ר׳ איסר זלמן מלצר. Contemporary reports describe an exceptionally large Jerusalem procession; numerical estimates vary widely and are not presented here as a settled figure. See the contemporary UPI report, the Los Angeles Times and the Har HaMenuchot history.

ר׳ אלעזר מנחם מן שך.event: ר׳ אלעזר מנחם מן שך is born in Vabalninkas on 1 January 1899. See the sourced biography.
At about ten, ר׳ אלעזר מנחם מן שך enters the Panevėžys yeshivah. See the biographical chronology.
ר׳ אלעזר מנחם מן שך transfers to Knesses Yisrael in Slabodka, part of a sequence of wartime Lithuanian yeshivot. See Moreshet’s Hebrew biography.
During the First World War ר׳ אלעזר מנחם מן שך reaches the Slutsk yeshivah and studies under ר׳ איסר זלמן מלצר. See The Jewish Observer memorial issue.
With eastern European yeshivah life in crisis, ר׳ אלעזר מנחם מן שך reaches Vilnius before obtaining passage to Mandatory Palestine. See the memorial biography.
ר׳ אלעזר מנחם מן שך immigrates to Mandatory Palestine and begins teaching in the yeshivah world. See the sourced biography.
ר׳ אלעזר מנחם מן שך joins the leadership of Ponovezh Yeshiva, where he remains the dominant senior rosh yeshiva for decades. See the career chronology.
ר׳ אלעזר מנחם מן שך backs the creation of Shas as a Sephardi Haredi political framework. See the political biography.
After a split within Agudath Israel, ר׳ אלעזר מנחם מן שך founds Degel HaTorah to represent the Lithuanian-Haredi constituency. See the political chronology.
ר׳ אלעזר מנחם מן שך dies on 2 November 2001 and is buried in Bnei Brak after a mass funeral. See the contemporary memorial issue.

ר׳ יעקב ישראל קניבסקי.event: ר׳ יעקב ישראל קניבסקי was born on 17 June 1899 (commonly given as 9 Tammuz 5659) in Tashan, where his father ר׳ חיים פרץ קניבסקי served as a shochet. Some English summaries incorrectly make Hornostaypil his birthplace; Hebrew biographical accounts distinguish Tashan from the family’s later home. The exact modern identification of this historical ‘Tashan’ is not entirely uniform, so the marker uses the Tashan/Teofipol identification preserved by the Volhynian heritage association. Hebrew biography; Volhynian heritage association

After the death of his father, eleven-year-old ר׳ יעקב ישראל קניבסקי moved with his mother to her family in Hornostaypil near Chernobyl. The nickname ‘Steipler’ derives from this town, not from a rabbinic office. Hebrew biography

Before reaching the age of twelve, ר׳ יעקב ישראל קניבסקי entered the Novardok yeshiva in Navahrudak, where the educational program shaped by ר׳ יוסף יוזל הורוביץ joined intensive Talmud study to the Novardok form of Mussar. Hebrew biography; Novardok background

As the First World War disrupted the region, ר׳ יעקב ישראל קניבסקי followed the Novardok yeshiva eastward to Homel, continuing his studies amid wartime displacement. Sources generally place this transfer in 1915 rather than the unsourced 1914 date in the former project record. Hebrew biographical profile

At approximately twenty, ר׳ יעקב ישראל קניבסקי was forcibly conscripted into the Red Army and assigned to guard military installations in the Moscow region. Accounts emphasize the difficulty of maintaining Sabbath observance and Torah practice; the marker is deliberately regional because a reliably identified barracks has not been found. Hebrew biographical profile; Routledge reference

ר׳ יעקב ישראל קניבסקי crossed the Soviet–Polish frontier and joined the central Beit Yosef–Novardok yeshiva in Białystok, where he became associated with the Polish branch of the movement. Manuscript provenance and biographical note

After marrying Pesha Miriam Karelitz, sister of ר׳ אברהם ישעיהו קרליץ, ר׳ יעקב ישראל קניבסקי moved to Pinsk and served from 1927 to 1934 as a senior lecturer in the Beit Yosef–Novardok yeshiva led by ר׳ שמואל וינטרוב. This corrects the former entry’s description of him as the yeshiva’s sole rosh yeshiva. Hebrew institutional history; Hebrew biography

ר׳ יעקב ישראל קניבסקי immigrated to Mandatory Palestine, settled in Bnei Brak, and became head of Beit Yosef–Novardok Yeshiva in the Givat Rokach neighbourhood. His arrival was encouraged by his brother-in-law ר׳ אברהם ישעיהו קרליץ and the yeshiva’s founder ר׳ מתתיהו שציגל. The marker represents the historic yeshiva area rather than a claimed surviving classroom. Yeshiva history; Contemporary immigration reference cited in biography

From Bnei Brak, ר׳ יעקב ישראל קניבסקי began issuing the series that became קהלות יעקב, publishing ten early volumes between 1936 and 1956 before later reorganizing and expanding the material by Talmudic tractate. This is a scholarly milestone at his residence, not a movement inferred from a printer’s address. Hebrew works bibliography; National Library of Israel authority record

When Beit Yosef–Novardok Yeshiva ceased operating around 1960, ר׳ יעקב ישראל קניבסקי remained in Bnei Brak, concentrating on study, publication, an annual public lesson at Kollel Chazon Ish, and receiving the growing number of people who sought scholarly or personal guidance. Yeshiva chronology; Hebrew biographical account

A contemporary visitor recorded meeting ר׳ יעקב ישראל קניבסקי at his home at 10 Rashbam Street in Bnei Brak and identified the nearby Lederman synagogue as his regular synagogue. This provides a building-level anchor for his final years, replacing the generic city-centre marker previously used. Contemporary recollection published in The Jewish Observer

ר׳ יעקב ישראל קניבסקי died in Bnei Brak on 10 August 1985, 23 Av 5745, and was buried in the Shomrei Shabbos cemetery beside ר׳ אברהם ישעיהו קרליץ. The marker is fixed to the cemetery, not merely to central Bnei Brak. Cemetery coordinates; Hebrew biography

ר׳ חיים לייב הלוי שמואלביץ.place: Kovno, Russian Empire; now Kaunas, Lithuania
ר׳ חיים לייב הלוי שמואלביץ.event: ר׳ חיים לייב הלוי שמואלביץ is born in Kovno on the second day of Rosh Hashanah 5663 to ר׳ רפאל אלתר שמואלביץ and Ettel Horowitz, daughter of ר׳ יוסף יוזל הורוויץ of Novardok. See Mir Yeshiva's institutional history and the JTA obituary.

After growing up partly in Stutchin, ר׳ חיים לייב הלוי שמואלביץ continues at the Shaarei Torah yeshiva in Grodno after his father dies in 1919. He studies under ר׳ שמעון יהודה שקופ and, while still young, is entrusted with an advanced class. See the contemporary JTA obituary and Eliahu Meir Klugman's biographical account.

ר׳ חיים לייב הלוי שמואלביץ joins the Mir Yeshiva with a group of Grodno students about 1924–25. He marries Chana Miriam, daughter of rosh yeshiva ר׳ אליעזר יהודה פינקל, in January 1930 and becomes a regular lecturer in 1936—not the yeshiva's mashgiach. See the JTA obituary and Mir Yeshiva history.

Following the German and Soviet invasions of Poland, ר׳ חיים לייב הלוי שמואלביץ and the Mir Yeshiva leave Mir for Vilna, where the refugee institution remains for roughly two months before moving onward. See the JewishGen history of the Mir Yeshiva's escape.

The Mir Yeshiva reassembles at Kėdainiai in 1940. When Soviet authorities order it to disperse, ר׳ חיים לייב הלוי שמואלביץ continues teaching and leads one division based at Krakės while plans for escape are pursued. See the JewishGen Mir Yeshiva history and the official Mir account.

Using transit visas issued through the Japanese consulate in Kaunas, the Mir refugees travel across the Soviet Union to Vladivostok and by sea to Japan. ר׳ חיים לייב הלוי שמואלביץ continues the yeshiva's learning during its approximately six-month stay in Kobe. See the JewishGen institutional history.

Forced from Japan to Shanghai, ר׳ חיים לייב הלוי שמואלביץ leads Mir's Talmudic program and bears major responsibility for hundreds of students, rabbis and family members until 1947; ר׳ יחזקאל לוינשטיין serves as mashgiach. He increases the general shiurim despite war, poverty and Japanese surveillance. See the official Mir Yeshiva history and a surviving Shanghai letter description.

When Mir's Shanghai contingent reaches the United States in 1947, ר׳ חיים לייב הלוי שמואלביץ spends about six months with it before answering his father-in-law's call to help build Mir in Jerusalem. See Mir Yeshiva's institutional history.

ר׳ חיים לייב הלוי שמואלביץ joins ר׳ אליעזר יהודה פינקל at Mir Jerusalem. After his father-in-law dies in 1965, he serves as rosh yeshiva; his Talmudic lectures and weekly mussar talks attract large audiences, and the 1971–73 talks form שיחות מוסר. See the official Mir history, the National Library catalogue, and the JTA obituary.

ר׳ חיים לייב הלוי שמואלביץ dies in Jerusalem late on 2 January 1979 (3 Tevet 5739), aged 76, after an illness. Thousands of yeshiva students and religious leaders attend his funeral, and he is buried at Har HaMenuchot. See the JTA report published the following day.

ר׳ מנחם מענדל שניאורסון.place: Nikolaev, Russian Empire; now Mykolaiv, Ukraine
